6.4. Outercollaring of flow categories, multimodules, and homotopies
Let 𝐂¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}} be a regular stratification category which admits the outercollaring construction. Let 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} be a flow category enriched in 𝐂¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}}. Fix an ϵ>0\epsilon>0 (the outercollaring width). Define the ϵ\epsilon-outercollaring of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}, which is a flow category ⌊𝔽{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{F}} enriched in ⌊𝐂¯{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf C}}, as follows. The set of objects is the same as 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}. For each pair p,q∈Ob​𝔽p,q\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}, the morphism space is
Mp​q⌊ϵ𝔽:=⌊Mp​q𝔽.M_{pq}^{{}_{\lfloor}{}_{\epsilon}{\mathbb{F}}}:={}_{\lfloor}M_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}.
For p≤r≤qp\leq r\leq q, the composition is the outercollaring
ιp​r​q⌊𝔽:=ιp​r​q𝔽⌊ϵ:(Mp​r𝔽×Mr​q𝔽)⌊≅Mp​r𝔽⌊×Mr​q𝔽⌊≅Mp​r⌊𝔽×Mr​q⌊𝔽→Mp​q𝔽⌊≅Mp​q⌊𝔽.\iota_{prq}^{{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{F}}}:={}_{\lfloor}{}_{\epsilon}\iota_{prq}^{\mathbb{F}}:{}_{\lfloor}(M_{pr}^{\mathbb{F}}\times M_{rq}^{\mathbb{F}})\cong{}_{\lfloor}M_{pr}^{\mathbb{F}}\times{}_{\lfloor}M_{rq}^{\mathbb{F}}\cong M_{pr}^{{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{F}}}\times M_{rq}^{{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{F}}}\to{}_{\lfloor}M_{pq}^{{\mathbb{F}}}\cong M_{pq}^{{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{F}}}.
It is straightforward to check that this set of data satisfies the definition of flow categories.
The case of outercollaring of multimodules and homotopies are similar. We omit the details. We remark that one must choose the same outercollaring width of involved flow categories to obtain a corresponding outercollaring of multimodules and homotopies.
6.5. Multimodule concatenations
6.5.1. Bimodule concatenations
Before we discuss the more general multimodule concatenation, we first consider the bimodule case, which was discussed in [2, Section 5].
We first describe the intuitive picture. Suppose 𝔽,𝔽′,𝔽′′{\mathbb{F}},{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime},{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime\prime} are flow categories enriched in 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}, 𝔹{\mathbb{B}} is a bimodule over (𝔽;𝔽′)({\mathbb{F}};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}) and 𝔹′{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime} is a bimodule over (𝔽′;𝔽′′)({\mathbb{F}}^{\prime};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime\prime}). For example, 𝔹{\mathbb{B}} and 𝔹′{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime} are bimodules corresponding to continuation maps. We would like to define a bimodule 𝔹∘𝔹′{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime} over (𝔽;𝔽′′)({\mathbb{F}};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime\prime}) which characterizes the features of compositions of continuation maps. Then given a pair of objects p∈Ob​𝔽p\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}} and p′′∈Ob​𝔽′′p^{\prime\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime\prime}, the space Mp;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′M_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} should be the quotient
(⨆p′∈Ob​𝔽′Mp;p′𝔹×Mp′;p′′𝔹′)/∼\left(\bigsqcup_{p^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}M_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times M_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\right)/\sim
(6.10)
where the equivalence relation is generated by viewing the images of points of
Mp;p′𝔹×Mp′​q′𝔽′×Mq′;p′′𝔹′M_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times M_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}\times M_{q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}
in either Mp;p′𝔹×Mp′;p′′𝔹′M_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times M_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} or Mp;q′𝔹×Mq′;p′′𝔹′M_{p;q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times M_{q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} the same point.
However, this construction does not work for any category 𝐂¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}}. For example, when 𝐂¯=𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}}=\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}, because of the symmetry groups, there is no obvious way to construct the above quotient in 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}.
To rigorously define the notion of concatenations, one needs some preparations. Let 𝔽,𝔽′,𝔽′′\mathbb{F},\mathbb{F}^{\prime},\mathbb{F}^{\prime\prime} be flow categories. Let 𝔹\mathbb{B} be a bimodule over (𝔽;𝔽′)({\mathbb{F}};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}) and 𝔹′\mathbb{B}^{\prime} be a bimodule over (𝔽′;𝔽′′)({\mathbb{F}}^{\prime};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime\prime}). For each pair of objects p∈Ob​𝔽p\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}} and p′′∈Ob​𝔽′′p^{\prime\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime\prime}, define the set
Ap;p′′𝔹′∘𝔹:=(⨆p′∈Ob​𝔽′Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′)/∼A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}\circ{\mathbb{B}}}:=\left(\bigsqcup_{p^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}\mathbb{F}^{\prime}}A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\right)/\sim
where the equivalence relation ∼\sim is defined as follows. For any p′,q′∈Ob​𝔽′p^{\prime},q^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} images of the two maps
Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′​q′𝔽′×Aq′;p′′𝔹′\textstyle{A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times A_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}\times A_{q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Id×ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′\scriptstyle{{\rm Id}\times\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}}ιp;p′​q′𝔹×Id\scriptstyle{\iota_{p;p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times{\rm Id}}Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′\textstyle{A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}}Ap;q′𝔹×Aq′;p′′𝔹′\textstyle{A_{p;q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times A_{q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}}
are identified. The equivalence relation ∼\sim is generated by this identification.
Lemma 6.8.
Two pairs (a′,a′′)∈Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′(a^{\prime},a^{\prime\prime})\in A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} and (b′,b′′)∈Ap;q′𝔹×Aq′;p′′𝔹′(b^{\prime},b^{\prime\prime})\in A_{p;q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times A_{q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} are equivalent if and only if one of the following conditions holds: 1) p′≤q′p^{\prime}\leq q^{\prime} and there exists v∈Ap′​q′𝔽′v\in A_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} such that
b′=ιp;p′​q′𝔹​(a′,v),\displaystyle\ b^{\prime}=\iota_{p;p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}(a^{\prime},v),\
a′′=ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(v,b′′);\displaystyle\ a^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(v,b^{\prime\prime});
2) q′≤p′q^{\prime}\leq p^{\prime} and there exists w∈Aq′​p′𝔽′w\in A_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} such that
a′=ιp;q′​p′𝔹​(b′,w),\displaystyle\ a^{\prime}=\iota_{p;q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}(b^{\prime},w),\
b′′=ιq′​p′;p′′𝔹′​(w,a′′).\displaystyle\ b^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,a^{\prime\prime}).
Proof.
We first check that the relation defined in the statement of this lemma, denoted by ≈\approx, is an equivalence relation. The only non-obvious condition is the transitivity. Suppose we have three elements (a′,a′′)∈Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′(a^{\prime},a^{\prime\prime})\in A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}, (b′,b′′)∈Ap;q′𝔹×Aq′;p′′𝔹′(b^{\prime},b^{\prime\prime})\in A_{p;q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times A_{q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}, and (c′,c′′)∈Ap;r′𝔹×Ar′;p′′𝔹′(c^{\prime},c^{\prime\prime})\in A_{p;r^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times A_{r^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. Suppose (a′,a′′)≈(b′,b′′)(a^{\prime},a^{\prime\prime})\approx(b^{\prime},b^{\prime\prime}) and (b′,b′′)≈(c′,c′′)(b^{\prime},b^{\prime\prime})\approx(c^{\prime},c^{\prime\prime}). Without loss of generality, we may assume one of the following holds.
(1)
p′≤q′≤r′p^{\prime}\leq q^{\prime}\leq r^{\prime}. In this case, there exists v∈Ap′​q′𝔽′v\in A_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} and w∈Aq′​r′𝔽′w\in A_{q^{\prime}r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} such that
b′=ιp;p′​q′𝔹​(a′,v),\displaystyle\ b^{\prime}=\iota_{p;p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(a^{\prime},v),\
a′′=ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(v,b′′)\displaystyle\ a^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(v,b^{\prime\prime})
and
c′=ιp;q′​r′𝔹​(b′,w),\displaystyle\ c^{\prime}=\iota_{p;q^{\prime}r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(b^{\prime},w),\
b′′=ιq′​r′;p′′𝔹′​(w,c′′).\displaystyle\ b^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{q^{\prime}r^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,c^{\prime\prime}).
Then by the associativity conditions for the bimodules, one has
c′=ιp;q′​r′𝔹​(b′,w)=ιp;q′​r′𝔹​(ιp;p′​q′𝔹​(a′,v),w)=ιp;p′​r′𝔹​(a′,ιp′​q′​r′𝔽′​(v,w))c^{\prime}=\iota_{p;q^{\prime}r^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}(b^{\prime},w)=\iota_{p;q^{\prime}r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(\iota_{p;p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(a^{\prime},v),w)=\iota_{p;p^{\prime}r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(a^{\prime},\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime}r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}(v,w))
and
a′′=ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(v,b′′)=ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(v,ιq′​r′;p′′𝔹′​(w,c′′))=ιp′​r′;p′′𝔹′​(ιp′​q′​r′𝔽′​(v,w),c′′).a^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(v,b^{\prime\prime})=\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(v,\iota_{q^{\prime}r^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,c^{\prime\prime}))=\iota_{p^{\prime}r^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime}r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}(v,w),c^{\prime\prime}).
Hence (a′,a′′)≈(c′,c′′)(a^{\prime},a^{\prime\prime})\approx(c^{\prime},c^{\prime\prime}).
(2)
p′≤q′p^{\prime}\leq q^{\prime} and r′≤q′r^{\prime}\leq q^{\prime}. In this case, there exists v∈Ap′​q′𝔽′v\in A_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} and w∈Ar′​q′𝔽′w\in A_{r^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} such that
b=ιp;p′​q′𝔹​(a,v),a′=ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(v,b′)b=\iota_{p;p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(a,v),\ a^{\prime}=\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(v,b^{\prime})
and
b=ιp;r′​q′𝔹​(c,w),c′=ιr′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(w,b′).b=\iota_{p;r^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(c,w),\ c^{\prime}=\iota_{r^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,b^{\prime}).
Then we see
b∈∂p;p′​q′Ap;q′𝔹∩∂p;r′​q′Ap;q′𝔹≠∅.b\in\partial^{p;p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}A_{p;q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\cap\partial^{p;r^{\prime}q^{\prime}}A_{p;q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\neq\emptyset.
Then by the condition for bimodule/multimodules (see (3) and (4) of Definition 6.3), either r′≤q′r^{\prime}\leq q^{\prime} or q′≤r′q^{\prime}\leq r^{\prime}. Without loss of generality, assume that p′≤r′p^{\prime}\leq r^{\prime}. Then one has
b∈Ap;p′​r′​q′𝔹b\in A_{p;p^{\prime}r^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}
As the poset maps underlying the structural maps are all injective (see Definition 6.1 and Definition 6.3), it follows that there exists u∈Ap′​r′𝔽′u\in A_{p^{\prime}r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} such that
c=ιp;p′​r′𝔹​(a,u),v=ιp′​r′​q′𝔽′​(u,w).c=\iota_{p;p^{\prime}r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(a,u),\ v=\iota_{p^{\prime}r^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}(u,w).
Then by using the associativity of the bimodules, one can conclude that
a′=ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(v,b′)=ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(ιp′​r′​q′𝔽′​(u,w),b′)=ιp′​r′;p′′𝔹′​(u,ιr′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(w,b′))=ιp′​r′;p′′𝔹′​(u,c′)a^{\prime}=\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(v,b^{\prime})=\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(\iota_{p^{\prime}r^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}(u,w),b^{\prime})=\iota_{p^{\prime}r^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(u,\iota_{r^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,b^{\prime}))=\iota_{p^{\prime}r^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(u,c^{\prime})
which implies (a,a′)≈(c,c′)(a,a^{\prime})\approx(c,c^{\prime}).
Therefore, ≈\approx is an equivalence relation.
Then one can see that the two relations ∼\sim and ≈\approx contain each other. Hence the lemma is proved.
∎
The following corollary is an obvious consequence.
Corollary 6.9.
The natural map
Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′→Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\to A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}
is injective.
Denote the image of the above map by
Ap;p′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′.A_{p;p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}.
More generally, assume p1′<⋯<pl′p_{1}^{\prime}<\cdots<p_{l}^{\prime} in 𝔽′{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}, denote
Ap;(p1′⋯pl′);p′′𝔹∘𝔹′=⋂i=1lAp;pi′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′.A_{p;(p_{1}^{\prime}\cdots p_{l}^{\prime});p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}=\bigcap_{i=1}^{l}A_{p;p_{i}^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}.
The following corollary is also obvious.
Corollary 6.10.
If Ap;p′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′∩Ap;q′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′≠∅A_{p;p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\cap A_{p;q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\neq\emptyset, then either p′≤q′p^{\prime}\leq q^{\prime} or q′≤p′q^{\prime}\leq p^{\prime}.
We define a partial order between two elements x,y∈Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′x,y\in A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} as follows. We denote x≤yx\leq y if there exist p′∈Ob​𝔽′p^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}, x′,y′∈Ap′​p′𝔹x^{\prime},y^{\prime}\in A_{p^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}, x′′,y′′∈Ap′;p′′𝔹′x^{\prime\prime},y^{\prime\prime}\in A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} such that x′≤y′x^{\prime}\leq y^{\prime} and x′′≤y′′x^{\prime\prime}\leq y^{\prime\prime} and such that xx is represented by (x′,x′′)(x^{\prime},x^{\prime\prime}) and yy is represented by (y′,y′′)(y^{\prime},y^{\prime\prime}).
Lemma 6.11.
This is a partial order. Moreover, the map Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′→Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\to A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is a poset map.
Proof.
The only non-obvious condition is the transitivity. Suppose x≤y≤zx\leq y\leq z, then there exists p′∈Ob​𝔽′p^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} such that xx is represented by (x′,x′′)∈Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′(x^{\prime},x^{\prime\prime})\in A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}, yy is represented by (y′,y′′)∈Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′(y^{\prime},y^{\prime\prime})\in A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} such that x′≤y′x^{\prime}\leq y^{\prime} and x′′≤y′′x^{\prime\prime}\leq y^{\prime\prime}. There also exists p~′∈Ob​𝔽′\tilde{p}^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} such that yy is represented by (y~′,y~′′)∈Ap;p~′𝔹×Ap~′;p′′𝔹′(\tilde{y}^{\prime},\tilde{y}^{\prime\prime})\in A_{p;\tilde{p}^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times A_{\tilde{p}^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} and zz is represented by (z~′,z~′′)∈Ap;p~′𝔹×Ap~′;p′′𝔹′(\tilde{z}^{\prime},\tilde{z}^{\prime\prime})\in A_{p;\tilde{p}^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times A_{\tilde{p}^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} such that y~′≤z~′\tilde{y}^{\prime}\leq\tilde{z}^{\prime} and y~′′≤z~′′\tilde{y}^{\prime\prime}\leq\tilde{z}^{\prime\prime}. Since (y′,y′′)≈(y~′,y~′′)(y^{\prime},y^{\prime\prime})\approx(\tilde{y}^{\prime},\tilde{y}^{\prime\prime}), by Lemma 6.8, either p′≤p~′p^{\prime}\leq\tilde{p}^{\prime} or p~′≤p′\tilde{p}^{\prime}\leq p^{\prime}.
(1)
When p′≤p~′p^{\prime}\leq\tilde{p}^{\prime}, there exists v∈Ap′​p~′𝔽′v\in A_{p^{\prime}\tilde{p}^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} such that
y~′=ιp;p′​p~′𝔹​(y′,v),\displaystyle\ \tilde{y}^{\prime}=\iota_{p;p^{\prime}\tilde{p}^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(y^{\prime},v),\
y′′=ιp′​p~′;p′′𝔹′​(v,y~′′).\displaystyle\ y^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{p^{\prime}\tilde{p}^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(v,\tilde{y}^{\prime\prime}).
Then define
x~′=ιp;p′​q′𝔹​(x′,v)\tilde{x}^{\prime}=\iota_{p;p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}(x^{\prime},v)
Then as x′≤y′x^{\prime}\leq y^{\prime}, one has x~′≤y~′\tilde{x}^{\prime}\leq\tilde{y}^{\prime}. Moreover, as x′′≤y′′=ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(v,y~′′)x^{\prime\prime}\leq y^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(v,\tilde{y}^{\prime\prime}), it follows that x′′=ιp′​q′;p′′𝔹′​(w,x~′′)x^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,\tilde{x}^{\prime\prime}) for some ww and x~′′\tilde{x}^{\prime\prime}. Moreover, x~′′≤y~′′\tilde{x}^{\prime\prime}\leq\tilde{y}^{\prime\prime}. It then follows that (x′,x′′)≈(x~′,x~′′)(x^{\prime},x^{\prime\prime})\approx(\tilde{x}^{\prime},\tilde{x}^{\prime\prime}) and x~′≤y~′≤z~′\tilde{x}^{\prime}\leq\tilde{y}^{\prime}\leq\tilde{z}^{\prime} and x~′′≤y~′′≤z~′′\tilde{x}^{\prime\prime}\leq\tilde{y}^{\prime\prime}\leq\tilde{z}^{\prime\prime}. Hence x≤zx\leq z.
(2)
When p~′≤p′\tilde{p}^{\prime}\leq p^{\prime}, the argument is similar. There exists w∈Ap~′​p′𝔽′w\in A_{\tilde{p}^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} such that
y′=ιp;p~′​p′𝔹​(y~′,w),\displaystyle\ y^{\prime}=\iota_{p;\tilde{p}^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}(\tilde{y}^{\prime},w),\
y~′′=ιp~′​p′;p′′𝔹′​(w,y′′).\displaystyle\ \tilde{y}^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{\tilde{p}^{\prime}p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,y^{\prime\prime}).
Then define x~′′=ιp~′​p′;p′′𝔹′​(w,x′′)\tilde{x}^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{\tilde{p}^{\prime}p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,x^{\prime\prime}). Then since x′′≤y′′x^{\prime\prime}\leq y^{\prime\prime}, one has
x~′′=ιp~′​p′;p′′𝔹′​(w,x′′)≤ιp~′​p′;p′′𝔹′​(w,y′′)=y~′′≤z~′′.\tilde{x}^{\prime\prime}=\iota_{\tilde{p}^{\prime}p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,x^{\prime\prime})\leq\iota_{\tilde{p}^{\prime}p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}(w,y^{\prime\prime})=\tilde{y}^{\prime\prime}\leq\tilde{z}^{\prime\prime}.
Moreover, as x′≤y′=ιp;p~′​p′𝔹​(y~′,w)∈Ap;p′𝔹x^{\prime}\leq y^{\prime}=\iota_{p;\tilde{p}^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}(\tilde{y}^{\prime},w)\in A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}, there exists x~′∈Ap;p~′𝔹\tilde{x}^{\prime}\in A_{p;\tilde{p}^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}} and u∈Ap~′​p′𝔽′u\in A_{\tilde{p}^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} such that x′=ιp;p~′​p′𝔹​(x~′,u)x^{\prime}=\iota_{p;\tilde{p}^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}(\tilde{x}^{\prime},u) and x~′≤y~′≤z~′\tilde{x}^{\prime}\leq\tilde{y}^{\prime}\leq\tilde{z}^{\prime}. Hence x≤zx\leq z.
Lastly, it follows immediately from the definition of the partial order that the map Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′→Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\to A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is a poset map.
∎
Lemma 6.12.
The poset Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is a normal poset.
Proof.
We first verify that this poset is homogeneous (see Definition 2.3). Let x∈Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′x\in A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} be an arbitrary element. Notice that each Ap;p′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′≅Ap;p′𝔹×Ap′;p′′𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\cong A_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is homogeneous. Hence if x∈Ap;p′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′x\in A_{p;p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}, the depth of xx in this subset is well-defined, denoted by dp′​(x)d_{p^{\prime}}(x). As maximal elements of Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} are exactly maximal elements of Ap;p′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} for all possible p′p^{\prime}, we only need to show that dp′​(x)d_{p^{\prime}}(x) is independent of p′p^{\prime}. Suppose x∈Ap;p′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′∩Ap;q′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′x\in A_{p;p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\cap A_{p;q^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. Without loss of generality, we can assume p′≤q′p^{\prime}\leq q^{\prime}. Then x∈Ap;(p′​q′);p′′𝔹∘𝔹′x\in A_{p;(p^{\prime}q^{\prime});p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. We need to show that dp′​(x)=dq′​(x)d_{p^{\prime}}(x)=d_{q^{\prime}}(x).
Claim. Maximal elements of Ap;(p′​q′);p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;(p^{\prime}q^{\prime});p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} have depth 11.
Proof of the claim. The depth is clearly at least one. If the depth is bigger than 11, then there exists a non-maximal element yy such that x<yx<y. Then there exists r′r^{\prime} different from p′,q′p^{\prime},q^{\prime} such that x∈Ap;r′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′x\in A_{p;r^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. Then by the definition of the equivalence relation, the three elements p′,q′,r′p^{\prime},q^{\prime},r^{\prime} are totally ordered. In either case, xx cannot be a maximal element of Ap;(p′​q′);p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;(p^{\prime}q^{\prime});p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. End of the proof of the claim.
Therefore, both dp′​(x)d_{p^{\prime}}(x) and dq′​(x)d_{q^{\prime}}(x) are 1 higher than the depth of xx in the subset Ap;(p′​q′);p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;(p^{\prime}q^{\prime});p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. Hence dp′​(x)=dq′​(x)d_{p^{\prime}}(x)=d_{q^{\prime}}(x). Hence Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is a homogeneous poset.
Next we need to show that the poset is regular (see Definition 2.4). Given any γ∈Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′\gamma\in A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}, the three conditions for γ\gamma in Definition 2.4 are about elements below γ\gamma. We may assume that γ∈Ap;p′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′\gamma\in A_{p;p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}, which is a regular poset. Hence all three conditions for γ\gamma holds. Therefore, Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is regular.
Lastly, we verify that Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is normal (Definition 2.5), i.e., there are only fake boundaries or true boundaries. Let γ\gamma be an element of depth 11.
Claim. There exist at most two distinct p′∈Ob​𝔽′p^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} such that γ∈Ap;p′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′\gamma\in A_{p;p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}.
Suppose it is not the case, then there exists three distinct p1′,p2′,p3′∈Ob​𝔽′p_{1}^{\prime},p_{2}^{\prime},p_{3}^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} such that γ\gamma is representable in Ap;pi′𝔹×Api′;p′′𝔹′A_{p;p_{i}^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times A_{p_{i}^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} for i=1,2,3i=1,2,3. Then the three elements p1′,p2′,p3′p_{1}^{\prime},p_{2}^{\prime},p_{3}^{\prime} are totally ordered; we may assume p1′<p2′<p3′p_{1}^{\prime}<p_{2}^{\prime}<p_{3}^{\prime}. Then it is easy to find an increasing path starting from γ\gamma of length 22. This contradicts the condition that γ\gamma has depth 11.
Now we discuss in two cases. First, suppose there exists a unique p′p^{\prime} such that γ∈Ap;p′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′\gamma\in A_{p;p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}, which is a normal poset. Hence γ\gamma is adjacent to at most two maximal elements. Second, suppose γ∈Ap;pi′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′\gamma\in A_{p;p_{i}^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} for p1′≠p2′p_{1}^{\prime}\neq p_{2}^{\prime}. Then we may assume p1′<p2′p_{1}^{\prime}<p_{2}^{\prime} and γ∈Ap;(p1′​p2′);p′′𝔹∘𝔹′\gamma\in A_{p;(p_{1}^{\prime}p_{2}^{\prime});p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. As γ\gamma has depth 1, it is a maximal element of Ap;(p1′​p2′);p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;(p_{1}^{\prime}p_{2}^{\prime});p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. Hence by the properties of bimodule/multimodules (see (2) of Definition 6.3), it is a true boundary in both Ap;p1′;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p_{1}^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} and Ap;p2′;p′′𝔹′A_{p;p_{2}^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. Hence γ\gamma is adjacent to exactly two maximal elements in Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}. This finishes the proof that Ap;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′A_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is normal.
∎
The above technical results allow us to do the following construction.
(1)
Let 𝐂¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}} be either 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯\underline{\smash{\bf Top}} or 𝚿​𝐌𝐚𝐧¯\underline{\smash{{\bf\Psi}{\bf Man}}}. If we define
Mp;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′:=(⨆p′∈Ob​𝔽′Mp;p′𝔹×Mp′;p′′𝔹′)/∼M_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}:=\left(\bigsqcup_{p^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}M_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times M_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\right)/\sim
as topological spaces, then it is naturally stratified by Ap′;p′′𝔹′∘𝔹A_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}\circ{\mathbb{B}}}. Moreover, if 𝐂¯=𝚿​𝐌𝐚𝐧¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}}=\underline{\smash{{\bf\Psi}{\bf Man}}}, then Mp;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′M_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is a stratified pseudomanifold. Moreover, one obtains a bimodule over (𝔽;𝔽′′)({\mathbb{F}};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime\prime}), denoted by 𝔹∘𝔹′{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}. If the flow categories and bimodules are enriched in the collared version of 𝐂¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}}, then 𝔹∘𝔹′{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime} is also collared.
(2)
If 𝐂¯=𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}}=\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}, let 𝒰p;p′𝔹{\mathcal{U}}_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}} and 𝒰p′;p′′𝔹′{\mathcal{U}}_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} be the underlying stratified orbifolds in Mp;p′𝔹M_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}} and Mp′;p′′𝔹′M_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} respectively. Then define
𝒰p;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′:=(⨆p′∈Ob​𝔽′𝒰p;p′𝔹×𝒰p′;p′′𝔹′)/∼{\mathcal{U}}_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}:=\left(\bigsqcup_{p^{\prime}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}{\mathcal{U}}_{p;p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times{\mathcal{U}}_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\right)/\sim
in the similar way. Then it is a stratified orbifold. Moreover, the obstruction bundles ℰp;p′𝔹→𝒰p;p′𝔹{\mathcal{E}}_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}}\to{\mathcal{U}}_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}} and ℰp′;p′′𝔹′→𝒰p′;p′′𝔹′{\mathcal{E}}_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\to{\mathcal{U}}_{p^{\prime};p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} induce orbifold vector bundles ℰp;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′→𝒰p;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′{\mathcal{E}}_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\to{\mathcal{U}}_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}, with induced Kuranishi sections
𝒮p;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′:𝒰p;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′→ℰp;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′.{\mathcal{S}}_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}:{\mathcal{U}}_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\to{\mathcal{E}}_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}.
Then one obtains objects Mp;p′′𝔹∘𝔹′M_{p;p^{\prime\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} in 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}} together with structural maps making a bimodule 𝔹∘𝔹′{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime} over (𝔽;𝔽′′)({\mathbb{F}};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime\prime}). Lastly, if the flow categories and bimodules are enriched in ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}, so is the concatenation 𝔹∘𝔹′{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}.
6.5.2. General concatenations
Now we consider concatenations in a general regular stratification category 𝐂¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}}. There is no canonical construction. We characterize the notion of concatenations in an axiomatic way.
Definition 6.13.
Let 𝔽1,…,𝔽m,𝔾1,…,𝔾n,𝔾′{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}}_{m},{\mathbb{G}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{G}}_{n},{\mathbb{G}}^{\prime} be flow categories enriched in 𝐂¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}}. Let i∈{1,…,n}i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}. Let 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} resp. 𝕐{\mathbb{Y}} be a multimodule over (𝔽1,…,𝔽m,𝔾i)({\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}}_{m};{\mathbb{G}}_{i}) resp. over (𝔾1,…,𝔾n,𝔾′)({\mathbb{G}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{G}}_{n};{\mathbb{G}}^{\prime}). Then a concatenation of 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} and 𝕐{\mathbb{Y}} at 𝔾i{\mathbb{G}}_{i}, denoted by 𝕏∘i𝕐{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}{\mathbb{Y}}, consists of the following objects.
(1)
A multimodule over (𝔾1,…,𝔾i−1,𝔽1,…,𝔽m,𝔾i+1,…,𝔾n,𝔾′)({\mathbb{G}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{G}}_{i-1},{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}}_{m},{\mathbb{G}}_{i+1},\ldots,{\mathbb{G}}_{n};{\mathbb{G}}^{\prime}).
(2)
For each two tuples (p1,…,pm,ri)(p_{1},\ldots,p_{m};r_{i}) and (r1,…,rn,r′)(r_{1},\ldots,r_{n};r^{\prime}) of objects, a codimension zero morphism
Mp1⋯pm;ri𝕏×Mr1⋯rn;r′𝕐→Mr1⋯ri−1p1⋯pmri+1⋯rn;r′𝕏∘i𝕐.M_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};r_{i}}^{\mathbb{X}}\times M_{r_{1}\cdots r_{n};r^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{Y}}\to M_{r_{1}\cdots r_{i-1}p_{1}\cdots p_{m}r_{i+1}\cdots r_{n};r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}{\mathbb{Y}}}.
They are required to satisfy the following conditions.
(1)
For each tuple (r1,⋯,ri−1,p1,⋯,pm,ri+1,⋯,rn,r′)(r_{1},\cdots,r_{i-1},p_{1},\cdots,p_{m},r_{i+1},\cdots,r_{n};r^{\prime}), the object Mr1⋯ri−1p1⋯pmri+1⋯rn;r′𝕏∘i𝕐M_{r_{1}\cdots r_{i-1}p_{1}\cdots p_{m}r_{i+1}\cdots r_{n};r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}{\mathbb{Y}}} is stratified by Ar1⋯ri−1p1⋯pmri+1⋯rn;r′𝕏∘i𝕐A_{r_{1}\cdots r_{i-1}p_{1}\cdots p_{m}r_{i+1}\cdots r_{n};r^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}{\mathbb{Y}}}.

The underlying poset maps of the structural maps of 𝕏∘i𝕐{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}{\mathbb{Y}} is the same as the previously discussed special cases.
