The positive integer dd will be the degree of an auxiliary line bundle over ℙ1{\mathbb{P}}^{1}.
Situation Module(ii).
In Situation Module(i), one fixes an outercollaring width and a compatible list of integral actions on the involved Floer categories. ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽1,…,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽m;⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽′{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} are flow categories enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} subject to the chosen integral actions as described in Situation Flow(ii). ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝕏{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{X}}} is the multimodule over (𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽1,…,𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽m;𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽′)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}).
The case of Situation Homotopy(i) is similar and we only describe the construction below without details.
Situation Homotopy(ii).
In Situation Homotopy(i), one fixes an outercollaring width and a compatible list of integral actions on involved Floer flow categories.
⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽1,…,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽m;⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽′{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}
are flow categories enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} subject to the chosen integral actions as described in Situation Flow(ii);
⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝕏0,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝕏1{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{X}}_{0}},{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{X}}_{1}}
are multimodules over them associated to Σ0\Sigma_{0} and Σ1\Sigma_{1} respectively as described in Situation Module(ii). ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,ℍ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{H}}} is a homotopy from ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝕏0{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{X}}_{0}} to ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝕏1{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{X}}_{1}} subject to the fixed outercollaring width and the integral actions.
15.2. Framed maps
In this subsection, we describe a suitable package describing flow categories, multimodules, and homotopies of infinite-dimensional spaces of maps into the target symplectic manifold.
15.2.1. Category of families of framed maps
The following definitions are rather artificial. However, they help us organize various constructions and package required properties. We use the following notations a lot: given any group GG, let G^=G×G\hat{G}=G\times G. We often denote the first factor by GLG_{L} and the second factor by GRG_{R}.
Definition 15.6.
(1)
The category 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr} has objects
𝒞^:=(𝒢,B,C,Y)\hat{\mathcal{C}}:=({\mathcal{G}},B,C,Y)
where (𝒢,B,C)({\mathcal{G}},B,C) is an object of 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}, YY is a 𝒢×𝒢{\mathcal{G}}\times{\mathcal{G}}-space together with a map π:Y→B\pi:Y\to B which is equivariant with respect to the projection 𝒢L×𝒢R→𝒢{\mathcal{G}}_{L}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{R}\to{\mathcal{G}} onto the first factor and the action by 𝒢R{\mathcal{G}}_{R} on YY is free.
(2)
Let 𝒞^i=(𝒢i,Bi,Ci,Yi)\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{i}=({\mathcal{G}}_{i},B_{i},C_{i},Y_{i}), i=1,2i=1,2 be two objects of 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}. A strict embedding from 𝒞^1\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{1} to 𝒞^2\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{2}, denoted by ζ^21\hat{\zeta}_{21}, consists of a strict embedding
ζ21:𝒞1→𝒞2\zeta_{21}:{\mathcal{C}}_{1}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{2}
in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}} and a map ζ21Y:Y1→Y2\zeta_{21}^{Y}:Y_{1}\to Y_{2} equivariant with respect to 𝒢^1→𝒢^2\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{1}\to\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{2} such that
(a)
The induced map
𝒢^2×𝒢^1Y1→Y2\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{2}\times_{\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{1}}Y_{1}\to Y_{2}
is an homeomorphism onto the corresponding union of strata.
(b)
The following diagram commutes.
B1\textstyle{B_{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}ζ21B\scriptstyle{\zeta_{21}^{B}}Y1\textstyle{Y_{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}ζ21Y\scriptstyle{\zeta_{21}^{Y}}B2\textstyle{B_{2}}Y2\textstyle{Y_{2}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
(3)
A rigidification of a strict embedding ζ^21\hat{\zeta}_{21} is a rigidification of the underlying strict embedding ζ21\zeta_{21} in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}.
(4)
The notion of unitary conjugations and embeddings are defined similar to many previous cases. We omit the details. Let 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr} be the category of framed maps with morphisms being embeddings and 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯rigfr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig} be the rigidified version.
15.2.2. Group reductions
By definition, Kuranishi spaces have symmetry group being a compact Lie group GG, while the corresponding AMS domain has the symmetry group being a complex Lie group 𝒢{\mathcal{G}}. The redundancy is reduced by choosing certain group reductions.
Definition 15.7 (The category of families of reduced framed maps).
(1)
Let 𝒞^=(𝒢,B,C,Y)\hat{\mathcal{C}}=({\mathcal{G}},B,C,Y) be an object of 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}. A group reduction of 𝒞^\hat{\mathcal{C}} is a map
Λ:Y→𝒢/G\Lambda:Y\to{\mathcal{G}}/G
which is 𝒢L{\mathcal{G}}_{L}-invariant and 𝒢R{\mathcal{G}}_{R}-equivariant.
(2)
The category of equivariant families of reduced framed maps, denoted by 𝐦𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf map}}^{\rm fr} consists of objects (𝒢,B,C,Y,Λ)({\mathcal{G}},B,C,Y,\Lambda) where (𝒢,B,C,Y)({\mathcal{G}},B,C,Y) is an object of 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr} and Λ\Lambda is a group reduction. A strict embedding ζ^21:𝒞^1→𝒞^2\hat{\zeta}_{21}:\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{1}\to\hat{\mathcal{C}}_{2} in 𝐦𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf map}}^{\rm fr} consists of a strict embedding of 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}, which induces a map
ζ21P:𝒢1/G1→𝒢2/G2\zeta_{21}^{P}:{\mathcal{G}}_{1}/G_{1}\to{\mathcal{G}}_{2}/G_{2}
such that following diagram commutes.
Y1\textstyle{Y_{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Λ1\scriptstyle{\Lambda_{1}}ζ21Y\scriptstyle{\zeta_{21}^{Y}}(𝒢1/G1)\textstyle{({\mathcal{G}}_{1}/G_{1})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}ζ21P\scriptstyle{\zeta_{21}^{P}}Y2\textstyle{Y_{2}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Λ2\scriptstyle{\Lambda_{2}}(𝒢2/G2)\textstyle{({\mathcal{G}}_{2}/G_{2})}
The notions of unitary conjugations and embeddings are defined in a way similar to previously considered situations. Morphisms in 𝐦𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf map}}^{\rm fr} are embeddings, i.e., strict embeddings modulo unitary conjugations.
(3)
A rigidification of a strict embedding ζ^21\hat{\zeta}_{21} as considered above is a rigidification of the underlying strict embedding in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}, and we denote the resulting category by 𝐦𝐚𝐩¯rigfr\underline{\smash{\bf map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig}.
As usual, we indicate the outercollaring using the notation ⌊.
15.2.3. Modification of energy density
Given an integral action 𝒜𝔽Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega} on 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}, there are also the induced modification of the energy density. Given any smooth map u:ℝ×S1→Xu:{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}\to X which converges to a pair of objects pp and qq with 𝒜H​(p)>𝒜H​(q){\mathcal{A}}_{H}(p)>{\mathcal{A}}_{H}(q), define
Ωu:=Ω⁡(∂su,∂tu−XHtΩ​(u))​d​s∧d​t∈Ω2​(ℝ×S1).\Omega_{u}:=\Omega(\partial_{s}u,\partial_{t}u-X^{\Omega}_{H_{t}}(u))ds\wedge dt\in\Omega^{2}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}).
(15.5)
Then its integral is the integer 𝒜𝔽Ω​(p)−𝒜𝔽Ω​(q){\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega}(p)-{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega}(q). We may regard Ωu\Omega_{u} as a modified energy density, which is everywhere nonnegative when uu is a Floer cylinder. Similarly, given a smooth map u:S2→Xu:S^{2}\to X representing a sphere class A∈π2​(X)A\in\pi_{2}(X), define
Ωu:=u∗​Ω∈Ω2​(S2).\Omega_{u}:=u^{*}\Omega\in\Omega^{2}(S^{2}).
Its integral is Ω⁡(A)\Omega(A); when uu is a JJ-holomorphic sphere, Ωu\Omega_{u} is everywhere nonnegative.
In general, given smooth map u:Σ→Xu:\Sigma\to X over a Floer domain with associated flow multimodudle 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} over (𝔽1,…,𝔽m,𝔽′)({\mathbb{F}}_{1},\dots,{\mathbb{F}}_{m},{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}), recall that we have chosen an integer n𝕏>0n^{\mathbb{X}}>0. In this setting, we consider the 22-form
Ωu:=u∗​Ω+FαΩ​(u)+n𝕏​d​volΣ,\Omega_{u}:=u^{*}\Omega+F^{\Omega}_{\alpha}(u)+n^{\mathbb{X}}d{\rm vol}_{\Sigma},
where α\alpha is the Hamiltonian connection from the Floer datum, and FαΩ​(u)F^{\Omega}_{\alpha}(u) denotes its curvature with respect to the symplectic form Ω\Omega. If uu solves the Floer equation, Ωu\Omega_{u} is everywhere nonnegative, and ∫ΣΩu\int_{\Sigma}\Omega_{u} recovers dp1⋯pm;p′d_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}} from (15.4). The same construction applies to maps from multimodule homotopies.
15.2.4. Floer admissible maps
and framed maps
Now we provide the concrete flow categories, multimodules, and homotopies enriched in 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}.
We first consider the flow category case. Let 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} be a Floer flow category associated to (X,ω,J)(X,\omega,J) and the Hamiltonian HH. Let 𝒜𝔽Ω:Ob​𝔽→ℤ{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\to{\mathbb{Z}} be an integral action with associated integral symplectic form Ω\Omega. Recall that one has obtained a flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}} with the same set of objects as 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}. For each p,q∈Ob​𝔽p,q\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}, one has the object
𝒞p​q𝔽=(𝒢p​q𝔽,Bp​q𝔽,Cp​q𝔽)∈Ob​𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rig.{\mathcal{C}}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}=({\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}},B_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}},C_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}})\in{\rm Ob}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}.
We define a 𝒢^p​q𝔽\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}-space Yp​q𝔽Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} as follows. For each ϕ∈Bp​q𝔽\phi\in B_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}, consider continuous maps u:Cϕ→Xu:C_{\phi}\to X which are smooth away from nodes and which converge exponentially fast towards 1-periodic orbits of HH. We require that uu converges to the orbits pp resp. qq at the negative resp. positive end of CϕC_{\phi}, and that the cappings satisfy p​#​u=qp\#u=q. In particular, the homotopy type of the map uu is constrained by the underlying curve; for example, if CϕC_{\phi} has a sphere component of degree d′d^{\prime}, then the restriction of uu to that component has the same degree d′d^{\prime} measured by the modified integral symplectic form Ω\Omega. For ϕ\phi and uu as above, there is a Hermitian holomorphic line bundle
Lu→CϕL_{u}\to C_{\phi}
determined by the 2-form Ωu∈Ω2​(Cϕ)\Omega_{u}\in\Omega^{2}(C_{\phi}) (see (15.5)) which decays exponentially along cylindrical end. The degree of LuL_{u} is dp​qd_{pq}. Then consider frames
F=(f0,⋯,fdp​q)F=(f_{0},\cdots,f_{d_{pq}})
of the space H0​(Lu)H^{0}(L_{u}) modulo ℂ∗{\mathbb{C}}^{*} such that 1) at the negative end z−z_{-} one has
[f0​(z−),…,fdp​q​(z−)]=[1,0,…,0]∈ℂ​ℙdp​q[f_{0}(z_{-}),\ldots,f_{d_{pq}}(z_{-})]=[1,0,\ldots,0]\in\mathbb{CP}^{d_{pq}}
and 2) the Hermitian matrix
(∫Cϕ⟨fμ,fν⟩​Ωu)μ​ν\left(\int_{C_{\phi}}\langle f_{\mu},f_{\nu}\rangle\Omega_{u}\right)_{\mu\nu}
is positive definite, where ⟨⋅,⋅⟩\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle is the fiberwise Hermitian metric on the bundle LuL_{u}. Notice that the set of such frames FF is a 𝒢p​q{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}-torsor. Then let Yp​q𝔽Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} be the set of all tuples (ϕ,u,F)(\phi,u,F) described as above.
The set Yp​q𝔽Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} has a natural topology and admits a natural forgetful map π0:Yp​q𝔽→Bp​q𝔽\pi_{0}:Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}\to B_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}. There is another map
π1:Yp​q𝔽→Bp​q𝔽,(ϕ,u,F)↦ϕF\pi_{1}:Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}\to B_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}},\ (\phi,u,F)\mapsto\phi_{F}
where ϕF:Cϕ→ℂ​ℙ𝐝p​q\phi_{F}:C_{\phi}\to\mathbb{CP}^{{\bf d}_{pq}} is the Kodaira embedding induced by the frame. Moreover, Yp​q𝔽Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} has an action by 𝒢^p​q≅𝒢p​q×𝒢p​q\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}\cong{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}, where the first factor acts by reparametrizing the domain and the second factor acts by linearly transforming the frame FF. One can see that the tuple
(𝒢p​q𝔽,Bp​q𝔽,Cp​q𝔽,Yp​q𝔽)({\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}},B_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}},C_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}},Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}})
together with the maps π0,π1\pi_{0},\pi_{1} is an object of 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}.
The cases of multimodules and homotopies are similar, using the modified energy from Section 15.2.3. One obtains on the level of spaces
Yp1⋯pm;p′𝕏,\displaystyle\ Y_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{X}}},\
Yp1⋯pm;p′ℍ\displaystyle\ Y_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{H}}}
as well as the corresponding objects in 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}.
15.2.5. The structural maps
We would like to make the spaces of framed maps into flow categories, multimodules, and homotopies enriched in 𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}. We only describe the flow category case. Given (ϕ,u,F)∈Yp​q𝔽(\phi,u,F)\in Y_{pq}^{{\mathbb{F}}} and (ϕ′,u′,F′)∈Yq​r𝔽(\phi^{\prime},u^{\prime},F^{\prime})\in Y_{qr}^{{\mathbb{F}}}, one has defined the composition
ϕ​#​ϕ′:=ζp​r​qB​(ϕ,ϕ′)∈Bdp​q+dq​r=Bp​r\phi\#\phi^{\prime}:=\zeta_{prq}^{B}(\phi,\phi^{\prime})\in B_{d_{pq}+d_{qr}}=B_{pr}
using the structural maps of the monotone flow category 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞k\mathbb{Dom}^{k} with the corresponding curve Cϕ​#​ϕ′C_{\phi\#\phi^{\prime}}. The maps uu and u′u^{\prime} obviously define a Floer admissible map
u​#​u′:Cϕ​#​ϕ′→X.u\#u^{\prime}:C_{\phi\#\phi^{\prime}}\to X.
Then for the two frames F=(f0,…,fd)F=(f_{0},\ldots,f_{d}) and F′=(f0′,…,fd′′)F^{\prime}=(f_{0}^{\prime},\ldots,f_{d^{\prime}}^{\prime}), we will define F​#​F′F\#F^{\prime} consisting of holomorphic sections of Lu​#​u′,H→Cϕ​#​ϕ′L_{u\#u^{\prime},H}\to C_{\phi\#\phi^{\prime}}. We can extend Lu,HL_{u,H} resp. Lu′,HL_{u^{\prime},H} to the other component of Cϕ​#​ϕ′C_{\phi\#\phi^{\prime}} by trivial bundle and denote the extension still by the same notation. Then one has the natural isomorphism
Lu​#​u′,H=Lu,H⊗Lu′,H.L_{u\#u^{\prime},H}=L_{u,H}\otimes L_{u^{\prime},H}.
Let τu∈Lu|z+\tau_{u}\in L_{u}|_{z_{+}} be the parallel transport of f0​(z−)f_{0}(z_{-}) along the lateral line with respect to the connection on Lu→CϕL_{u}\to C_{\phi}. Then in the same way as we define the concatenating ϕ​#​ϕ′\phi\#\phi^{\prime}, consider the frame
F​#​F′=(f0⊗f0′,…,fd⊗f0′,τu⊗f1′,…,τu⊗fd′′).F\#F^{\prime}=\Big(f_{0}\otimes f_{0}^{\prime},\ldots,f_{d}\otimes f_{0}^{\prime},\tau_{u}\otimes f_{1}^{\prime},\ldots,\tau_{u}\otimes f_{d^{\prime}}^{\prime}\Big).
Hence we have obtained a map
ζ^p​r​q:Yp​r𝔽×Yr​q𝔽→∂p​r​qYp​q𝔽.\hat{\zeta}_{prq}:Y_{pr}^{\mathbb{F}}\times Y_{rq}^{\mathbb{F}}\to\partial^{prq}Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}.
We can also prove the associativity of the composition maps as the case of the monotone flow category 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞\mathbb{Dom}. Hence we obtained a flow category.
Proposition 15.8.
(1)
The spaces Yp​q𝔽Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} together with the composition maps form a flow category 𝕄​𝕒​𝕡𝔽𝕗​𝕣\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\mathbb{fr}} enriched in ⌊𝐌𝐚𝐩¯frrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig} which lifts the flow category 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Ω,𝔽\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}}.
(2)
The spaces Yp1⋯pm;p′𝕏,frY_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{X}},{\rm fr}} together with the structural maps form a multimodule 𝕄​𝕒​𝕡𝕏𝕗​𝕣\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{fr}} enriched in ⌊𝐌𝐚𝐩¯frrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig} over (𝕄​𝕒​𝕡𝔽1𝕗​𝕣,⋯,𝕄​𝕒​𝕡𝔽m𝕗​𝕣,𝕄​𝕒​𝕡𝔽′𝕗​𝕣)(\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\cdots,\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}}^{\mathbb{fr}};\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{fr}}).
(3)
The spaces Yp1⋯pm;p′ℍ,frY_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{H}},{\rm fr}} together with the structural maps form a homotopy 𝕄​𝕒​𝕡ℍ𝕗​𝕣\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{H}}^{\mathbb{fr}} enriched in ⌊𝐌𝐚𝐩¯frrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig} from 𝕄​𝕒​𝕡𝕏0𝕗​𝕣\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{X}}_{0}}^{\mathbb{fr}} to 𝕄​𝕒​𝕡𝕏1𝕗​𝕣\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{X}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}}.
Proof.
We just need to point out that the difference between the image of Mapp​rfr×Mapr​qfr{\rm Map}_{pr}^{\rm fr}\times{\rm Map}_{rq}^{\rm fr} and the stratum ∂p​r​qMapp​qfr\partial^{prq}{\rm Map}_{pq}^{\rm fr} lies in the difference of the domains. The concatenations of frame maps into XX do not affect the rigidification.
∎
15.2.6. Group reductions
We have the following proposition showing the existence of compatible systems of group reductions.
Proposition 15.9.
Let 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}, 𝔽1,…,𝔽m,𝔽′,𝕏,𝕏0,𝕏1,ℍ{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}}_{m},{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime},{\mathbb{X}},{\mathbb{X}}_{0},{\mathbb{X}}_{1},{\mathbb{H}} be as above. Let ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽𝕗​𝕣,⋯,⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡ℍ𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\cdots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{H}}}^{\mathbb{fr}} be the corresponding flow categories, multimodules, and homotopy enriched in enriched in ⌊𝐌𝐚𝐩¯frrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig}.
(1)
There exists a lift of ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\mathbb{fr}} to ⌊𝐦𝐚𝐩¯frrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig}, denoted by ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{map}{}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\mathbb{fr}}.
(2)
Given lifts ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽1𝕗​𝕣,⋯,⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽m𝕗​𝕣,⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽′𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\cdots,{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{\mathbb{F}_{m}}^{\mathbb{fr}},{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{fr}} of ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽1𝕗​𝕣,⋯,⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽m𝕗​𝕣,⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽′𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\cdots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}}^{\mathbb{fr}},{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{fr}} respectively, there exists a lift of ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝕏𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{Map}}_{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{fr}} to ⌊𝐦𝐚𝐩¯frrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig} as a multimodule over (𝕞⌊𝕒𝕡,𝕗​𝕣𝔽1⋯,𝕞⌊𝕒𝕡;𝕗​𝕣𝔽m𝕞⌊𝕒𝕡)𝕗​𝕣𝔽′({}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\cdots,{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{\mathbb{F}_{m}}^{\mathbb{fr}};{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{fr}}), which is denoted by ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝕏𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{X}}}^{\mathbb{fr}}.
(3)
Given lifts ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽1𝕗​𝕣,⋯,⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽m𝕗​𝕣,⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽′𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\cdots,{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{\mathbb{F}_{m}}^{\mathbb{fr}},{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{fr}} of ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽1𝕗​𝕣,⋯,⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽m𝕗​𝕣,⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽′𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\cdots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}}^{\mathbb{fr}},{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{fr}} to ⌊𝐦𝐚𝐩¯frrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig} and lifts ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝕏0𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{X}}_{0}}^{\mathbb{fr}}, ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝕏1𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{X}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}} of ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝕏0𝕗​𝕣,⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝕏1𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{X}_{0}}^{\mathbb{fr}},{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}{}_{{\mathbb{X}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}} respectively, as multimodules over the tuple (𝕞⌊𝕒𝕡,𝕗​𝕣𝔽1⋯,𝕞⌊𝕒𝕡;𝕗​𝕣𝔽m𝕞⌊𝕒𝕡)𝕗​𝕣𝔽′({}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\cdots,{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{\mathbb{F}_{m}}^{\mathbb{fr}};{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{fr}}), there exists a lift of ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡ℍ𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}{}_{{\mathbb{H}}}^{\mathbb{fr}} to ⌊𝐦𝐚𝐩¯frrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig} as a homotopy from ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝕏0𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{X}}_{0}}^{\mathbb{fr}} to ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝕏1𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{X}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}}.
Proof.
We prove by induction. The construction of the base situation was provided in [3], whose construction is recalled as follows. Given p,qp,q and a framed map (ϕ,u,F)∈Mapp​q𝔽,fr(\phi,u,F)\in{\rm Map}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F},{\rm fr}}, consider the (dp​q+1)×(dp​q+1)(d_{pq}+1)\times(d_{pq}+1) positive-definite Hermitian matrix
(HF)a​b=∫Cϕ⟨fa,fb⟩​Ωu.(H_{F})_{ab}=\int_{C_{\phi}}\langle f_{a},f_{b}\rangle\Omega_{u}.
(15.6)
As frames are well-defined up to ℂ∗{\mathbb{C}}^{*}-rescaling, this Hermitian matrix is well-defined up to positive rescaling, hence defines a map
Λp​q𝔽:Yp​q𝔽→𝒢p​q/Gp​q=Pp​q.\Lambda_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}:Y_{pq}^{{\mathbb{F}}}\to{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}/G_{pq}=P_{pq}.
This map is obviously equivariant with respect to the 𝒢R{\mathcal{G}}_{R}-action; moreover, as 𝒢L{\mathcal{G}}_{L} acts by reparametrizing the map and pulling back the framings, Λp​q𝔽\Lambda_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} is 𝒢L{\mathcal{G}}_{L}-invariant. Therefore, one obtains a group reduction on Yp​q𝔽Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}.
If Yp​q𝔽Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} has no lower stratum, then its outercollaring is itself and hence one obtains the base case of the induction. Suppose inductively, one has constructed compatible collared group reductions
Λr​s𝔽:⌊Yr​s𝔽→Pr​s\Lambda_{rs}^{\mathbb{F}}:{}_{\lfloor}Y_{rs}^{\mathbb{F}}\to P_{rs}
for all pairs r,sr,s satisfying 𝒜⁡(r)−𝒜⁡(s)<𝒜⁡(p)−𝒜⁡(q){\mathcal{A}}(r)-{\mathcal{A}}(s)<{\mathcal{A}}(p)-{\mathcal{A}}(q). Notice that for each triple p<r<qp<r<q, one has a strict embedding
⌊Yp​r𝔽×⌊Yr​q𝔽→∂p​r​q⌊Yp​q𝔽{}_{\lfloor}Y_{pr}^{\mathbb{F}}\times{}_{\lfloor}Y_{rq}^{\mathbb{F}}\to\partial^{prq}{}_{\lfloor}Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}
which is equivariant with respect to the complex group embedding 𝒢^p​r×𝒢^r​q→𝒢^p​q\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{pr}\times\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{rq}\to\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}. Hence one obtains an extension

The compatibility assumption and the 𝒢^p​q\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}-equivariance imply that one obtains a group reduction on the boundary of ⌊Yp​q𝔽{}_{\lfloor}Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} which is collared. We also have a group reduction in Yp​q𝔽Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} (viewed as a subset away from boundary) given by (15.6). Then using the product structure on the collar region (where the actions by the complex Lie groups fix the collar coordinates) and choosing a homotopy, one can interpolate over the collar region to get a continuous group reduction on the whole of ⌊Yp​q𝔽{}_{\lfloor}Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}.
The constructions for the cases of multimodules and homotopies are completely the same and we omit the details.
∎
15.2.7. Linearizing the group reduction
We would like to regard the group reduction as a section of a vector bundle rather than a nonlinear fiber bundle. This requires linearizing the homogeneous space 𝒢/G{\mathcal{G}}/G, which has a contractible set of choices.
Recall that we have constructed a collection of germs of maps

15.3. The topological Kuranishi lifts
15.3.1. Thickening data
Given an equivariant family 𝒞=(𝒢,B,C){\mathcal{C}}=({\mathcal{G}},B,C) and an almost complex manifold (X,J)(X,J). Recall C̊⊆C\mathring{C}\subseteq C is the complement of nodes and markings. Consider the vector bundle
ΛC̊/B0,1⊗T​X→C̊×X.\Lambda^{0,1}_{\mathring{C}/B}\otimes TX\to\mathring{C}\times X.
Definition 15.10.
A thickening datum on an equivariant family of curves 𝒞=(𝒢,B,C){\mathcal{C}}=({\mathcal{G}},B,C) consists of a pair (W,ν)(W,\nu) where WW is a finite-dimensional complex unitary representation2222
22
We restrict to complex representation in order to simplify the discussion of normal complex structures. of the maximal compact subgroup G⊆𝒢G\subseteq{\mathcal{G}} and
ν:W→Γc​(C̊×X,ΛC̊/B0,1⊗T​X)\nu:W\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}\times X,\Lambda^{0,1}_{\mathring{C}/B}\otimes TX)
is a GG-equivariant linear map. Here Γc\Gamma_{c} stands for smooth sections with compact support.
Notice that given a thickening datum (W,ν)(W,\nu) on 𝒞{\mathcal{C}}, for each ϕ∈B\phi\in B and a smooth map u:Cϕ→Xu:C_{\phi}\to X, there is an induced linear map
νϕ,u:W→Ωc0,1​(C̊ϕ,u∗​T​X)\nu_{\phi,u}:W\to\Omega^{0,1}_{c}(\mathring{C}_{\phi},u^{*}TX)
given by restricting ν⁡(e)\nu(e) to the graph of uu in C̊ϕ×X\mathring{C}_{\phi}\times X. These maps will be used to thicken up the moduli space of Floer equation.
Definition 15.11.
The category of curves-with-thickening data, denoted by 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}} is defined as follows. The objects are tuples
(𝒢,B,C,W,ν)({\mathcal{G}},B,C,W,\nu)
where (𝒢,B,C)({\mathcal{G}},B,C) is an equivariant family of curves and (W,ν)(W,\nu) is a thickening datum on 𝒞{\mathcal{C}}.
A strict embedding of perturbations consists of a strict embedding
ζ21=(ζ21𝒢,ζ21B,ζ21C):(𝒢1,B1,C1)→(𝒢2,B2,C2)\zeta_{21}=(\zeta_{21}^{\mathcal{G}},\zeta_{21}^{B},\zeta_{21}^{C}):({\mathcal{G}}_{1},B_{1},C_{1})\to({\mathcal{G}}_{2},B_{2},C_{2})
(see Definition 14.7) and a ζ21G\zeta_{21}^{G}-equivariant isometric linear embedding ζ21W:W1→W2\zeta_{21}^{W}:W_{1}\to W_{2} such that 1) the following diagram commutes;
W1\textstyle{W_{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}ν1\scriptstyle{\nu_{1}}ζ21W\scriptstyle{\zeta_{21}^{W}}Γc​(C̊1×X,ΛC̊1/B10,1⊗T​X)\textstyle{\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{1}\times X,\Lambda_{\mathring{C}_{1}/B_{1}}^{0,1}\otimes TX)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}W2\textstyle{W_{2}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}ν2\scriptstyle{\nu_{2}}Γc​(C̊2×X,ΛC̊2/B20,1⊗T​X)\textstyle{\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{2}\times X,\Lambda_{\mathring{C}_{2}/B_{2}}^{0,1}\otimes TX)}
(here the right vertical arrow is induced from the morphism ζ21\zeta_{21}) and 2) the restriction of ν2\nu_{2} to the orthogonal complement W1⊥⊆W2W_{1}^{\bot}\subseteq W_{2} vanishes.
The conjugation of (𝒢,B,C,W,ν)({\mathcal{G}},B,C,W,\nu) is a strict embedding induced by g∈Gg\in G. An embedding of curvs-with-thickening-datum is a conjugacy class of strict embeddings.
The category 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}} is a regular stratification category with a forgetful functor 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯→𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯¯\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}}\to\underline{\smash{\bf Curv}}. One can easily formulate the category ⌊𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}} of collared curves-with-thickening-datum, together with forgetful functor
⌊𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯→⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯.{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}}\to{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}.
We need to consider the rigidified version. Recall that for a strict embedding
ζ21:(𝒢1,B1,C1)→(𝒢2,B2,C2)\zeta_{21}:({\mathcal{G}}_{1},B_{1},C_{1})\to({\mathcal{G}}_{2},B_{2},C_{2})
a rigidification is a germ of G1G_{1}-equivariant map θ21:B1×Q21→𝒢2\theta_{21}:B_{1}\times Q_{21}\to{\mathcal{G}}_{2} satisfying an appropriate condition.
Definition 15.12.
Let (ζ21,ζ21W)(\zeta_{21},\zeta_{21}^{W}) be a strict embedding in 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}} from (𝒢1,B1,C1,W1,ν1)({\mathcal{G}}_{1},B_{1},C_{1},W_{1},\nu_{1}) to (𝒢2,B2,C2,W2,ν2)({\mathcal{G}}_{2},B_{2},C_{2},W_{2},\nu_{2}). A rigidification of (ζ21,ζ21W)(\zeta_{21},\zeta_{21}^{W}) consists of a rigidification θ21:B1×Q21→𝒢2\theta_{21}:B_{1}\times Q_{21}\to{\mathcal{G}}_{2} of ζ21\zeta_{21} satisfying the following condition. Fix b1∈B1b_{1}\in B_{1}. The rigidification induces identifications
Cζ21B​(b1)≅Cθ21​(b1,q)​(ζ21B​(b1))C_{\zeta_{21}^{B}(b_{1})}\cong C_{\theta_{21}(b_{1},q)(\zeta_{21}^{B}(b_{1}))}
for all q∈Q21q\in Q_{21} sufficient close to the origin. Then we can regard ν2\nu_{2} as a family of linear maps
ν2​(b1,q):W2→Γc​(C̊ζ21​(b1)×X,Λ0,1⊗T​X).\nu_{2}(b_{1},q):W_{2}\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{\zeta_{21}(b_{1})}\times X,\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes TX).
We require that these family only depends on b1b_{1}. In particular, for qq close to the origin, ν2\nu_{2} vanishes on the orthogonal complement of W1W_{1}.
Definition 15.13.
A thickening datum on a flow category/multimodule/homotopy enriched in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}} is a lift in 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}}. If the flow category/multimodule/homotopy is enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}, then a perturbation is called collared and rigidified if it is a lift in ⌊𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}}_{\rm rig}.
In the following steps, one needs to choose perturbations satisfying additional properties. The construction of such perturbations will be provided in due course.
Now we can describe the AMS lift of the Floer flow categories, bimodules, and homotopies to the category of topological Kuranishi spaces.
15.3.2. The thickenings
We describe the thickened moduli spaces as candidates of the Kuranishi regularizations of the moduli spaces. We first consider the flow category case. Return to the domain flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig} whose morphism spaces are equivariant families of curves 𝒞p​q𝔽{\mathcal{C}}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}. A thickening datum of ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}} is denoted by 𝕎𝔽\mathbb{W}^{\mathbb{F}} which consists of thickening data
νp​q𝔽:Wp​q𝔽→Γc​(C̊p​q𝔽×X,ΛC̊p​q𝔽/Bp​q𝔽0,1⊗T​X).\nu_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}:W_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}\times X,\Lambda_{\mathring{C}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}/B_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}}^{0,1}\otimes TX).
Definition 15.14.
Given any collared and rigidified thickening datum 𝕎𝔽\mathbb{W}^{\mathbb{F}} on the flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}} and the flow category ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}}^{\mathbb{fr}} of reduced framed maps, for each pair p,qp,q of objects in the Floer flow category 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}, define the following items.
(1)
The thickened moduli space is
Vp​q:=Vp​q𝔽:={(ϕ,u,F,e)|(ϕ,u,F)∈Yp​q𝔽,ϵ,e∈Wp​q𝔽,∂¯Hu+νp​q𝔽(e)=0,ϕ=ϕF∈⌊Bp​q𝔽.}.V_{pq}:=V_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}:=\left\{(\phi,u,F,e)\ \left|\ \begin{array}[]{c}(\phi,u,F)\in Y_{pq}^{{\mathbb{F}},\epsilon},\ e\in W_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}},\\
\overline{\partial}_{H}u+\nu_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}(e)=0,\ \phi=\phi_{F}\in{}_{\lfloor}B_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}.\end{array}\right.\right\}.
(2)
The Gp​qG_{pq}-action on Vp​qV_{pq} is the product of the diagonal Gp​qG_{pq}-action on Yp​q𝔽,ϵY_{pq}^{\mathbb{F},\epsilon} space of framed maps and the action on Wp​qW_{pq}.
(3)
The obstruction bundle is the trivial bundle
Ep​q:=Ep​q𝔽:=Q¯p​q𝔽⊕W¯p​q𝔽→Vp​q.E_{pq}:=E_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}:=\underline{\smash{Q}}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}\oplus\underline{\smash{W}}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}\to V_{pq}.
(4)
The Kuranishi section is (given by) the equivariant map
Sp​q𝔽​(ϕ,u,F,e)=(λp​q𝔽​(ϕ,u,F),e).S_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}(\phi,u,F,e)=(\lambda_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}(\phi,u,F),e).
Theorem 15.15.
The natural “footprint” map
(Sp​q𝔽)−1(0)/Gp​q𝔽→ℳ¯p​q𝔽⌊(S_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}})^{-1}(0)/G_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}\to{}_{\lfloor}\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}
which sends the orbit of (ϕ,u,F,0)(\phi,u,F,0) to the equivalence class of the stable Floer trajectory u:Cϕ→Xu:C_{\phi}\to X is an isomorphism of orbispaces.
Proof.
We drop 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} from the notations for simplification. We also assume k=1k=1. We prove that the footprint map is surjective. Given any point of ⌊ℳ¯p​q{}_{\lfloor}\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{pq} represented by a stable Floer trajectory u:Σ→Xu:\Sigma\to X (assume that this point is not in the outer collar; the case that it is in the outer collar can be deduced similarly). Then uu determines a unitary line bundle Lu→ΣL_{u}\to\Sigma whose Chern connection has curvature Ωu\Omega_{u}. Let FF be a frame of LuL_{u} satisfying the negative (or positive) constraint, which determines a holomorphic map ϕF:Σ→ℙdp​q\phi_{F}:\Sigma\to{\mathbb{P}}^{d_{pq}} and hence can be identified with a point ϕF∈Bp​q\phi_{F}\in B_{pq}. The domain Σ\Sigma can be then identified with CϕFC_{\phi_{F}}. Let uF:C̊ϕF→Xu_{F}:\mathring{C}_{\phi_{F}}\to X be the pullback map. As two different frames FF and F′F^{\prime} differ by an element of the group 𝒢p​q,R{\mathcal{G}}_{pq,R}, one obtains a 𝒢p​q{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}-orbit (where we regard 𝒢p​q{\mathcal{G}}_{pq} as the diagonal of 𝒢p​q,L×𝒢p​q,R{\mathcal{G}}_{pq,L}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{pq,R}) of framed maps
(ϕF,uF,F)∈Yp​q𝔽.(\phi_{F},u_{F},F)\in Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}.
By the definition of a structural group reduction scheme, there is a unique Gp​qG_{pq}-orbit (for the diagonal action) of framed maps such that
Λp​q𝔽​(ϕF,uF,F)=[1]∈Pp​q\Lambda_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}(\phi_{F},u_{F},F)=[1]\in P_{pq}
Then (ϕF,uF,F)∈Yp​q𝔽,ϵ(\phi_{F},u_{F},F)\in Y_{pq}^{\mathbb{F},\epsilon}. Hence λp​q𝔽​(ϕF,uF,F)=0\lambda_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}(\phi_{F},u_{F},F)=0. This Gp​qG_{pq}-orbit is then sent by the footprint map to the given point of ℳ¯p​q\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{pq}. Therefore the footprint map is surjective.
We prove that the footprint map is injective. Suppose (ϕ,u,F,0)(\phi,u,F,0) and (ϕ′,u′,F′,0)(\phi^{\prime},u^{\prime},F^{\prime},0) are sent to the same point of ⌊ℳ¯p​q{}_{\lfloor}\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{pq}. By definition, there is a domain isomorphism Cϕ≅Cϕ′C_{\phi}\cong C_{\phi^{\prime}}, which must be given by an element g∈𝒢p​qg\in{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}. As ϕ=ϕF\phi=\phi_{F}, ϕ′=ϕF′\phi^{\prime}=\phi_{F^{\prime}}, it follows that
g⁡(ϕ,u,F,0)=(ϕ′,u′,F′,0).g(\phi,u,F,0)=(\phi^{\prime},u^{\prime},F^{\prime},0).
As in the same 𝒢p​q{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}-orbit there can only be one normalized Gp​qG_{pq}-oribt, it follows that g∈Gp​qg\in G_{pq}. This implies that the footprint map is injective.
∎
Now we turn to the case of multimodules 𝕏:=𝕏Σ{\mathbb{X}}:=\mathbb{X}^{\Sigma} associated to a connected Floer domain Σ\Sigma over (𝔽1,…,𝔽m,𝔽′)({\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}}_{m};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}). Previously one has constructed a multimodule ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝕏{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{Dom}}^{\mathbb{X}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}, together with the group reductions
λp1⋯pm;p′𝕏:⌊Yp1⋯pm;p′𝕏→𝒢p1⋯pm;p′/Gp1⋯pm;p′\lambda_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}:{}_{\lfloor}Y_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{X}}}\to{\mathcal{G}}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}/G_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}
which extends the group reductions on the involved flow categories of framed maps.
Definition 15.16.
Given a thickening datum 𝕎Σ\mathbb{W}^{\Sigma} on the multimodule ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝕏{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{X}}} (as a multimodule over the flow categories equipped with thickening data, enriched in ⌊𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}}_{\rm rig}), for objects p1,…,pm;p′p_{1},\ldots,p_{m};p^{\prime}, define the following objects.
(1)
The thickened moduli space is
Vp1⋯pm;p′:=Vp1⋯pm;p′𝕏:={(ϕ,u,F,e)|(ϕ,u,F)∈⌊Yp1⋯pm;p′𝕏,ϵ,e∈Wp1⋯pm;p′𝕏,∂¯σu+νp1⋯pm;p′𝕏(e)=0,ϕ=ϕF∈⌊Bp1⋯pm;p′𝕏.}V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}:=V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}:=\left\{(\phi,u,F,e)\ \left|\begin{array}[]{l}(\phi,u,F)\in{}_{\lfloor}Y_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{X}},\epsilon},\ e\in W_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}},\\
\overline{\partial}_{\sigma}u+\nu_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}(e)=0,\ \phi=\phi_{F}\in{}_{\lfloor}B_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}.\end{array}\right.\right\}
(2)
The Gp1⋯pm;p′G_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}-action on Vp1⋯pm;p′V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}} is the restriction of the diagonal action on ⌊Yp1⋯pm;p′𝕏,ϵ×Wp1⋯pm;p′𝕏{}_{\lfloor}Y_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X},\epsilon}\times W_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}.
(3)
The obstruction bundle is the trivial bundle
Ep1⋯pm;p′:=Ep1⋯pm;p′𝕏:=Q¯p1⋯pm;p′⊕W¯p1⋯pm;p′→Vp1⋯pm;p′.E_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}:=E_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}:=\underline{\smash{Q}}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\oplus\underline{\smash{W}}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\to V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}.
(4)
The Kuranishi section is (equivalent to) the map
Sp1⋯pm;p′𝕏(ϕ,u,F,e)↦(λp1⋯pm;p′𝕏(ϕ,u,F),e)S_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}(\phi,u,F,e)\mapsto(\lambda_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}(\phi,u,F),e)
where λp1⋯pm;p′\lambda_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}} is the linearized group reduction.
The case of homotopies is the same. We omit the detailed discussions. We will use ℍ{\mathbb{H}} to indicate the relationship with a multimodule homotopy ℍ{\mathbb{H}} coming from the Floer theory background.
15.3.3. Transversality
Next we deal with transversality. For this we need to set up a certain Fredholm problem. For each pair of objects p,qp,q, define
Vp​q′:={(ϕ,u,e)|ϕ∈Bp​q𝔽⌊,e∈Wp​q𝔽,u:Cϕ→X satisfies ∂¯Hu+νp​q𝔽(e)=0}.V_{pq}^{\prime}:=\Big\{(\phi,u,e)|\ \phi\in{}_{\lfloor}B^{\mathbb{F}}_{pq},e\in W_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}},u:C_{\phi}\to X\text{ satisfies }\overline{\partial}_{H}u+\nu_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}(e)=0\Big\}.
Lemma 15.17.
There is a canonical Gp​qG_{pq}-equivariant isomorphism Vp​q′≅Vp​qV_{pq}^{\prime}\cong V_{pq}.
Proof.
We show the natural map Vp​q→Vp​q′V_{pq}\to V_{pq}^{\prime} is bijective. Indeed, given any (ϕ,u,e)∈Vp​q′(\phi,u,e)\in V_{pq}^{\prime}, the set of all frames FF on it are related by an element of 𝒢R{\mathcal{G}}_{R} which linearly transforms the frame. Each frame FF induces a map ϕF:Cϕ→ℙ𝐝\phi_{F}:C_{\phi}\to\mathbb{P}^{\bf d}. The condition that ϕF=ϕ\phi_{F}=\phi specifies a unique frame. Hence the map Vp​q→Vp​q′V_{pq}\to V_{pq}^{\prime} is surjective. As it is obviously injective and Gp​qG_{pq}-equivariant, the lemma follows.
∎
For a fixed ϕ\phi, let Vp​q′​(ϕ)⊆Vp​q′V_{pq}^{\prime}(\phi)\subseteq V_{pq}^{\prime} be the preimage of ϕ\phi. Then Vp​q′​(ϕ)V_{pq}^{\prime}(\phi) is the zero locus of a smooth Fredholm section defined on a certain Banach manifold of maps from CϕC_{\phi} to XX; the concrete choice of the Banach manifold depends on certain Sobolev parameters.
Definition 15.18.
We say that (ϕ,u,e)∈Vp​q′​(ϕ)(\phi,u,e)\in V_{pq}^{\prime}(\phi) is transverse if the linearization of the corresponding Fredholm section is surjective (which is independent of the Sobolev parameters). We say that the perturbation 𝕎\mathbb{W} is transverse if all points of Vp​q′​(ϕ)V_{pq}^{\prime}(\phi) for all p,qp,q are transverse.
We can choose the thicikening data appropriately so that transversality holds.
Proposition 15.19.
We omit the dependence on Ω\Omega from the notations.
(1)
Given any integral modification of the topological energy, there exists a transverse thickening datum 𝕎𝔽\mathbb{W}^{\mathbb{F}} on the flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}}, i.e., a transverse lift to ⌊𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}}_{\rm rig}.
(2)
Consider the multimodule ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝕏{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{X}} over (𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔽1,⋯𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔽m;𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔽′)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\cdots{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}). Suppose 𝕎𝔽1\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}, ⋯\cdots, 𝕎𝔽m;𝕎𝔽′\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} are transverse thickening data on these flow categories. Then there exists a transverse thickening datum 𝕎𝕏{\mathbb{W}}^{\mathbb{X}} which is a multimodule over (𝕎𝔽1,⋯𝕎𝔽m;𝕎𝔽′)(\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\cdots\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}).
(3)
Suppose 𝕎𝕏0\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{X}}_{0}} resp. 𝕎𝕏1\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{X}}_{1}} are two transverse thickening data on 𝕏0{\mathbb{X}}_{0} resp. 𝕏1\mathbb{X}_{1} as multimodules over (𝕎𝔽1,⋯,𝕎𝔽m,𝕎𝔽′)(\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\cdots,\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}). Then there exists a lift of ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞ℍ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{H}}} to ⌊𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}}_{\rm rig}, denoted by 𝕎ℍ\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{H}}}, as a homotopy from 𝕎𝕏0\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{X}}_{0}} to 𝕎𝕏1\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{X}}_{1}}.
Proof.
See Subsubsection 15.3.6.
∎
Transversality implies the regularity of the thickened moduli spaces.
Proposition 15.20.
Suppose we choose transverse thickening data as claimed in Proposition 15.19.
(1)
For each p,q∈Ob​𝔽p,q\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}, the thickened moduli space Vp​q𝔽V_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} is an Ap​q𝔽A_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}-stratified topological Gp​q𝔽G_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}-manifold near (Sp​q𝔽)−1​(0)(S_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}})^{-1}(0).
(2)
Each thickened moduli space Vp1⋯pm;p′𝕏V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} is an Ap1⋯pm;p′𝕏A_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}-stratified topological Gp1⋯pm;p′𝕏G_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}-manifold near (Sp1⋯pm;p′𝕏)−1(0)(S_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}})^{-1}(0).
(3)
Each thickened moduli space Vp1⋯pm;p′ℍV_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{H}} is an Ap1⋯pm;p′ℍA_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{H}}-stratified topological Gp1⋯pm;p′ℍG_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{H}}-manifold near (Sp1⋯pm;p′ℍ)−1(0)(S_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{H}})^{-1}(0).
Proof.
We only discuss the flow category case. By definition, transversality implies that each Vp​q′​(ϕ)≅Vp​qV_{pq}^{\prime}(\phi)\cong V_{pq} is a topological manifold near where e=0e=0 for all ϕ∈Bp​q\phi\in B_{pq}. The gluing argument implies that Vp​q′V_{pq}^{\prime} is a stratified manifold. Since the thickening datum is collared, Vp​q′V_{pq}^{\prime} is also collared. Finally the canonical identification Vp​q′≅Vp​qV_{pq}^{\prime}\cong V_{pq} shows Vp​qV_{pq} is a collared manifold.
∎
15.3.4. The topological AMS lifts
Now assuming transversality, by abuse of notations, the “regular locus” of Vp​qV_{pq} is still denoted by Vp​qV_{pq} (similar treatment for thickenings for multimodules and homotopies). Then one obtains topological Kuranishi spaces
Kp​q=(Gp​q,Vp​q,Ep​q,Sp​q),p,q∈Ob​𝔽.K_{pq}=(G_{pq},V_{pq},E_{pq},S_{pq}),\ p,q\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}.
Together with the structural maps, one obtains a lift of ⌊𝔽{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{F}} to the category ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}, denoted by 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}}.
Lemma 15.21.
The topological AMS lift 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} can be canonically lifted to ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
Proof.
We only need to construct rigidifications of the embeddings
ιp​r​q:Kp​r×Kr​q→∂p​r​qKp​q.\iota_{prq}:K_{pr}\times K_{rq}\to\partial^{prq}K_{pq}.
By definition, one needs to find an orthogonal representation Np​r​qN_{prq} of Gp​r×Gr​qG_{pr}\times G_{rq} and a germ of open embedding
Gp​q×Gp​r×Gr​q(Kp​r×Kr​q×Np​r​q)→∂p​r​qKp​qG_{pq}\times_{G_{pr}\times G_{rq}}(K_{pr}\times K_{rq}\times N_{prq})\to\partial^{prq}K_{pq}
which extends ιp​r​q\iota_{prq}. Let
Wp​r​q⊆Wp​qW_{prq}\subseteq W_{pq}
be the orthogonal complement of Wp​r⊕Wr​q⊆Wp​qW_{pr}\oplus W_{rq}\subseteq W_{pq}. Moreover, the underlying strict embedding in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}} is also rigidified via a representation Qp​r​q⊆Qp​qQ_{prq}\subseteq Q_{pq}. Set
Np​r​q:=Wp​r​q⊕Qp​r​q.N_{prq}:=W_{prq}\oplus Q_{prq}.
Then one can check that there is a natural strict open embedding
Gp​q×Gp​r​q(StabNp​r​qϵ​(Kp​r×Kr​q))→∂p​r​qKp​qG_{pq}\times_{G_{prq}}\left({\rm Stab}_{N_{prq}^{\epsilon}}(K_{pr}\times K_{rq})\right)\to\partial^{prq}K_{pq}
(for a sufficiently small ball Np​r​qϵ⊆Np​r​qN_{prq}^{\epsilon}\subseteq N_{prq}) which extends ιp​r​q𝔽\iota_{prq}^{\mathbb{F}}.
∎
15.3.5. Multimodules and homotopies
Similarly, for the flow multimodule 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} over (𝔽1,…,𝔽m,𝔽′)({\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}}_{m};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}) induced from a Floer domain Σ\Sigma, choose integral modifications
𝒜𝔽iΩ:Ob​𝔽i→ℤk,\displaystyle\ {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{i}}^{\Omega}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}_{i}\to{\mathbb{Z}}^{k},\
𝒜𝔽′Ω:Ob​𝔽′→ℤk\displaystyle\ {\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}^{\Omega}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}\to{\mathbb{Z}}^{k}
(and the constant n𝕏∈ℤn_{\mathbb{X}}\in{\mathbb{Z}}, see Definition 15.2). Make choices for
⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽i𝕗​𝕣,\displaystyle\ {}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{i}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\
⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝔽′𝕗​𝕣,\displaystyle\ {}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}^{\prime}}}^{\mathbb{fr}},
namely group reductions, by Lemma 15.9, one can find a multimodule
⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝕏𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{X}}}^{\mathbb{fr}}
over (𝕞⌊𝕒𝕡,𝕗​𝕣𝔽1⋯𝕞⌊𝕒𝕡;𝕗​𝕣𝔽m𝕞⌊𝕒𝕡)𝕗​𝕣𝔽′({}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{\mathbb{F}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}},\cdots{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}}^{\mathbb{fr}};{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{fr}}) enriched in the category ⌊𝐦𝐚𝐩¯rigfr{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf map}}{}_{\rm rig}^{\rm fr}.
In parallel, choose collared and rigidified thickening data 𝕎𝔽i\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{i}} resp. 𝕎𝔽′\mathbb{W}^{\mathbb{F}^{\prime}} over ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽i{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}_{i}} resp. ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝛀,𝔽′{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\bm{\Omega}},{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}, by Proposition 15.19, one can find a thickening datum 𝕎𝕏{\mathbb{W}}^{{\mathbb{X}}} as a multimodule over (𝕎𝔽1,…,𝕎𝔽m,𝕎𝔽′)(\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\ldots,\mathbb{W}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};\mathbb{W}^{\mathbb{F}^{\prime}}). Then the data ⌊𝕞𝕒𝕡𝕏𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{map}}{}_{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{fr}} and 𝕎𝕏\mathbb{W}^{\mathbb{X}} induce the collection of topological Kuranishi spaces
Kp1⋯pm;p′𝕏=(Gp1⋯pm;p′𝕏,Vp1⋯pm;p′𝕏,Ep1⋯pm;p′𝕏,Sp1⋯pm;p′𝕏).K_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}=(G_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}},V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}},E_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}},S_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}).
This provides a lift of ⌊𝕏{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{X}} to ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}, denoted by 𝕏^\widehat{\mathbb{X}} and called a topological AMS lift of the multimodule ⌊𝕏{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{X}}. It is a multimodule over (𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^′)(\widehat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\widehat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\widehat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}). Similar to Lemma 15.21, this lift can be further lifted (in a natural way) to ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}{}_{\rm rig}.
The case of homotopies is similar and omited.
15.3.6. Proof of Proposition 15.19
The existence of a transverse thickening datum for a single moduli space was (essentially) given in [4, Section 4.1]. To construct a transverse thickening datum on a flow category, one needs a more systematic treatment.
All the constructions towards the proof is ad hoc.
Definition 15.22.
Let GG be a Lie group.
(1)
A μ\mu-representation of a Lie group GG is a direct system of complex representations (Wμ)μ≥1(W_{\mu})_{\mu\geq 1} of GG where Wμ→Wμ+1W_{\mu}\to W_{\mu+1} is an embedding. A μ\mu-representation is said to be exhaustive if any finite-dimensional representation RR of GG can be embedded into WμW_{\mu} for μ\mu sufficiently large.
(2)
A single representation WW is regarded as a μ\mu-representation with Wμ≡WW_{\mu}\equiv W.
(3)
A μ\mu-representation is called finite-dimensional if all WμW_{\mu} are finite-dimensional; is called unitary if all WμW_{\mu} are equipped with GG-invariant Hermitian inner products and the embeddings Wμ→Wμ+1W_{\mu}\to W_{\mu+1} are isometric.
(4)
A strict embedding of μ\mu-representations from (Wμ)(W_{\mu}) to (Wμ′)(W_{\mu}^{\prime}) is a sequence of GG-equivariant linear isometric embeddings Wμ→Wμ′W_{\mu}\to W_{\mu}^{\prime} such that
Wμ\textstyle{W_{\mu}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Wμ′\textstyle{W_{\mu}^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Wμ+1\textstyle{W_{\mu+1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Wμ+1′\textstyle{W_{\mu+1}^{\prime}}
Recall the definition of the category 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}. One can define another category 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯μ\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\mu} whose objects are (𝒢,B,C,(Wμ))({\mathcal{G}},B,C,(W_{\mu})) where (𝒢,B,C)({\mathcal{G}},B,C) is an object of 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}} and (Wμ)(W_{\mu}) is a finite-dimensional, exhaustive, and unitary μ\mu-representation of G⊆𝒢G\subseteq{\mathcal{G}}. One can similarly define strict embeddings; the morphisms are conjugacy classes of strict embeddings. Then there is an obvious forgetful functor
𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯μ→𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯.\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\mu}\to\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}.
Proposition 15.23.
(1)
There exist a lift of the monotone flow category 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞\mathbb{Dom} to 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯μ\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\mu}, denoted by 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞μ\mathbb{Dom}_{\mu}.
(2)
For each smooth Floer domain Σ\Sigma with mm negative cylindrical ends and one positive cylindrical end2323
23
The case with zero positive cylindrical ends, e.g., the case for Poincaré pairing, can be proved as well., a lift of 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma} to 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯μ\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\mu}, denoted by 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞μΣ\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma}_{\mu}, which is a monotone multimodule over (𝔻​𝕠​𝕞μ,…,𝔻​𝕠​𝕞μ,𝔻​𝕠​𝕞μ)(\mathbb{Dom}_{\mu},\ldots,\mathbb{Dom}_{\mu};\mathbb{Dom}_{\mu}).
(3)
For any 1-parameter family of Floer domains ΣI\Sigma^{I} and the associated homotopy 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞I\mathbb{Dom}^{I} from 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ0\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma_{0}} to 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ1\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma_{1}}, a lift to 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯μ\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\mu}, denoted by 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞μI\mathbb{Dom}_{\mu}^{I}, which is a monotone homotopy from 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞μΣ0\mathbb{Dom}_{\mu}^{\Sigma_{0}} to 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞μΣ1\mathbb{Dom}_{\mu}^{\Sigma_{1}}.
Proof.
Consider the standard unitary representation Wd=ℂdW_{d}={\mathbb{C}}^{d} of Gd≅U⁡(d)G_{d}\cong U(d). The induced representation of the exterior algebra Λ​Wd\Lambda W_{d} is also unitary. Then define the μ\mu-representation with
Wd,μ:=(⨁i=1μ(Λ​Wd)⊗i)⊕2μW_{d,\mu}:=\left(\bigoplus_{i=1}^{\mu}(\Lambda W_{d})^{\otimes i}\right)^{\oplus 2^{\mu}}
whose Hermitian structure is the direct sum of the Hermitian structures of summands. The inclusion of Wd,μW_{d,\mu} into Wd,μ+1W_{d,\mu+1} is the composition
Wd,μ=(⨁i=1μ(Λ​Wd)⊗i)⊕2μ→(⨁i=1μ+1(Λ​Wd)⊗i)⊕2μ⊕{0}⊆(⨁i=1μ+1(Λ​Wd)⊗i)⊕2μ⊕(⨁i=1μ+1(Λ​Wd)⊗i)⊕2μ=Wd,μ+1W_{d,\mu}=\left(\bigoplus_{i=1}^{\mu}(\Lambda W_{d})^{\otimes i}\right)^{\oplus 2^{\mu}}\to\left(\bigoplus_{i=1}^{\mu+1}(\Lambda W_{d})^{\otimes i}\right)^{\oplus 2^{\mu}}\oplus\{0\}\\
\subseteq\left(\bigoplus_{i=1}^{\mu+1}(\Lambda W_{d})^{\otimes i}\right)^{\oplus 2^{\mu}}\oplus\left(\bigoplus_{i=1}^{\mu+1}(\Lambda W_{d})^{\otimes i}\right)^{\oplus 2^{\mu}}=W_{d,\mu+1}
which is isometric. As any finite-dimensional representation of U⁡(d)U(d) is contained in a sufficiently higher tensor power (Λ​Wd)⊗i(\Lambda W_{d})^{\otimes i}, one obtains a μ\mu-representation.
Then for any decomposition d=d0+d1d=d_{0}+d_{1}, one has the canonical isometry
Wd0⊕Wd1≅WdW_{d_{0}}\oplus W_{d_{1}}\cong W_{d}
which is equivariant with respect to U⁡(d0)×U⁡(d1)→U⁡(d)U(d_{0})\times U(d_{1})\to U(d). This map induces an equivariant isometric embeddings of the exterior algebras
Λ​Wd0⊕Λ​Wd1→Λ​Wd\Lambda W_{d_{0}}\oplus\Lambda W_{d_{1}}\to\Lambda W_{d}
and hence isometric embeddings
Wd0,μ⊕Wd1,μ→Wd,μ.W_{d_{0},\mu}\oplus W_{d_{1},\mu}\to W_{d,\mu}.
There is an obvious associativity property of such embeddings, which induces well-defined maps for each partition d=d0+⋯+dld=d_{0}+\cdots+d_{l}
Wd0,μ⊕⋯⊕Wdl,μ→Wd,μ.W_{d_{0},\mu}\oplus\cdots\oplus W_{d_{l},\mu}\to W_{d,\mu}.
Then for each dd, the quadruple (𝒢d,Bd,Cd,(Wd,μ))({\mathcal{G}}_{d},B_{d},C_{d},(W_{d,\mu})) is an object of 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯μ\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\mu} and they form a monotone flow category enriched in this category. The cases of multimodules and homotopies are the same; notice that in these cases, there are no well-defined strict embeddings but up to conjugacy, the embeddings are well-defined.
∎
We explain what we will do next. We explain for the flow category case. We will choose sufficiently large μp​q\mu_{pq} for each pair p,qp,q inductively, such that Wp​q,μp​qW_{pq,\mu_{pq}} can cover all possible cokernels of the linearized operator of the Floer equation.
First we recall the following definition and lemma from [4] with slight modification.
Definition 15.24.
Let GG be a compact Lie group acting smoothly on a manifold BB and π:V→B\pi:V\to B be a smooth complex GG-vector bundle. A finite-dimensional approximation scheme is a finite-dimensional μ\mu-representation (Vμ)(V_{\mu}) and a morphism of μ\mu-representations λμ:Vμ→Cc∞​(B,V)\lambda_{\mu}:V_{\mu}\to C_{c}^{\infty}(B,V) such that the union of λμ​(Vμ)\lambda_{\mu}(V_{\mu}) over μ\mu is dense with respect to the Cloc∞C^{\infty}_{\rm loc}-topology.
Lemma 15.25.
[4, Lemma 4.2]
There exists a finite-dimensional approximation scheme for given G,B,VG,B,V.
Corollary 15.26.
When G=U⁡(d)G=U(d), the finite-dimensional approximation scheme can be taken such that Vμ=Wd,μV_{\mu}=W_{d,\mu} where (Wd,μ)(W_{d,\mu}) is the μ\mu-representation specified in the proof of Proposition 15.23.
Proof.
This is because any VμV_{\mu} is contained in some Wμ′W_{\mu^{\prime}} for μ′\mu^{\prime} sufficiently large.
∎
Now we can prove Proposition 15.19.
Proof of Proposition 15.19.
We can choose a collection of collared thickening data
νp​q,μ:Wp​q,μ→Cc∞(C̊p​q⌊×X,Λ⌊C̊p​q/⌊Bp​q0,1⊗TX)\nu_{pq,\mu}:W_{pq,\mu}\to C_{c}^{\infty}({}_{\lfloor}\mathring{C}_{pq}\times X,\Lambda^{0,1}_{{}_{\lfloor}\mathring{C}_{pq}/{}_{\lfloor}B_{pq}}\otimes TX)
such that they are compatible with the structural maps of the flow category. Then using the compactness of each Mp​qM_{pq}, there exists μp​q\mu_{pq} such that the image of νp​q,μp​q\nu_{pq,\mu_{pq}}, when restricted to the domain of each solution, covers the cokernel of the linearization. Then we can choose μp​q\mu_{pq} inductively. Then define Wp​q:=Wp​q,μp​qW_{pq}:=W_{pq,\mu_{pq}} and νp​q:=νp​q,μp​q\nu_{pq}:=\nu_{pq,\mu_{pq}}. This provides a transverse thickening datum on the flow category. The inductive construction on multimodules and homotopies are exactly the same.
∎
15.4. Relatively smooth AMS lifts
The topological AMS lifts actually admit refinement in the so-called relatively smooth category (see [34]). The discussion in this category is important for eventually obtaining smooth Kuranishi spaces. We introduce the category of Kuranishi spaces in this version.
15.4.1. Relative spaces and relative smooth structures
Definition 15.27 (Relative spaces).
(1)
A (stratified) relative space consists of a pair of AA-stratified topological spaces YY, SS and a stratified continuous map π:Y→S\pi:Y\to S. When π\pi is understood from the context, we denote a relative space by Y/SY/S.
(2)
A relative map from Y/SY/S to Z/TZ/T is a commutative diagram
Y Z π⁡(Y) π⁡(Z) .\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 13.75293pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&\cr&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-7.01389pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{Y\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 44.49197pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-23.66666pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 44.49197pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{Z\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 51.2628pt\raise-23.66666pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern-13.75293pt\raise-31.66666pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\pi(Y)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 37.75293pt\raise-31.66666pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\lx@xy@droprule}}{\hbox{\kern 37.75293pt\raise-31.66666pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\pi(Z)}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}\ignorespaces.
When S=TS=T, without further declaration, we will assume that the underlying map from π⁡(Y)\pi(Y) to π⁡(Z)\pi(Z) is the restriction of the identity map of SS.
(3)
A relative homeomorphism is a relative map φ:Y/S→Z/T\varphi:Y/S\to Z/T consisting of a homeomorphism from YY to ZZ and a homeomorphism from SS to TT.
(4)
If GG is a topological group, a GG-action on relative space is a continuous action via relative homeomorphisms. In particular, the map π:Y→S\pi:Y\to S is equivariant.
(5)
Let DD be another topological space. The horizontal stabilization of a relative space Y/SY/S by DD is the relative space
StabDhor​(Y/S)=(Y×D)/(S×D).{\rm Stab}_{D}^{\rm hor}(Y/S)=(Y\times D)/(S\times D).
The vertical stabilization of Y/SY/S is the relative space
StabDvert​(Y/S)=(Y×D)/S.{\rm Stab}_{D}^{\rm vert}(Y/S)=(Y\times D)/S.
Notice that both horizontal and vertical stabilizations are functors on the categories of relative spaces. Moreover, given D1,D2D_{1},D_{2}, there is a natural transformation
StabD1hor∘StabD2vert→StabD2vert∘StabD1hor.{\rm Stab}_{D_{1}}^{\rm hor}\circ{\rm Stab}_{D_{2}}^{\rm vert}\to{\rm Stab}_{D_{2}}^{\rm vert}\circ{\rm Stab}_{D_{1}}^{\rm hor}.
Remark 15.28.
A fiber bundle is a canonically a relative space. In particular, we denote by ℝ¯k/S\underline{\smash{\mathbb{R}}}^{k}/S the relative space associated to the trivial ℝk{\mathbb{R}}^{k} bundle over SS.
Definition 15.29.
Let U/S⊆ℝ¯m/SU/S\subseteq\underline{\smash{\mathbb{R}}}^{m}/S and V/T⊆ℝ¯n/TV/T\subseteq\underline{\smash{\mathbb{R}}}^{n}/T be open subsets. A continuous map φ:U/S→V/T\varphi:U/S\to V/T is called rel-C∞,kC^{\infty,k} if the map F:U→ℝnF:U\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n}, determined by
φ⁡(v,x)=(F⁡(v,x),φ¯​(x))\varphi(v,x)=(F(v,x),\underline{\smash{\varphi}}(x))
has all partial derivatives in v∈ℝmv\in{\mathbb{R}}^{m} and those up order kk varies continuously in x∈Sx\in S uniformly on compact subsets of ℝm{\mathbb{R}}^{m}. A rel-C∞,kC^{\infty,k}-map is called a rel-C∞,kC^{\infty,k}-diffeomorphism if it has a rel-C∞,kC^{\infty,k}-inverse. φ\varphi is called relatively smooth, or rel-C∞C^{\infty}, if it is rel-C∞,kC^{\infty,k} for all kk.
Definition 15.30.
A relative smooth structure on Y/SY/S consists of an atlas φα:Uα/S→ℝ¯n/S\varphi_{\alpha}:U_{\alpha}/S\to\underline{\smash{\mathbb{R}}}^{n}/S which are rel-C∞C^{\infty}-compatible. More precisely 1) Y=∪UαY=\cup U_{\alpha} and 2) for any α,β\alpha,\beta, the map
φα∘φβ−1:φβ​((Uα∩Uβ)/S)→φα​((Uα∩Uβ)/S)\varphi_{\alpha}\circ\varphi_{\beta}^{-1}:\varphi_{\beta}((U_{\alpha}\cap U_{\beta})/S)\to\varphi_{\alpha}((U_{\alpha}\cap U_{\beta})/S)
is a rel-C∞C^{\infty}-diffeomorphism.
Notice that if Y/SY/S has a relative smooth structure, then each fiber of YY has a well-defined smooth structure. Then there is a well-defined rel-C∞C^{\infty} vector bundle
Tvert​Y/S→Y,T^{\rm vert}Y/S\to Y,
called the vertical tangent bundle.
15.4.2. The category of relative smooth Kuranishi spaces
Definition 15.31 (Category of relatively smooth Kuranishi spaces).
(1)
A relative smooth Kuranishi space is a quadruple K/B=(G,V/B,E,S)K/B=(G,V/B,E,S) where (G,V,E,S)(G,V,E,S) is a topological Kuranishi space, BB is a smooth GG-manifold, together with a GG-invariant rel-C∞C^{\infty} structure on V/BV/B.
(2)
A stabilization of a relative smooth Kuranishi space K/BK/B by a GG-equivariant disk bundle
D=Dhor⊕Dvert⊆Nhor⊕NvertD=D^{\rm hor}\oplus D^{\rm vert}\subseteq N^{\rm hor}\oplus N^{\rm vert}
is the relative Kuranishi space
StabD​(K/B)=(G,V~/B~,E~,S~){\rm Stab}_{D}(K/B)=(G,\tilde{V}/\tilde{B},\tilde{E},\tilde{S})
where V~/B~\tilde{V}/\tilde{B} is the stabilization of the relative space V/BV/B by DD (which carries a canonically induced relative smooth structure), E~\tilde{E} and S~\tilde{S} are the natural stabilization.
(3)
A strict embedding of relative smooth Kuranishi spaces from K1/B1=(G1,V1/B1,E1,S1)K_{1}/B_{1}=(G_{1},V_{1}/B_{1},E_{1},S_{1}) to K2/B2=(G2,V2/B2,E2,S2)K_{2}/B_{2}=(G_{2},V_{2}/B_{2},E_{2},S_{2}) consists of a strict embedding
ι21:K1→K2\iota_{21}:K_{1}\to K_{2}
(which includes a group embedding ι21G:G1→G2\iota_{21}^{G}:G_{1}\to G_{2}) and an ι21G\iota_{21}^{G}-equivariant smooth embedding B1→B2B_{1}\to B_{2}.
(4)
An embedding of relative Kuranishi spaces from K1/B1K_{1}/B_{1} to K2/B2K_{2}/B_{2} is a conjugacy class of strict embeddings.
(5)
Let 𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}} be the category of relatively smooth Kuranishi spaces whose morphisms are embeddings. One can also consider the rigidified and collared versions of this category.
Notice that there is an obvious functor
𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯→𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}\to\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}
by sending
(G,V/B,E,S)↦(G,V,E,S).(G,V/B,E,S)\mapsto(G,V,E,S).
Proposition 15.32 (Relative smooth structures on AMS lifts).
(1)
In Situation Flow(i), any topological AMS lift of the Floer flow category is canonically lifted to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
(2)
In Situation Module(i), let 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} be the AMS lift of the outercollaring of 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} to ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig} as a multimodule over the topological AMS lifts (𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^′)(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}) enriched in ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig}. Then 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} is canonically lifted to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
(3)
In Situation Homotopy(i), let ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} be a topological AMS lift of the outercollaring of ℍ{\mathbb{H}} to ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig}. Then ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} is canonically enriched in ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
Proof.
We only discuss the case about the flow category. The other cases can be proved in the same manner. For each pair p<qp<q of objects in 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}, the fiberwise smooth structure of ⌊Vp​q→⌊Bp​q{}_{\lfloor}V_{pq}\to{}_{\lfloor}B_{pq} follows from the implicit function theorem. The fact that these fiberwise structures vary in the rel-C∞C^{\infty} sense can be proved using the method of [68] (which treats the case of Gromov–Witten theory). Alternatively, it follows from the proof of [14, Proposition 6.2].
∎
We summarize the construction so far in the following situations.
Situation Flow(iii).
In Situation Flow(ii), the domain flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}} induces an associated flow category ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\mathbb{fr}}. Choose a transverse thickening datum 𝕎𝔽{\mathbb{W}}^{\mathbb{F}} and a group reduction, which gives a relatively smooth AMS lift 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} enriched in ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
Situation Module(iii).
In Situation Module(ii), 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} is a relatively smooth AMS lift subject to an outercollaring width and a compatible list of integral actions on the involved flow categories. 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} is a multimodule over (𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^′)(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}) where each member of this tuple is a relative smooth AMS lift of an involved Floer flow category subject to the outercollaring width and the chosen integral action.
Situation Homotopy(iii).
In Situation Homotopy(ii), ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} is a relatively smooth AMS lift of the homotopy ℍ{\mathbb{H}} enriched in ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig} subject to an outercollaring width and a compatible list of integral actions on the involved Floer flow categories based on the homotopy ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,ℍ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{H}}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}. The two boundaries of ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} are relatively smooth AMS lifts of multimodules 𝕏0\mathbb{X}_{0} resp. 𝕏1\mathbb{X}_{1}.
16. Vertical Normal Complex Structures and orientations
16.1. Main statements about normal complex structures
Recall that one has defined the category of relatively smooth Kuranishi spaces 𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}. Given any object K/B=(G,V/B,E,S)K/B=(G,V/B,E,S), one has a well-defined vertical tangent bundle
Tvt​V→VT^{\rm vt}V\to V
which is a GG-equivariant relatively smooth vector bundle. Recall the definition of equivariant normal complex structures (Definition 3.23). Given a relatively smooth Kuranishi space K/B=(G,V/B,E,S)K/B=(G,V/B,E,S), a relative NC structure on K/BK/B is by definition a GG-equivariant NC structure on Tvt​V→VT^{\rm vt}V\to V. One can then define the category of relative NC Kuranishi spaces, denoted by
𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NC.\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}^{\rm NC}.
We can also consider the rigidified and collared versions. We omit the detailed definitions.
Now we state our main theorems about the existence of fiberwise stable complex structures of Floer flow categories, multimodules, and homotopies.
Theorem 16.1.
In Situation Flow(iii), the relatively smooth AMS lift 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} admits a set of lifts, denoted temporarily by 𝔽^^\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}, to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. We call such a lift a relatively NC AMS lift.
Proof.
See Subsection 16.3.
∎
Remark 16.2.
In the following theorem, what we call a relative NC AMS lifts of 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} actually involves more data than the lifts to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}; they also include certain choices made for the construction. The construction of the relative NC AMS lifts for multimodules actually depends on these choices, not only on the resulting lifts of the flow categories.
Theorem 16.3.
In Situation Module(iii), suppose 𝔽^^1,…,𝔽^^m;𝔽^^′\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{m};\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}^{\prime} are relatively NC AMS lifts of them provided by Theorem 16.1. Then 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} admits a set of lifts, denoted temporarily by 𝕏^^\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}}, to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as a multimodule over (𝔽^^1,…,𝔽^^m,𝔽^^′)(\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{m};\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}^{\prime}). Each of such 𝕏^^\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}} is called a relatively NC AMS lifts (of 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} or 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}}).
Proof.
See Subsection 16.4.
∎
Theorem 16.4.
In Situation Homotopy(iii), suppose 𝔽^^1,…,𝔽^^m,𝔽^^′\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{m},\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}^{\prime} are relatively NC AMS lifts of the involved Floer flow categories, 𝕏^^0\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}}_{0} and 𝕏^^1\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}}_{1} are relatively NC AMS lifts of the two multimodules subject to the fixed outercollaring width and the fixed list of compatible integral actions. Then the relatively smooth AMS lift ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} admits a lift, denoted by ℍ^^\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{H}}}} temporarily, to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as a homotopy from 𝕏^^0\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}}_{0} to 𝕏^^1\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}}_{1}. We call ℍ^^\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{H}}}} a relatively NC AMS lift (of ℍ{\mathbb{H}} or ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}}).
Proof.
A tedious reformulation of the proofs of Theorem 16.1 and Theorem 16.3. There are no essential new ingredients.
∎
16.2. Abouzaid–Blumberg’s construction for a single moduli space
We first review the construction of [1, Section 11] in the case of a single moduli space from the Floer flow category. Let 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} be the Floer flow category associated to the Hamiltonian HH. Consider a pair of objects p<qp<q such that there is no intermediate object rr with p<r<qp<r<q. Let Kp​q=(Gp​q,Vp​q,Ep​q,Sp​q)K_{pq}=(G_{pq},V_{pq},E_{pq},S_{pq}) be an AMS global chart of Mp​q𝔽M_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}, viewed as an object of 𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}. We can ignore Ep​qE_{pq} and Sp​qS_{pq} for the discussion but should remember the reletive structure Vp​q/Bp​qV_{pq}/B_{pq}. We will also drop the outercollaring for a moment.
16.2.1. A complex-linear Cauchy–Riemann operator and an interpolation
We first specify a family of complex linear Cauchy–Riemann operator for points in Vp​qV_{pq}. Fix an almost complex structure J0J_{0} and a J0J_{0}-linear connection ∇T​X\nabla^{TX} such that its holonomy along each 1-periodic orbit of HtH_{t} is trivial. Choose τ>2\tau>2.
We first look at an individual smooth map u:ℝ×S1→Xu:{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}\to X which converges exponentially to 1-periodic orbits of HH. Define the space
W~1,τ​(u∗​T​X)⊆Wloc1,τ​(u∗​T​X)\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}(u^{*}TX)\subseteq W^{1,\tau}_{\rm loc}(u^{*}TX)
to be the space of sections which differ from ∇T​X\nabla^{TX}-parallel sections along the limiting periodic orbits by W1,τW^{1,\tau}-small terms near infinity. Then the J0J_{0}-linear connection ∇T​X\nabla^{TX} induces a complex-linear Cauchy–Riemann operator
Duℂ:W~1,τ​(u∗​T​X)→Lτ​(Λ0,1⊗u∗​T​X).D_{u}^{\mathbb{C}}:\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}(u^{*}TX)\to L^{\tau}(\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes u^{*}TX).
As uu converges exponentially to periodic orbits, it is easy to see that DuℂD_{u}^{\mathbb{C}} is Fredholm.
The operator DuℂD_{u}^{\mathbb{C}} and the linearization of the Floer equation can be connected by a particular 1-parameter family of Fredholm operators modulo certain finite-dimensional corrections. Choose a cut-off function
χ:Dom⁡(u)≅ℝ×S1→[0,1]\chi:{\rm Dom}(u)\cong{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}\to[0,1]
which only depends on the ℝ{\mathbb{R}}-variable such that χ⁡(s)=0\chi(s)=0 for s≪0s\ll 0 and χ⁡(s)=1\chi(s)=1 for s≫0s\gg 0. For each object pp, let up:ℝ×S1→Xu_{p}:{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}\to X be the corresponding constant solution to the Floer equation (which does not depend on the capping). Then there is an associated linearized operator
Dup​(ξ)=∂sξ+Jt​(∇tξ−∇ξXHt​(p)).D_{u_{p}}(\xi)=\partial_{s}\xi+J_{t}\left(\nabla_{t}\xi-\nabla_{\xi}X_{H_{t}}(p)\right).
Let
W~1,τ​(ℝ×S1,up∗​T​X)⊆Wloc1,τ​(ℝ×S1,up∗​T​X)\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},u_{p}^{*}TX)\subseteq W^{1,\tau}_{\rm loc}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},u_{p}^{*}TX)
be the subspace of Wloc1,τW^{1,\tau}_{\rm loc}-sections which satisfies the same asymptotic condition near −∞-\infty as W~1,τ​(u∗​T​X)\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}(u^{*}TX) and which is W1,τW^{1,\tau}-small near +∞+\infty. Then consider the interpolation
Dp:W~1,τ​(ℝ×S1,up∗​T​X)→Lτ​(ℝ×S1,Λ0,1⊗up∗​T​X)ξ↦(1−χ)​(∇T​Xξ)J00,1+χ​Dup​(ξ).\begin{split}D_{p}:\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},u_{p}^{*}TX)\to&\ L^{\tau}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes u_{p}^{*}TX)\\
\xi\mapsto&\ (1-\chi)(\nabla^{TX}\xi)_{J_{0}}^{0,1}+\chi D_{u_{p}}(\xi).\end{split}
(16.1)
Then DpD_{p} is a real-linear Fredholm operator. Notice that from the definition, DpD_{p} only depends on the underlying 1-periodic orbit but not the capping.
We now choose, for each object pp (actually, as discussed above, only depending on the underlying orbit), a finite-dimensional complex vector space Rp+R_{p}^{+}, a linear map
νp:Rp+→C0∞​(ℝ×S1,Λ0,1⊗up∗​T​X)\nu_{p}:R_{p}^{+}\to C_{0}^{\infty}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes u_{p}^{*}TX)
(16.2)
such that the map
νp⊕Dp:Rp+⊕W~1,τ​(ℝ×S1,u∗​T​X)→Lτ​(ℝ×S1,Λ0,1⊗up∗​T​X)\nu_{p}\oplus D_{p}:R_{p}^{+}\oplus\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},u^{*}TX)\to L^{\tau}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes u_{p}^{*}TX)
is surjective. Denote
Rp−:=Ker⁡(θp⊕Dp)⊆Rp+⊕W~1,τ​(ℝ×S1,u∗​T​X).R_{p}^{-}:={\rm Ker}(\theta_{p}\oplus D_{p})\subseteq R_{p}^{+}\oplus\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},u^{*}TX).
Notice that the pair (Rp−,Rp+)(R_{p}^{-},R_{p}^{+}) does not depend on the Sobolev exponent τ\tau.
Now we would like to construct interpolations between DuD_{u} and DuℂD_{u}^{\mathbb{C}}, up to factors coming from DpD_{p} and DqD_{q}, in a 1-parameter family. The basic idea has been described in [1, Section 11] and [2, Appendix B]. However, we need to be more careful when generalizing to the case of multimodules.
More precisely, we would like to construct an interpolation between
Dp⊕Du:W~1,τ​(up∗​T​X)⊕W1,τ​(u∗​T​X)→Lτ​(Λ0,1⊗up∗​T​X)⊕Lτ​(Λ0,1⊗u∗​T​X)D_{p}\oplus D_{u}:\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}(u_{p}^{*}TX)\oplus W^{1,\tau}(u^{*}TX)\to L^{\tau}(\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes u_{p}^{*}TX)\oplus L^{\tau}(\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes u^{*}TX)
and
Duℂ​⊕~​Dq:W~1,τ​(u∗​T​X)​⊕~​W~1,τ​(uq∗​T​X)→Lτ​(Λ0,1⊗uq∗​T​X).D_{u}^{\mathbb{C}}\widetilde{\oplus}D_{q}:\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}(u^{*}TX)\widetilde{\oplus}\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}(u_{q}^{*}TX)\to L^{\tau}(\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes u_{q}^{*}TX).
Here ⊕~\widetilde{\oplus} means the subset of the direct sum satisfying the matching condition.
To build the interpolation, consider the family of cut-off functions
χρ:ℝ→[0,1],χρ​(s)=χ⁡(s−ρ).\chi_{\rho}:{\mathbb{R}}\to[0,1],\ \chi_{\rho}(s)=\chi(s-\rho).
Then for all t∈ℝt\in{\mathbb{R}}, define
Du,ρ:W~1,τ​(u∗​T​X)→Lτ​(Λ0,1⊗u∗​T​X),ξ↦(1−χρ)​(∇T​Xξ)J00,1+χρ​Du​(ξ).\begin{split}D_{u,\rho}:\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}(u^{*}TX)\to&\ L^{\tau}(\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes u^{*}TX),\\
\xi\mapsto&\ (1-\chi_{\rho})(\nabla^{TX}\xi)_{J_{0}}^{0,1}+\chi_{\rho}D_{u}(\xi).\end{split}
(16.3)
Notice that even if uu has bubble components, these operators are still defined. Then intuitively, we have
limρ→−∞Du,ρ≈Dp⊕Du,\displaystyle\ \lim_{\rho\to-\infty}D_{u,\rho}\approx D_{p}\oplus D_{u},\
limρ→+∞Du,ρ≈Duℂ​⊕~​Dq.\displaystyle\ \lim_{\rho\to+\infty}D_{u,\rho}\approx D_{u}^{\mathbb{C}}\widetilde{\oplus}D_{q}.
This is the underlying idea of interpolating the linearized operator DuD_{u} and a complex linear operator DuℂD_{u}^{\mathbb{C}}, up to the two operators DpD_{p} and DqD_{q} which are independent of uu.
To better formulate this construction over the whole Kuranishi chart Vp​qV_{pq}, we need to introduce an auxiliary space. Denote
B~p​q:=Bp​q×[−∞,+∞],\widetilde{B}_{pq}:=B_{pq}\times[-\infty,+\infty],
viewed as a product of stratified spaces where [−∞,+∞][-\infty,+\infty] has one open stratum and two boundary strata. We define an auxiliary universal curve C~p​q→B~p​q\widetilde{C}_{pq}\to\widetilde{B}_{pq} whose fiber C~ϕ,ρ\widetilde{C}_{\phi,\rho} at (ϕ,ρ)(\phi,\rho) with ϕ∈Bp​q\phi\in B_{pq} and ρ∈(−∞,+∞)\rho\in(-\infty,+\infty) is still CϕC_{\phi}, while for ρ=−∞\rho=-\infty resp. ρ=+∞\rho=+\infty, C~ϕ,ρ\widetilde{C}_{\phi,\rho} has the additional component of the domain of the map upu_{p} resp. the domain of uqu_{q}. One can then define the additional space V~p​q\widetilde{V}_{pq} which is identical to Vp​q×[−∞,+∞]V_{pq}\times[-\infty,+\infty]. However, for each point (ϕ~,u~,e,F)∈V~p​q(\widetilde{\phi},\widetilde{u},e,F)\in\widetilde{V}_{pq}, we regard uu as a map u~:C~ϕ,ρ→X\widetilde{u}:\widetilde{C}_{\phi,\rho}\to X where if ρ=±∞\rho=\pm\infty, u~\widetilde{u} maps the extra cylindrical component to the constant loop at the negative or the positive end. Then V~p​q→B~p​q\widetilde{V}_{pq}\to\widetilde{B}_{pq} is still relatively smooth. The operator Du,ρD_{u,\rho} can be viewed as a Cauchy–Riemann operator Du~D_{\widetilde{u}} acting on the bundle u~∗​T​X\widetilde{u}^{*}TX (and extended to suitable Sobolev completions). We remark that, this setup facilitates the gluing construction: when ρ∈±∞\rho\in\pm\infty, if the operator Du,ρD_{u,\rho} is surjective, then each vector in the kernel can be glued to an element in the kernel at a nearby point.
With the above viewpoint understood, using basic gluing construction, one obtains the following technical lemma. Let
ℰ̊p​q0→V~p​q\mathring{\mathcal{E}}_{pq}^{0}\to\widetilde{V}_{pq}
be the infinite-dimensional vector bundle whose fiber over x~=(ϕ~,u~,e,F)\widetilde{x}=(\widetilde{\phi},\widetilde{u},e,F) is the space
ℰ̊x~0=Ωc0,1​(C~ϕ,ρ,u~∗​T​X).\mathring{\mathcal{E}}_{\widetilde{x}}^{0}=\Omega_{c}^{0,1}(\widetilde{C}_{\phi,\rho},\widetilde{u}^{*}TX).
Notice that when ρ=±∞\rho=\pm\infty, one has the splitting
ℰ̊x~0=Ωc0,1​(ℝ×S1,up∗​T​X)⊕Ωc0,1​(Cϕ,u∗​T​X)\mathring{\mathcal{E}}_{\widetilde{x}}^{0}=\Omega_{c}^{0,1}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},u_{p}^{*}TX)\oplus\Omega_{c}^{0,1}(C_{\phi},u^{*}TX)
(16.4)
or
ℰ̊x~0=Ωc0,1​(Cϕ,u∗​T​X)⊕Ωc0,1​(ℝ×S1,uq∗​T​X).\mathring{\mathcal{E}}_{\widetilde{x}}^{0}=\Omega_{c}^{0,1}(C_{\phi},u^{*}TX)\oplus\Omega_{c}^{0,1}({\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1},u_{q}^{*}TX).
(16.5)
Lemma 16.5.

(1)
When ρ=−∞\rho=-\infty, with respect to the splitting (16.4), ν~p​q\widetilde{\nu}_{pq} has the block form

where νp\nu_{p} is specified in (16.2).

where

(3)
For each x~∈V~p​q\widetilde{x}\in\widetilde{V}_{pq}, the image of ν~p​q\widetilde{\nu}_{pq} at x~\widetilde{x} is transverse to the image of the operator Du~D_{\widetilde{u}}.
Proof.

16.2.2. An extended index bundle
Now assume Wp​qW_{pq} and ν~p​q\widetilde{\nu}_{pq} is given as in Lemma 16.5, consider the family of linear maps parametrized by x~=(ϕ~,u~,e,F)∈V~p​q\widetilde{x}=(\widetilde{\phi},\widetilde{u},e,F)\in\widetilde{V}_{pq}:
νx~⊕Du~:(Rp+⊕Wp​q⊕Rq+)⊕W~1,τ​(u~∗​T​X)→Lτ​(Λ0,1⊗u~∗​T​X).\nu_{\widetilde{x}}\oplus D_{\widetilde{u}}:\big(R_{p}^{+}\oplus W_{pq}\oplus R_{q}^{+}\big)\oplus\widetilde{W}^{1,\tau}(\widetilde{u}^{*}TX)\to L^{\tau}(\Lambda^{0,1}\otimes\widetilde{u}^{*}TX).
Proposition 16.6.
The union of kernels of ν~x~⊕Du~\widetilde{\nu}_{\widetilde{x}}\oplus D_{\widetilde{u}} form a continuous 2424

In fact it is a relative smooth vector bundle. vector bundle
I~p​q→V~p​q.\widetilde{I}_{pq}\to\widetilde{V}_{pq}.
Proof.
The proof is based on the typical gluing construction. However, one needs to maintain the linear structure in the gluing procedure. The pregluing is constructed using parallel transport on the target manifold XX and cut-paste on the domain, which are linear in the input. The use of the implicit function theorem can also respect the linear feature.
∎
Hence the vector bundles on the two boundary pieces, ∂±V~p​q:=Vp​q×{±∞}≅Vp​q\partial^{\pm}\widetilde{V}_{pq}:=V_{pq}\times\{\pm\infty\}\cong V_{pq} are (non-canonically) isomorphic. The family of kernels selects a homotopy class of isomorphisms. By the specific characterization of ν~p​q\widetilde{\nu}_{pq} given in Lemma 16.5, one can see that
I~p​q|∂−V~p​q≅R¯p−⊕Tvt​Vp​q⊕W¯p​q⊕R¯q+;\widetilde{I}_{pq}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{pq}}\cong\underline{\smash{R}}_{p}^{-}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{pq}\oplus\underline{\smash{W}}_{pq}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{q}^{+};
and
I~p​q|∂+V~p​q≅R¯p+⊕Ip​qℂ⊕R¯q−.\widetilde{I}_{pq}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{pq}}\cong\underline{\smash{R}}_{p}^{+}\oplus I_{pq}^{\mathbb{C}}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{q}^{-}.
Here Ip​qℂI_{pq}^{\mathbb{C}} is formed by the kernels of the complex-linear operator
