We can then choose a continuous bundle isomorphism
R¯p−⊕Tvt​Vp​q⊕W¯p​q⊕R¯q+≅R¯p+⊕Ip​qℂ⊕R¯q−.\underline{\smash{R}}_{p}^{-}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{pq}\oplus\underline{\smash{W}}_{pq}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{q}^{+}\cong\underline{\smash{R}}_{p}^{+}\oplus I_{pq}^{\mathbb{C}}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{q}^{-}.
Notice that Gp​qG_{pq} acts trivially on the vector spaces Rp±R_{p}^{\pm} and Rq±R_{q}^{\pm}. As Wp​qW_{pq} is complex, one can see that this is a stable isomorphism from Tvt​Vp​qT^{\rm vt}V_{pq} to Ip​qℂI_{pq}^{\mathbb{C}} and hence induces an NC structure on Tvt​Vp​qT^{\rm vt}V_{pq}.
16.3. Proof of Theorem 16.1
16.3.1. An extended Kuranishi flow category
We extend the previous construction to all moduli spaces involved in a single Floer flow category 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}. To construct the interpolation in a compatible way for all moduli spaces, we utilize the lateral lines (see Definition 14.5). Recall that for each pair of objects p≤qp\leq q, in the AMS construction there is a Gp​qG_{pq}-manifold Bp​qB_{pq} parametrizing certain curves in ℂ​ℙdp​q\mathbb{CP}^{d_{pq}}. Consider the moduli space
ℳ¯(ℂℙdp​q,dp​q)ℝ0,2,+\overline{\mathcal{M}}{}_{0,2,+}^{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{CP}^{d_{pq}},d_{pq})

ℳ¯(ℂℙdp​q,dp​q)ℝ0,2,+→ℳ¯(ℂℙdp​q,dp​q)ℝ0,2.\overline{\mathcal{M}}{}_{0,2,+}^{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{CP}^{d_{pq}},d_{pq})\to\overline{\mathcal{M}}{}_{0,2}^{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{CP}^{d_{pq}},d_{pq}).
Let B~p​q\widetilde{B}_{pq} be the preimage of Bp​qB_{pq}; let ϕ~\widetilde{\phi} denote a typical element of B~p​q\widetilde{B}_{pq} with the underlying point ϕ∈Bp​q\phi\in B_{pq}. We use the convention that this interior marked point does not go to sphere bubbles but only stay in cylindrical components; namely, it can coincide with a node. Let

be the pullback of Cp​q→Bp​qC_{pq}\to B_{pq}, which still gives an equivariant family of curves

which contains the marked point.
Notice that there two disjoint closed subsets

Notice that B~p​q\widetilde{B}_{pq} and C~p​q\widetilde{C}_{pq} can also be organized as morphism spaces of a flow category. —The family of Cauchy–Riemann operators—Then we would like to build a family of Fredholm operators indexed by x~=(ϕ~,u~,e,F)∈V~p​q⌊\widetilde{x}=(\widetilde{\phi},\widetilde{u},e,F)\in{}_{\lfloor}\widetilde{V}_{pq}. we have
ν~p​q=[0νx~000νq].\widetilde{\nu}_{pq}=\left[\begin{array}[]{ccc}0&\nu_{\widetilde{x}}&0\\

Here νx~:Wp​q→Ωc0,1​(Cϕ,u∗​T​X)\nu_{\widetilde{x}}:W_{pq}\to\Omega_{c}^{0,1}(C_{\phi},u^{*}TX) is a complex-linear map.
(3)
(Flow category structure I) The above conditions imply that ν~p​r\widetilde{\nu}_{pr} and ν~r​q\widetilde{\nu}_{rq} determine a bundle map

(5)
(Transversality) For each x~∈V~p​q\widetilde{x}\in\widetilde{V}_{pq}, the image ν~p​q\widetilde{\nu}_{pq} contained in ℰ̊x~0⊆ℰx~0\mathring{\mathcal{E}}_{\widetilde{x}}^{0}\subseteq{\mathcal{E}}_{\widetilde{x}}^{0} is transverse to the image of Dx~D_{\widetilde{x}} (which is a condition true for all τ>2\tau>2).
(6)

(7)
(Rigidification) ν~p​q\widetilde{\nu}_{pq} does not vary in the normal direction to V~p​r​q\widetilde{V}_{prq} specified by the rigidfication.
(8)
(Novikov equivariance) These objects are equivariant with respect to the natural Π\Pi-action.
Lemma 16.9.
There exists an index bundle interpolator on 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}}.
Proof.
This is an inductive construction. The spaces Rp+R_{p}^{+} and the maps νp\nu_{p} can be chosen independently for all objects. The construction of Abouzaid–Blumberg recalled previously provides the required space Wp​qW_{pq} and the bundle map ν~p​q\widetilde{\nu}_{pq} for p<qp<q which does not have intermediate objects. Suppose for a pair of objects p<qp<q, one has constructed such structures for all r<sr<s with dr−ds<dp−dqd_{r}-d_{s}<d_{p}-d_{q}, then for Wp​qW_{pq}, one can choose initially Wp​qW_{pq} to be the direct sum of all Wp​r⊕Rp+⊕Wr​qW_{pr}\oplus R_{p}^{+}\oplus W_{rq} for intermediate objects rr. The value of ν~p​q\widetilde{\nu}_{pq} on the boundary is then determined by first three conditions of Definition 16.8 as well as the rigidification condition. The collar condition allows us to extend slightly into the interior of V~p​q\widetilde{V}_{pq}. The transversality achieved on the boundary strata is carried over to such an extension. To achieve global transversality, one may need to enlarge Wp​qW_{pq} by taking direct sum with another complex vector space.
∎
Once the index bundle interpolator is chosen, one automatically obtains a system of vector bundles over the spaces V~p​q\widetilde{V}_{pq}. Indeed, for each x~∈V~p​q\widetilde{x}\in\widetilde{V}_{pq}, denote
I~p​q|x~:=ker⁡(ν~p​q|x~⊕Dx~)⊆ℰp​q1|x~.\widetilde{I}_{pq}|_{\widetilde{x}}:={\rm ker}(\widetilde{\nu}_{pq}|_{\widetilde{x}}\oplus D_{\widetilde{x}})\subseteq{\mathcal{E}}_{pq}^{1}|_{\widetilde{x}}.
They form a topological vector bundle I~p​q→V~p​q\widetilde{I}_{pq}\to\widetilde{V}_{pq}. We consider its restriction to ∂±V~p​q\partial^{\pm}\widetilde{V}_{pq}. By the first two conditions of Definition 16.8, one has Gp​qG_{pq}-equivariant identifications
I~p​q|∂−V~p​q≅R¯p−⊕Tvt​Vp​q⊕W¯p​q⊕R¯q+\widetilde{I}_{pq}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{pq}}\cong\underline{\smash{R}}_{p}^{-}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{pq}\oplus\underline{\smash{W}}_{pq}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{q}^{+}
and
I~p​q|∂+V~p​q≅R¯p+⊕Ip​qℂ⊕R¯q−.\widetilde{I}_{pq}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{pq}}\cong\underline{\smash{R}}_{p}^{+}\oplus I_{pq}^{\mathbb{C}}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{q}^{-}.
Here Ip​qℂI_{pq}^{\mathbb{C}} has fiber over x~\widetilde{x} being
ker⁡(νx~⊕Duℂ){\rm ker}(\nu_{\widetilde{x}}\oplus D_{u}^{\mathbb{C}})
hence a Gp​qG_{pq}-equivariant complex vector bundle. Notice that ∂−V~p​q≅Vp​q≅∂+V~p​q\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{pq}\cong V_{pq}\cong\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{pq} canonically and the inclusions of Vp​qV_{pq} into V~p​q\widetilde{V}_{pq} from both sides are Gp​qG_{pq}-equivariant homotopy equivalences. Hence the two restriction bundles are equivariantly isomorphic.
To construct a normal complex structure on the flow category, one must choose such bundle isomorphisms in a way compatible with the flow category structure. Notice that the product V~p​r​q≅V~p​r⊠V~r​q\widetilde{V}_{prq}\cong\widetilde{V}_{pr}\boxtimes\widetilde{V}_{rq}, it is the union
V~p​r×∂−V~r​q​∪∂+V~p​r×∂−V~r​q​∂+V~p​r×V~r​q.\widetilde{V}_{pr}\times\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{rq}\underset{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{pr}\times\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{rq}}{\cup}\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{pr}\times\widetilde{V}_{rq}.
Hence I~p​r\widetilde{I}_{pr} and I~r​q\widetilde{I}_{rq} determine a vector bundle
I~p​r​q→V~p​r​q\widetilde{I}_{prq}\to\widetilde{V}_{prq}
which is I~p​r⊕R¯r−⊕Tvt​Vr​q⊕W¯r​q⊕R¯q+\widetilde{I}_{pr}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{r}^{-}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{rq}\oplus\underline{\smash{W}}_{rq}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{q}^{+} on the first piece and which is R¯p+⊕Ip​qℂ⊕I~r​q\underline{\smash{R}}_{p}^{+}\oplus I_{pq}^{\mathbb{C}}\oplus\widetilde{I}_{rq} on the second piece.
Lemma 16.10.
There exists a system of Gp​qG_{pq}-equivariant real vector bundle isomorphisms
I~p​q|∂−V~p​q≅I~p​q|∂+V~p​q\widetilde{I}_{pq}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{pq}}\cong\widetilde{I}_{pq}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{pq}}
satisfying the following conditions.
(1)
Whenever p<r<qp<r<q, the following diagram commutes.
I~p​r​q|∂−V~p​r×∂−V~r​q\textstyle{\widetilde{I}_{prq}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{pr}\times\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{rq}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}I~p​r​q|∂+V~p​r×∂−V~r​q\textstyle{\widetilde{I}_{prq}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{pr}\times\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{rq}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}I~p​r​q|∂+V~p​r×∂+V~r​q\textstyle{\widetilde{I}_{prq}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{pr}\times\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{rq}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}I~p​q|∂−V~p​r​q\textstyle{\widetilde{I}_{pq}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{prq}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}I~p​q|∂+V~p​r​q\textstyle{\widetilde{I}_{pq}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{prq}}}
(2)

Proof.
Induction and homotopy triviality of the interpolating interval [0,1][0,1].
∎
Now as Ip​qℂI_{pq}^{\mathbb{C}} is complex and Rp±R_{p}^{\pm}, Rq±R_{q}^{\pm} are trivial representations of Gp​qG_{pq}, the isomorphism induces an NC structure on Tvt​Vp​qT^{\rm vt}V_{pq}. The compatibility condition given in Lemma 16.10 implies that the structural maps of the flow category respect the vertical NC structures. Therefore, one obtains a lift of 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. This finishes the proof of Theorem 16.1.
16.4. Proof of Theorem 16.3
Let Σ𝕏\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}} be the smooth Floer domain in Situation Module(iii). One still needs to relate the linearization of the Floer equation with a complex-linear operator on Σ𝕏\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}} via a certain interpolation. However, in order to be compatible with chosen interpolations for the involved flow categories, the interpolation here needs to depend on generally mm parameters instead of just one, where mm is the number of negative cylindrical ends, or more generally, the number of lateral lines in Σ𝕏\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}.
Let ℓ1,…,ℓm⊆Σ𝕏\ell_{1},\ldots,\ell_{m}\subseteq\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}} be the lateral lines. Choose diffeomorphisms
ρj:ℓj≅ℝ\rho_{j}:\ell_{j}\cong{\mathbb{R}}
such that on cylindrical ends, ρj\rho_{j} coincides with the radial coordinates up to a shift. Let
B~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}
be the version of the moduil Bp1⋯pm;p′𝕏B_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} whose elements are (ϕ,z1,…,zm)(\phi,z_{1},\ldots,z_{m}) where zjz_{j} is contained in the jj-th lateral line ℓj⊆Cϕ\ell_{j}\subseteq C_{\phi} and
either​ρj​(zj)≤0​∀jor​ρ1​(z1)=⋯=ρm​(zm)≥0.{\rm either}\ \rho_{j}(z_{j})\leq 0\ \forall j\ \ {\rm or}\ \rho_{1}(z_{1})=\cdots=\rho_{m}(z_{m})\geq 0.
Compactify the spaces to allow the marked points to escape from cylindrical ends: notice that they can either escape from negative ends independently, or escape from the positive end simultaneously. Then the foregetful map
B~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏→Bp1⋯pm;p′\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\to B_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}
has generic fibers being homeomorphic to a mm-dimensional complex. Notice that the functions ρj\rho_{j} extend to a continuous and Gp1⋯pm;p′𝕏G_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}-invariant map
ρ:B~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏→[−∞,+∞]m\rho:\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\to[-\infty,+\infty]^{m}
such that either all ρj\rho_{j} are negative or all ρj\rho_{j} are nonnegative and identical.
Moreover, one can pullback the universal curve to
C~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏→B~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏.\widetilde{C}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\to\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}.
Similar to before, one has “structural maps”
B~pi​qi𝔽i⊠B~p1⋯pi−1qipi+1⋯pm;p′𝕏→B~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏,\displaystyle\ \widetilde{B}_{p_{i}q_{i}}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{i}}\boxtimes\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{i-1}q_{i}p_{i+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\to\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}},\
B~p1⋯pm;q′𝕏⊠B~q′​p′𝔽′→B~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏\displaystyle\ \widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\boxtimes\widetilde{B}_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}\to\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}
which satisfy the usual compatibility condition.
We choose compatible cut-off functions, whose existence follow again from an induction argument.
Lemma 16.11.
Suppose χpj​qj𝔽j\chi_{p_{j}q_{j}}^{\mathbb{F}_{j}} and χp′​q′𝔽′\chi_{p^{\prime}q^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}} have been chosen independently as given by Lemma 16.7. Then there exists a family of Gp1⋯pm;p′𝕏G_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}-invariant continuous functions

satisfying the following conditions. We characterize the property by considering its restriction to the fiber at each point ϕ~∈B~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏\widetilde{\phi}\in\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}. Denote the restriction by χϕ~:Cϕ~→[0,1]\chi_{\widetilde{\phi}}:C_{\widetilde{\phi}}\to[0,1].
(1)
When ρ1,…,ρm≤0\rho_{1},\ldots,\rho_{m}\leq 0, the support of χϕ~\chi_{\widetilde{\phi}} is the disjoint union of mm connected cylindrical regions contained in the mm negative ends of Cϕ~C_{\widetilde{\phi}}.
(2)
When ρ1=…=ρm≫0\rho_{1}=\ldots=\rho_{m}\gg 0, the support of χϕ~\chi_{\widetilde{\phi}} is contained in the positive cylindrical end.
(3)
χp1⋯pm;p′𝕏\chi_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} respects the structural maps of the multimodule about the concatenation from the negative side. More precisely, when pj<qjp_{j}<q_{j} and ϕ~∈B~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′𝕏\widetilde{\phi}\in\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}, χϕ~\chi_{\widetilde{\phi}} is determined by χpj​qj𝔽j\chi_{p_{j}q_{j}}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{j}} and χp1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′𝕏\chi_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} in the canonical way.
(4)
χp1⋯pm;p′𝕏\chi_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} respects the structural map of the multimodule about concatenation from the positive side. More precisely, if ϕ~∈B~p1⋯pm;q′p′𝕏\widetilde{\phi}\in\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}, then χϕ~\chi_{\widetilde{\phi}} is canonically determined by χp1⋯pm;q′𝕏\chi_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} and χq′​p′𝔽′\chi_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}.
(5)
χp1⋯pm;p′𝕏\chi_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} is collared. Namely, near each stratum, it is constant in collar coordinates.
(6)
χp1⋯pm;p′𝕏\chi_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} respects the rigidification.
(7)
The collection of functions are equivariant with respect to the action by Πm\Pi^{m}. Namely, if a1,…,am∈Πa_{1},\ldots,a_{m}\in\Pi and q1=a1​p1,…,qm=am​pmq_{1}=a_{1}p_{1},\ldots,q_{m}=a_{m}p_{m}, q′=(a1+⋯+am)​p′q^{\prime}=(a_{1}+\cdots+a_{m})p^{\prime}, with respect to the identification C~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏≅C~q1⋯qm;q′𝕏\widetilde{C}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\cong\widetilde{C}_{q_{1}\cdots q_{m};q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}, one has
χp1⋯pm;p′𝕏=χq1⋯qm;q′𝕏.\chi_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}=\chi_{q_{1}\cdots q_{m};q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}.
Now similar to the flow category case, for each x~=(ϕ~,u~,e,F)∈V~p1⋯pm;p′\widetilde{x}=(\widetilde{\phi},\widetilde{u},e,F)\in\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}, there are a pair of Banach spaces
ℰx~1,\displaystyle\ {\mathcal{E}}_{\widetilde{x}}^{1},\
ℰx~0\displaystyle\ {\mathcal{E}}_{\widetilde{x}}^{0}
which form equivariant “vector bundles”
ℰp1⋯pm;p′1,\displaystyle\ {\mathcal{E}}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{1},\
ℰp1⋯pm;p′0.\displaystyle\ {\mathcal{E}}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{0}.
The cut-off functions also induce a family of Cauchy–Riemann operators

Before we state the definition of index bundle interpolators for the multimodule case, we specify certain boundary strata of V~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}. For j=1,…,mj=1,\ldots,m, there is a corresponding codimension 1 stratum

corresponding to configurations where the jj-th marked point goes to the very left of the underlying curve. There is also a positive end

∂−V~p1⋯pm;p′:=⋂j=1m∂jV~p1⋯pm;p′≅Vp1⋯pm;p′.\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}:=\bigcap_{j=1}^{m}\partial^{j}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\cong V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}.
We consider the compactly supported version of ℰp1⋯pm;p′0{\mathcal{E}}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{0}, which is denoted by

We give the analogue of Definition 16.8.

Lemma 16.13.
Given index bundle interpolators for 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m;𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}, there exists an index bundle interpolator for 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}}.
Proof.
Induction.
∎
Then we obtain a family of continuous real Gp1⋯pm;p′𝕏G_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}-equivariant vector bundles
I~p1⋯pm;p′→V~p1⋯pm;p′\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\to\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}
whose fiber over x~\widetilde{x} is the kernel of the operator
ν~p1⋯pm;p′𝕏⊕Dx~.\widetilde{\nu}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\oplus D_{\widetilde{x}}.
We examine its restrictions to specific lower strata. By one of the conditions of Definition 16.12, one has
I~p1⋯pm;p′|∂−V~p1⋯pm;p′≅⨁j=1mR¯pj−⊕W¯p1⋯pm;p′𝕏⊕R¯p′+⊕TvtVp1⋯pm;p′\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}}\cong\bigoplus_{j=1}^{m}\underline{\smash{R}}_{p_{j}}^{-}\oplus\underline{\smash{W}}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{p^{\prime}}^{+}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}
which is a stabilization of the original vertical tangent bundle. On the other hand,
I~p1⋯pm;p′|∂+V~p1⋯pm;p′≅⨁j=1mR¯pj+⊕Ip1⋯pm;p′ℂ⊕R¯p′−\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}}\cong\bigoplus_{j=1}^{m}\underline{\smash{R}}_{p_{j}}^{+}\oplus I_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{C}}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{p^{\prime}}^{-}
where Ip1⋯pm;p′ℂI_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{C}} is fiberwise the kernel of the complex-linear operator
νx~⊕Duℂ.\nu_{\widetilde{x}}\oplus D_{u}^{\mathbb{C}}.
Since both the negative and positive inclusions
Vp1⋯pm;p′≅∂±V~p1⋯pm;p′→V~p1⋯pm;p′V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\cong\partial^{\pm}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\to\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}
are equivariant homotopy equivalences, the above two restriction bundles are isomorphic. One needs to choose a compatible system of isomorphisms in order to obtain a relative normal complex structure on the Kuranishi multimodule.
We consider certain codimension 1 strata of the thickenings.
(1)
Suppose pj<qjp_{j}<q_{j} in 𝔽j{\mathbb{F}}_{j}. Then there is a corresponding relative space V~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′→B~pj​qj⊠B~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\to\widetilde{B}_{p_{j}q_{j}}\boxtimes\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}. Notice that there are further lower strata of the form
∂−V~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′≅∂−V~pj​qj×∂−V~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\cong\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{j}q_{j}}\times\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}
corresponding to where the jj-th marked point is on the very left,
∂+V~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′≅∂+V~pj​qj×∂+V~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\cong\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{j}q_{j}}\times\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}
where all the marked points are on the very right. Notice that here we have the usual direct product but not ⊠\boxtimes. There is also an intermediate strata
∂0V~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′≅∂+V~pj​qj×∂−V~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′\partial^{0}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}\cong\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{j}q_{j}}\times\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}
corresponding to configurations where the jj-th marked point is at the breaking at qjq_{j} and all other marked points are on the very left. Notice that all these strata are isomorphic with Vp1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}. Notice that, the bundle I~p1⋯pm;p′\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}, when restricted to V~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}, contains a subbudnle I~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}} coming from the index bundle interpolators, whose restrictions to the above three strata are canonically identified with
I~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′|∂−V~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′≅I~pj​qj|∂−V~pj​qj⊕I~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′|∂−V~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′,\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}}\\
\cong\widetilde{I}_{p_{j}q_{j}}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{j}q_{j}}}\oplus\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}},
I~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′|∂0V~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′≅I~pj​qj|∂+V~pj​qj⊕I~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′|∂−V~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′,\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}|_{\partial^{0}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}}\\
\cong\widetilde{I}_{p_{j}q_{j}}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{j}q_{j}}}\oplus\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}|_{\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}},
and
I~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′|∂+V~p1⋯pj−1(pjqj)pj+1⋯pm;p′≅I~pj​qj|∂+V~pj​qj⊕I~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′|∂+V~p1⋯pj−1qjpj+1⋯pm;p′.\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}(p_{j}q_{j})p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}}\\
\cong\widetilde{I}_{p_{j}q_{j}}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{j}q_{j}}}\oplus\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}|_{\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{j-1}q_{j}p_{j+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}}.
(2)
Suppose q′<p′q^{\prime}<p^{\prime} in 𝔽′{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}. Then there is a corresponding relative space V~p1⋯pm;q′p′→B~p1⋯pm;q′⊠B~q′​p′\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}\to\widetilde{B}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}}\boxtimes\widetilde{B}_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}. The three further lower strata are
∂−V~p1⋯pm;q′p′≅∂−V~p1⋯pm;q′×∂−V~q′​p′,∂0V~p1⋯pm;q′p′≅∂+V~p1⋯pm;q′×∂−V~q′​p′,∂+V~p1⋯pm;q′p′≅∂+V~p1⋯pm;q′×∂+V~q′​p′.\begin{split}\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}\cong&\ \partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}}\times\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime}},\\
\partial^{0}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}\cong&\ \partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}}\times\partial^{-}\widetilde{V}_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime}},\\
\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}\cong&\ \partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}}\times\partial^{+}\widetilde{V}_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}.\end{split}
The extended index bundle I~p1⋯pm;p′\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}, when restricted to then, has the subbundle I~p1⋯pm;q′p′\widetilde{I}_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}p^{\prime}} and is identified respectively as

16.5. Orientations
We explain how to obtain coherent orientations on the AMS construction. We give orientations on the tangent bundles of the domain moduli spaces as well as the vertical tangent bundles. After the stable smoothing to be done in the next section, they induce coherent orientations on the AMS lifts.
We first look at the operator DpD_{p} given by (16.1). Its Fredholm index is congruent (mod 22) to the cohomological degree of the periodic orbit pp, denoted by |p||p|. Let detDp\det D_{p} be its real determinant line.
Consider the flow category case. For each pair of objects p,qp,q, one can use the 1-parameter family of operators (16.3) to obtain an interpolation; in particular an isomorphism between determinant lines
detDp⊗detDu≅det(Duℂ⊕Dq)≅detDq.\det D_{p}\otimes\det D_{u}\cong\det(D_{u}^{\mathbb{C}}\oplus D_{q})\cong\det D_{q}.
The last isomorphism comes from the fact that DuℂD_{u}^{\mathbb{C}} is complex. We may regard the orientation of the moduli space as the family of isomorphismss on the determinant lines
detDu:detDp→detDq.\det D_{u}:\det D_{p}\to\det D_{q}.
In terms of the AMS lift, this means one obtains a family of isomorphisms (well-defined up to homotopy)
σp​q:detDp→detDq\sigma_{pq}:\det D_{p}\to\det D_{q}
over the thickened moduli Vp​qV_{pq}. The construction implies
σr​q∘σp​r=σp​q.\sigma_{rq}\circ\sigma_{pr}=\sigma_{pq}.
The case with multimodules and homotopies are essentially the same. For a Floer multimodule 𝕏{\mathbb{X}}, using the interpolation constructed before, one obtains a family of isomorphisms
σp1⋯pm;p′𝕏:⨂i=1mdetDpi→detDp′.\sigma_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}:\bigotimes_{i=1}^{m}\det D_{p_{i}}\to\det D_{p^{\prime}}.
By considering indices, one has that
σp1⋯pm;p′𝕏=(−1)(∑j<i|pj|)​(|pi|−|qi|)σp1⋯pi−1qipi+1⋯pm;p′𝕏∘σpi​qi𝔽i\sigma_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}=(-1)^{(\sum_{j<i}|p_{j}|)(|p_{i}|-|q_{i}|)}\sigma_{p_{1}\cdots p_{i-1}q_{i}p_{i+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\circ\sigma_{p_{i}q_{i}}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{i}}
and
σp1⋯pm;p′𝕏=σq′​p′𝔽′∘σp1⋯pm;q′𝕏.\sigma_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}=\sigma_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}\circ\sigma_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}.
The case of homotopy is similar and we omit it.
17. Stable Smoothings
We proceed with the last step of constructing the AMS lifts. The original argument of such abstract smoothing of moduli spaces was contained in [3]. The inductive argument in the setting of Floer theories was first systematically discussed in [14].
17.1. Main results about stable smoothings
In the construction we will frequently stabilize thickened moduli spaces obtained in the AMS construction. To simplify the discussion, we always stabilize by trivial complex vector bundles. We make the following formal definition.
Definition 17.1.
The category 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯+\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}^{+} has objects being (K,R)(K,R) where K=(G,V,E,S)K=(G,V,E,S) is a Kuranishi space and RR is a finite-dimensional unitary complex representation of GG. A strict embedding from (K1,R1)(K_{1},R_{1}) to (K2,R2)(K_{2},R_{2}) consists of a strict embedding of Kuranishi spaces ι21:K1→K2\iota_{21}:K_{1}\to K_{2} and an ι21G\iota_{21}^{G}-equivariant isometric linear embedding ι21R:R1→R2\iota_{21}^{R}:R_{1}\to R_{2}. Morphisms of 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯+\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}^{+} are unitary conjugacy classes of strict embeddings.
Similarly, one can consider the collared and rigidified versions. Then there are two natural functors from 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯+\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}^{+} to 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}: the first is to forget the representation RR; the other is to take the stabilization by RR. What we would consider is the version
⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig+{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{+}
for collared, rigidified, relatively smooth Kuranishi spaces.
Definition 17.2.
A stabilizer of a flow category/multimodule/homotopy enriched in 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}} is a lift to 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯+\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}^{+}.
Remark 17.3.
In the AMS construction, a stabilizer can be viewed as adding trivial pieces to the thickening data.
Notice that there are two natural functors from ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig+{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{+} to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}. The first is to forget the stabilizer. The second is to stabilize each Kuranishi space by the corresponding trivial vector bundle via the vertical stabilization (see Definition 15.27). We often freely switch between the stabilizer, which is a system of representations, and the corresponding vertical stabilization, viewed as total space of the corresponding product equivariant vector bundles.
Definition 17.4.
A smoothing of a flow category/multimodule/homotopy enriched in ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig} is a lift to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}. A stable smoothing of a flow category/multimodule/homotopy enriched in ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig} consists of a lift to ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig+{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{+} and a smoothing of the corresponding stabilization.
Theorem 17.5.
(Stable Smoothing Theorem)
(1)
In Situation Flow(i), suppose 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} is a relatively smooth AMS lift of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} subject to a certain outercollaring width. Then there exists a stable smoothing of 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}}. In other words, there exists a vertical stabilization 𝔽^+\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{+} and a smoothing of 𝔽^+\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{+}. We still denote the flow category enriched in ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig} by 𝔽^+\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{+} and call it an AMS stable smoothing of 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}}.
(2)
In Situation Module(i), suppose 𝔽^1,⋯,𝔽^m;𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\cdots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} are relatively smooth AMS lifts and 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} is a relatively smooth AMS lift as a multimodule over (𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^′)(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}). Suppose 𝔽^1+,…,𝔽^m+,𝔽^′+\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{+},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}^{+},\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}{}^{+} are AMS stable smoothings of 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m},\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} respectively. Then there exists a class of stable smoothings of 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} as multimodules over (𝔽^1+,…,𝔽^m+;𝔽^′)+(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{+},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}^{+};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}{}^{+}). These stable smoothings are called AMS stable smoothings of 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}}.
(3)
In Situation Homotopy(iii), let 𝔽^1+,⋯,𝔽^m+,𝔽^′+\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{+},\cdots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}^{+},\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}{}^{+} be AMS stable smoothings of the relatively smooth AMS lifts 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m},\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}. Let 𝕏^0+\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0}^{+} resp. 𝕏^1+\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{+} be AMS stable smoothings of 𝕏^0\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0} resp. 𝕏^1\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1} as multimodules over (𝔽^1+,…,𝔽^m+;𝔽^′)+(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{+},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}^{+};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}{}^{+}). Then the relatively smooth AMS lift ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} has a class of stable smoothings as a homotopy from 𝕏^0+\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0}^{+} to 𝕏^1+\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{+}. Such stable smoothings are called AMS stable smoothings of ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}}.
17.2. Preliminaries
17.2.1. Microbundles
Recall that a microbundle of rank kk over a topological space MM, denoted by ℱ{\mathscr{F}}, is a topological space ℱ{\mathscr{F}} together with two structural maps p:ℱ→Mp:{\mathscr{F}}\to M, i:M→ℱi:M\to{\mathscr{F}} such that p∘i=IdMp\circ i={\rm Id}_{M} and such that near the image of ii, locally ℱ{\mathscr{F}} is an ℝk{\mathbb{R}}^{k}-bundle. Any real vector bundle F→MF\to M together with the bundle projection and the zero section induces a microbundle FμF_{\mu}. If MM is a topological manifold, then its tangent microbundle 𝒯μ​M{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}M has the total space M×MM\times M with pp the projection onto the first factor and ii the diagonal embedding of MM.
A morphism of microbundles over MM from ℱ{\mathscr{F}} to ℱ′{\mathscr{F}}^{\prime} is a germ of continuous maps from a neighborhood of i⁡(M)⊆ℱi(M)\subseteq{\mathscr{F}} to ℱ′{\mathscr{F}}^{\prime} which commutes with the structural maps. A morphism is called an isomorphism if it can be represented by a homeomorphism. An isotopy of microbundle isomorphisms from ϕ0:ℱ→ℱ′\phi_{0}:{\mathscr{F}}\to{\mathscr{F}}^{\prime} to ϕ1:ℱ→ℱ′\phi_{1}:{\mathscr{F}}\to{\mathscr{F}}^{\prime} is a microbundle isomorphism from ℱ~→ℱ~′\tilde{\mathscr{F}}\to\tilde{\mathscr{F}}^{\prime} over M×[0,1]M\times[0,1] whose restriction to M×{i}M\times\{i\} coincides with ϕi\phi_{i} (as germs) for i=0,1i=0,1.
In particular, a vector bundle reduction of a microbundle ℱ→M{\mathscr{F}}\to M consists of a vector bundle F→MF\to M and a microbundle isomorphism Fμ→ℱF_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{F}}. When a topological manifold MM is equipped with a smooth structure, denoted by MαM_{\alpha}, then there is a vector bundle reduction (T​Mα)μ→𝒯μ​M(TM_{\alpha})_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}M: a concrete choice could be the exponential map associated to a Riemannian metric. The isotopy class of such a vector bundle reduction is canonical. Hence it is a necessary condition for a topological manifold to admit a smooth structure that its tangent microbundle admits a vector bundle reduction.
All the above notions admit equivariant extensions with respect to actions by compact Lie groups. In particular, when a topological GG-manifold MM is equipped with a smooth structure MαM_{\alpha} such that the GG-action is smooth, then there is a well-defined isotopy class of GG-equivariant vector bundle reduction (T​Mα)μ→𝒯μ​M(TM_{\alpha})_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}M.
Remark 17.6.
We need the notion of smooth microbundles over smooth manifolds. These are microbundles whose total spaces and structural maps are all in the C∞C^{\infty} category. One can also define smooth microbundle maps and smooth vector bundle reductions. Equivariant versions can be formulated as well. For example, when MM is already a smooth manifold, the tangent microbundle is smooth and any vector bundle reduction of 𝒯μ​M{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}M using a smooth Riemannian metric is smooth.
17.2.2. Stable GG-smoothings
Now we recall notions about equivariant smoothings. Let MM be a topological manifold with an action by a compact Lie group GG. A GG-smoothing of MM is a smooth structure α\alpha on MM such that the GG-action is smooth. Two GG-smoothings α0\alpha_{0} and α1\alpha_{1} are called equivalent if the identity map Mα0→Mα1M_{\alpha_{0}}\to M_{\alpha_{1}} is a diffeomorphism; they are called isotopic if the identity map is homotopic through GG-equivariant homeomorphisms to a diffeomorphism. More generally, a stable GG-smoothing of MM consists of an orthogonal GG-representation RR and a GG-smoothing on M×RM\times R. Notice that given any stable GG-smoothing (M×R)α(M\times R)_{\alpha} and any other orthogonal GG-representation R′R^{\prime}, the product smooth structure (M×R)α×R′(M\times R)_{\alpha}\times R^{\prime} gives another stable GG-smoothing. Two stable GG-smoothings (M×R1)α1(M\times R_{1})_{\alpha_{1}} and (M×R2)α2(M\times R_{2})_{\alpha_{2}} are stably isotopic if there exist orthogonal GG-representations R1′,R2′R_{1}^{\prime},R_{2}^{\prime} such that R1⊕R1′≅R2⊕R2′R_{1}\oplus R_{1}^{\prime}\cong R_{2}\oplus R_{2}^{\prime} as orthogonal GG-representations and such that the two GG-smoothings (M×R1)α1×R1′(M\times R_{1})_{\alpha_{1}}\times R_{1}^{\prime} and (M×R2)α2×R2′(M\times R_{2})_{\alpha_{2}}\times R_{2}^{\prime} on M×R1×R1′=M×R2×R2′M\times R_{1}\times R_{1}^{\prime}=M\times R_{2}\times R_{2}^{\prime} are isotopic.
Notice that given a GG-smoothing MαM_{\alpha} on MM, there is an induced isotopy class of GG-equivariant vector bundle reductions (T​Mα)μ→𝒯μ​M(TM_{\alpha})_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}M. In view of stable smoothings, one also need to define the notion of stable isotopy of stable vector bundle reductions.
Definition 17.7.
[38, Page 300]
Let ℱ→M{\mathscr{F}}\to M be a GG-microbundle. A stable GG-vector bundle reduction of ℱ{\mathscr{F}} consists of a GG-vector bundle FF and an orthogonal GG-representation RR together with a GG-microbundle isomorphism
ϕ:Fμ→ℱ⊕R¯μ.\phi:F_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{F}}\oplus\underline{\smash{R}}_{\mu}.
Two stable GG-vector bundle reductions ϕi:(Fi)μ→ℱ⊕(R¯i)μ\phi_{i}:(F_{i})_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{F}}\oplus(\underline{\smash{R}}_{i})_{\mu}, i=0,1i=0,1, are called stably isotopic if there exist orthogonal GG-representations R0′,R1′R_{0}^{\prime},R_{1}^{\prime} such that R0⊕R0′≅R1⊕R1′R_{0}\oplus R_{0}^{\prime}\cong R_{1}\oplus R_{1}^{\prime} and the stabilizations ϕ0⊕IdR¯0′\phi_{0}\oplus{\rm Id}_{\underline{\smash{R}}_{0}^{\prime}} and ϕ1⊕IdR¯1′\phi_{1}\oplus{\rm Id}_{\underline{\smash{R}}_{1}^{\prime}} are isotopic vector bundle reductions of ℱ⊕(R¯0)μ⊕(R¯0′)μ≅ℱ⊕(R¯1)μ⊕(R¯1′)μ{\mathscr{F}}\oplus(\underline{\smash{R}}_{0})_{\mu}\oplus(\underline{\smash{R}}_{0}^{\prime})_{\mu}\cong{\mathscr{F}}\oplus(\underline{\smash{R}}_{1})_{\mu}\oplus(\underline{\smash{R}}_{1}^{\prime})_{\mu}.
Remark 17.8.
In the above discussions, we can replace “orthogonal representations” by “unitary representations” to suit our purpose. Any orthogonal representation can be stabilized to a unitary representation.
Now given any stable GG-smoothing (M×R)α(M\times R)_{\alpha} of MM, there is an isotopy class of GG-vector bundle reductions T​(M×R)α→𝒯μ​(M×R)T(M\times R)_{\alpha}\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}(M\times R). The restriction of this reduction to M×{0}M\times\{0\} gives a stable isotopy class of GG-vector bundle reductions of 𝒯μ​M{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}M. Lashof’s theorem says that this association has an inverse.
Theorem 17.9.
[38] Let MM be a topological GG-manifold with finitely many orbit types. Then the above map which sends each stable isotopy class of stable GG-smoothings to a stable isotopy class of GG-vector bundle reductions of 𝒯μ​M{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}M is invertible. In particular, if 𝒯μ​M{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}M admits a GG-vector bundle reduction, then MM admits a stable GG-smoothing.
17.2.3. Micro-connections
Let π:V→B\pi:V\to B be a GG-equivariant relatively smooth manifold such that BB is a smooth GG-manifold. Then there is a well-defined GG-microbundle over VV:
π∗​𝒯μ​B⊕𝒯μvt​V.\pi^{*}{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}B\oplus{\mathscr{T}}^{\rm vt}_{\mu}V.
To facilitate the stable smoothing of VV, we need to identify the above microbundle with the tangent microbundle of VV. Notice that there are natural microbundle maps
𝒯μvt​V→𝒯μ​V→π∗​𝒯μ​B.{\mathscr{T}}^{\rm vt}_{\mu}V\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}V\to\pi^{*}{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}B.
Hence such an identification can be regarded as a microbundle version of connections.
Definition 17.10.
Let V/BV/B be a GG-equivariant topological submersion. A micro-connection is a GG-equivariant microbundle map ∇μ:𝒯μ​V→𝒯μvt​V\nabla_{\mu}:{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}V\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}^{\rm vt}V satisfying
(1)
The restriction of ∇μ\nabla^{\mu} to 𝒯μvt​V{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}^{\rm vt}V is the identity map.
(2)
∇μ\nabla_{\mu} is represented by a germ of the map ϕ:Δ+​(V)→V\phi:\Delta^{+}(V)\to V such that for any (b,b′)∈(π×π)​(Δ+​(V))⊆B×B(b,b^{\prime})\in(\pi\times\pi)(\Delta^{+}(V))\subseteq B\times B and p∈π−1​(b)⊆Vp\in\pi^{-1}(b)\subseteq V, the restriction of ϕ\phi to Δ+​(V)∩({p}×π−1​(b′))\Delta^{+}(V)\cap(\{p\}\times\pi^{-1}(b^{\prime})) is a homeomorphism onto an open neighborhood of (p,p)(p,p) in OPEN{p}×π−1​(b))\{p\}\times\pi^{-1}(b)).
Notice that a micro-connection induces a microbundle isomorphism 𝒯μ​M≅π∗​𝒯μ​B⊕𝒯μvt​M{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}M\cong\pi^{*}{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}B\oplus{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}^{\rm vt}M.
Lemma 17.11.
Let C⊆VC\subseteq V be a GG-invariant closed subset and U⊆VU\subseteq V be a GG-invariant open neighborhood of CC. Let D⊆VD\subseteq V be another GG-invariant closed set. Suppose ∇μ:𝒯μ​U→𝒯μvt​U\nabla_{\mu}:{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}U\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}^{\rm vt}U is a GG-invariant micro-connection. Then there exists a GG-invariant open neighborhood WW of C∪DC\cup D and a GG-invariant micro-connection ∇μ′:𝒯μ​W→𝒯μvt​W\nabla_{\mu}^{\prime}:{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}W\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}^{\rm vt}W which coincides with ∇μ\nabla_{\mu} near CC.
Proof.
This is a restatement of the extension lemma [3, Lemma 4.24] and a relative version of [3, Proposition 4.25].
∎
17.3. Pre-smoothed relatively smooth Kuranishi spaces
To describe the structures one needs to perform the stable smoothing, we enhance the category of relatively smooth Kuranishi spaces to include various specific add-ons.
Definition 17.12.
Let K=(G,V/B,E,S)K=(G,V/B,E,S) be an object of ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
(1)
A pre-smoothing on KK consists of
(a)
A GG-invariant Riemannian metric gT​Bg^{TB} on BB and a GG-invariant metric hTvt​Vh^{T^{\rm vt}V} on Tvt​VT^{\rm vt}V.
(b)
A micro-connection ∇μ\nabla_{\mu} on V/BV/B.
(2)
A pre-smoothing is called collared if for each stratum Vα/BαV_{\alpha}/B_{\alpha}, the following holds.
(a)
Near BαB_{\alpha}, gT​Bg^{TB} is the product of gT​Bαg^{TB_{\alpha}} and the standard metric on the collar.
(b)
Near VαV_{\alpha}, hTvt​Vh^{T^{\rm vt}V} is constant in collar coordinates.
(c)
Near VαV_{\alpha}, ∇μ\nabla_{\mu} factors as
𝒯μ​V\textstyle{{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}V\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}𝒯μ​Vα\textstyle{{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}V_{\alpha}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}𝒯μvt​Vα\textstyle{{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}^{\rm vt}V_{\alpha}}
where the first arrow is induced from the collar structure and the second arrow is the restriction of the micro-connection on the stratum Vα/BαV_{\alpha}/B_{\alpha}.
(3)
A pre-smoothed Kuranishi space is a relatively smooth Kuranishi space equipped with a pre-smoothing.
(4)
A stabilization of a pre-smoothed Kuranishi space KK by a trivial GG-equivariant disk bundle D=Dhor⊕DvtD=D^{\rm hor}\oplus D^{\rm vt} is the stabilized Kuranishi space StabD​K{\rm Stab}_{D}K together with the naturally induced pre-smoothing (where DhorD^{\rm hor} and DvtD^{\rm vt} are equipped with linear metrics).
(5)
A rigidified strict embedding of pre-smoothed Kuranishi spaces from K1K_{1} to K2K_{2} consists of a rigidified strict embedding ι21:K1→K2\iota_{21}:K_{1}\to K_{2} (with normal disk bundle D21=D21hor⊕D21vtD_{21}=D_{21}^{\rm hor}\oplus D_{21}^{\rm vt} equipped with the direct sum of linear metrics) such that the induced germ of strict open embedding preserves the pre-smoothings.
(6)
A rigidified embedding is a unitary conjugacy class of rigidified strict embeddings. Let ⌊𝐒pre​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm pre}Kur}}_{\rm rig} be the regular stratification category whose objects are collared, pre-smoothed Kuranishi spaces and whose morphisms are rigidified embeddings. There is an obvious forgetful functor
⌊𝐒pre​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig→⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig.{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm pre}Kur}}_{\rm rig}\to{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
(7)
A pre-smoothing of a flow category/multimodule/homotopy enriched in ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig} is a lift to ⌊𝐒pre​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm pre}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
Lemma 17.13.
(1)
In Situation Flow(iii), the relatively smooth AMS lift 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} admits a pre-smoothing.
(2)
In Situation Module(iii), suppose the AMS lifts 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m;𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} of the involved Floer flow categories are equipped with pre-smoothings, then 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} admits a pre-smoothing as a multimodule enriched in ⌊𝐒pre​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm pre}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
(3)
In Situation Homotopy(iii), suppose the AMS lifts 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^′,𝕏^0,𝕏^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m},\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime},\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0},\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1} are equipped with pre-smoothings so 𝕏^0\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0} and 𝕏^1\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1} are multimodules over the tuple of pre-smoothed flow categories, then ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} admits a pre-smoothing as a homotopy enriched in ⌊𝐒pre​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm pre}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
Proof.
The collared and rigidified structure of the relatively smooth AMS lifts allows us to choose invariant horizontal and vertical Riemannian metrics inductively. On the other hand, Lemma 17.11 allows us to inductively construct micro-connections.
∎
Once one obtains a pre-smoothed Kuranishi space K=(G,V/B,E,S)K=(G,V/B,E,S), one obtains a GG-vector bundle reduction of the tangent microbundle. More precisely, the exponential map of gT​Bg^{TB} induces a reduction
(T​B)μ→𝒯μ​B.(TB)_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}B.
The vertical exponential map of hTvt​Vh^{T^{\rm vt}V} induces a reduction
(Tvt​V)μ→𝒯μvt​V.(T^{\rm vt}V)_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}^{\rm vt}V.
Together with the micro-connection, one obtains
(π∗​T​B⊕Tvt​V)μ→𝒯μ​V.(\pi^{*}TB\oplus T^{\rm vt}V)_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}V.
Notice that such GG-vector bundle reductions are compatible with morphisms of ⌊𝐒pre​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm pre}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
17.3.1. Post-smoothed Kuranishi spaces
Definition 17.12 ensures the existence of coherent vector bundle lifts. The next definition is designed to make the stabizers explicit in order to carry out the inductive smoothing construction.
Definition 17.14.
Let K=(G,V/B,E,S)K=(G,V/B,E,S) be an object of ⌊𝐒pre​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm pre}Kur}}_{\rm rig}. A post-smoothing on KK consists of a GG-smoothing of VV, a collared smooth GG-invariant vector bundle reduction
exp:(T​V)μ→𝒯μ​V,\exp:(TV)_{\mu}\to{\mathscr{T}}_{\mu}V,
and a collared GG-equivariant vector bundle isomorphism
T​V≅π∗​T​B⊕Tvt​VTV\cong\pi^{*}TB\oplus T^{\rm vt}V
such that exp\exp and the GG-vector bundle reduction induced from the pre-smoothing are in the same stable GG-isotopy class on the interior of each stratum.
Now we state the results about constructing stable smoothings. Since we need to constantly stabilize charts, we would like to use the convenient system of unitary representations of Gd≅U⁡(d)G_{d}\cong U(d) specified by Proposition 15.23.
Lemma 17.15.
(1)
In Situation Flow(iii), let 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} be a pre-smoothed AMS lift of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} provided by Lemma 17.13. Then there exists a stabilization 𝔽^+\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{+} and a post-smoothing of 𝔽^+\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{+}. Each such flow category is called a post-smoothed AMS lift of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}.
(2)
In Situation Module(iii), let 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m;𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} be pre-smoothed AMS lifts of the involved Floer flow categories. Let 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} be a pre-smoothed AMS lift of the multimodule 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} provided by Lemma 17.13. Suppose 𝔽^1+,…,𝔽^m+;𝔽^′+\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{+},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}^{+};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}{}^{+} are post-smoothings of 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m;𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}. Then there exists a stabilization 𝕏^+\hat{\mathbb{X}}^{+} of 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} and a post-smoothing of it as a multimodule over (𝔽^1+,…,𝔽^m+;𝔽^′)+(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{+},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}^{+};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}{}^{+}).
(3)
In Situation Homotopy(iii), let 𝔽^1+,…,𝔽^m+;𝔽^′+\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{+},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}^{+};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}{}^{+} be post-smoothed AMS lifts of the involved flow categories and 𝕏^0+\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0}^{+}, 𝕏^1+\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{+} be post-smoothed AMS lifts of the two multimodules 𝕏0{\mathbb{X}}_{0} and 𝕏1{\mathbb{X}}_{1}. Let ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} be a pre-smoothed AMS lift of the homotopy provided by Lemma 17.13. Then there exists a stabilization ℍ^+\hat{\mathbb{H}}^{+} of ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} and a post-smoothing of it as a homotopy from 𝕏^0+\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0}^{+} to 𝕏^1+\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{+}.
Proof.
Again, it suffices to demonstrate the argument in the case of flow categories. Recall the system of unitary representations Wd,μW_{d,\mu}. For each pair p<qp<q, denote Wp​q,μ:=Wdp​q,μW_{pq,\mu}:=W_{d_{pq},\mu} where dp​qd_{pq} is the integer specified via the choice of integral action. Notice that once we choose a system of positive integers μp​q\mu_{pq} satisfying
μp​q>max{μp​r,μr​q|p<r<q}\mu_{pq}>\max\{\mu_{pr},\mu_{rq}\ |\ p<r<q\}
(17.1)
then one obtains a stabilization 𝔽^+\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{+} with each chart Kp​qK_{pq} vertically stabilized by Wp​q,μp​qW_{pq,\mu_{pq}}. The main claim is that one can choose such a stabilizer together with a post-smoothing of 𝔽^+\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{+} satisfying the condition on stable isotopy classes of GG-vector bundle reductions.
We construct μp​q\mu_{pq} and the post-smoothing inductively. For the base case when Vp​qV_{pq} has no boundary strata, the existence of Wp​q,μp​qW_{pq,\mu_{pq}} and the post-smoothing is a consequence of Lashof’s theorem (Theorem 17.9), since every finite-dimensional representation of Gp​qG_{pq} is contained in a certain Wp​q,μW_{pq,\mu} for μ\mu sufficiently large. Choose such μp​q\mu_{pq} and denote Vp​q+=Vp​q×Wp​q,μp​qV_{pq}^{+}=V_{pq}\times W_{pq,\mu_{pq}}. Then we can choose a smooth Gp​qG_{pq}-invariant Riemannian metric on Vp​q+V_{pq}^{+} and obtain the exponential map expp​q\exp_{pq} as a smooth vector bundle reduction of the tangent microbundle.
Now we state the induction hypothesis. Given p<qp<q, suppose we have chosen μr​s\mu_{rs} for all r,sr,s satisfying dr​s<dp​qd_{rs}<d_{pq} satisfying (17.1) and post-smoothings such that the induced embeddings of the smoothed Kuranishi spaces are morphisms of ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}. 2525
25
This claim is a purpose of using rigidified embeddings: the trivialized normal bundle induces a canonical smoothing in the tubular neighborhood of the embedding. If we do not require the normal bundle to be trivialized, then one needs to make the painful choices of smooth bundle structures.
Now we can construct the stable smoothing on Vp​qV_{pq}. Choose μp​q′\mu_{pq}^{\prime} sufficiently large such that the already stabilized boundary strata can all be included into Vp​q×Wp​q,μp​q′V_{pq}\times W_{pq,\mu_{pq}^{\prime}}. On the other hand, the interior Int​Vp​q{\rm Int}V_{pq} can be stably smoothed by Theorem 17.9, meaning that one can choose μp​q′′\mu_{pq}^{\prime\prime} sufficiently large and a smoothing of Int​Vp​q×Wp​q,μp​q′′{\rm Int}V_{pq}\times W_{pq,\mu_{pq}^{\prime\prime}}. By choosing μp​q\mu_{pq} greater than both μp​q′\mu_{pq}^{\prime} and μp​q′′\mu_{pq}^{\prime\prime}, one can assume μp​q′=μp​q′′\mu_{pq}^{\prime}=\mu_{pq}^{\prime\prime}. Notice that the induction hypothesis implies a canonically induced smoothing near the boundary. On overlaps, these two smoothings induce the same stable GG-isotopy class of microbundle reductions. Hence by the relative smoothing result proved in [14, Appendix B], one can interpolate the two smoothings in the collar region, possibly after a further enlargement of μp​q\mu_{pq}, so that near the boundary the smoothing is still the one canonically induced from other already-stabilized charts. Therefore, one obtains a stabilization by Wp​q,μp​qW_{pq,\mu_{pq}}, a smoothing of this stabilization, so that all the chart embeddings are morphisms of ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}. Further, we choose the smooth vector bundle reduction on the stabilized chart Vp​q×Wp​q,μp​qV_{pq}\times W_{pq,\mu_{pq}}.
∎
17.4. Normally complex AMS lifts
Finally we are at the last step of proving Theorem O and counterparts for Floer multimodules and homotopies.
Theorem 17.16.
(1)
In Situation Flow(iii), let 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} be a post-smoothed AMS lift of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}. Then 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}}, viewed as a lift in ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}, admits a class of lifts to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. Each of such lifts, denoted by 𝔽^^\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}} temporarily, is called an NC AMS lift of (either 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} or 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}}).
(2)
In Situation Module(i), let 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m},\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} be post-smoothed AMS lifts of involved Floer flow categories and let 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} be a post-smoothed AMS lift of the multimodule 𝕏{\mathbb{X}}. Suppose 𝔽^^1,…,𝔽^^m;𝔽^^′\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{m};\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}^{\prime} are NC AMS lifts of 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m;𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}. Then there exists a class of lifts of 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as multimodules over (𝔽^^1,…,𝔽^^m,𝔽^^′)(\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{m};\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}^{\prime}). Each of such lifts, denoted by 𝕏^^\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}} temporarily, is called an NC AMS lift of (either 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} or 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}}).
(3)
In Situation Homotopy(i), let 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^,𝕏^0,𝕏^1,ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m},\hat{\mathbb{F}},\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0},\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1},\hat{\mathbb{H}} be post-smoothed AMS lifts of the involved flow categories, multimodules, and homotopy. Suppose 𝔽^^1,…,𝔽^^m,𝔽^^′,𝕏^^0,𝕏^^1\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}_{m},\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{F}}}}^{\prime},\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}}_{0},\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}}_{1} be NC AMS lifts. Then there exists a lift of ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as a homotopy from 𝕏^^0\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}}_{0} to 𝕏^^1\hat{\vphantom{\rule{1.0pt}{5.71527pt}}\smash{\hat{\mathbb{X}}}}_{1}.
Proof.
Recall that the post-smoothing of a relatively smooth Kuranishi space K=(G,V/B,E,S)K=(G,V/B,E,S) still remembers the vector bundle π∗​T​B⊕Tvt​V\pi^{*}TB\oplus T^{\rm vt}V although the relative structure is destroyed. As the post-smoothing also includes the identification between this vector bundle and the smooth tangent bundle, we may assume T​VTV has the canonical splitting.
Now notice that Tvt​VT^{\rm vt}V is equipped with the GG-equivariant NC structure while T​BTB is equipped with the GG-equivariant stable complex structure. This does not yet provide an NC structure on T​VTV since T​VTV contains the subbundle of the infinitesimal GG-action. To obtain the NC structure, one needs to make the obstruction bundle complex first.
Recall that from the construction of the AMS lifts, the obstruction bundle is always trivial and decomposes as
E=W¯⊕Q¯E=\underline{\smash{W}}\oplus\underline{\smash{Q}}
where WW is a complex representation of GG and QQ is a real representation of GG. However, we observe that in all the Kuranishi spaces we obtained in the construction, the direct sum
𝔤⊕Q{\mathfrak{g}}\oplus Q
is naturally isomorphic to the Lie algebra of the complex Lie group 𝒢{\mathcal{G}}. Therefore, we can stabilize all charts by the Lie algebra. Denote by
K~:=Stab𝔤​(K)=(G,V~,E~,S~).\tilde{K}:={\rm Stab}_{\mathfrak{g}}(K)=(G,\tilde{V},\tilde{E},\tilde{S}).
In this way, the obstruction bundles of all involved Kuranishi spaces are equivariant complex vector bundles. Let
𝔤V~⊆T​V~{\mathfrak{g}}_{\tilde{V}}\subseteq T\tilde{V}
be the subbundle spanned by infinitesimal GG-actions. Then by Definition 3.24, it remains to construct GG-equivariant NC structures on the bundles T​V~/𝔤V~T\tilde{V}/{\mathfrak{g}}_{\tilde{V}}. Indeed, for each chart K~=(G,V~,E~,S~)\tilde{K}=(G,\tilde{V},\tilde{E},\tilde{S}) after the stabilization, let π:V~→V\pi:\tilde{V}\to V be the projection. Then one has
T​V~=π∗​T​V⊕𝔤¯T\tilde{V}=\pi^{*}TV\oplus\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}}
where the previous constructions provide T​VTV with NC structures. Therefore, it surfaces to define compatible equivariant bundle isomorphisms
π∗​T​V≅(π∗​T​V⊕𝔤¯)/𝔤V~.\pi^{*}TV\cong(\pi^{*}TV\oplus\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}})/{\mathfrak{g}}_{\tilde{V}}.
One chooses such isomorphisms in the following way. Choose a compatible system of GG-invariant metrics on VV inductively. Then one obtains an equivariant splitting
T​V≅𝔤V⊥⊕𝔤V.TV\cong{\mathfrak{g}}_{V}^{\bot}\oplus{\mathfrak{g}}_{V}.
Notice that 𝔤V{\mathfrak{g}}_{V} is isomorphic with the trivial bundle 𝔤¯\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}}. Then define
π∗​T​V≅π∗​(𝔤V⊥)⊕π∗​𝔤V→π∗​(T​V⊕𝔤¯)\pi^{*}TV\cong\pi^{*}({\mathfrak{g}}_{V}^{\bot})\oplus\pi^{*}{\mathfrak{g}}_{V}\to\pi^{*}(TV\oplus\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}})
by sending π∗​𝔤V\pi^{*}{\mathfrak{g}}_{V} into π∗​T​V\pi^{*}TV while sending π∗​𝔤V\pi^{*}{\mathfrak{g}}_{V} onto 𝔤¯\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}}. It is then easy to see that the composition
π∗​T​V→π∗​(T​V⊕𝔤¯)→π∗​(T​V⊕𝔤¯)/𝔤V~\pi^{*}TV\to\pi^{*}(TV\oplus\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}})\to\pi^{*}(TV\oplus\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}})/{\mathfrak{g}}_{\tilde{V}}
is an isomorphism. This equips the Kuranishi spaces GG-equivariant NC structures.
∎
17.5. Coherent orientations
For all involved flow categories and all objects p∈𝕆​b​𝔽p\in{\mathbb{O}b}{\mathbb{F}}, choose a trivialization of the determinant line detDp\det D_{p}. In last section, the isomorphism σp​q𝔽\sigma_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}} hence determines an orientation on the vertical tangent bundle Tvt​Vp​q𝔽T^{\rm vt}V_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}. Similarly, there are orientations on the vertical tangent bundle TvtVp1⋯pm;p′𝕏T^{\rm vt}V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} for a multimodule.
After stable smoothing, one has equivariant bundle isomorphisms
T​Vp​q≅πp​q∗​T​Bp​q⊕Tvt​Vp​q.TV_{pq}\cong\pi_{pq}^{*}TB_{pq}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{pq}.
Both summands have been given certain orientations. We then orient Vp​qV_{pq} using the above decomposition.
One can then verify the coherence requirement of Definition 7.12. Indeed, for p<r<qp<r<q, the isomorphism
(πp​r∗​T​Bp​r𝔽⊕Tvt​Vp​r𝔽)⊕(πr​q∗​T​Br​q𝔽⊕Tvt​Vr​q𝔽)→π∗​T​Bp​q𝔽⊕Tvt​Vp​q𝔽\Big(\pi_{pr}^{*}TB_{pr}^{\mathbb{F}}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{pr}^{\mathbb{F}}\Big)\oplus\Big(\pi_{rq}^{*}TB_{rq}^{\mathbb{F}}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{rq}^{\mathbb{F}}\Big)\to\pi^{*}TB_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}
is orientation preserving up to a sign
(−1)rank​Tvt​Vr​q=(−1)|p|−|r|(-1)^{{\rm rank}T^{\rm vt}V_{rq}}=(-1)^{|p|-|r|}
because Br​q𝔽B_{rq}^{\mathbb{F}} is odd-dimensional.
Suppose the AMS lifts of 𝔽1,…,𝔽m;𝔽′{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}}_{m};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} are oriented as above. W orient the multimodule 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} as follows. For each tuple (p1,…,pm,p′)(p_{1},\ldots,p_{m};p^{\prime}), orient the tangent bundle of the thickening Vp1⋯pm;p′𝕏V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}} via the direct sum decomposition
TVp1⋯pm;p′𝕏≅πp1⋯pm;p′∗TBp1⋯pm;p′𝔽⊕TvtVp1⋯pm;p′𝕏.TV_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\cong\pi_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{*}TB_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{F}}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}.
Notice that the domain moduli is even-dimensional. Then one can see that with respect to breakings, the isomorphism
TVpi​qi𝔽i⊕TVp1⋯pi−1qipi+1⋯pm;p′𝕏→TVp1⋯pm;p′𝕏TV_{p_{i}q_{i}}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{i}}\oplus TV_{p_{1}\cdots p_{i-1}q_{i}p_{i+1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\to TV_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}
has a sign (−1)(∑j<i|pi|)​(|pi|−|qi|)(-1)^{(\sum_{j<i}|p_{i}|)(|p_{i}|-|q_{i}|)} while the isomorphism
TVp1⋯pm;q′𝕏⊕TVq′​p′𝔽′≅TVp1⋯pm;p′𝕏TV_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}\oplus TV_{q^{\prime}p^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}\cong TV_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}
has a sign (−1)rankTvtVp1⋯pm;q′𝕏(-1)^{{\rm rank}T^{\rm vt}V_{p_{1}\cdots p_{m};q^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{X}}}.
18. Proofs of the Main Theorems on AMS Lifts
In this section we summarize the previous constructions as formal proofs of the main theorems about the AMS lifts for Floer flow categories, multimodules and homotopies to the category of (rigidified and collared) normally complex derived orbifolds ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}.
18.1. Proof of Theorem O
Assume we are in Situation Flow(i). The construction is illustrated and summarized in Figure 9. Each step of the roadmap is completed by a concrete theorem or proposition in previous sections. Upon taking the quotient orbifold, we obtain the proof of Theorem O except the orientation part.
Outercollaring width (Section 5.2)
Integral modification of energy 𝒜𝔽Ω:Ob​𝔽→ℤk{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\to{\mathbb{Z}}^{k} (Proposition 15.4)
Flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯ℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}^{\mathbb{C}} (Subsection 15.1.1)
Rigidification: lift to ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} (Proposition 14.17)
Flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝛀,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\bm{\Omega},{\mathbb{F}}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} and ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡Ω,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}^{\Omega,\mathbb{F}} enriched in ⌊𝐌𝐚𝐩¯frrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}_{\rm rig} (Proposition 15.8)

Figure 9. Roadmap of the AMS construction for Floer flow categories. Here the pink, rounded rectangles involve choices to be made and the orange rectangles are items canonically induced from previous steps.
Now we explain how to obtain a coherent orientation for the AMS lift. Given a pair of objects p,q∈Ob​𝔽p,q\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}, one needs to specify an orientation on the virtual vector bundle
T⁡(Vp​q/Gp​q)−Ep​q/Gp​q.T(V_{pq}/G_{pq})-E_{pq}/G_{pq}.
Recall that Ep​q=Wp​q⊕Qp​qE_{pq}=W_{pq}\oplus Q_{pq} where Wp​qW_{pq} comes from the thickening data and Qp​qQ_{pq} corresponds to 𝔤p​qℂ/𝔤p​q{\mathfrak{g}}_{pq}^{\mathbb{C}}/{\mathfrak{g}}_{pq}. As the thickening space Wp​qW_{pq} is complex, it can be neglected for orientation considerations. Moreover, if we stabilize the virtual vector bundle by 𝔤p​q{\mathfrak{g}}_{pq}, then as Qp​q⊕𝔤p​q≅𝔤ℂQ_{pq}\oplus{\mathfrak{g}}_{pq}\cong{\mathfrak{g}}^{\mathbb{C}} is complex and hence canonically oriented, it is equivalent to orient the vector bundle
T⁡(Vp​q/Gp​q)⊕𝔤¯p​q/Gp​qT(V_{pq}/G_{pq})\oplus\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}}_{pq}/G_{pq}
where 𝔤¯p​q→Vp​q\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}}_{pq}\to V_{pq} is the trivial bundle with fibres being 𝔤p​q{\mathfrak{g}}_{pq} and 𝔤¯p​q/Gp​q\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}}_{pq}/G_{pq} is the induced orbifold vector bundle.
On the other hand, the stable smoothing operation preserves the (C0C^{0}) isomorphism
T​Vp​q≅πp​q∗​T​Bp​q⊕Tvert​Vp​qTV_{pq}\cong\pi_{pq}^{*}TB_{pq}\oplus T^{\rm vert}V_{pq}
where both summands have been given Gp​qG_{pq}-invariant orientations. Moreover, there is a summand 𝔤p​q⊆T​Vp​q{\mathfrak{g}}_{pq}\subseteq TV_{pq} corresponding to the infinitesimal Gp​qG_{pq}-actions. Then the direct sum orientation descends to an orientation on the bundle
T⁡(Vp​q/Gp​q)⊕𝔤¯p​q/Gp​qT(V_{pq}/G_{pq})\oplus\underline{\smash{\mathfrak{g}}}_{pq}/G_{pq}
which is what we need.
It remains to verify that the individual orientations on the derived orbifolds are coherent. Suppose p<r<qp<r<q in 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}. Recall that the domain moduli spaces Bp​qB_{pq} are oriented in a way which respects breakings (see Lemma 14.20). On the other hand, the orientations on the vertical tangent bundles Tvt​Vp​qT^{\rm vt}V_{pq} satisfy
detTvt​Vp​q|∂p​r​qVp​q≅detTvt​Vp​r⊗detTvt​Vr​q\det T^{\rm vt}V_{pq}|_{\partial^{prq}V_{pq}}\cong\det T^{\rm vt}V_{pr}\otimes\det T^{\rm vt}V_{rq}
as oriented bundles. As Bp​qB_{pq} are always odd-dimensional, there holds
det(πp​q∗​T​Bp​q⊕Tvt​Vp​q)|∂p​r​qVp​q≅det(πp​r∗​T​Bp​r⊕πr​q∗​T​Br​q⊕Qp​r​q)⊗det(Tvt​Vp​r⊕Tvt​Vr​q⊕Wp​r​q)≅(−1)rank​Tvt​Vp​r​det(πp​r∗​T​Bp​r⊕Tvt​Vp​r)⊗det(πr​q∗​T​Br​q⊕Tvt​Vr​q).\det\Big(\pi_{pq}^{*}TB_{pq}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{pq}\Big)|_{\partial^{prq}V_{pq}}\cong\det\Big(\pi_{pr}^{*}TB_{pr}\oplus\pi_{rq}^{*}TB_{rq}\oplus Q_{prq}\Big)\otimes\det\Big(T^{\rm vt}V_{pr}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{rq}\oplus W_{prq}\Big)\\
\cong(-1)^{{\rm rank}T^{\rm vt}V_{pr}}\det\Big(\pi_{pr}^{*}TB_{pr}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{pr}\Big)\otimes\det\Big(\pi_{rq}^{*}TB_{rq}\oplus T^{\rm vt}V_{rq}\Big).
Notice that here Qp​r​qQ_{prq} and Wp​r​qW_{prq} are both complex. The rank of the vertical bundle here is congruent mod 2 to the difference |p|−|r||p|-|r| of cohomological gradings. This means the orientations on the derived orbifolds specified above provide a coherent orientation on 𝔽~\tilde{\mathbb{F}}.
18.2. Proof of Theorem P
We also summarize the construction of AMS lifts of multimodules associated to a smooth Floer domain.
Proposition 18.1.
In Situation Module(i), fix an outercollaring width and choose a list of integral actions on the involved flow categories which are compatible with respect to 𝕏{\mathbb{X}}. Let 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m;𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} be AMS lifts to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} (subject to the fixed outercollaring width and the integral actions). Then there exists a lift of the outercollaring of 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as a multimodule over (𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m,𝔽^′)(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}).
Proof.
To save notations, we write the proof in the case of bimodules and write 𝕏=𝔹{\mathbb{X}}={\mathbb{B}}. The case of multimodules is the same. Abbreviate 𝔽1{\mathbb{F}}_{1} by 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}. The constructions of 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} and 𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} start with the monotone flow categories ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom} and ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞′{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\prime}. Then by Proposition 14.22, there exists a monotone bimodule ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Σ𝕏{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}} over (𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞;𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞′)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\prime}). Then using the compatible integral actions, one obtains the corresponding bimodule ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝕏{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{X}}} over (𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽;𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞Ω,𝔽′)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}). The choices of transverse thickening data for 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} and 𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} can be extended, by Proposition 15.19, to a transverse thickening datum 𝕎𝕏{\mathbb{W}}^{\mathbb{X}}. The choices of the group reductions for 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} and 𝔽^′\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime} can be extended, by Proposition 15.9, to a group reduction on ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝕏𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{X}}}^{\mathbb{fr}}. Then by Definition 15.16, one obtains the collections of thickenings Vp;p′𝔹V_{p;p^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}} which provides (in a canonical way) a lift of the outercollaring of 𝔹{\mathbb{B}} to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig} as a bimodule over (𝔽^;𝔽^′)(\hat{\mathbb{F}};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}). The remaining structures, including the relative NC structure, the stable smoothing, and the NC structure can all be constructed using the inductive procedure. We omit the details.
∎
The two exceptional cases, i.e., the multimodules for Poincaré pairing and the cigar bimodule can be established similarly. We only give the statement without detailed proofs.
Proposition 18.2.
Let 𝔽1,𝔽2{\mathbb{F}}_{1},{\mathbb{F}}_{2} be Floer flow categories associated to (H1,J1)(H_{1},J_{1}) and (H2,J2)(H_{2},J_{2}) respectively. Let 𝕏PD{\mathbb{X}}^{\rm PD} be the Poincaré multimodule over (𝔽1,𝔽2,𝕆)({\mathbb{F}}_{1},{\mathbb{F}}_{2};{\mathbb{O}}) associated to a Floer data interpolating on the infinite cylinder. Fix an outercollaring width and choose integral actions 𝒜𝔽1Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}^{\Omega}, 𝒜𝔽2Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{2}}^{\Omega} which are compatible with respect to this multimodule. Let 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1} resp. 𝔽^2\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{2} be AMS lifts of 𝔽1{\mathbb{F}}_{1} resp. 𝔽2{\mathbb{F}}_{2} to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} subject to the outercollaring width and the chosen integral actions. Then there exists a lift of the outercollaring of 𝕏PD{\mathbb{X}}^{\rm PD} to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as a multimodule over (𝔽^1,𝔽^2,𝕆)(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{2};{\mathbb{O}}), which we call an AMS lift subject to the outercollaring width and the chosen integral actions.
Proposition 18.3.
Let 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} be a Floer flow category associated to (H,J)(H,J). Let 𝔹cigar{\mathbb{B}}^{\rm cigar} be the cigar bimodule over (𝕆;𝔽)({\mathbb{O}};{\mathbb{F}}) associated to a Floer data on the complex plane. Let 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} be an AMS lift of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} subject to an outercollaring width and an integral action 𝒜𝔽Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega} which is compatible with respect to the bimodule 𝔹cigar{\mathbb{B}}^{\rm cigar}. Then there exists a lift of the outercollaring of 𝔹cigar{\mathbb{B}}^{\rm cigar} to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} which is a bimodule over (𝕆;𝔽^)({\mathbb{O}};\hat{\mathbb{F}}), which we call an AMS lift of 𝔹cigar{\mathbb{B}}^{\rm cigar} subject to the outercollaring width and the chosen integral action.
Propositions 18.1–18.3 lead to the first item of Theorem P (without the orientation claim). To establish the second item, consider the trivial homotopy ℍ{\mathbb{H}} from 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} to itself. Notice that the chosen integral actions are still compatible with respect to ℍ{\mathbb{H}}. Then for any two AMS lifts 𝕏^0\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0} and 𝕏^1\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1} subject to the same outercollaring width and the same set of integral actions, one can construct a lift of the outercollaring of ℍ{\mathbb{H}} to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} by using the corresponding homotopy version of each step of the AMS construction. We omit the details. After passing to derived orbifolds, one obtains the second item of Theorem P (without the orientation claim).
To obtain coherent orientations, one can follow the same argument as in the proof of Theorem O. The signs come from the properties of the orientations on the domain moduli spaces (see Proposition 14.22) as well as the orientations on vertical tangent bundles (see Subsection 16.5).
18.3. Proof of Theorem Q
The proof is simply a different organization of the previous constructions for flow categories and multimodules. Notice that it is important to choose integral actions which are compatible throughout the consideration. Then each stage of the AMS construction, starting from the domain flow category, rigidifications, choosing thickening data and group reductions, constructing relative NC structures, stable smoothing, and smooth NC structures, can all be inductively accomplished. The statement of Theorem Q then follows without any new difficulties than flow category and multimodule cases.
19. Concatenation and Gluing—Proof of Theorem R
In this section we prove Theorem 12.4 and Theorem R. Note that, although the statement of Theorem 12.4 is on the level of derived orbifolds, the constructions of the rigidification and NC structure require us to go through the AMS construction on the level of Kuranishi spaces.

19.1.2. Concatenations of domains

Proposition 19.2.
In Situation Concatenation(i), let
⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔽1,…,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔽m,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔾1,…,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔾n,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔾′{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}},\ {}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{n}},\ {}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{G}}^{\prime}}
be the monotone flow categories enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} subject to the same outercollaring width. Let ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Σ𝕏{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}} resp. ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Σ𝕐{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{{\mathbb{Y}}}} be monotone multimodules over (𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔽1,…,𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔽m;𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔾i)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{i}}) resp. over (𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔾1,…,𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔾n;𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔾′)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{n}};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{G}}^{\prime}}) constructed in Subsection 14.4. Proof.
The underlying monotone multimodules enriched in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}} have a canonical concatenation. Indeed, let Σ𝕏∘i𝕐\Sigma^{{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}{\mathbb{Y}}} be the singular curve with two components Σ𝕏\Sigma^{{\mathbb{X}}} and Σ𝕐\Sigma^{{\mathbb{Y}}} glued along the cylindrical end of the concatenation. Notice that the lateral lines in Σ𝕏\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}} and Σ𝕐\Sigma^{\mathbb{Y}} glue together to lateral lines in the singular domain. Then the same construction of 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma} can be applied to Σ𝕏∘i𝕐\Sigma^{{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}{\mathbb{Y}}}, providing a monotone multimodule 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕏∘i𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕐\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}}\circ_{i}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{Y}}}. It is straightforward to check that the outercollaring of 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕏∘i𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕐\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}}\circ_{i}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{Y}}} is also a concatenation of the corresponding outercollarings of 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕏\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}} and 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕐\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{Y}}}.
The remaining is to construct the rigidifications and the stable complex structures. For simplicity, we assume that 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} is a bimodule 𝔹\mathbb{B} over (𝔽;𝔽′)({\mathbb{F}};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}) and 𝕐{\mathbb{Y}} is a bimodule 𝔹′{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime} over (𝔽′;𝔽′′)({\mathbb{F}}^{\prime};{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime\prime}); the general case is essentially the same with only additional notational complexities.
We first consider the stable complex structure on the concatenation. Recall the case of smooth domains is obtained in Proposition 14.19 where the stable complex structure is naturally induced. The same fact holds for the concatenated domain. Therefore, the natural concatenation 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔹∘𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔹′\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\circ\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} is in fact in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯ℂ\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}^{\mathbb{C}}.
Now we consider rigidifications. We first rigidify the embeddings
𝒞d𝔹×𝒞d′𝔹′→𝒞d+d′𝔹∘𝔹′.{\mathcal{C}}_{d}^{\mathbb{B}}\times{\mathcal{C}}_{d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}^{\prime}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{d+d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}.
Notice that this is a codimension zero embedding and there is a target top stratum
𝒞d;d′𝔹∘𝔹′⊆𝒞d+d′𝔹∘𝔹′{\mathcal{C}}_{d;d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\subseteq{\mathcal{C}}_{d+d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}
such that
𝒢d+d′×𝒢d×𝒢d′(𝒞d𝔹×𝒞d′𝔹′)≅𝒞d;d′𝔹∘𝔹′.{\mathcal{G}}_{d+d^{\prime}}\times_{{\mathcal{G}}_{d}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{d^{\prime}}}({\mathcal{C}}_{d}^{\mathbb{B}}\times{\mathcal{C}}_{d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}^{\prime}})\cong{\mathcal{C}}_{d;d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}\circ\mathbb{B}^{\prime}}.
Recall that a rigidification of the above codimension zero embedding (see Definition 14.9) is a map
θd;d′:Bd𝔹×Bd′𝔹′×Qd;d′ϵ→Bd;d′𝔹∘𝔹′.\theta_{d;d^{\prime}}:B_{d}^{\mathbb{B}}\times B_{d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}^{\prime}}\times Q_{d;d^{\prime}}^{\epsilon}\to B_{d;d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}\circ\mathbb{B}^{\prime}}.
These maps have to incorporate the existing one defining rigidifications of ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔹{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{B}} and ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔹′{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{B}^{\prime}}. One can construct these maps inductively, from the deepest strata up.
First, if Bd;d′𝔹∘𝔹′B_{d;d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}\circ\mathbb{B}^{\prime}} has no lower strata, then there is no constraint coming from rigidifications of ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔹{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{B}} and ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔹′{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}} and one can choose the rigidification arbitrarily.
In general one needs to construct θd;d′\theta_{d;d^{\prime}} inductively. We only explain how to construct it when Bd;d′𝔹∘𝔹′B_{d;d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}\circ\mathbb{B}^{\prime}} has only a codimension one stratum given by a decomposition d=d1+d2d=d_{1}+d_{2}. This codimension one stratum is shared with another open stratum Bd1;d2+d′𝔹∘𝔹′B_{d_{1};d_{2}+d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{B}\circ\mathbb{B}^{\prime}}. The rigidifications for these two open strata (with different symmetry groups) must be compatible along the shared fake boundary. We first choose rigidification of the codimension 1 embedding
Bd1𝔹×Bd2𝔹×Bd′𝔹′→∂d1;d2;d′Bd+d′𝔹∘𝔹′.B_{d_{1}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times B_{d_{2}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times B_{d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\to\partial^{d_{1};d_{2};d^{\prime}}B_{d+d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}.
Notice that the embedding can be factorized in two ways
∂d1​d2Bd𝔹×Bd′𝔹′\textstyle{\partial^{d_{1}d_{2}}B_{d}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times B_{d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Bd1𝔹×Bd2𝔹×Bd′𝔹′\textstyle{B_{d_{1}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times B_{d_{2}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times B_{d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}∂d1;d2;d′Bd+d′𝔹∘𝔹′\textstyle{\partial^{d_{1};d_{2};d^{\prime}}B_{d+d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}}Bd1𝔹×∂d2​d′Bd2+d′𝔹′\textstyle{B_{d_{1}}^{{\mathbb{B}}}\times\partial^{d_{2}d^{\prime}}B_{d_{2}+d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}
where the two arrows on the left are already rigidified. Consider
Qd1;d2;d′=Qd1+d2+d′/Qd1⊕Qd2⊕Qd′.Q_{d_{1};d_{2};d^{\prime}}=Q_{d_{1}+d_{2}+d^{\prime}}/Q_{d_{1}}\oplus Q_{d_{2}}\oplus Q_{d^{\prime}}.
The rigidification on this lower stratum should be a germ of maps
θd1;d2;d′:(Bd1𝔹×Bd2𝔹×Bd′𝔹′)×Qd1;d2;d′→∂d1;d2;d′Bd+d′𝔹∘𝔹′\theta_{d_{1};d_{2};d^{\prime}}:\Big(B_{d_{1}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times B_{d_{2}}^{\mathbb{B}}\times B_{d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}\Big)\times Q_{d_{1};d_{2};d^{\prime}}\to\partial^{d_{1};d_{2};d^{\prime}}B_{d+d^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{B}}\circ{\mathbb{B}}^{\prime}}
Notice that there is a natural inclusion
Qd1​d2⊕Qd2​d′⊆Qd1;d2;d′Q_{d_{1}d_{2}}\oplus Q_{d_{2}d^{\prime}}\subseteq Q_{d_{1};d_{2};d^{\prime}}
where the value of the rigidification is already determined. One then only has to extend it to the complement. Choosing such an extension equivariantly, one hence obtains the rigidification θd1;d2;d′\theta_{d_{1};d_{2};d^{\prime}} on this lower stratum.
Notice that this lower stratum is shared by two top strata. One uses the collar regions in both directions to extend to a rigidification for both separately.
∎
19.1.3. Gluing of domains
Now suppose we are in Situation Homotopy(i). Suppose on the family of domains Σt\Sigma_{t} (t∈[0,1]t\in[0,1]) one chooses a smooth family of lateral lines. Here t=0t=0 corresponds to the broken domain. Then without making further choices, one has the monotone flow categories
𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔽1,…,𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔽m,𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔾1,…,𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔾n,𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔾′\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}_{1}},\ldots,\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}_{m}},\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{G}}_{1}},\ldots,\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{G}_{n}},\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{G}^{\prime}}
monotone multimodules
𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕏,\displaystyle\ \mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}},\
𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕐.\displaystyle\ \mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{Y}}}.
As demonstrated above, the concatenation 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕏∘i𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Σ𝕐\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}}\circ_{i}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{Y}}} within the category 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}} is canonically defined. Moreover, by varying tt, one also obtains a monotone homotopy 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞ℍ\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{H}} from the concatenation to 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝕄\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{M}} which is the multimodule associated to Σ1\Sigma_{1}.
What we do below is the construction of the further choices such as rigidifications and stable complex structure.
Proposition 19.3.
Fix an outercollaring width. Let ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔽1,…,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔽m{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}_{m}}, ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔾1,…,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔾n{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{G}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{G}_{n}}, ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔾′{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{G}^{\prime}}, ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Σ𝕏{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}}, ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Σ𝕐{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{Y}}}, ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Σ𝕏∘i⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Σ𝕐{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}}\circ_{i}{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{Y}}} be as in Proposition 19.2. Let ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝕄{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{M}} be a monotone multimodule associated to the smooth domain Σ1\Sigma_{1} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}.
