Then for the outercollaring ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞ℍ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{H}}, there exists a lift to ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} as a monotone homotopy from ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Σ𝕏∘i⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Σ𝕐{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}}\circ_{i}{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Sigma^{\mathbb{Y}}} to ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝕄{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{M}}.
Proof.
Again, it only remains to construct the rigidifications and stable complex structures. The construction of rigidification is still based on the same induction principle. Then stable complex structure can be chosen after choosing a rigidification.
∎
19.2. Relatively smooth AMS lifts for concatenations and gluing
In this subsection we treat the topological AMS construction for concatenations of Floer multimodules associated to smooth Floer domains.
19.2.1. Concatenation
Assume we are in Situation Concatenation(i). We have constructed relatively smooth AMS lifts 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} and 𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{Y}} to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig} respectively. The purpose of this subsection is to demonstrate how to extend the constructions of 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} and 𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{Y}} to a lift of the concatenation 𝕏∘i𝕐{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}{\mathbb{Y}} to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
Theorem 19.4.
In Situation Concatenation(i), let 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} and 𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{Y}} be relatively smooth AMS lifts of the outercollarings of 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} and 𝕐{\mathbb{Y}} respectively, subject to the same outercollaring width and integral actions which induce the same integral symplectic form on XX. Then there exists a set of concatenations 𝕏^∘i𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}\hat{\mathbb{Y}} enriched in ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
Proof.
As in Subsection 19.1.1, we only describe the construction in the case of concatenations of bimodules. The case of multimodules differs only in notation. Denote 𝕏=𝔹01{\mathbb{X}}={\mathbb{B}}_{01} and 𝕐=𝔹12{\mathbb{Y}}={\mathbb{B}}_{12} where 𝔹01{\mathbb{B}}_{01} is a bimodule over (𝔽0;𝔽1)({\mathbb{F}}_{0};{\mathbb{F}}_{1}) and 𝔹12\mathbb{B}_{12} is a bimodule over (𝔽1;𝔽2)({\mathbb{F}}_{1};\mathbb{F}_{2}), where 𝔽i{\mathbb{F}}_{i} is the Floer flow category associated to Hamiltonian HiH_{i}. Let Σ\Sigma be the broken domain with two cylinders equipped with Floer datum σ\sigma from the concatenation of the two Floer data for 𝔹01\mathbb{B}_{01} and 𝔹12\mathbb{B}_{12}.
First consider the concatenation of domains. The AMS constructions of 𝔽^0,𝔽^1,𝔽^2\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{0},\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{2} and 𝔹^01\hat{\mathbb{B}}_{01}, 𝔹^12\hat{\mathbb{B}}_{12} start with choosing monotone flow categories ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞0,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞1,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞2{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{0},{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{1},{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{2} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} as considered in Section 14, as well as monotone bimodules ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞01,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞12{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{01},{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{12} respectively. Then Proposition 19.2 allows us to choose a concatenation ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞01∘⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞12{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{01}\circ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{12} as a monotone bimodule over (𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞0;𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞2)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{0};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{2}).
Now using the chosen integral actions, one can obtain pullbacks
⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔽i,i=0,1,2;\displaystyle\ {}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{i}},i=0,1,2;\
⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔹01,⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔹12\displaystyle\ {}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{B}}_{01}},\ {}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{B}}_{12}}
as ordinary flow categories and bimodules. The corresponding bimodules of framed maps are also obtained
⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔹01fr,\displaystyle\ {}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{B}_{01}}^{\rm fr},\
⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔹12fr\displaystyle\ {}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{B}_{12}}^{\rm fr}
with a concatenation
⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔹01fr∘⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔹12fr{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{B}_{01}}^{\rm fr}\circ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{B}_{12}}^{\rm fr}
canonically determined by the concatenation ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔹01∘⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔹12{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{B}}_{01}}\circ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{B}_{12}}.
We need to show that the two further systems of choices, i.e., group reductions and thickening data, can be extended to the concatenation.
We first explain why the group reduction can be naturally extended. Indeed, given a triple of objects p0,p1,p2p_{0},p_{1},p_{2} of the three involved flow categories, one has the morphism
⌊Mapp0;p1fr×⌊Mapp1;p2fr→⌊Mapp0;p2fr{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{p_{0};p_{1}}^{{\rm fr}}\times{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{p_{1};p_{2}}^{{\rm fr}}\to{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{p_{0};p_{2}}^{{\rm fr}}
(19.2)
in the category of framed maps. One can see that if we choose any strict embedding representing the conjugacy class, then the strict embedding induces an open embedding onto the closure of a top stratum
𝒢^p0;p2×𝒢^p0;p1×𝒢^p1;p2(Mapp0;p1fr⌊×Mapp1;p2fr⌊)→Mapp0;p2fr⌊\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{p_{0};p_{2}}\times_{\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{p_{0};p_{1}}\times\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{p_{1};p_{2}}}\Big({}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{p_{0};p_{1}}^{{\rm fr}}\times{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{p_{1};p_{2}}^{{\rm fr}}\Big)\to{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{p_{0};p_{2}}^{{\rm fr}}
(recall 𝒢^=𝒢L×𝒢R\hat{\mathcal{G}}={\mathcal{G}}_{L}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{R} where 𝒢L{\mathcal{G}}_{L} acts by reparametrizing the maps and frames while 𝒢R{\mathcal{G}}_{R} acts by linearly rearranging the frames). As the group reduction is invariant under the first group action and equivariant under the second action, the open embedding naturally induces an extension of the group reduction. One can check that the extension is well-defined on fake boundaries of ⌊Mapp0;p2fr{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{p_{0};p_{2}}^{\rm fr} (which are adjacent to two such top strata).
The extension of the thickening datum is also canonical in a neighborhood of the morphism (19.2), because the embedding is rigidified. Using the rigidification of this embedding, we can extend the thickening datum in a way which is constant in each normal fiber specified by the rigidification. As one can always shrink the resulting charts, up to shrinking, the extension of the thickening datum is canonically extended.
Then one can write down the thickenings in the same way as for a multimodule with a smooth domain. We can verify easily that one obtains a topological Kuranishi lift 𝔹^\hat{\mathbb{B}} which is also a concatenation 𝔹^01∘𝔹^12\hat{\mathbb{B}}_{01}\circ\hat{\mathbb{B}}_{12} within the category ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig}. The relative smooth structure is canonically given and one can also easily see that the concatenation is indeed in ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
∎
19.2.2. Gluing
Theorem 19.5.
In Situation Glue(i), fix an outercollaring width and integral actions on the involved flow categories compatible with respect to ℍ{\mathbb{H}}. Let 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}} and 𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{Y}} be relatively smooth AMS lifts of 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} and 𝕐{\mathbb{Y}} subject to the outercollaring width and the integral actions. Let 𝕏^∘𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{X}}\circ\hat{\mathbb{Y}} be a concatenation provided by Theorem 19.4. Let 𝕄^\hat{\mathbb{M}} be an AMS lift of the multimodule 𝕄{\mathbb{M}}. Then there exists a set of lifts of the outercollaring of the homotopy ℍ{\mathbb{H}} to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig} as a homotopy from 𝕏^∘𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{X}}\circ\hat{\mathbb{Y}} to 𝕄^\hat{\mathbb{M}}.
Proof.
At this stage, it follows from the same strategy as the proof of Theorem Q. The choices of rigidifications of domains are provided by Proposition 19.3. The choices of group reductions and thickening datum can also be interpolated over the homotopy. The relative smooth structures are canonically obtained.
∎
19.3. Normal complex structure and stable smoothing
Finally, we sketch the discussion on normal complex structures and stable smoothing of the objects arising in concatenation and gluing, which will finish the proof of Theorem 12.4 and Theorem R.
Proof of Theorem 12.4.
We continue after Theorem 19.4. Suppose the relatively smooth AMS lifts 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}, 𝔾^1,…,𝔾^n\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{n}, 𝔾^′\hat{\mathbb{G}}^{\prime}, and the multimodules 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}}, 𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{Y}} are lifted to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} using the construction of Section 16. We would like to see if the composition 𝕏^∘i𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}\hat{\mathbb{Y}} provided by Theorem 19.4 can also be lifted to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as a composition. In fact, the vertical tangent bundles contained in the composition 𝕏^∘i𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}\hat{\mathbb{Y}} are canonically determined by the corresponding vertical tangent bundles. Hence the vertical NC structures are canonically induced. Therefore, we see that 𝕏^∘i𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}\hat{\mathbb{Y}} is lifted to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}.
The stable smoothing of the concatenation is also automatically induced. We briefly explain for the bimodule case. Let 𝔽0,𝔽1,𝔽2{\mathbb{F}}_{0},{\mathbb{F}}_{1},{\mathbb{F}}_{2} and 𝔹01\mathbb{B}_{01}, 𝔹12\mathbb{B}_{12} be as in the proof of Theorem 19.4. For each triple of objects p0,p1,p2p_{0},p_{1},p_{2}, one has the embedding
Kp0;p1𝔹01×Kp1;p2𝔹12→Kp0;p2𝔹01∘𝔹12.K_{p_{0};p_{1}}^{\mathbb{B}_{01}}\times K_{p_{1};p_{2}}^{\mathbb{B}_{12}}\to K_{p_{0};p_{2}}^{\mathbb{B}_{01}\circ\mathbb{B}_{12}}.
The difference essentially lies in the difference between the complex Lie groups 𝒢p0;p1×𝒢p1;p2{\mathcal{G}}_{p_{0};p_{1}}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{p_{1};p_{2}} and 𝒢p0;p2{\mathcal{G}}_{p_{0};p_{2}}. In terms of Kuranishi charts, the unitary part of the difference is realized by changing the symmetry groups while the non-unitary part of the difference is realized by having a further stabilization. Therefore, if both Kp0;p1𝔹01K_{p_{0};p_{1}}^{\mathbb{B}_{01}} and Kp1;p2𝔹12K_{p_{1};p_{2}}^{\mathbb{B}_{12}} is equipped with a (stable) smoothing, then the corresponding top stratum of Kp0;p2𝔹01∘𝔹12K_{p_{0};p_{2}}^{\mathbb{B}_{01}\circ\mathbb{B}_{12}} has an induced stable smoothing (possibly after doing further stabilizations).
Lastly, we combine the stable complex structures of the domain moduli space discussed in the proof of Proposition 19.2, the NC structures on the vertical tangent bundles to obtain an NC structure on the quotient derived orbifolds.
∎
Proof of Theorem R.
We continue after Theorem 19.5. Suppose the relatively smooth AMS lifts 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}, 𝔾^1,…,𝔾^n\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{n}, 𝔾^′\hat{\mathbb{G}}^{\prime}, 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}}, 𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{Y}}, 𝕄^\hat{\mathbb{M}} are lifted to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. Suppose we also have a concatenation 𝕏^∘i𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{X}}\circ_{i}\hat{\mathbb{Y}} enriched in ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. The homotopy ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} is also lifted to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}. We first can lift ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. This can be done by using the same argument as using a family of Cauchy–Riemann operators interpolating between the linearization of the Floer equation and a complex-linear one. We omit the details, which would be a tedious repetition of the flow category and multimodule case already considered.
Next, suppose 𝔽^1,…,𝔽^m\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}, 𝔾^1,…,𝔾^n\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{1},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{G}}_{n}, 𝔾^′\hat{\mathbb{G}}^{\prime}, 𝕏^\hat{\mathbb{X}}, 𝕐^\hat{\mathbb{Y}}, 𝕄^\hat{\mathbb{M}} are also lifted to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} after further stabilization and smoothing. The stable smoothing and NC structures of ℍ^\hat{\mathbb{H}} can be constructed using the same inductive argument as we always did. The result is obtained by passing to the orbifold quotient.
∎
20. Comparing Non-homotopic Choices
The comparison between different choices which are not homotopic requires more setup. Choices in this category include
(1)
The choice of integral actions (see Definition 15.1) in construction the AMS lifts.
(2)
Different choices of lateral lines in Floer domains.
We remove the dependence on these two choices uniformly via a doubling construction (cf. [3, Section 6.10]). Here, different integral actions give rise to different moduli spaces of curves of projective spaces; as for different choices of lateral lines under the same choice of integral actions, they induce different composition laws. Despite the different effects, we can handle them in the same way.
20.1. Curves in products of projective spaces
We can generalize the notion of monotone flow categories/multimodules/homotopies (see Definition 14.1, Definition 14.4, Definition 14.5) in the following way. Fix k≥2k\geq 2 and consider the monoid ℤ≥0k{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}^{k} instead of ℤ≥0{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}. Then for each 𝐝=(d1,…,dk)∈ℤ≥0k{\bf d}=(d^{1},\ldots,d^{k})\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}^{k}, there is a natural poset
A𝐝={(𝐝0,…,𝐝l)|𝐝i∈ℤ≥0k∖{0},𝐝=𝐝0+⋯+𝐝l}.A_{\bf d}=\Big\{({\bf d}_{0},\ldots,{\bf d}_{l})\ |\ {\bf d}_{i}\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}^{k}\setminus\{0\},\ {\bf d}={\bf d}_{0}+\cdots+{\bf d}_{l}\Big\}.
A monotone flow category of rank kk enriched in 𝐂¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}}, denoted by 𝕗{\mathbb{f}}, consists of a collection of A𝐝A_{\bf d}-stratified objects
M𝐝𝕗,∀𝐝∈ℤ≥0kM_{\bf d}^{\mathbb{f}},\ \forall{\bf d}\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}^{k}
and a collection of morphisms
M𝐝1𝕗×M𝐝2𝕗→∂𝐝1,𝐝2M𝐝1+𝐝2𝕗M_{{\bf d}_{1}}^{\mathbb{f}}\times M_{{\bf d}_{2}}^{\mathbb{f}}\to\partial^{{\bf d}_{1},{\bf d}_{2}}M_{{\bf d}_{1}+{\bf d}_{2}}^{\mathbb{f}}
which satisfy the natural associativity condition, similar to that imposed in Definition 14.1. One can see any monotone flow category 𝕗{\mathbb{f}} of rank kk induces an ordinary flow category 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} with Ob​𝔽≅ℤk{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\cong{\mathbb{Z}}^{k}. Similarly, one can define monotone multimodules and homotopies of higher ranks as we did in Definition 14.4 and Definition 14.5: we leave it to the interested reader to spell out the details.
Now we would like to build rank kk monotone flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞k{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{k} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}. Indeed, for 𝐝=(d1,…,dk){\bf d}=(d^{1},\ldots,d^{k}), define
ℙ𝐝=ℙd1×⋯×ℙdk.{\mathbb{P}}^{\bf d}={\mathbb{P}}^{d^{1}}\times\cdots\times{\mathbb{P}}^{d^{k}}.
Each element is an equivalence class of maps with kk components. Indeed, one can consider the moduli space ℳ¯(ℙ𝐝,𝐝)ℝ0,2\overline{\mathcal{M}}{}_{0,2}^{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{P}^{\bf d},{\bf d}) of cylinders in ℙ𝐝\mathbb{P}^{\bf d} of multidegree 𝐝{\bf d} and the open subset
B𝐝⊆ℳ¯(ℙ𝐝,𝐝)ℝ0,2B_{\bf d}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal{M}}{}_{0,2}^{\mathbb{R}}(\mathbb{P}^{\bf d},{\bf d})
of cylinders satisfying 1) the evaluations of the ii-th component at +∞+\infty is [0,⋯,0,1]∈ℙdi[0,\cdots,0,1]\in\mathbb{P}^{d^{i}} and 2) the image of the ii-th component is not contained in any hyperplanes of ℙdi\mathbb{P}^{d^{i}}. Then B𝐝B_{\bf d} is an A𝐝A_{\bf d}-stratified manifold with a smooth action by the complex Lie group
𝒢𝐝:=𝒢d1×⋯×𝒢dk{\mathcal{G}}_{\bf d}:={\mathcal{G}}_{d^{1}}\times\cdots\times{\mathcal{G}}_{d^{k}}
which contains a maximal compact subgroup
G𝐝:=Gd1×⋯×Gdk≅U(d1)×⋯×U(dk).G_{\bf d}:=G_{d^{1}}\times\cdots\times G_{d^{k}}\cong U(d^{1})\times\cdots\times U(d^{k}).
Similar to the rank 1 case, one obtains a collection of objects
𝒞𝐝=(𝒢𝐝,B𝐝,C𝐝)∈Ob​𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯{\mathcal{C}}_{\bf d}=({\mathcal{G}}_{\bf d},B_{\bf d},C_{\bf d})\in{\rm Ob}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}
where C𝐝→B𝐝C_{\bf d}\to B_{\bf d} is the universal curve.
One can define similar structural maps to obtain a monotone flow category, denoted by
𝔻​𝕠​𝕞k.\mathbb{Dom}^{k}.
Similarly, for any smooth Floer domain Σ𝕏\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}, one obtains a monotone multimodule 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞k,Σ𝕏\mathbb{Dom}^{k,\Sigma^{\mathbb{X}}} over (𝔻​𝕠​𝕞k,…,𝔻​𝕠​𝕞k,𝔻​𝕠​𝕞k)(\mathbb{Dom}^{k},\ldots,\mathbb{Dom}^{k};\mathbb{Dom}^{k}).
A slight difference from the previous rank 11 case is that we choose not to construct rigidifications and stable complex structures at this stage (although we could do so). We would like to do the construction later after pulling back so that certain compatibility holds directly from our construction. At this point, we only take outercollarings and the monotone flow categories/multimodules are enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}.
20.2. Double-framed thickenings
We may carry out the roadmap of the AMS construction for the higher-rank approach which facilitates the comparison of different integral actions. We only need to consider the k=2k=2 case and call such a construction a “double-framed” AMS construction.
We briefly go through the construction for Floer flow categories. Assume one is in Situation Flow(i). Fix an outercollaring width. Let
𝒜𝔽Ω1,𝒜𝔽Ω2:Ob​𝔽→ℤ{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{1}},\ {\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{2}}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\to{\mathbb{Z}}
be two integral actions on 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}. Denote their direct sum by
𝒜𝔽Ω1⊕Ω2:Ob​𝔽→ℤ2.{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2}}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\to{\mathbb{Z}}^{2}.
Then for each pair p<qp<q of objects of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}, define
𝐝p​q=(dp​q1,dp​q2)=𝒜𝔽Ω1⊕Ω2​(p)−𝒜𝔽Ω1⊕Ω2​(q)∈ℤ≥02.{\bf d}_{pq}=(d_{pq}^{1},d_{pq}^{2})={\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2}}(p)-{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2}}(q)\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}^{2}.
Then for each pair p<qp<q, let
𝒞p​q=(𝒢p​q,Bp​q,Cp​q),{\mathcal{C}}_{pq}=({\mathcal{G}}_{pq},B_{pq},C_{pq}),
be the restriction of 𝒞𝐝p​q{\mathcal{C}}_{{\bf d}_{pq}} to the strata whose associated degrees can be realized by integralized actions of broken Floer trajectories of HH. This provides a pullback
⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{F}}}
which is a flow category enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}} whose objects are those of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}.
One can write down the associated flow category of framed maps in the same way as the rank 11 case. More precisely, given objects p<qp<q, the space of framed maps consists of tuples (ϕ,u,F)(\phi,u,F) where ϕ∈Bp​q\phi\in B_{pq}, u:Cϕ→Xu:C_{\phi}\to X is a smooth map satisfying the exponential decay condition, and F=(F1,F2)F=(F_{1},F_{2}) consists of two frames where FiF_{i}, called an Ωi\Omega_{i}-frame along uu, is a frame of the holomorphic line bundle Lu,Ωi→CϕL_{u,\Omega_{i}}\to C_{\phi} satisfying the positive constraint.
The following fact is important for the comparison. For each p<qp<q, write
𝒢p​q=𝒢p​q1×𝒢p​q2=𝒢dp​q1×𝒢dp​q2.{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}={\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{1}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{2}={\mathcal{G}}_{d_{pq}^{1}}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{d_{pq}^{2}}.
Lemma 20.1.
Bp​qB_{pq} is a 𝒢p​q1{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{1}-equivariant principal 𝒢p​q2{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{2}-bundle over Bp​q1B_{pq}^{1}.
Proof.
Abbreviate
di=𝒜𝔽Ωi(p)−𝒜𝔽Ωi(q),i=1,2.d^{i}={\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{i}}(p)-{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{i}}(q),\ i=1,2.
Each element of Bp​qB_{pq} is represented by a holomorphic map (u1,u2):Cϕ→ℙd1×ℙd2(u^{1},u^{2}):C_{\phi}\to\mathbb{P}^{d^{1}}\times\mathbb{P}^{d^{2}}. Then there is an obvious free 𝒢d2{\mathcal{G}}_{d^{2}}-action on Bp​qB_{pq} by linearly transforming the second component. Moreover, fix ϕ1∈Bp​q1\phi^{1}\in B_{pq}^{1}, all holomorphic maps into ℙd2{\mathbb{P}}^{d^{2}} which have the prescribed degrees on each irreducible component are in the same free 𝒢p​q2{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{2}-orbit. They come from projective embeddings of the irreducible components into ℙd2{\mathbb{P}}^{d^{2}} induced by a basis of global sections of the line bundle with prescribed degree, with matching condition on the nodes. This amounts to looking at all framings with positive evaluation constraint, thereby producing 𝒢p​q2{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{2}.
∎
We denote the natural projection
πi:⌊Bp​q→⌊Bp​qi,i=1,2.\pi_{i}:{}_{\lfloor}B_{pq}\to{}_{\lfloor}B_{pq}^{i},\ i=1,2.
We will use these projections to pull back all choices made for the rank 1 construction to the rank 2 case and take direct sums.
Corollary 20.2.
The lifts of ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ωi,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{i},{\mathbb{F}}} to ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} canonically induce a lift of ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{F}}}.
Proof.
By Definition 14.9, the rigidification for ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ωi,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{i},{\mathbb{F}}} is given by maps
θp​r​qi:⌊Bp​ri×⌊Br​qi×Qp​r​qi→𝒢p​qi\theta_{prq}^{i}:{}_{\lfloor}B_{pr}^{i}\times{}_{\lfloor}B_{rq}^{i}\times Q_{prq}^{i}\to{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}^{i}
satisfying certain conditions. One can simply pullback θp​r​qi\theta_{prq}^{i} to ⌊Bp​r×⌊Br​q{}_{\lfloor}B_{pr}\times{}_{\lfloor}B_{rq}. More precisely, define
θp​r​q:⌊Bp​r×⌊Br​q→Qp​r​q(ϕp​r,ϕr​q)↦(θp​r​q1​(π1​(ϕp​r),π1​(ϕr​q)),θp​r​q2​(π2​(ϕp​r),π2​(ϕr​q))).\begin{split}\theta_{prq}:{}_{\lfloor}B_{pr}\times{}_{\lfloor}B_{rq}\to&\ Q_{prq}\\
(\phi_{pr},\phi_{rq})\mapsto&\ \Big(\theta_{prq}^{1}(\pi_{1}(\phi_{pr}),\pi_{1}(\phi_{rq})),\theta_{prq}^{2}(\pi_{2}(\phi_{pr}),\pi_{2}(\phi_{rq}))\Big).\end{split}
These maps define a rigidification of ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{F}}}.
On the other hand, the stable complex structure can also be obtained by using such pullbacks, whose compatibility can be checked easily.
∎
Now we assume that ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{F}}} is enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}. Of course, such a lift does not necessarily come from pullbacks, but for our purpose, it suffices to consider this special situation.
Similarly, for a flow multimodule 𝕏{\mathbb{X}} over (𝔽1,…,𝔽m,𝔽)({\mathbb{F}}_{1},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}}_{m};{\mathbb{F}}), if each of the flow categories are equipped with integral actions for i=1,2i=1,2,
𝒜𝔽1Ωi,…,𝒜𝔽mΩi,𝒜𝔽′Ωi.{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}^{\Omega_{i}},\ldots,{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}}^{\Omega_{i}},{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}^{\Omega_{i}}.
we obtain a multimodule ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝕏{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{X}}} over (𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝔽1,…,𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝔽m;𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝔽′)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{F}}_{1}},\ldots,{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{F}}_{m}};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}) enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}.
20.3. Flow category situation
We spell out the comparison between different integral actions on the same flow category in detail.
20.3.1. Framed maps and group reductions
We can write down the flow category of framed maps
⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝕗​𝕣𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}^{\mathbb{fr}}_{\mathbb{F}}
which assigns to each pair p<qp<q a space ⌊Mapp​qfr{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{pq}^{\rm fr} consisting of triples (ϕ,u,F)(\phi,u,F) where ϕ∈⌊Bp​q\phi\in{}_{\lfloor}B_{pq}, u:Cϕ→Xu:C_{\phi}\to X is a component-wise smooth map which extends continuously over nodes and which converges exponentially fast to periodic orbits, and F=(F1,F2)F=(F_{1},F_{2}) is a double-frame where FiF_{i} is a frame of the holomorphic line bundle Lu,Ωi→CϕL_{u,\Omega_{i}}\to C_{\phi} satisfying the pre-chosen positive or negative constraint.
Notice that there are still natural projection maps
πi:⌊Mapp​qfr→⌊Mapp​q,ifr(ϕ,u,F)↦(πi​(ϕ),u,Fi).\begin{split}\pi_{i}:{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{pq}^{\rm fr}\to&\ {}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{pq,i}^{\rm fr}\\
(\phi,u,F)\mapsto&(\pi_{i}(\phi),u,F_{i}).\end{split}
(20.1)
Now denote
𝒢^p​q=𝒢L,p​q×𝒢R,p​q≅𝒢p​q×𝒢p​q.\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}={\mathcal{G}}_{L,pq}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{R,pq}\cong{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}.
It acts on ⌊Mapp​qfr{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{pq}^{\rm fr} as before, where 𝒢L,p​q{\mathcal{G}}_{L,pq} reparametrizes the maps and the frames, while 𝒢R,p​q{\mathcal{G}}_{R,pq} linearly transforms the frames. Recall that a group reduction (Definition 15.7) consists of a compatible system of 𝒢^p​q\hat{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}-equivariant maps
Λp​q:⌊Mapp​qfr→𝒢p​q/Gp​q.\Lambda_{pq}:{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{pq}^{\rm fr}\to{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}/G_{pq}.
If we have chosen independently group reductions for ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽i𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{i}}^{\mathbb{fr}}, then using the projection map (20.1), we can pull them back to obtain a group reduction on the double-framed construction ⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\mathbb{fr}}.
20.3.2. Thickening data
The last step of constructing the topological AMS lift is to choose transverse thickening data. By slightly generalizing Definition 15.10, a thickening datum on the flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{F}}} consists of a collection of unitary Gp​qG_{pq}-representations and Gp​qG_{pq}-equivariant linear maps
νp​q:Wp​q→Γc​(C̊p​q×X,ΛC̊p​q/Bp​q0,1⊗T​X).\nu_{pq}:W_{pq}\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{pq}\times X,\Lambda_{\mathring{C}_{pq}/B_{pq}}^{0,1}\otimes TX).
satisfying the natural compatibility condition with the structural maps. With or without transversality condition, one can write down the thickening (cf. Definition 15.14)
Vp​q={(ϕ,u,e,F)|(ϕ,u,F)∈Mapp​qfr⌊,e∈Wp​q,ϕF=ϕ∈Bp​q⌊,∂¯Hu+νp​q(e)=0}.V_{pq}=\Big\{(\phi,u,e,F)\ |\ (\phi,u,F)\in{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{pq}^{\rm fr},e\in W_{pq},\ \phi_{F}=\phi\in{}_{\lfloor}B_{pq},\ \overline{\partial}_{H}u+\nu_{pq}(e)=0\Big\}.
The obstruction bundle Ep​qE_{pq} is still the direct sum of the trivial bundles Wp​q⊕Qp​qW_{pq}\oplus Q_{pq} and the Kuranishi section Sp​q:Vp​q→Ep​qS_{pq}:V_{pq}\to E_{pq} is the direct sum of the (linearized) group reduction λp​q\lambda_{pq} and the forgetful map (ϕ,u,e,F)↦e(\phi,u,e,F)\mapsto e. There is the natural footprint map
Sp​q−1(0)/Gp​q→Mp​q𝔽⌊S_{pq}^{-1}(0)/G_{pq}\to{}_{\lfloor}M_{pq}^{\mathbb{F}}
sending the Gp​qG_{pq}-orbit of (ϕ,u,e,F)(\phi,u,e,F) to the equivalence class of u:Cϕ→Xu:C_{\phi}\to X.
Then suppose one has chosen independently thickening datum
νp​qi:Wp​qi→Γc(C̊p​qi×X,ΛC̊p​qi/Bp​q,i0,1⊗TX),i=1,2,\nu_{pq}^{i}:W_{pq}^{i}\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{pq}^{i}\times X,\Lambda_{\mathring{C}_{pq}^{i}/B_{pq,i}}^{0,1}\otimes TX),\ i=1,2,
then one can pullback each of them
(πi)∗​νp​qi:Wp​qi→Γc​(C̊p​q×X,ΛC̊p​q/Bp​q0,1⊗T​X).(\pi_{i})^{*}\nu_{pq}^{i}:W_{pq}^{i}\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{pq}\times X,\Lambda_{\mathring{C}_{pq}/B_{pq}}^{0,1}\otimes TX).
Lemma 20.3.
If νp​qi\nu_{pq}^{i} is transverse, so is πi∗​νp​qi\pi_{i}^{*}\nu_{pq}^{i}.
Proof.
This follows from the observation that if Wp​qiW_{pq}^{i} is mapped surjectively onto the cokernel of the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator, so is the pullback.
∎
20.3.3. Finalizing proof
Now we would like to compare the two lifts 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} using a rank 1 construction and 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} using a rank 2 construction where the thickening datum is pulled back from the choices made for 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}}.
Recall the notion of free quotient of Kuranishi spaces (Definition 3.11).
Definition 20.4.
Let 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} be a flow category enriched in 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}} with morphism space
Kp​q∼=(Gp​q∼,Vp​q∼,Ep​q∼,Sp​q∼).K_{pq}^{\sim}=(G_{pq}^{\sim},V_{pq}^{\sim},E_{pq}^{\sim},S_{pq}^{\sim}).
A free quotient of 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} consists of for each pair of objects p,q∈Ob​𝔽p,q\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}} a decomposition
Gp​q∼=Gp​q×Gp​q′G_{pq}^{\sim}=G_{pq}\times G_{pq}^{\prime}
of compact Lie groups satisfying 1) the conjugacy class of group embeddings Gp​r∼×Gr​q∼→Gp​q∼G_{pr}^{\sim}\times G_{rq}^{\sim}\to G_{pq}^{\sim} respect the decomposition and 2) Gp​q′G_{pq}^{\prime} acts freely on Vp​q∼V_{pq}^{\sim}. Notice that one obtains a new flow category 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} with morphism spaces Kp​qK_{pq} being the free quotient of Kp​q∼K_{pq}^{\sim} by Gp​q′G_{pq}^{\prime} (see Definition 3.11). By abuse of notation, we also call the resulting flow category consisting of these free quotients a free quotient of 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim}.
Notice that in the above definition, if 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} is enriched in 𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}, then the resulting flow category 𝔽~∼\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} enriched in 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}} obtained by taking the quotient by the full group is isomorphic to the one obtained from the free quotient obtained by taking the residual group action.
Proposition 20.5.
Assume we are in Situation Flow(i). Fix an outercollaring width. Let 𝒜𝔽Ωi:Ob​𝔽→ℤ{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{i}}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\to{\mathbb{Z}}, i=1,2i=1,2 be two integral actions. Let 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} be an AMS lift of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} (of rank 11, subject to an outercollaring width and 𝒜𝔽Ωi{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{i}}). Then there exists a rank 2 AMS lift 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} (subject to the same outercollaring width and the rank 2 integral action) and another rank 22 lift of the outercollaring 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}, denoted by 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} such that 1) 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1} is isomorphic to a free quotient of 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} and 2) 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} is isomorphic to a stabilization of 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}}. The same applies to an AMS lift 𝔽^2\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{2} of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} subject to an outercollaring width and 𝒜𝔽Ωi{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{i}}.
Proof.
We provide a construction that works equally well for both 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1} and 𝔽^2\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{2}: their relations with our 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} are completely symmetric. We will focus on explaining the situation for 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}.
Recall the roadmap of constructing 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}. First, consider the flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω1,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1},{\mathbb{F}}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}. By Lemma 20.1, there is another flow category 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝔽\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{F}}} whose corresponding moduli spaces are principal bundles over those in ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω1,𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1},{\mathbb{F}}}. Then the flow category 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} is naturally induced from it in the following way. The differences between 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} and 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1} lie in: 1) the compact Lie group associated to objects p<qp<q is Gp​q1×Gp​q2G^{1}_{pq}\times G^{2}_{pq}; 2) the space Bp​q1B^{1}_{pq} is replaced by a principal Gp​q2G^{2}_{pq}-bundle over Bp​q1B^{1}_{pq}, which is a subspace of Bp​qB_{pq} discussed in Lemma 20.3 where we replace each fiber of the principal 𝒢p​q2{\mathcal{G}}^{2}_{pq}-bundle Bp​q→Bp​q1B_{pq}\to B^{1}_{pq} by the maximal compact subgroup, i.e., looking at the unitary framings on the second factor; 3) the obstruction bundle and Kuranishi section are pulled back to the principal Gp​q2G^{2}_{pq}-bundle constructed in 2). By construction, we see that 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1} is isomorphic to the free quotient of 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}}.
On the other hand, we define 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} taking full advantage of the double framing. This time, along each map u:Cϕ→Xu:C_{\phi}\to X there are two sets of frames, one for the line bundle induced from Ω1\Omega_{1} and the other for the line bundle induced from Ω2\Omega_{2}. The group reduction chosen for 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1} can be extended to this “double-framed” version. This time, we consider the total space Bp​qB_{pq} for each p<qp<q, acted on by Gp​q=Gp​q1×Gp​q2G_{pq}=G^{1}_{pq}\times G^{2}_{pq}. As for the obstruction bundle, we first pull back the thickening data 𝕎1𝔽{\mathbb{W}}^{\mathbb{F}}_{1} and 𝕎2𝔽{\mathbb{W}}^{\mathbb{F}}_{2}, which is still transverse by Lemma 20.3, then we take the direct sum with Q¯p​q1\underline{\smash{Q}}_{pq}^{1} and Q¯p​q2\underline{\smash{Q}}_{pq}^{2} so that the obstruction bundle is
W¯p​q𝔽1⊕W¯p​q𝔽2⊕Q¯p​q1⊕Q¯p​q2\underline{\smash{W}}_{pq}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}\oplus\underline{\smash{W}}_{pq}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{2}}\oplus\underline{\smash{Q}}_{pq}^{1}\oplus\underline{\smash{Q}}_{pq}^{2}
where the Q¯p​q2\underline{\smash{Q}}_{pq}^{2}-component of the Kuranishi section is induced from the group reduction for the Ω2\Omega_{2}-frames. Therefore, in the category ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}, the statement of Proposition 20.5 holds, where we construct the rigidification by pullback.
To complete the construction of 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim}, one needs to extend the statement to the category ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. Notice that the pullback is induced from maps between domain moduli. Hence the construction of the relative NC structure for 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1} can be canonically lifted to 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim}. To extend the smoothing, notice that for each p,qp,q, the ambient space associated with p<qp<q in 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} is a topological Gp​q2G_{pq}^{2}-principal bundle over the ambient space associated with p<qp<q in 𝔽^1\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}. One can always use the group actions to construct smooth bundle structures inductively, hence 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} is smoothed. Then using the stabilization structure between 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} and 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim}, one can induce a canonical smooth structure on 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim}. Hence the statement is also true within the category ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}. Lastly, the NC structure construction is quite elementary and can also be respected.
∎
Proof of Proposition 12.2.
Using the notations introduced in Proposition 20.5, recall that the flow categories 𝔽~1,𝔽~2\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{2} enriched in ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} are obtained as quotients of the flow categories 𝔽^1,𝔽^2\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1},\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{2} enriched in ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. We can use the intermediate flow category 𝔽^∼\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\sim} to provide the desired construction. Indeed, recall that the Floer flow category requires passing to the quotient under the ℝ{\mathbb{R}}-translation action if the energy is strictly greater than 00. To obtain the lift of the diagonal bimodule Δ𝔽​𝔽\mathbb{\Delta}^{\mathbb{FF}}, we take the normally complex Kuranishi spaces before taking the quotient. By passing to the orbifold quotient, we finish the proof.
∎
In fact we can also prove that given a pair of integral actions 𝒜𝔽Ωi{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega_{i}}, i=1,2i=1,2, the double-framed construction together with FOP perturbation produces a chain complex C⁡(𝔽)C({\mathbb{F}}) which is well-defined up to homotopy given by a continuation map also defined via a double-framed construction. The proof of Proposition 12.2 can be viewed as a special case of this fact.
20.4. Multimodules
Compared with flow categories, for multimodules and homotopies, the lateral lines specified in Definition 14.8 may not be homotopically unique. Note that under the double-frame construction, we need to use the lateral lines from two different versions simultaneously to define concatenation maps of the framings. They exactly facilitate the construction of the doubly-thickened moduli spaces.
Proof of Proposition 12.3.
We only present the proof in the first situation; the second situation (the Poincaré duality multimodule) only differs in notations. Fix an outercollaring width. For any involved flow category 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}, the double-framed construction produces AMS lifts 𝔽^double\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{\rm double} (to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}), which depends on choices made in the construction. Two particular choices as described above are the “pullbacks” from each single-framed versions, denoted by
𝔽^(0)double,\displaystyle\ \hat{\mathbb{F}}_{(0)}^{{\rm double}},\
𝔽^(1)double.\displaystyle\ \hat{\mathbb{F}}_{(1)}^{{\rm double}}.
Now turn to the multimodule 𝕏{\mathbb{X}}. Starting from ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω1⊕Ω2,𝕏{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega_{1}\oplus\Omega_{2},{\mathbb{X}}}. For any collection of double-framed AMS lifts
𝔽^1double,…,𝔽^mdouble,𝔽^double′\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{\rm double},\ \ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}^{\rm double},\ \hat{\mathbb{F}}^{{}^{\prime}{\rm double}}
then one can construct a double-framed AMS lift
𝕏^double\hat{\mathbb{X}}^{\rm double}
as a multimodule over (𝔽^1double,…,𝔽^mdouble,𝔽^double′)(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{\rm double},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m}^{\rm double};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{{}^{\prime}{\rm double}}). Moreover, the construction is compatible with continuation maps connecting different double-framed AMS lifts of each individual flow category.
Notice that one has two particular situations of 𝕏^double\hat{\mathbb{X}}^{\rm double} coming from pulling back the single-framed construction 𝕏^(s)double\hat{\mathbb{X}}^{\rm double}_{(s)} for s=0,1s=0,1, which are, respectively, multimodules over (𝔽^1,(s)double,…,𝔽^m,(s)double,𝔽^(s)double′)(\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{1,(s)}^{{\rm double}},\ldots,\hat{\mathbb{F}}_{m,(s)}^{\rm double};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{{}^{\prime}{\rm double}}_{(s)}). Now let Δ^(01)𝔽j​𝔽j\hat{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{j}\mathbb{F}_{j}}_{(01)} and Δ^(10)𝔽′​𝔽′\hat{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}_{(10)} be the double-framed AMS lift of the diagonal bimodules. Then the double-framed concatenation/gluing produces a homotopy from
(Δ^(01)𝔽1​𝔽1×⋯×Δ^(01)𝔽m​𝔽m)∘𝕏^(1)double∘Δ^(10)𝔽′​𝔽′\left(\hat{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{1}{\mathbb{F}}_{1}}_{(01)}\times\cdots\times\hat{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{m}{\mathbb{F}}_{m}}_{(01)}\right)\circ\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{(1)}^{\rm double}\circ\hat{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}{\mathbb{F}}^{\prime}}_{(10)}
to 𝕏^(1)double\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{(1)}^{\rm double}. This requires extending the proof of Theorem 12.4 provided in the last section to the double-framed setting, which is nothing more complicated. Passing to the quotient via the functor ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}, one obtains a homotopy exactly expected in Proposition 12.3.
∎
21. AMS Construction for Other Flow categories, Multimodules, and Homotopies
In this section we discuss the AMS construction for flow categories etc. which are not from smooth Floer domains.
21.1. Pearly flow category
Recall that the Pearly flow category ℙ\mathbb{P} is associated to an almost Kähler manifold (X,ω,J)(X,\omega,J) and a Morse–Smale pair (f,g)(f,g) on XX. The object set is
Ob​ℙ=crit​f×Π\displaystyle\ {\rm Ob}\mathbb{P}={\rm crit}f\times\Pi\
where​Π=π2​(X)ker​c1∩ker​ω.\displaystyle\ {\rm where}\ \Pi=\frac{\pi_{2}(X)}{{\rm ker}c_{1}\cap{\rm ker}\omega}.
An object is written as x=(x¯,ax)x=(\underline{\smash{x}},a_{x}) where x¯∈crit​f\underline{\smash{x}}\in{\rm crit}f and ax∈Πa_{x}\in\Pi. We will construct AMS lifts of outercollarings of ℙ\mathbb{P} as declared in Theorem 12.7. The main difference from the case of the Floer flow category is that the boundary strata of moduli spaces are given by fiber products instead of direct products.
21.1.1. Fibered topological spaces, Kuranishi spaces, and derived orbifolds
Definition 21.1.
Let YY be a smooth manifold (without boundary and corners).
(1)
Let 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(Y) be the regular stratification category whose objects are pairs (N,f−,f+)(N,f_{-},f_{+}) where N∈Ob​𝐓𝐨𝐩¯N\in{\rm Ob}\underline{\smash{\bf Top}} and f±:N→Yf_{\pm}:N\to Y is a pair of continuous maps. A morphism in 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(Y) from (N1,f1,±)(N_{1},f_{1,\pm}) to (N2,f2,±)(N_{2},f_{2,\pm}) is a morphism of stratified spaces ρ:N1→N2\rho:N_{1}\to N_{2} such that the following diagram commutes.
N1\textstyle{N_{1}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}f1,±\scriptstyle{f_{1,\pm}}ρ\scriptstyle{\rho}Y\textstyle{Y\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}IdY\scriptstyle{{\rm Id}_{Y}}N2\textstyle{N_{2}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}f2,±\scriptstyle{f_{2,\pm}}Y\textstyle{Y}
The (non-symmetric) product of (N1,f1,±)(N_{1},f_{1,\pm}) and (N2,f2,±)(N_{2},f_{2,\pm}) is the fiber product
(N1​×𝑌​N2,π1∗​f1,−,π2∗​f2,+):=(N1​×𝑌f1,+​N2f2,−,π1∗​f1,−,π2∗​f2,+).\left(N_{1}\underset{Y}{\times}N_{2},\ \pi_{1}^{*}f_{1,-},\ \pi_{2}^{*}f_{2,+}\right):=\left(N_{1}\ {}_{f_{1,+}}\underset{Y}{\times}{}_{f_{2,-}}N_{2},\ \pi_{1}^{*}f_{1,-},\ \pi_{2}^{*}f_{2,+}\right).
The monoidal unit is (Y,IdY,IdY)(Y,{\rm Id}_{Y},{\rm Id}_{Y}).
(2)
Let 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}(Y) be the regular stratification category whose objects are (K,f−,f+)(K,f_{-},f_{+}) where K=(G,V,E,S)K=(G,V,E,S) is a Kuranishi space and f±:V→Yf_{\pm}:V\to Y is a pair of GG-invariant topological submersions. Let 𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}(Y) be the corresponding category of smooth Kuranishi spaces together with smooth submersions to YY. Let 𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NC​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}^{\rm NC}(Y) be the subcategory whose objects are smooth normally complex Kuranishi spaces with GG-invariant submersions. Let 𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}(Y) be the category of relatively smooth Kuranishi spaces K/B=(G,V/B,E,S)K/B=(G,V/B,E,S) together with GG-invariant maps f±:V→Yf_{\pm}:V\to Y such that they are fiberwise submersions. Let 𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NC​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}^{\rm NC}(Y) be the subcategory where the relative Kuranishi spaces are equipped with relative NC structures.
(3)
Let 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}(Y) be the category whose objects are pairs (𝒟,f−,f+)({\mathcal{D}},f_{-},f_{+}) where 𝒟=(𝒰,ℰ,𝒮){\mathcal{D}}=({\mathcal{U}},{\mathcal{E}},{\mathcal{S}}) is a derived orbifold and f±:𝒰→Yf_{\pm}:{\mathcal{U}}\to Y are smooth submersions. Let 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NC​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}(Y) be the category whose objects are (𝒟,f−,f+)({\mathcal{D}},f_{-},f_{+}) where 𝒟{\mathcal{D}} is an NC derived orbifold and f±:𝒰→Yf_{\pm}:{\mathcal{U}}\to Y are smooth submersions.
Remark 21.2.
Unlike the presumed stable complex versions, the monoidal structure given by fiber products in the NC versions (𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NC​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}^{\rm NC}(Y), 𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NC​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}^{\rm NC}(Y), 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NC​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}(Y)) does not require the almost complex structure on YY because YY is assumed to be a manifold.
Notice that one can also talk about collared and rigidified versions of 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯​(𝐘),𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}(Y),\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}(Y), and 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}(Y).
One needs to generalize the discussion of stable smoothings of topological Kuranishi spaces to the category 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯​(𝐘)\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}(Y).
Definition 21.3.
A stable smoothing of an object (K,f±)∈𝐊𝐮𝐫¯​(𝐘)(K,f_{\pm})\in\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}(Y) where K=(G,V,E,S)K=(G,V,E,S) consists of a unitary representation WW of GG, a GG-smoothing on V×WV\times W, a GG-invariant extension f~±:V×W→Y\tilde{f}_{\pm}:V\times W\to Y of f±:V≅V×{0}→Yf_{\pm}:V\cong V\times\{0\}\to Y such that f~±\tilde{f}_{\pm} are smooth submersions.
Lemma 21.4 (Stable smoothing with maps).
(cf. [3, Lemma 4.5])
Let VV be a smooth GG-manifold and f0:V→Yf_{0}:V\to Y be a continuous GG-invariant map. Then there exists a unitary representation WW of GG, a GG-smoothing on V×WV\times W which is in the same stable isotopy class of the given smooth structure on VV, and a smooth submersion f~:V×W→Y\tilde{f}:V\times W\to Y whose restriction to V×{0}V\times\{0\} coincides with f0f_{0}.
Proof.
The proof is essentially that of [3, Lemma 4.5], which we reproduce using our language. Choose a Riemannian metric on YY. Then one can choose a smooth GG-invariant approximation f:V→Yf:V\to Y and a smooth GG-invariant function ϵ:V→ℝ+\epsilon:V\to{\mathbb{R}}_{+} such that for all v∈Vv\in V, there is a unique shortest geodesic of length shorter than ϵ⁡(v)\epsilon(v) connecting f0​(v)f_{0}(v) and f⁡(v)f(v), and such that the exponential map expf⁡(v)⁡ξ\exp_{f(v)}\xi is well-defined for ξ\xi in the ϵ⁡(v)\epsilon(v)-ball of Tf⁡(v)​YT_{f(v)}Y. Then there is a smooth equivariant bundle map ρ:f∗​T​Y→f∗​T​Y\rho:f^{*}TY\to f^{*}TY compressing f∗​T​Yf^{*}TY diffeomorphically into the ϵ\epsilon-disk bundle. Therefore the map
f~:f∗​T​Y→Y,f~​(v,ξ)=expf⁡(v)⁡(ρ⁡(ξ)).\tilde{f}:f^{*}TY\to Y,\ \tilde{f}(v,\xi)=\exp_{f(v)}(\rho(\xi)).
is a smooth submersion. Choose another smooth (real) GG-vector bundle E→VE\to V such that
E⊕f∗​T​Y≅V×WE\oplus f^{*}TY\cong V\times W
for some unitary representation WW of GG. f~\tilde{f} clearly extends to a smooth GG-equivariant map from V×WV\times W to YY, which is still a smooth submersion.
We would like to define a self-homeomorphism of V×WV\times W to pullback the smooth structure on V×WV\times W. Indeed, we can write
f0​(v)=expf⁡(v)⁡ξ0​(v),ξ0​(v)∈Tf⁡(v)​Y.f_{0}(v)=\exp_{f(v)}\xi_{0}(v),\ \xi_{0}(v)\in T_{f(v)}Y.
Define a nonlinear bundle map
F:f∗​T​Y→f∗​T​Y,(v,ξ)↦(v,ξ+ξ0​(v)).F:f^{*}TY\to f^{*}TY,\ (v,\xi)\mapsto(v,\xi+\xi_{0}(v)).
Extend it to a smooth map V×W→V×WV\times W\to V\times W which is the identity on the summand EE. Then we can see the following diagram commutes.
V\textstyle{V\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}f0\scriptstyle{f_{0}}v↦(v,0)\scriptstyle{v\mapsto(v,0)}Y\textstyle{Y}V×W\textstyle{V\times W\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}F\scriptstyle{F}V×W\textstyle{V\times W\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}f~\scriptstyle{\tilde{f}}
Therefore, f0f_{0} is extended to a smooth submersion from V×WV\times W to YY. Lastly, the smoothing on V×WV\times W is in the same stable isotopy class because the choices made in the proof, especially the smooth approximation ff of f0f_{0}, can all be made isotopic.
∎
21.1.2. The monotone flow category of holomorphic cylinders
Let (X,ω,J)(X,\omega,J) be an almost Kähler manifold. Denote
Πeff:={a∈Π|ω⁡(a)>0}∪{0}\Pi^{\rm eff}:=\Big\{a\in\Pi\ |\ \omega(a)>0\Big\}\cup\{0\}
which is an abelian monoid whose Grothendieck construction is Π\Pi.
We would like to generalize the notion of monotone flow categories. Recall that a monotone flow category enriched in 𝐂¯\underline{\smash{\bf C}} contains objects Md𝕗M_{d}^{\mathbb{f}} indexed by d∈ℤ≥0d\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}. In the current case, one can define a generalization consisting of objects Ma𝕗M_{a}^{\mathbb{f}} indexed by a∈Πeffa\in\Pi^{\rm eff}, together with structural maps from the fiber product of Ma𝕗M_{a}^{\mathbb{f}} and Mb𝕗M_{b}^{\mathbb{f}} over a space to Ma+b𝕗M_{a+b}^{\mathbb{f}} satisfying a version of associativity condition. We describe such a monotone flow category 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X)\mathbb{cyl}(X) enriched in 𝐂¯=𝐓𝐨𝐩¯​(𝐗)\underline{\smash{\bf C}}=\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(X) by defining
Ma𝕔​𝕪​𝕝(X):=(⨆ω⁡(A)=aℳ¯(X,J,A)ℝ0,2,ev−,ev+)∈Ob𝐓𝐨𝐩¯(𝐗),M_{a}^{\mathbb{cyl}}(X):=\left(\bigsqcup_{\omega(A)=a}\overline{\mathcal{M}}{}_{0,2}^{\mathbb{R}}(X,J,A),\ {\rm ev}_{-},\ {\rm ev}_{+}\right)\in{\rm Ob}\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(X),
where ev±{\rm ev}_{\pm} are the evaluation maps at the marked points. Then for a,b∈Πeffa,b\in\Pi^{\rm eff}, there is a natural map
Ma𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X)​×𝑋​Mb𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X)→Ma+b𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X).M_{a}^{\mathbb{cyl}}(X)\underset{X}{\times}M_{b}^{\mathbb{cyl}}(X)\to M_{a+b}^{\mathbb{cyl}}(X).
These structures define the monotone flow category 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X)\mathbb{cyl}(X). By taking the Grothendieck construction, it induces an ordinary flow category
ℂ​𝕪​𝕝​(X)\mathbb{Cyl}(X)
called the cylinder flow category enriched in 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯​(𝐗)\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(X) whose object set is Π\Pi.
To carry out the AMS construction, we first choose an integral symplectic form Ω∈Ω2​(X)\Omega\in\Omega^{2}(X) satisfying 1) JJ is tamed by Ω\Omega and 2) Ker​Ω=ker​ω⊆π2​(X){\rm Ker}\Omega={\rm ker}\omega\subseteq\pi_{2}(X). Then for each a∈Πeffa\in\Pi^{\rm eff}, there is an associated integer d=dad=d_{a}. As JJ is tamed by Ω\Omega, da≥0d_{a}\geq 0.
Proposition 21.5.
There exists a lift 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝^​(X)\widehat{\mathbb{cyl}}(X) of the outercollaring 𝕔⌊𝕪𝕝(X){}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{cyl}(X) to 𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}(X) as a monotone flow category supported over Πeff\Pi^{\rm eff}.
Proof.
We first describe a monotone flow category of curves ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}, which is the restriction of ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom} (specified in Section 14) to open sets induced from Ω\Omega. For each dd, let
AdΩ⊆AdA_{d}^{\Omega}\subseteq A_{d}
to be the Alexandrov open subset of partitions d=d0+⋯+dld=d_{0}+\cdots+d_{l} such that for each dld_{l}, there exists al∈Πeffa_{l}\in\Pi^{\rm eff} with dl=Ω⁡(al)d_{l}=\Omega(a_{l}). Recall that the monotone flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom} gives objects
𝒞d=(𝒢d,Bd,Cd)∈Ob​𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯.{\mathcal{C}}_{d}=({\mathcal{G}}_{d},B_{d},C_{d})\in{\rm Ob}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}.
For a∈Πeffa\in\Pi^{\rm eff}, let BaΩ⊆BΩ⁡(a)B_{a}^{\Omega}\subseteq B_{\Omega(a)} be the union of strata prescribed by AdΩA_{d}^{\Omega}, which is open and 𝒢d{\mathcal{G}}_{d}-invariant. Define
𝒞aΩ∈Ob⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{\mathcal{C}}_{a}^{\Omega}\in{\rm Ob}{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}
to be the restriction of 𝒞Ω⁡(a){\mathcal{C}}_{\Omega(a)} to BaΩB_{a}^{\Omega}. Then one obtains a monotone flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞Ω,𝕔​𝕪​𝕝{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\Omega,\mathbb{cyl}}.
Then one has a corresponding monotone flow category of framed maps consisting of objects
Mapafr(X)→BaΩ⌊{\rm Map}_{a}^{\rm fr}(X)\to{}_{\lfloor}B_{a}^{\Omega}
whose fiber of ϕ∈⌊BaΩ\phi\in{}_{\lfloor}B_{a}^{\Omega} is the space of pairs (u,F)(u,F) where u:C̊ϕ→Xu:\mathring{C}_{\phi}\to X is a smooth map on each irreducible component which extends continuously to CϕC_{\phi} and which converges exponentially at cylindrical nodes and markings and where FF is a frame of the holomorphic line bundle Lu,Ω→CϕL_{u,\Omega}\to C_{\phi}.
One can also choose a collection of transverse thickening data
νa:Wa→Γc(C̊aΩ⌊×X,Λ⌊C̊aΩ/⌊BaΩ0,1⊗TX)\nu_{a}:W_{a}\to\Gamma_{c}({}_{\lfloor}\mathring{C}_{a}^{\Omega}\times X,\Lambda_{{}_{\lfloor}\mathring{C}_{a}^{\Omega}/{}_{\lfloor}B_{a}^{\Omega}}^{0,1}\otimes TX)
which are collared and respect the structural maps. Here WaW_{a} is a collection of unitary representations of GΩ⁡(a)G_{\Omega(a)}. On the other hand, one can choose a group reduction scheme, given by a collection of continuous maps
λa:Mapafr​(X)→Qa≅𝒢Ω⁡(a)/GΩ⁡(a).\lambda_{a}:{\rm Map}_{a}^{\rm fr}(X)\to Q_{a}\cong{\mathcal{G}}_{\Omega(a)}/G_{\Omega(a)}.
Then one obtains a corresponding thickening
Ka=(Ga,Va,Ea,Sa)∈Ob𝐊𝐮𝐫¯⌊K_{a}=(G_{a},V_{a},E_{a},S_{a})\in{\rm Ob}{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}
where
Va={(ϕ,u,F,e)|(ϕ,u,F)∈Mapafr(X),e∈Wa,ϕ=ϕF∈BaΩ⌊,∂¯Ju+νa(e)=0},V_{a}=\Big\{(\phi,u,F,e)\ |\ (\phi,u,F)\in{\rm Map}_{a}^{\rm fr}(X),\ e\in W_{a},\ \phi=\phi_{F}\in{}_{\lfloor}B_{a}^{\Omega},\ \overline{\partial}_{J}u+\nu_{a}(e)=0\Big\},
with the natural GaG_{a}-action, EaE_{a} is the trivial bundle with fiber Wa⊕QaW_{a}\oplus Q_{a}, and SaS_{a} is the section given by
Sa​(ϕ,u,F,e)=(e,λa​(ϕ,u,F)).S_{a}(\phi,u,F,e)=(e,\lambda_{a}(\phi,u,F)).
Similar to Theorem 15.15, the natural map
Sa−1(0)/Ga→Ma𝕔​𝕪​𝕝⌊(X)S_{a}^{-1}(0)/G_{a}\to{}_{\lfloor}M_{a}^{\mathbb{cyl}}(X)
is an isomorphism of orbispaces. By an abuse of notation, let VaV_{a} denote the regular locus for the operator ∂¯J​u+νa​(e)=0\overline{\partial}_{J}u+\nu_{a}(e)=0, i.e., the subspace such that the linearization of this equation is surjective. Then, it contains the zero locus by the transversality assumption. Then one obtains a lift of the monotone flow category 𝕔⌊𝕪𝕝(X){}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{cyl}(X) to the category 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig}(X). In the same way as argued in Subsection 15.4, the lift is in fact enriched in 𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}(X). We denote this lift by
𝕔​𝕪​𝕝^​(X).\widehat{\mathbb{cyl}}(X).
The construct of normal complex structure is slightly easier than the case of Floer flow categories. Indeed, because we do not have Hamiltonian perturbations, the (vertical) linearized operators are the Cauchy–Riemann operators
Du,e=[Du​∂¯J+Du​νa​(u,e)+νa​(u)]:Ω0​(Cϕ,u∗​T​X)⊕Wa→Ω0,1​(Cϕ,u∗​T​X)D_{u,e}=\left[D_{u}\overline{\partial}_{J}+D_{u}\nu_{a}(u,e)+\nu_{a}(u)\right]:\Omega^{0}(C_{\phi},u^{*}TX)\oplus W_{a}\to\Omega^{0,1}(C_{\phi},u^{*}TX)
where WaW_{a} is a complex representation. Recall that the canonical linearization is calculated by the Levi–Civita connection on XX induced from the symplectic form and the almost complex structure, which is not necessarily complex-linear. However, one can choose a 1-parameter family of linear operators connecting Du,eD_{u,e} to a complex linear one, without using the complicated interpolation argument as in the Floer case. This means for each individual moduli space, one has a canonical homotopy class of isomorphisms between the vertical tangent bundle and a complex vector bundle. One can choose concrete isomorphisms inductively. This provides a lift to 𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}(X).
The smoothing procedure is slightly different from the previous case as we also need to make the evaluation maps smooth. However, by Lemma 21.4, one can perform stable smoothing on (Ka,ev±)(K_{a},{\rm ev}_{\pm}) so that not only the Kuranishi spaces become smooth, but also the evaluation maps become smooth submersions. Then following the same inductive procedure, after stabilization, one obtains a lift to the category 𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}(X). Together with the stable complex structures on the domain flow categories, this is a lift to 𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}(X).
∎
Proof of Theorem 12.7.
We first describe the lift of the pearly flow category ℙ{\mathbb{P}}. Choose a lift 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝^​(X)\widehat{\mathbb{cyl}}(X) provided by Proposition 21.5. By taking quotient, one obtains a monotone flow category enriched in 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}(X), which induces an ordinary flow category, denoted by ℂ​𝕪​𝕝~​(X)\widetilde{\mathbb{Cyl}}(X), whose objects are elements of Π\Pi.
Then one can obtain a lift of the corresponding outercollaring of ℙ{\mathbb{P}} by “inserting flow lines.” We do this inductively. In the lowest energy case, one only needs to add flow rays at the negative and positive ends to obtain Kuranishi charts of moduli spaces labelled by a pair of critical points. In higher energy case, there are configurations where in the interior there are gradient segments of positive length. An inductive scheme can be designed in a rather elementary way to produce inductively all charts for involved moduli spaces. Hence one obtains a lift of the outercollaring of ℙ{\mathbb{P}} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} (inserting flow lines does not affect the NC structure).
Next, we discuss the regularization of the bimodule Δℙ​ℙ\mathbb{\Delta}^{\mathbb{PP}}. In fact, one can take different Morse–Smale pairs and different almost complex structures to define ℙ\mathbb{P} and consider the bimodule as an interpolation between them. However, we choose the same one to simplify the notations.
The construction is very similar to the regularization of the Pearly flow category. First, there is a monotone bimodule Δ𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X)\mathbb{\Delta}^{\mathbb{cyl}(X)} given by holomorphic cylinders which have a parametrized principal component. This is a monotone bimodule over (𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X);𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X))(\mathbb{cyl}(X);\mathbb{cyl}(X)).
Then after outercollaring, following the same procedure as the proof of Proposition 21.5, one obtains an AMS lift to 𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}(X), denoted by Δ^𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X)\widehat{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{\mathbb{cyl}(X)}. After taking quotient, one obtains a bimodule Δ~𝕔​𝕪​𝕝ℙ​(X)\widetilde{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{\mathbb{cyl}^{\mathbb{P}}(X)} over (𝕔​𝕪​𝕝~​(X);𝕔​𝕪​𝕝~​(X))(\widetilde{\mathbb{cyl}}(X);\widetilde{\mathbb{cyl}}(X)) enriched in 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}(X). Then using the fact that evaluation maps are smooth submersions, by inserting Morse flow lines, one obtains a lift of ⌊Δℙ​ℙ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{\Delta}^{\mathbb{PP}} as a bimodule over (ℙ~;ℙ~)(\tilde{\mathbb{P}};\tilde{\mathbb{P}}). This proves the second item of Theorem 12.7.
∎
21.2. Deformed Morse-to-Morse bimodule
The regularization of the Morse-to-Morse bimodule was discussed in [14] using the original perturbation from [3].
Proposition 21.6.
Upon choosing an integral symplectic form Ω\Omega, there exists a lift of Δ𝕄​𝕄\Delta^{\mathbb{MM}} of the deformed Morse-to-Morse bimodule to 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig} as a bimodule over (𝕄;𝕄)(\mathbb{M};\mathbb{M}) (without outercollaring).
Proof.
For each dd, consider the moduli space ℳ¯0,2​(ℂ​ℙd,d)\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,2}(\mathbb{CP}^{d},d) of 2-pointed stable holomorphic spheres in ℂ​ℙd\mathbb{CP}^{d}. Choose the negative convention; the other choice works as well. Let Bd=Bd−B_{d}=B_{d}^{-} be the subset of curves whose images are not contained in any hyperplane and whose value at the negative end is [1,0,…,0][1,0,\ldots,0]. Then consider the curve 𝒞d=(𝒢d,Bd,Cd){\mathcal{C}}_{d}=({\mathcal{G}}_{d},B_{d},C_{d}). Notice that this is a family of curves without boundary or corners.
Now choose an integral symplectic form Ω\Omega. For each a∈Πeffa\in\Pi^{\rm eff}, denote d=dad=d_{a}. Consider the space of framed maps
Mapdfr={(ϕ,u,F)|ϕ∈Bd,u:Cϕ→X,F=(f0,…,fd)isabasisofH0(Lu,Ω)}.{\rm Map}_{d}^{\rm fr}=\Big\{(\phi,u,F)\ |\ \phi\in B_{d},u:C_{\phi}\to X,\ F=(f_{0},\ldots,f_{d})\ {\rm is\ a\ basis\ of\ }H^{0}(L_{u,\Omega})\Big\}.
Choose a group reduction scheme λd:Mapdfr→Qd\lambda_{d}:{\rm Map}_{d}^{\rm fr}\to Q_{d} and a transverse perturbation
ι:W→Γc​(C̊d×X,ΛC̊d/Bd0,1⊗T​X).\iota:W\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{d}\times X,\Lambda^{0,1}_{\mathring{C}_{d}/B_{d}}\otimes TX).
This induces a topological Kuranishi space
Kd=(Gd,Vd,Ed,Sd)K_{d}=(G_{d},V_{d},E_{d},S_{d})
with ambient space
Vd={(ϕ,u,F,e)|(ϕ,u,F)∈Mapd,e∈Wa,ϕ=ϕF∈Bd,∂¯Ju+ι(e)=0},V_{d}=\Big\{(\phi,u,F,e)\ |\ (\phi,u,F)\in{\rm Map}_{d},\ e\in W_{a},\ \phi=\phi_{F}\in B_{d},\ \overline{\partial}_{J}u+\iota(e)=0\Big\},
obstruction bundle Ed=W⊕QdE_{d}=W\oplus Q_{d}, and Kuranishi section
Sd​(ϕ,u,F,e)=(e,λd​(ϕ,u,F)).S_{d}(\phi,u,F,e)=(e,\lambda_{d}(\phi,u,F)).
It also comes with a ref-C∞,1C^{\infty,1}-structure on Vd/BdV_{d}/B_{d} as well as continuous evaluation maps ev±:Vd→X{\rm ev}_{\pm}:V_{d}\to X. Then using Lemma 21.4, one can find a stable smoothing of VdV_{d} making the evaluation maps submersive.
Last, using the submersiveness of the evaluation maps, one obtains a lift of the bimodule Δ𝕄​𝕄\mathbb{\Delta}^{\mathbb{MM}} by taking fiber products with stable/unstable manifolds of the Morse flow.
∎
Remark 21.7.
In [14] one considered the Morse-to-Floer and Floer-to-Morse bimodules and their concatenation along the Floer flow category. However, their concatenation along the Morse flow category is difficult to regularize (the codimension two gluing is hard to fit into the framework of flow bimodules). In this paper, we do not consider these two bimodules and their concatenations. The Morse-to-Morse bimodule will arise from the concatenations of the Morse-to-Pearly and the Pearly-to-Morse bimodules, whose regularization will be addressed later.
21.3. Pearly-to-Morse and Morse-to-Pearly bimodules
In this subsection we regularize the two bimodules shown in the title. To simplify the notations, we will only use a single integral symplectic form Ω∈Ω2​(X)\Omega\in\Omega^{2}(X) which is a multiple of a rational approximation of ω\omega which also tames JJ. The case with different choices of Ω\Omega can be discussed in a similar way as the case of pair-of-pants multimodules.
21.3.1. The domains
The model for the Morse flow category can be viewed as a monotone flow category over the trivial monoid {0}\{0\}. Let such a trivial monotone flow category be 𝕠\mathbb{o}, which has only one object M0𝕠M_{0}^{\mathbb{o}} chosen to be a singleton in the category 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}. We would like to define a monotone flow bimodule over ℤ≥0{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 0}. For each dd, we consider the family of curves
𝒞dℙ​𝕄=(𝒢d,Bdℙ​𝕄,Cdℙ​𝕄){\mathcal{C}}_{d}^{\mathbb{PM}}=({\mathcal{G}}_{d},B_{d}^{\mathbb{PM}},C_{d}^{\mathbb{PM}})
where the space of curves Bdℙ​𝕄B_{d}^{\mathbb{PM}} in ℂ​ℙd\mathbb{CP}^{d} is different from previous cases. Indeed, consider the moduli space of parametrized holomorphic cylinders
u:ℝ×S1→ℂ​ℙdu:{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}\to\mathbb{CP}^{d}
of degree dd. When compactifying this space, the bubbling near the negative and positive ends is treated differently. Near the negative ends, the broken pieces are considered modulo only the real translation; near the positive end, the broken pieces are considered modulo ℂ∗{\mathbb{C}}^{*}, i.e., translations and rotations. The domain of a point in the compactification still has two distinguished points: z−z_{-} and z+z_{+}. Then let Bdℙ​𝕄B_{d}^{\mathbb{PM}} be the subspace in the compactification satisfying 1) the image is not contained in any hyperplane and 2) the map satisfies the positive:
u⁡(z+)=[0,0,…,0,1]∈ℙd.u(z_{+})=[0,0,\ldots,0,1]\in{\mathbb{P}}^{d}.
The structural map of this bimodule only contains the negative part as we view it as a bimodule with one side the trivial flow category: namely, given d,d′d,d^{\prime}, there is a morphism
𝒞d×𝒞d′ℙ​𝕄→𝒞d+d′ℙ​𝕄.{\mathcal{C}}_{d}\times{\mathcal{C}}_{d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{PM}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{d+d^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{PM}}.
The construction is similar to before and hence skipped. One can check that the collection of equivariant families of curves 𝒞dℙ​𝕄\mathcal{C}_{d}^{\mathbb{PM}} defines a monotone bimodule.
21.3.2. Cylinders in XX
We would like to construct monotone bimodules enriched in 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC​(𝐗)\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}(X). For the Morse side, there is still the trivial monotone flow category with a single object whose only morphism space is the singleton, i.e., the triple
(X,Id,Id)(X,{\rm Id},{\rm Id})
where XX is regarded as a normally complex derived orbifold. On the other hand, one has constructed the lift 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝~​(X)\widetilde{\mathbb{cyl}}(X) of 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X)\mathbb{cyl}(X) to 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}(X). By considering parametrized cylinders in XX, one can easily formulate a monotone bimodule
𝕔​𝕪​𝕝ℙ​𝕄​(X)\mathbb{cyl}^{\mathbb{PM}}(X)
over (𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X);𝕠)(\mathbb{cyl}(X);\mathbb{o}) consisting of moduli spaces of parametrized cylinders in XX with two marked points where the compactification at negative and positive marked points is taken differently.
Proposition 21.8.
Given an AMS lift 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝~​(X)\widetilde{\mathbb{cyl}}(X) of the outercollaring 𝕔⌊𝕪𝕝(X){}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{cyl}(X), there exists a lift of the outercollaring 𝕔⌊𝕪𝕝(X)ℙ​𝕄{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{cyl}{}^{\mathbb{PM}}(X) to 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}(X), denoted by 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝~(X)ℙ​𝕄\widetilde{\mathbb{cyl}}{}^{\mathbb{PM}}(X), as a monotone bimodule over (𝕔​𝕪​𝕝~​(X);𝕠)(\widetilde{\mathbb{cyl}}(X);\mathbb{o}).
Sketch of Proof.
It is completely parallel to the proof of Proposition 21.5.
∎
Corollary 21.9.
Given an AMS lift ℙ~\tilde{\mathbb{P}} of the pearly flow category ℙ{\mathbb{P}} subject to a fixed outercollaring width and an integral symplectic form, there exists a lift 𝔹~ℙ​𝕄\tilde{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{PM}} resp. 𝔹~𝕄​ℙ\tilde{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MP}} of the corresponding collaring of 𝔹ℙ​𝕄\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{PM}} resp. 𝔹𝕄​ℙ\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MP}} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as a bimodule over (ℙ~;𝕄⌊)(\tilde{\mathbb{P}};{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{M}) resp. over (𝕄⌊;ℙ~)({}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{M}};\tilde{\mathbb{P}}). Moreover, any two such lifts are homotopic.
Proof.
We work over the domain bimodule 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝~(X)ℙ​𝕄\widetilde{\mathbb{cyl}}{}^{\mathbb{PM}}(X) (and in parallel 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝~​𝕄​ℙ​(X)\widetilde{\mathbb{cyl}}{\mathbb{MP}}(X)). Extend thickening data used in the construction of ℙ~\tilde{\mathbb{P}} to thickening data over 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝~​ℙ​𝕄​(X)\widetilde{\mathbb{cyl}}{\mathbb{PM}}(X). The construction of NC structures and stable smoothing can all be reproduced in the same way as before. This provides the AMS lifts of outercollarings of 𝔹ℙ​𝕄\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{PM}} and 𝔹𝕄​ℙ\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MP}}.
∎
21.4. Pearly-to-Floer and Floer-to-Pearly bimodules
The AMS constructions for the bimodules 𝔹𝔽​ℙ\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{FP}} and 𝔹ℙ​𝔽\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{PF}} are slight variants of that for Δℙ​ℙ\mathbb{\Delta}^{\mathbb{PP}}. We describe in detail the construction for 𝔹ℙ​𝔽\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{PF}}.
21.4.1. A new category of fibered spaces
In order to deal with the mixture of fiber products (in the Pearly part) and direct products (in the Floer part), we introduce the space X+=X⊔{pt}X^{+}=X\sqcup\{{\rm pt}\} which is a smooth manifold of mixed dimensions. Then similar to Definition 21.1, one can consider the category 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯​(𝐗+)\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(X^{+}) whose objects are spaces with continuous maps to X+X^{+}, as well as the categories 𝐊𝐮𝐫¯​(𝐗+)\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}(X^{+}) and 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯​(𝐗+)\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}(X^{+}). Then there are natural functors
𝐓𝐨𝐩¯​(𝐗) 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯ 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯​(𝐗+) .\vbox{\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\kern 13.7361pt\hbox{\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\hbox{\vtop{\halign{\entry@#!@&&\entry@@#!@\cr&&\cr&&\crcr}}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern-13.7361pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(X)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 40.41243pt\raise-23.76886pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}{\hbox{\kern 51.79166pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}{\hbox{\kern 95.84721pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\kern 67.014pt\raise-23.76886pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\lx@xy@tip{1}\lx@xy@tip{-1}}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}\ignorespaces{\hbox{\lx@xy@drawline@}}{\hbox{\kern-3.0pt\raise-32.23112pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}{\hbox{\kern 37.7361pt\raise-32.23112pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(X^{+})}$}}}}}}}{\hbox{\kern 98.34721pt\raise-32.23112pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 3.0pt\raise-2.5pt\hbox{$\textstyle{}$}}}}}}}\ignorespaces}}}}}.
Similar functors exist for Kuranishi spaces or derived orbifolds.
Now consider the flow category ℂ​𝕪​𝕝​(X)\mathbb{Cyl}(X) (obtained from the monotone flow category 𝕔​𝕪​𝕝​(X)\mathbb{cyl}(X)), which can be viewed as enriched in 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯​(𝐗+)\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(X^{+}). Similarly, the Floer flow category 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} associated to a Hamiltonian HH and an almost complex structure JJ is also enriched in 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯​(𝐗+)\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}(X^{+}). Then the Floer data used for defining the bimodules 𝔹ℙ​𝔽\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{PF}} resp. 𝔹𝔽​ℙ\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{FP}} also induces a bimodule
ℂ𝕪𝕝ℙ​𝔽(X)resp.ℂ𝕪𝕝(X)𝔽​ℙ\mathbb{Cyl}^{\mathbb{PF}}(X)\ {\rm resp.}\ \mathbb{Cyl}{}^{\mathbb{FP}}(X)
over (ℂ​𝕪​𝕝​(X);𝔽)(\mathbb{Cyl}(X);\mathbb{F}) resp. over (𝔽;ℂ​𝕪​𝕝​(X))(\mathbb{F};\mathbb{Cyl}(X)).
Proposition 21.10.
Given an AMS lift ℂ​𝕪​𝕝~​(X)\widetilde{\mathbb{Cyl}}(X) of ℂ⌊𝕪𝕝(X){}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Cyl}(X) to 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC⌊(𝐗){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}(X) and an AMS lift 𝔽~\tilde{\mathbb{F}} of ⌊𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{F} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}, there exists a lift (called an AMS lift) of the outercollaring ℂ⌊𝕪𝕝(X)ℙ​𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Cyl}{}^{\mathbb{PF}}(X) resp. ℂ⌊𝕪𝕝(X)𝔽​ℙ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Cyl}{}^{\mathbb{FP}}(X) to 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯⌊(𝐗+)NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}{}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}(X^{+}), denoted by ℂ​𝕪​𝕝~(X)ℙ​𝔽\widetilde{\mathbb{Cyl}}{}^{\mathbb{PF}}(X) resp. ℂ​𝕪​𝕝~(X)𝔽​ℙ\widetilde{\mathbb{Cyl}}{}^{\mathbb{FP}}(X).
Sketch of Proof.
There is no essential difference from the previous cases.
∎
Corollary 21.11.
Given an AMS lift ℙ~\tilde{\mathbb{P}} of the outercollaring of the pearly flow category ℙ\mathbb{P} and an AMS lift 𝔽~\tilde{\mathbb{F}} of the Floer flow category, there exists a lift of ⌊𝔹ℙ​𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{PF}} resp. ⌊𝔹𝔽​ℙ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{FP}} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}.
Proof.
It follows from the same arguments as we have seen many times, building on Proposition 21.10. The only difference is that we should insert Morse flow lines on the pearly side to complete the construction.
∎
21.5. Morse-to-Floer and Floer-to-Morse bimodules
Now we consider the AMS lift of the bimodules 𝔹𝕄​𝔽\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF}} and 𝔹𝔽​𝕄\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{FM}}, which are responsible for the PSS and SSP maps claimed in Theorem E. The claim of such AMS lifts is stated as Theorem S. As the PSS map on the homology level is supposed to be canonical, we also need to compare different choices.
Proof of Theorem S.
We sketch the construction for 𝔹𝕄​𝔽\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF}}. The other case has no difference other than a simple reversal. See [14, Section 7] for a more explicit discussion in a slightly different framework.
By removing the Morse flow ray, the Morse-to-Floer bimodule 𝔹𝕄​𝔽{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF}} becomes the cigar bimodule 𝔹cigar\mathbb{B}^{\rm cigar}, which is enriched in Top⁡(X+){\rm Top}(X^{+}). Recall that it is a bimodule over (𝕆;𝔽)({\mathbb{O}};{\mathbb{F}}) where 𝕆{\mathbb{O}} is the Π\Pi-covering of the trivial flow category. Then the AMS construction is similar to that for the cigar bimodule 𝔹cigar\mathbb{B}^{\rm cigar}. When construct an AMS lift 𝔹~cigar\tilde{\mathbb{B}}^{\rm cigar} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} (which is covered by Theorem P), especially for smoothing, one can make the evaluation maps at the incoming marked point smooth submersions onto XX. Hence one obtains a lift, still denoted by 𝔹~cigar\tilde{\mathbb{B}}^{\rm cigar}, enriched in 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC⌊(𝐗+){}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}(X^{+}). Then by adding gradient rays, one obtains a lift 𝔹~𝕄​𝔽\tilde{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF}} to 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as a bimodule over (𝕄⌊;𝔽~)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{M};\tilde{\mathbb{F}}).
For the second item of Theorem S, one also needs to compare different choices of integral actions. This can be done using the double-framed construction introduced in Section 20 in a similar way as proving Proposition 12.3. We omit the details.
∎
Proof of Theorem 12.6.
For the concatenation 𝔹𝔽​𝔽′∘𝔹𝔽′​𝕄′\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{FF}^{\prime}}\circ\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{F^{\prime}}\mathbb{M}^{\prime}} at the Floer flow category and its homotopy to 𝔹𝔽​𝕄′\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{F}\mathbb{M}^{\prime}}, the corresponding AMS construction is similar to what is required for establishing the naturality of the continuation map. For the concatenation 𝔹𝔽​𝕄∘𝔹𝕄​𝕄′\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{FM}}\circ\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MM}^{\prime}} at the Morse flow category 𝕄\mathbb{M}, the construction is even simpler. We omit the details.
∎
21.6. Proof of Theorem T
We have constructed the lifts of flow categories and bimodules listed in the statement of Theorem T. We choose a common outercollaring width and a compatible set of integral actions. To finish the proof of Theorem T, one needs to establish corresponding lifts of homotopies involving certain concatenations and gluings. Notice that we only glue at the Floer flow category or the pearly flow category, but not the Morse flow category. We need to construct such homotopies for many triangles of the diagram (12.1). However, the constructions for each triangle have no substantial differences. Hence we only give proofs for two typical cases.
21.6.1. Concatenation at the Floer flow category
We prove the following statement.
Lemma 21.12.
Fix an outercollaring width and an integral action 𝒜𝔽Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega} which is compatible with all involved Floer data. Let 𝔽^\hat{\mathbb{F}} be an AMS lift of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} subject to the outercollaring width and 𝒜𝔽Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega}. Let ℙ^\hat{\mathbb{P}} be an AMS lift of the pearly flow category subject to the same outercollaring width and the integral symplectic form Ω\Omega. Let 𝔹^ℙ​𝔽\hat{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{PF}} be an AMS lift of 𝔹ℙ​𝔽{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{PF}} and 𝔹^𝔽​ℙ\hat{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{FP}} be an AMS lift of 𝔹𝔽​ℙ\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{FP}}. Let Δ^ℙ​ℙ\hat{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{\mathbb{PP}} be an AMS lift of the diagonal bimodule. Then there exists a concatenation 𝔹^ℙ​𝔽∘𝔹^𝔽​ℙ\hat{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{PF}}\circ\hat{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{FP}} and a homotopy from this concatenation to Δ^ℙ​ℙ\hat{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{\mathbb{PP}}.
Proof.
The construction of a concatenation 𝔹^ℙ​𝔽∘𝔹^𝔽​ℙ\hat{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{PF}}\circ\hat{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{FP}} is no different from other situations involving concatenating at a Floer flow category. The construction of the lift of the homotopy to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} also only differs in notation.
∎
21.6.2. Concatenation at the pearly flow category
The concatenation at the pearly flow category is slightly more complicated. We consider the reversed concatenation 𝔹𝔽​ℙ∘𝔹ℙ​𝔽{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{FP}}\circ\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{PF}}.
Notice that the homotopy between the concatenation 𝔹𝔽​ℙ∘𝔹ℙ​𝔽\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{FP}}\circ\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{PF}} and Δ𝔽​𝔽\mathbb{\Delta}^{\mathbb{FF}} is the union of two parts: the first part is when there are gradient flow segments of a positive total length (where the length is a parameter for the homotopy); the second part is when there are no gradient segments. See Figure 6 for an illustration. The boundary between the two parts can be viewed as another concatenation
ℂ​𝕪​𝕝𝔽​ℙ​(X)∘ℂ​𝕪​𝕝ℙ​𝔽​(X)\mathbb{Cyl}^{\mathbb{FP}}(X)\circ\mathbb{Cyl}^{\mathbb{PF}}(X)
at the flow category ℂ​𝕪​𝕝​(X)\mathbb{Cyl}(X). Notice that one has constructed AMS lifts ℂ​𝕪​𝕝^𝔽​ℙ​(X)\widehat{\mathbb{Cyl}}^{\mathbb{FP}}(X) and ℂ​𝕪​𝕝^ℙ​𝔽​(X)\widehat{\mathbb{Cyl}}^{\mathbb{PF}}(X) to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. The concatenation can be constructed in a straightforward way. Then we extend the concatenation in the two directions. One direction is the gluing, which has no essential new features for this case. The other direction is to insert gradient flow segments. This is similar to the cases of ℙ\mathbb{P} and Δℙ​ℙ\mathbb{\Delta}^{\mathbb{PP}}. We omit the details.
Part IV EQUIVARIANT FLOER THEORY AND STEENROD OPERATIONS
Outline of Part 4
Note that we would like to switch to the cohomological convention. The Floer equation will remain the same. However, it will be the equation for the ascending gradient flow equation of the action functional (which differs from the one used previously by a negative sign). Hence the differential increases the action functional. The grading is also changed to the cohomological one so that the pair-of-pants product is degree-preserving. Moreover, we make use of the coherent orientations without explicitly mentioning them.
22. Morse Theory on Classifying Spaces
The Borel ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant cohomology of a point with 𝐅𝗉{\bf F}_{\sf p}-coefficient is the ring
Hℤ𝗉Borel​(pt,𝐅𝗉)≅H∗​(B​ℤ𝗉,𝐅𝗉)={𝐅𝗉​[𝚄,θ]/⟨θ2=0⟩,𝗉>2;𝐅2​[θ],𝗉=2.H_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm Borel}({\rm pt};{\bf F}_{\sf p})\cong H^{*}(B{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}};{\bf F}_{\sf p})=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}{\bf F}_{\sf p}[\mathtt{U},\uptheta]/\langle\uptheta^{2}=0\rangle,&\ {\sf p}>2;\\
{\bf F}_{2}[\uptheta],&\ {\sf p}=2.\end{array}\right.
where 𝚄\mathtt{U} has degree 22 while θ\uptheta has degree 11. One usually considers the completion by allowing formal power series rather than polynomials in 𝚄\mathtt{U} and θ\uptheta. We denote the completion by
𝐊~𝗉,0:={𝐅𝗉​[[𝚄]]​⟨θ⟩,𝗉>2,𝐅2​[[θ]],𝗉=2.\widetilde{\bf K}_{{\sf p},0}:=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}{\bf F}_{\sf p}{[\![\mathtt{U}]\!]}\langle\uptheta\rangle,&\ {\sf p}>2,\\
{\bf F}_{2}{[\![\uptheta]\!]},&\ {\sf p}=2.\end{array}\right.
By inverting 𝚄\mathtt{U} for p≥3p\geq 3 and inverting θ\uptheta for p=2p=2, one get the Laurent version
𝐊~𝗉:={𝐅𝗉​((𝚄))​⟨θ⟩,𝗉>2,𝐅2​((θ)),𝗉=2.\widetilde{\bf K}_{\sf p}:=\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}{\bf F}_{\sf p}{(\!(\mathtt{U})\!)}\langle\uptheta\rangle,&\ {\sf p}>2,\\
{\bf F}_{2}{(\!(\uptheta)\!)},&\ {\sf p}=2.\end{array}\right.
This ring is not the cohomology of any natural topological space. However, it can be realized as the cohomology of a certain flow category which will be convenient for establishing the Tate equivariant theories. We will also use the notation
𝐊𝗉:=𝐅𝗉​((𝚄)){\bf K}_{\sf p}:={\bf F}_{\sf p}{(\!(\mathtt{U})\!)}
for 𝗉>2{\sf p}>2, dropping θ\uptheta, in later discussions.
22.1. An equivariant Morse flow category
We provide a concrete Morse model for equivariant cohomology of a point. We will use this Morse model throughout all the equivariant constructions.
22.1.1. 𝗉=2{\sf p}=2 case
Consider the “real S∞S^{\infty}”
Sℝ∞:={η=(η0,η1,…)|ηl∈ℝ,ηl=0 for ∀l≫0,∑l=0∞ηl2=1}S^{\infty}_{\mathbb{R}}:=\Big\{\eta=(\eta_{0},\eta_{1},\ldots)\ |\ \eta_{l}\in{\mathbb{R}},\ \eta_{l}=0\text{ for }\forall l\gg 0,\ \sum_{l=0}^{\infty}\eta_{l}^{2}=1\Big\}
which is a contractible infinite CW complex. The group ℤ2{\mathbb{Z}}_{2} acts freely by changing ηl\eta_{l} to −ηl-\eta_{l} with quotient being ℝ​ℙ∞\mathbb{RP}^{\infty}, which is a model for the classifying space of ℤ2{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}. As Sℝ∞S_{\mathbb{R}}^{\infty} is the colimit of finite-dimensional spheres, we can define notion of smoothness in the naive way. For example, a function on Sℝ∞S_{\mathbb{R}}^{\infty} is smooth if its restriction to each truncation Sk⊆Sℝ∞S^{k}\subseteq S_{\mathbb{R}}^{\infty} is smooth.
Consider the function
f𝔼:Sℝ∞→ℝ,f𝔼​(η)=∑l=0∞l​ηl2.f^{\mathbb{E}}:S_{\mathbb{R}}^{\infty}\to{\mathbb{R}},\ f^{\mathbb{E}}(\eta)=\sum_{l=0}^{\infty}l\eta_{l}^{2}.
Its trunctions to each SkS^{k} is a Morse function. The critical point set is
critf𝔼={η=±wl|ηj=±δj​l,l=0,1,…}.{\rm crit}f^{\mathbb{E}}=\{\eta=\pm w_{l}\ |\ \eta_{j}=\pm\delta_{jl},\ l=0,1,\ldots\}.
It is easy to see that the standard metric g𝔼g^{\mathbb{E}} on S∞S^{\infty} makes it Morse–Smale. Define the grading by
|±wl|=l.|\pm w_{l}|=l.
The Tate equivariant theory suggests to consider a formal “negative extension” of Sℝ∞S_{\mathbb{R}}^{\infty}. Define
