Notice that the quasi-Frobenius map is compatible with continuation maps. To see that the composition is independent of the choice of the Morse–Smale pair (f,g)(f,g), we can concatenate the multimodule 𝕏ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{QSt}} with Morse bimodules interpolating different choices of the Morse–Smale pairs, therefore we obtain the following statement using standard ideas.
Lemma 24.5.
Let 𝕄′{\mathbb{M}}^{\prime} be another Morse flow category on XX associated to a different Morse–Smale pair (f′,g′)(f^{\prime},g^{\prime}). Then the following diagram commutes.
H​M∗​(f,g)\textstyle{HM^{*}(f,g)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Hℤ𝗉∗​(C∗​(𝕄)⊗𝗉)\textstyle{H_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{*}(C^{*}(\mathbb{M})^{\otimes{\sf p}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}H∗​(C∗​(𝕄​#​𝔼))\textstyle{H^{*}(C^{*}(\mathbb{M}\#{\mathbb{E}}))\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}H​M∗​(f′,g′)\textstyle{HM^{*}(f^{\prime},g^{\prime})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Hℤ𝗉∗​(C∗​(𝕄′)⊗𝗉)\textstyle{H_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{*}(C^{*}({\mathbb{M}}^{\prime})^{\otimes{\sf p}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}H∗​(C∗​(𝕄′​#​𝔼))\textstyle{H^{*}(C^{*}(\mathbb{M}^{\prime}\#{\mathbb{E}}))}
Here vertical arrows are isomorphisms induced from continuation maps.
Notice that
H∗​(C∗​(𝕄​#​𝔼))≅H∗​(X,Λ𝐅𝗉Π​⟨θ⟩).H^{*}(C^{*}({\mathbb{M}}\#{\mathbb{E}}))\cong H^{*}(X;\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}\langle\uptheta\rangle).
Then the above lemma shows that, after tensoring with Λ𝐊~𝗉Π\Lambda_{\widetilde{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}, one obtains a canonical map
Q​S​t𝗉:H∗​(X,𝐅𝗉)→H∗​(X,Λ𝐊~𝗉Π).QSt_{{\sf p}}:H^{*}(X;{\bf F}_{\sf p})\to H^{*}(X;\Lambda_{\widetilde{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}).
By construction, the chain map Φ~ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\widetilde{\Phi}^{\mathbb{QSt}} does not decrease the 𝚄\mathtt{U}-grading, hence it indeed defines a map for each degree kk:
Q​S​t𝗉:Hk​(X,𝔽2)→{H2​k​(X,Λ𝐅2​[[θ]]Π),𝗉=2,H𝗉​k​(X,Λ𝐅𝗉​[[𝚄]]Π​⟨θ⟩),𝗉>2.QSt_{{\sf p}}:H^{k}(X;{\mathbb{F}}_{2})\to\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}H^{2k}(X;\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{2}{[\![\uptheta]\!]}}^{\Pi}),&\ {\sf p}=2,\\
H^{{\sf p}k}(X;\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}{[\![\mathtt{U}]\!]}}^{\Pi}\langle\uptheta\rangle),&\ {\sf p}>2.\end{array}\right.
This is called the quantum Steenrod operation. The proof of the claim that the classical part of Q​S​t𝗉QSt_{{\sf p}} (which comes from constant holomorphic spheres) coincides with the classical Steenrod operation is the same as the semi-positive case considered by Seidel–Wilkins [59]. This finishes the proof of part (1) of Theorem H.
24.3. AMS construction
We would like to construct ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant AMS lifts which is also equivariant with respect to the monoid morphism (24.1). It suffices to construct the lift for the corresponding moduli space of 𝗉+1{\sf p}+1-marked curves, from which the flow multimodule is constructed by taking fiber products with moduli spaces of Morse trajectories.
24.3.1. The domain moduli
We first consider the moduli space of domain curves. For each d≥0d\geq 0, consider
ℳ¯Σℚ​𝕊​𝕥​(ℂ​ℙd,d)\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{\Sigma^{\mathbb{QSt}}}(\mathbb{CP}^{d},d)
of holomorphic maps from the special marked curve Σ𝗉𝕊​𝕥\Sigma_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{St}} to ℂ​ℙd\mathbb{CP}^{d} of degree dd. Let
Bdℚ​𝕊​𝕥⊆ℳ¯(ℂℙd,d)Σℚ​𝕊​𝕥B_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\subseteq\overline{\mathcal{M}}{}_{\Sigma^{\mathbb{QSt}}}(\mathbb{CP}^{d},d)
be the open subset whose images are not contained in any hyperplane. Then Bdℚ​𝕊​𝕥B_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}} is a 𝒢dℚ​𝕊​𝕥:=P​G​L​(d+1){\mathcal{G}}_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}:=PGL(d+1)-invariant open subset. Moreover, there is an action by ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} which permutes the incoming marked points. Then one has the object
𝒞dℚ​𝕊​𝕥=(ℤ𝗉×𝒢dℚ​𝕊​𝕥,Bdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,Cdℚ​𝕊​𝕥)∈Ob​𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯.{\mathcal{C}}_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}=({{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}\times{\mathcal{G}}_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},B_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},C_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}})\in{\rm Ob}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}.
Since this is not stratified, we do not need to consider outercollaring or rigidifications at this moment. We can equip 𝒞dℚ​𝕊​𝕥{\mathcal{C}}_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}} a ℤ𝗉×Gdℚ​𝕊​𝕥{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}\times G_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}-equivariant stable complex structure, hence an object of 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯ℂ\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}^{\mathbb{C}}, using the complex analytic structure.
24.3.2. The thickenings
Choose an integral symplectic form Ω\Omega which is tamed by JJ. Consider the space of maps and framed maps
Mapd​(Cdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,X),\displaystyle\ {\rm Map}_{d}(C_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},X),\
Mapdfr​(Cdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,X)\displaystyle\ {\rm Map}_{d}^{\rm fr}(C_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},X)
whose elements are (ϕ,u)(\phi,u) resp. (ϕ,u,F)(\phi,u,F) where ϕ∈Bdℚ​𝕊​𝕥\phi\in B_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}, u:Cϕ→Xu:C_{\phi}\to X is a smooth map satisfying ∫u∗​Ω=d\int u^{*}\Omega=d, and FF is a framing associated to uu and the integral symplectic form Ω\Omega.
One can choose a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant group reduction scheme
λdℚ​𝕊​𝕥:Mapdfr​(Cdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,X)→Qdℚ​𝕊​𝕥:=T1​(𝒢dℚ​𝕊​𝕥/Gdℚ​𝕊​𝕥),\lambda_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}:{\rm Map}_{d}^{\rm fr}(C_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},X)\to Q_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}:=T_{1}({\mathcal{G}}_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}/G_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}),
for example, using the formula (15.6). On the other hand, choose a thickening datum
ιdℚ​𝕊​𝕥:Wdℚ​𝕊​𝕥→Γc​(C̊dℚ​𝕊​𝕥×X,ΩC̊dℚ​𝕊​𝕥/Bdℚ​𝕊​𝕥0,1⊗T​X)\iota_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}:W_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\times X,\Omega^{0,1}_{\mathring{C}_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}/B_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}}\otimes TX)
where Wdℚ​𝕊​𝕥W_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}} is a unitary representation of Gdℚ​𝕊​𝕥≅P​U​(d+1)G_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\cong PU(d+1) such that ιdℚ​𝕊​𝕥\iota_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}} is equivariant with respect to both the GdG_{d}-action and the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action.
Then one has the thickened moduli space
Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥:={(ϕ,u,F,e)|(ϕ,u,F)∈Mapdfr(Cdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,X),e∈Wdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,∂¯​u+ιdℚ​𝕊​𝕥​(e)=0,ϕ=ϕF∈Bdℚ​𝕊​𝕥}V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}:=\left\{(\phi,u,F,e)\ \left|\begin{array}[]{c}(\phi,u,F)\in{\rm Map}_{d}^{\rm fr}(C_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},X),\ e\in W_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},\\
\overline{\partial}u+\iota_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}(e)=0,\ \phi=\phi_{F}\in B_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\end{array}\right.\right\}
The obstruction bundle
Edℚ​𝕊​𝕥→Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥E_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\to V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}
is the trivial bundle with fiber Wdℚ​𝕊​𝕥⊕Qdℚ​𝕊​𝕥W_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\oplus Q_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}} and the Kuranishi section is
Sdℚ​𝕊​𝕥​(ϕ,u,F,e)=(e,λdℚ​𝕊​𝕥​(ϕ,u,F)).S_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}(\phi,u,F,e)=(e,\lambda_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}(\phi,u,F)).
The obtained topological Kuranishi space is denoted by
Kdℚ​𝕊​𝕥:=(Gdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,Edℚ​𝕊​𝕥,Sdℚ​𝕊​𝕥)K_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}:=(G_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},E_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},S_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}})
which also has a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action commuting with Gdℚ​𝕊​𝕥G_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}.
Notice that there is a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant evaluation map
ev:Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥→X𝗉+1{\rm ev}:V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\to X^{{\sf p}+1}
at the markings, where ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} acts on the first 𝗉{\sf p} copies of XX by permutation.
One still have the relative smoothness of the forgetful map
Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥→Bdℚ​𝕊​𝕥.V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\to B_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}.
One can then also follow the approach of Section 16 (which is much simplified here) to equip the vertical tangent bundle an NC structure. See [13, Section 6.2] for related setups in Gromov–Witten theory.
Since we are working with a single space without boundary or corners, one can apply the smoothing strategy of [3] to obtain a stable Gd×ℤ𝗉G_{d}\times{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-smoothing of Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}; the stabilization factor needed for the smoothing can be absorbed into the thickening space Wdℚ​𝕊​𝕥W_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}. Moreover, one can make the evaluation map ev{\rm ev} a smooth submersion at the expense of introducing further stabilization.
Then eventually one can use the stable complex structure of Bdℚ​𝕊​𝕥B_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}} and the NC structure on vertical tangent bundles to construct a ℤ𝗉×Gdℚ​𝕊​𝕥{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}\times G_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}-equivariant NC structure on Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}. Then one obtains an object of 𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NC\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}^{\rm NC} written as
Kdℚ​𝕊​𝕥=(ℤ𝗉×Gdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥,Edℚ​𝕊​𝕥,Sdℚ​𝕊​𝕥)K_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}=({{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}\times G_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},E_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}},S_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}})
with an equivariant smooth evaluation map
ev:Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥→X𝗉+1.{\rm ev}:V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}\to X^{{\sf p}+1}.
24.3.3. The Kuranishi and derived orbifold multimodule
Now we will insert Morse constraints and couple with the diagonal bimodule of 𝔼{{\mathbb{E}}}. For critical points x¯1,…,x¯𝗉,x¯′\underline{\smash{x}}_{1},\ldots,\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p},\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime} of f𝕄f^{\mathbb{M}}, w,w′w,w^{\prime} of f𝔼f^{{{\mathbb{E}}}}, consider
ev−1(Wx¯1us×⋯×Wx¯𝗉us×Wx′st)×M̊w;w′Δ𝔼{\rm ev}^{-1}(W_{\underline{\smash{x}}_{1}}^{\rm us}\times\cdots\times W_{\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p}}^{\rm us}\times W_{x^{\prime}}^{\rm st})\times\mathring{M}_{w;w^{\prime}}^{{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{{\mathbb{E}}}}
where Wx¯iusW_{\underline{\smash{x}}_{i}}^{\rm us} resp. Wx¯′stW_{\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime}}^{\rm st} is the uncompactified unstable resp. stable manifold and M̊w;w′Δ𝔼\mathring{M}_{w;w^{\prime}}^{\mathbb{\Delta}^{{\mathbb{E}}}} is the uncompactified moduli space of parametrized trajectories in S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty} connecting ww and w′w^{\prime}. Then we compactify by allowing breaking as follows: at negative ends, the breakings at different gradient rays/lines are independent; at the positive end, the breaking is regarded as breaking in the product space X×S∞X\times S^{\infty}, therefore “synchronized.” Let the compactified space be
Vdℚ​𝕊​𝕥(x¯1⋯x¯𝗉w;(x¯′,w′)).V_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}(\underline{\smash{x}}_{1}\cdots\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p}w;(\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime},w^{\prime})).
Then one obtains a stratified smooth Kuranishi space
Kdℚ​𝕊​𝕥(x¯1⋯x¯𝗉w;(x¯′,w′))K_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}(\underline{\smash{x}}_{1}\cdots\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p}w;(\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime},w^{\prime}))
whose symmetry group is reduced to Gdℚ​𝕊​𝕥G_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}.
We define a lift of the Steenrod multimodule to 𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NC\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}^{\rm NC}, denoted by 𝕏^ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\hat{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{QSt}}. Given objects xi=(ai,x¯i)x_{i}=(a_{i},\underline{\smash{x}}_{i}) where ai∈Πa_{i}\in\Pi and x¯i∈crit​f\underline{\smash{x}}_{i}\in{\rm crit}f, i=1,…,𝗉i=1,\ldots,{\sf p} and x′=(a′,x¯′)x^{\prime}=(a^{\prime},\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime}), denote d=Ω⁡(a′−a1−⋯−a𝗉)d=\Omega(a^{\prime}-a_{1}-\cdots-a_{\sf p}) and
Kx1⋯x𝗉w;(x′,w′)ℚ​𝕊​𝕥:=Kdℚ​𝕊​𝕥(x¯1⋯x¯𝗉w;(x′,w′))∈𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯NC.K_{x_{1}\cdots x_{{\sf p}}w;(x^{\prime},w^{\prime})}^{\mathbb{QSt}}:=K_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}}(\underline{\smash{x}}_{1}\cdots\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p}w;(x^{\prime},w^{\prime}))\in\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}^{\rm NC}.
The multimodule structural maps are obtained in a very simple way as we only need to consider broken Morse trajectories. Hence one obtains a multimodule 𝕏^ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\hat{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{QSt}} over (𝕄,…,𝕄,𝔼,𝕄​#​𝔼)({\mathbb{M}},\ldots,{\mathbb{M}},{{\mathbb{E}}};{\mathbb{M}}\#{\mathbb{E}}). One is readily to verify that it is a lift of 𝕏ℚ​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{QSt}} and satisfies the expected equivariance property.
Finally one takes group quotient by Gdℚ​𝕊​𝕥G_{d}^{\mathbb{QSt}} and obtains a lift to 𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NC\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}, denoted by 𝕏~ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{QSt}}. One can do the outercollaring as the last step, providing the desired AMS construction claimed in Theorem 24.2.
Lastly, if we make a different set of choices, then the trivial homotopy from 𝕏ℚ​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{QSt}} to itself can be lifted to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} in the equivariant way, between the AMS lifts of two different choices. This finishes the proof of Theorem 24.2.
24.4. Comparing to Seidel–Wilkins’ definition in semi-positive case
When (X,ω)(X,\omega) is semi-positive, Seidel–Wilkins [59] defined their quantum Steenrod operations using the classical approach. We prove that our definition agrees with theirs.
Theorem 24.6.
When (X,ω)(X,\omega) is semi-positive, the quantum Steenrod operation defined above agrees with the definition of Seidel–Wilkins.
Remark 24.7.
Strictly speaking, we are referring to the operations denoted by Q​S​tQSt instead of Q​ΣbQ\Sigma_{b} in [59], where the latter is featured more in recent studies of arithmetic properties of quantum connections on semi-positive symplectic manifolds (cf. [19, 18], [40, 39], [10, 9]). We can extend our Q​S​t𝗉QSt_{\sf p} to define analogs of Q​ΣbQ\Sigma_{b} using our framework and prove that it reduces to the Seidel–Wilkins operation when (X,ω)(X,\omega) is semi-positive. Moreover, such an extension is covariantly constant under the quantum connection defined using FOP perturbations. We will not discuss such extensions in this manuscript.
24.4.1. The construction of Seidel–Wilkins
The quantum Steenrod operation defined in [59] is based on the classical transversality via adding ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant inhomogeneous terms parametrized by S∞S^{\infty}. We extend the perturbation to S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty}. Consider inhomogeneous terms
νS2,η,z,xeq:Tz​S2→Tx​X​for​(η,z,x)∈S^∞×S2×X\nu_{S^{2},\eta,z,x}^{\rm eq}:T_{z}S^{2}\to T_{x}X\ {\rm for\ }(\eta,z,x)\in\widehat{S}^{\infty}\times S^{2}\times X
which satisfies
νS2,σ⁡(η),z,xeq=νS2,η,σ⁡(z),xeq∘D​σ:Tz​S2→Tx​M∀σ∈ℤ𝗉.\nu_{S^{2},\sigma(\eta),z,x}^{\rm eq}=\nu_{S^{2},\eta,\sigma(z),x}^{\rm eq}\circ D\sigma:T_{z}S^{2}\to T_{x}M\ \ \forall\sigma\in{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}.
Then one can consider the moduli space of maps u:S2→Xu:S^{2}\to X satisfying the perturbed Cauchy–Riemann equation. More precisely, consider pairs (η,u)(\eta,u) where η∈S^∞\eta\in\widehat{S}^{\infty} and u:S2→Xu:S^{2}\to X such that
∂¯J​u​(z)+νS2,η,z,u⁡(z)eq=0.\overline{\partial}_{J}u(z)+\nu_{S^{2},\eta,z,u(z)}^{\rm eq}=0.
We modify Seidel–Wilkins’ formulation slightly using the Morse model. For a comprehensive comparison with the original Seidel–Wilkins’ setup, which is based on finding explicit cycles representing generators if H∗​(B​ℤ𝗉,𝔽p)H^{*}(B{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}};{\mathbb{F}}_{p}), we refer the reader to [12, Appendix A]. Recall that one has identified critical points of f𝔼f^{{\mathbb{E}}}. For each pair of critical points w,w′∈crit​f𝔼w,w^{\prime}\in{\rm crit}f^{{\mathbb{E}}}, denote
Δ̊w;w′:={η:ℝ→S^∞|η′(s)=∇f𝔼(η(s))=0,lims→−∞η(s)=w,lims→+∞η(s)=w′}.\mathring{\Delta}_{w;w^{\prime}}:=\Big\{\eta:{\mathbb{R}}\to\widehat{S}^{\infty}\ |\ \eta^{\prime}(s)=\nabla f^{{\mathbb{E}}}(\eta(s))=0,\ \lim_{s\to-\infty}\eta(s)=w,\ \lim_{s\to+\infty}\eta(s)=w^{\prime}\Big\}.
Then elements of Δ̊w;w′\mathring{\Delta}_{w;w^{\prime}} is determined by its evaluation at s=0s=0. On the other hand, one has
S^∞=⨆w,w′Δ̊w;w′.\widehat{S}^{\infty}=\bigsqcup_{w,w^{\prime}}\mathring{\Delta}_{w;w^{\prime}}.
Then given critical points x¯1,…,x¯𝗉,x¯′\underline{\smash{x}}_{1},\ldots,\underline{\smash{x}}_{{\sf p}},\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime} of f:X→ℝf:X\to{\mathbb{R}} and a∈Πa\in\Pi, consider the moduli space
ℳ̊x¯1⋯x¯𝗉;x¯′SW(a;Δ̊w;w′)\mathring{\mathcal{M}}_{\underline{\smash{x}}_{1}\cdots\underline{\smash{x}}_{{\sf p}};\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime}}^{\rm SW}(a;\mathring{\Delta}_{w;w^{\prime}})
which consists of pairs (u,η)(u,\eta) where u:S2→Xu:S^{2}\to X is a smooth map and η∈Δ̊w;w′\eta\in\mathring{\Delta}_{w;w^{\prime}} satisfying
∂¯J​u​(z)+νS2,η,z,u⁡(z)eq=0\overline{\partial}_{J}u(z)+\nu_{S^{2},\eta,z,u(z)}^{\rm eq}=0
and
u⁡(zi)∈Wx¯ius,u⁡(z∞)∈Wx¯′st.u(z_{i})\in W^{\rm us}_{\underline{\smash{x}}_{i}},\ u(z_{\infty})\in W^{\rm st}_{\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime}}.
Seidel–Wilkins proved that for a generic inhomogeneous term νS2eq\nu_{S^{2}}^{\rm eq}, whenever the expected dimension of the above moduli space is zero or one, the defining perturbed JJ-holomorphic map equation is transverse.
Lemma 24.8.
(cf. [59, Lemma 4.1]) For a generic ω\omega-compatible almost complex structure JJ and a ℤ×ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{Z}}\times{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant inhomogeneous term νS2,η,z,xeq\nu_{S^{2},\eta,z,x}^{\rm eq}, any moduli space ℳ̊x¯1⋯x¯𝗉;x¯′SW(a;Δ̊w;w′)\mathring{\mathcal{M}}_{\underline{\smash{x}}_{1}\cdots\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p};\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime}}^{\rm SW}(a;\mathring{\Delta}_{w;w^{\prime}}) is transverse provided that its expected dimension is at most 11. Moreover,
(1)
When the expected dimension is zero, ℳ̊x¯1⋯x¯𝗉;x¯′SW(a;Δ̊w;w′)\mathring{\mathcal{M}}_{\underline{\smash{x}}_{1}\cdots\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p};\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime}}^{\rm SW}(a;\mathring{\Delta}_{w;w^{\prime}}) consists of finitely many points.
(2)
When the expected dimension is one, ℳ̊x¯1⋯x¯𝗉;x¯′SW(a;Δ̊w;w′)\mathring{\mathcal{M}}_{\underline{\smash{x}}_{1}\cdots\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p};\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime}}^{\rm SW}(a;\mathring{\Delta}_{w;w^{\prime}}) admits a natural compactification which is a compact 1-dimensional manifold with boundary.
Proof.
The only difference between our case and the case of [59] is that there is no requirement for ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}-symmetry in [59]. However, this can be achieved as the ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}-action is free.
∎
Then the chain-level quantum Steenrod operation can be defined using the count of zero-dimensional moduli spaces. One can use the standard argument to show that up to chain homotopy the chain-level map is well-defined.
24.4.2. The AMS lifts and FOP perturbations with an inhomogeneous term
Now we define a perturbation of the quantum Steenrod multimodule 𝕏ℚ​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{QSt}} by using the inhomogeneous term. Notice that each η∈S^∞\eta\in\widehat{S}^{\infty} corresponds uniquely to a smooth parametrized Morse flow line yw​(s)y_{w}(s) in S∞S^{\infty}. Then for objects x1,…,x𝗉,w;(x′,w′)x_{1},\ldots,x_{\sf p},w;(x^{\prime},w^{\prime}), consider the moduli space
M̊x1⋯x𝗉w;(x′,w′)𝕏1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥={(u,η)|u:Σℚ​𝕊​𝕥→X,η∈Wusw∩Wstw′⊆S^∞,∂¯J​u+ν=0,u⁡(zi)∈Wx¯ius,u⁡(z∞)∈Wx¯′st}.\mathring{M}_{x_{1}\cdots x_{\sf p}w;(x^{\prime},w^{\prime})}^{\mathbb{X}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}}}=\left\{(u,\eta)\ \left|\ \begin{array}[]{c}u:\Sigma^{\mathbb{QSt}}\to X,\ \eta\in W^{\rm us}_{w}\cap W^{\rm st}_{w^{\prime}}\subseteq\widehat{S}^{\infty},\\
\overline{\partial}_{J}u+\nu=0,\\
u(z_{i})\in W^{\rm us}_{\underline{\smash{x}}_{i}},\ u(z_{\infty})\in W^{\rm st}_{\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime}}\end{array}\right.\right\}.
It can be compactified in a natural way, which is denoted by
Mx1⋯x𝗉w;(x′,w′)𝕏1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥.M_{x_{1}\cdots x_{\sf p}w;(x^{\prime},w^{\prime})}^{\mathbb{X}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}}}.
These moduli spaces form a multimodule 𝕏1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}} over (𝕄,…,𝕄,𝔼,𝕄​#​𝔼)({\mathbb{M}},\ldots,\mathbb{M},{{\mathbb{E}}};{\mathbb{M}}\#{{\mathbb{E}}}), which is a variant of the ν=0\nu=0 case considered previously, which is denoted by 𝕏0ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}_{0}^{\mathbb{QSt}}. After outercollaring, using the same method as proving Theorem 24.2, one can construct an AMS lift 𝕏^1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}} enriched in ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. The inhomogeneous term ν\nu can be dealt with by considering the graph graph⁡(u):Σℚ​𝕊​𝕥→Σℚ​𝕊​𝕥×X\mathrm{graph}(u):\Sigma^{\mathbb{QSt}}\to\Sigma^{\mathbb{QSt}}\times X, where the product Σℚ​𝕊​𝕥×X\Sigma^{\mathbb{QSt}}\times X is equipped with the sheared almost complex structure (e.g. [3, Lemma 6.18]) so that we can go back to the standard situation. The resulting lift in ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig} is denoted by 𝕏~1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}}.
Lemma 24.9.
When the virtual dimension is zero, the original section is FOP transverse.
Proof.
By the monotonicity condition and the classical transversality condition, when the virtual dimension is zero, the moduli space M̊x1⋯x𝗉w;(x′,w′)𝕏1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathring{M}_{x_{1}\cdots x_{\sf p}w;(x^{\prime},w^{\prime})}^{\mathbb{X}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}}} agrees with its compactification and there are no orbifold points in the moduli space. The Kuranishi section on the thickening is transverse to the zero section because the Cauchy–Riemann equation is transversely cut out. Then by the (Classical Transversality) property of FOP transverse perturbations, the original section is FOP transverse.
∎
Proposition 24.10.
There exists an FOP transverse perturbation of 𝕏~1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}} such that for moduli spaces of dimension at most 00, the perturbation agrees with the original Kuranishi section.
Proof.
This follows from the same proof of Lemma 13.13.
∎
Furthermore, there is a clear homotopy ℍℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{H}^{\mathbb{QSt}} from 𝕏0ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}_{0}^{\mathbb{QSt}} to 𝕏1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}} by adding an additional parameter t∈[0,1]t\in[0,1] and changing ν\nu to t​νt\nu in the equation. One can further construct an AMS lift ℍ^ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\hat{\mathbb{H}}^{\mathbb{QSt}} as a homotopy from 𝕏^0ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{0}^{\mathbb{QSt}} to 𝕏^1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\hat{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}}. Moreover, one can extend the FOP transverse perturbations 𝕏~0ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}_{0}^{\mathbb{QSt}} and 𝕏~1ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}_{1}^{\mathbb{QSt}} to an FOP transverse perturbation on ℍ^ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\hat{\mathbb{H}}^{\mathbb{QSt}}, denoted by ℍ~ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{H}}^{\mathbb{QSt}}, in an equivariant way. This leads to a chain homotopy between the chain maps defined with or without the inhomogeneous term. This concludes the proof of Theorem 24.6.
25. The Equivariant Floer theory for iterations—Proof of Theorem I
In this section we construct the equivariant Floer theory, including equivariant Floer cohomology, equivariant continuation maps, and equivariant PSS/SSP maps, induced from a prime iteration of a Hamiltonian. Let 𝗉{\sf p} be a prime.
25.1. Equivariant Floer flow category as a coupling
25.1.1. Coupling of Floer and Morse flow categories
We define a notion called coupling of flow categories. This notion cannot be defined on the abstract level but rely on the geometric setup.
Let 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} be the Floer flow category on XX associated to a pair (H,J)(H,J). Let 𝕄{\mathbb{M}} be the Morse flow category on another manifold YY associated to a Morse–Smale pair (f,g)(f,g). Define 𝔽​#​𝕄{\mathbb{F}}\#{\mathbb{M}} be a flow category as follows. The set of objects is
Ob⁡(𝔽​#​𝕄)=Ob​𝔽×Ob​𝕄{\rm Ob}({\mathbb{F}}\#{\mathbb{M}})={\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\times{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{M}}
whose elements are denoted by p=(p𝔽,p𝕄)p=(p^{\mathbb{F}},p^{\mathbb{M}}). For the morphism space Mp​q𝔽​#​𝕄M_{pq}^{{\mathbb{F}}\#{\mathbb{M}}}, consider the moduli space of pairs (u,v)(u,v) where u:ℝ×S1→Xu:{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}\to X is a solution to the Floer equation connection p𝔽p^{\mathbb{F}} and q𝔽q^{\mathbb{F}} and v:ℝ→Yv:{\mathbb{R}}\to Y is a Morse trajectory connection p𝕄p^{\mathbb{M}} and q𝕄q^{\mathbb{M}}; two pairs (u,v)(u,v) and (u′,v′)(u^{\prime},v^{\prime}) are equivalent if there exists s0∈ℝs_{0}\in{\mathbb{R}} such that
u(⋅,⋅)=u′(⋅+s0,⋅),\displaystyle\ u(\cdot,\cdot)=u^{\prime}(\cdot+s_{0},\cdot),\
v(⋅)=v′(⋅+s0).\displaystyle\ v(\cdot)=v^{\prime}(\cdot+s_{0}).
One then compactifies this moduli spaces by allowing “synchronized” breakings (as well as sphere bubblings).
Now we describe the equivariant Floer flow category as a special coupling.
Definition 25.1.
Let HH be a 1-periodic Hamiltonian on (X,ω)(X,\omega) such that the 𝗉{\sf p}-th iteration H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}} is nondegenerate. Let JJ be a fixed ω\omega-compatible almost complex structure. Define the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant Floer flow category to be the coupling
𝔽ℤ𝗉:=𝔽​#​𝔼{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:={\mathbb{F}}\#{\mathbb{E}}
where 𝔼{\mathbb{E}} is the Morse flow category on S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty}.
On 𝔽ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} there is an action
𝒜=(𝒜1,𝒜2):Ob​𝔽ℤ𝗉→ℝ2{\mathcal{A}}=({\mathcal{A}}_{1},{\mathcal{A}}_{2}):{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{2}
where
𝒜1​(p𝔽,p𝔼)=𝒜H♮​p​(p𝔽),\displaystyle\ {\mathcal{A}}_{1}(p^{\mathbb{F}},p^{{\mathbb{E}}})={\mathcal{A}}_{H^{\natural p}}(p^{\mathbb{F}}),\
𝒜2​(p𝔽,p𝔼)=f𝔼​(p𝔼).\displaystyle\ {\mathcal{A}}_{2}(p^{\mathbb{F}},p^{{\mathbb{E}}})=f^{{\mathbb{E}}}(p^{{\mathbb{E}}}).
The grading is given by
deg⁡(p𝔽,p𝔼):=deg⁡(p𝔽)+deg⁡(p𝔼)∈ℤ.{\rm deg}(p^{\mathbb{F}},p^{{\mathbb{E}}}):={\rm deg}(p^{\mathbb{F}})+{\rm deg}(p^{{\mathbb{E}}})\in{\mathbb{Z}}.
Moreover, there is a free action on Ob​𝔽ℤ𝗉{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} the twisted Novikov group
Π𝗉:=Π×ℤ×ℤ𝗉=Π×ℤ𝗉.{\mathbb{\Pi}}_{\sf p}:=\Pi\times{\mathbb{Z}}\times{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}={\mathbb{\Pi}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}.
For different Hamiltonians one can also define an equivariant continuation bimodule. Let Hi♮​𝗉H_{i}^{\natural{\sf p}} be pairs as above for i=0,1i=0,1. Choose a Floer data on the infinite cylinder connecting H0H_{0} and H1H_{1}, denoted by σ\sigma. Let σ♮​𝗉\sigma^{\natural{\sf p}} be the 𝗉{\sf p}-th iteration as a Floer daum on the infinite cylinder connecting H0♮​𝗉H_{0}^{\natural{\sf p}} and H1♮​𝗉H_{1}^{\natural{\sf p}}. By coupling the bimodule induced from σ♮​𝗉\sigma^{\natural{\sf p}} and the diagonal bimodule Δ𝔼{\mathbb{\Delta}}^{{{\mathbb{E}}}}, one obtains a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant Novikov bimodule over (𝔽0ℤ𝗉;𝔽1ℤ𝗉)({\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}};{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}), denoted by 𝔹01ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{B}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}_{01}.
Proposition 25.2.
𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} is a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant Novikov flow category enriched in 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯\underline{\smash{\bf Top}} and 𝔹01ℤ𝗉\mathbb{B}_{01}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} is a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant Novikov flow bimodule over (𝔽0ℤ𝗉;𝔽1ℤ𝗉)(\mathbb{F}_{0}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}};\mathbb{F}_{1}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}).
Now we state the technical theorem regarding equivariant AMS lifts of 𝔽ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} as well as 𝔹01ℤ𝗉\mathbb{B}_{01}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}.
Theorem 25.3 (Equivariant AMS lifts).
(1)
Let 𝔽ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} be the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant Floer flow category defined in Definition 25.1. Fix the outercollaring width and an integral action on 𝔽{\mathbb{F}}. There is a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant lift 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} of the outercollaring of 𝔽ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} to the category ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}, called the equivariant AMS lift of 𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} (subject to the outercollaring width and the integral action).
(2)
Choose integral actions on 𝔽0{\mathbb{F}}_{0} and 𝔽1{\mathbb{F}}_{1} (not necessarily compatible with respect to the interpolating Floer data). Given equivariant AMS lifts of 𝔽~0ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} resp. 𝔽~1ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} of 𝔽0ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} resp. 𝔽1ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} subject to the outercollaring width and the chosen integral actions, there exists a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant lift of the outercollaring of 𝔹01ℤ𝗉\mathbb{B}_{01}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig} as a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant bimodule over (𝔽~0ℤ𝗉;𝔽~1ℤ𝗉)(\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}};\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}).
Proof.
See next Subsection.
∎
Now assuming this theorem, one can define the equivariant Floer chain complex. Since the Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-action is free, by Theorem N, one can find a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant FOP perturbation on 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}, denoted by 𝔽̊ℤ𝗉\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}. Therefore, by taking the isotropy free part of the perturbed zero locus, one obtains a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}-graded Novikov flow category enriched in 𝚿​𝐌𝐚𝐧¯\underline{\smash{{\bf\Psi}{\bf Man}}}. Notice that there is still the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action which preserves all structures. Then applying the abstract construction in Section 7, one obtains a ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}-graded cochain complex
C​F∗​(H♮​𝗉,J♮​𝗉,Ξ♮​𝗉):=C∗​(𝔽̊ℤ𝗉)CF^{*}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},J^{\natural{\sf p}},\Xi^{\natural{\sf p}}):=C^{*}(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}})
which is a graded ΛℤΠ\Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}-module with a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action. The ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-fixed part, denoted by
C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉),CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}),
is called the (Tate) equivariant Floer complex of H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}}.
Furthermore, suppose one has two such equivariant complexes
C​F∗​(H1♮​𝗉),\displaystyle\ CF^{*}(H_{1}^{\natural{\sf p}}),\
C​F∗​(H2♮​𝗉),\displaystyle\ CF^{*}(H_{2}^{\natural{\sf p}}),
one can extend, by Theorem N, the Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant FOP perturbation over 𝔹~01ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{B}}_{01}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}, which induces a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant chain map
Φ01ℤ𝗉:C​F∗​(H1♮​𝗉)→C​F∗​(H2♮​𝗉).\Phi_{01}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:CF^{*}(H_{1}^{\natural{\sf p}})\to CF^{*}(H_{2}^{\natural{\sf p}}).
Then, upon taking ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-fixed part, one has the continuation maps
Φ01:C​Fℤ𝗉​(H1♮​𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉​(H2♮​𝗉).\Phi_{01}:CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H_{1}^{\natural{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H_{2}^{\natural{\sf p}}).
One can proceed in the same way as proving Theorem A and Theorem B. Therefore, one obtains a well-defined chain homotopy class of cochain complexes of ΛℤΠ\Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}-modules, hence a well-defined symplectic invariant
H​Fℤ𝗉​(X)HF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(X)
which is a module over Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}.
25.2. AMS construction for coupling of Floer and Morse flow categories
In this subsection we carry out the AMS construction for the coupled flow category.
25.2.1. The domain flow category
We modify the previous construction of AMS lifts for non-equivariant Floer theory. We do not consider the monotone flow category of domains as we have to couple it with the Morse flow category. Instead, one describes a flow category 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞ℤ𝗉\mathbb{Dom}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} with objects the same as those of 𝔽ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}.
First we choose an integral action 𝒜𝔽Ω:Ob​𝔽→ℤ{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}}^{\Omega}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\to{\mathbb{Z}} for the Floer flow category associated to H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}}. Notice that from the construction in the proof of Proposition 15.4, the integral action can be chosen to be ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant. Then for each pair of objects p=(p𝔽,p𝔼)p=(p^{\mathbb{F}},p^{\mathbb{E}}), q=(q𝔽,q𝔼)q=(q^{\mathbb{F}},q^{\mathbb{E}}), denote
dp​q:=𝒜Ω​(q𝔽)−𝒜Ω​(p𝔽)∈ℤ.d_{pq}:={\mathcal{A}}^{\Omega}(q^{{\mathbb{F}}})-{\mathcal{A}}^{\Omega}(p^{\mathbb{F}})\in{\mathbb{Z}}.
We describe an object
𝒞p​q=(𝒢p​q,Bp​q,Cp​q)∈Ob​𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯{\mathcal{C}}_{pq}=({\mathcal{G}}_{pq},B_{pq},C_{pq})\in{\rm Ob}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}
as follows. Define 𝒢x​y=𝒢dp​q{\mathcal{G}}_{xy}={\mathcal{G}}_{d_{pq}} as considered before. Consider the moduli space of pairs
ϕ:ℝ×S1→ℂ​ℙdp​q,v:ℝ→S^∞\phi:{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}\to\mathbb{CP}^{d_{pq}},\ v:{\mathbb{R}}\to\widehat{S}^{\infty}
where ϕ\phi is holomorphic of degree dd and vv is a flow line connection p𝔼p^{\mathbb{E}} and q𝔼q^{\mathbb{E}}. Two pairs (u,v)(u,v), (u′,v′)(u^{\prime},v^{\prime}) are equivalent if they differ by a common translation in ℝ{\mathbb{R}}. Then we compactify this space in the usual way, requiring the positive constraint
ϕ⁡(z+)=[0,…,0,1]∈ℂ​ℙdp​q\phi(z_{+})=[0,\ldots,0,1]\in\mathbb{CP}^{d_{pq}}
and requiring the image of ϕ\phi is not contained in any hyperplane. The space we obtain is denoted by Bp​qB_{pq}, whose dimension is
dimℝ​Bp​q=2​dp​q​(dp​q+1)+index⁡(q𝔼)−index⁡(p𝔼)−1.{\rm dim}_{\mathbb{R}}B_{pq}=2d_{pq}(d_{pq}+1)+{\rm index}(q^{{\mathbb{E}}})-{\rm index}(p^{{\mathbb{E}}})-1.
Let Cp​q→Bp​qC_{pq}\to B_{pq} be the universal curve whose fiber at ϕ∈Bp​q\phi\in B_{pq} is the corresponding rational curve in ℂ​ℙd\mathbb{CP}^{d}. This is a 𝒢p​q{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}-equivariant family, hence one obtains an object 𝒞x​y{\mathcal{C}}_{xy} in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}.
Notice that the space Bp​qB_{pq} is stratified by the following poset
Ap​q={((d0,…,dl),p𝔼r1𝔼⋯rl𝔼q𝔼)|di≥0,∑idi=d,p𝔼=r0𝔼≤r1𝔼≤⋯≤rl𝔼≤rl+1𝔼=q𝔼,di=0⟹ri𝔼≠ri+1𝔼}.A_{pq}=\left\{\Big((d_{0},\ldots,d_{l}),p^{{\mathbb{E}}}r_{1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\cdots r_{l}^{{\mathbb{E}}}q^{{\mathbb{E}}}\Big)\ \left|\begin{array}[]{c}\ d_{i}\geq 0,\ \displaystyle\sum_{i}d_{i}=d,\\
p^{{\mathbb{E}}}=r_{0}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\leq r_{1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\leq\cdots\leq r_{l}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\leq r_{l+1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}=q^{{\mathbb{E}}},\\
d_{i}=0\Longrightarrow r_{i}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\neq r_{i+1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\end{array}\right.\right\}.
Notice that there is a free ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action on the object 𝒞p​q{\mathcal{C}}_{pq}, given by the domain rotation and the action on S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty}: for γ∈ℤ𝗉\gamma\in{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} and ϕ∈Bx​y\phi\in B_{xy} represented by u:Σ→ℂ​ℙdu:\Sigma\to\mathbb{CP}^{d} and v:ℝ→S^∞v:{\mathbb{R}}\to\widehat{S}^{\infty}, define
γ⋅ϕ=[u∘γ−1,γ⋅v]\gamma\cdot\phi=[u\circ\gamma^{-1},\gamma\cdot v]
where u∘γ−1u\circ\gamma^{-1} is the composition with the domain rotation and γ⋅v\gamma\cdot v is induced by the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action on S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty}. This action commutes with the action of 𝒢p​q{\mathcal{G}}_{pq} for the following reason: the 𝒢p​q{\mathcal{G}}_{pq}-action comes from the geometry of the target space ℂ​ℙd\mathbb{CP}^{d} while ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} acts by reparametrizing the maps. On the other hand, there is also an action by ℤ{\mathbb{Z}} by the corresponding action on S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty}.
Using the construction of Section 14, one can define the following morphisms
ζp​r​q:𝒞p​r×𝒞r​q→𝒞p​q\zeta_{prq}:{\mathcal{C}}_{pr}\times{\mathcal{C}}_{rq}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{pq}
in the category 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}. From the explicit construction of the domain curves, this morphism is Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant. Hence one obtains a flow category enriched in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}, denoted by 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}.
Proposition 25.4.
Any outercollaring of 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}} admits a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant lift to ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}.
Proof.
The rigidification can be constructed in the same way as in Section 14. The freeness of the Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-action allows us to achieve the equivariance easily.
∎
25.2.2. Thickenings and group reductions
We follow the construction of Section 15. We can write down the flow category
⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔽ℤ𝗉𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}}^{\mathbb{fr}}
which gives each pair of objects p,qp,q an object
⌊Mapp​qfr{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{pq}^{\rm fr}
of framed maps. This flow category is canonically induced from previous steps and still carries the same symmetry.
Lemma 25.5.
There exist Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant group reduction schemes.
Proof.
This can be constructed in the same way as in Proposition 15.9. The freeness of the action allows us to maintain the symmetry.
∎
Hence one obtains a compatible system of maps
λp​q:Mapp​qfr→Qp​q.\lambda_{pq}:{\rm Map}_{pq}^{\rm fr}\to Q_{pq}.
Next we choose thickening data.
Lemma 25.6.
There exists a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant and transverse thickening datum on ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔽ℤ𝗉{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}}.
Proof.
The same argument as in Proposition 15.19 applies. The freeness of the Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-action allows us to maintain the symmetry.
∎
Hence, we obtain a compatible system of maps
νp​q:Wp​q→Γc​(C̊p​q×X,ΛC̊p​q/Bp​q0,1⊗T​X).\nu_{pq}:W_{pq}\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{pq}\times X,\Lambda_{\mathring{C}_{pq}/B_{pq}}^{0,1}\otimes TX).
Then similar to Definition 15.14, one can write down the thickened moduli spaces
Kp​q=(Gx​y,Vx​y,Ex​y,Sx​y)∈Ob𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig⌊K_{pq}=(G_{xy},V_{xy},E_{xy},S_{xy})\in{\rm Ob}{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig}
and obtain a lift of the outercollaring of 𝔽ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} to ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
25.2.3. Stable smoothing and NC structure
Next, the stable smoothing procedure works in a similar way. Indeed, the projection map Vx​y→⌊Bx​yV_{xy}\to{}_{\lfloor}B_{xy} has a rel-C∞,1C^{\infty,1}-structure, allowing us to inductively perform stable smoothing. We omit the details. After taking quotient, one obtains a lift to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}. The construction of stable complex structure is also the same. Hence one obtains
𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}
enriched in ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}. This finishes the proof of (1) of Theorem 25.3.
25.2.4. Equivariant continuation maps
To prove (2) of Theorem 25.3, i.e., the lift of the equivariant continuation bimodule, we also modify the previous non-equivariant case. Let 𝔽0ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} and 𝔽1ℤ𝗉\mathbb{F}_{1}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} be the two equivariant flow categories associated to the (iterations of) Hamiltonian H0,H1H_{0},H_{1}. Let 𝔹01ℤ𝗉\mathbb{B}_{01}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} be the equivariant continuation bimodule associated to the 𝗉{\sf p}-th iteration of a flow data on the cylinder interpolating between H0♮​𝗉H_{0}^{\natural{\sf p}} and H1♮​𝗉H_{1}^{\natural{\sf p}}.
We first define a collection of objects
𝒞x0;x1=(𝒢x0;x1,Bx0;x1,Cx0;x1)∈Ob​𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯.{\mathcal{C}}_{x_{0};x_{1}}=({\mathcal{G}}_{x_{0};x_{1}},B_{x_{0};x_{1}},C_{x_{0};x_{1}})\in{\rm Ob}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}.
Using the same integral modification of the symplectic action Ω\Omega, for x0=(x0𝔽,x0𝔼)x_{0}=(x_{0}^{\mathbb{F}},x_{0}^{{\mathbb{E}}}) and x1=(x1𝔽,x1𝔼)x_{1}=(x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}},x_{1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}), consider solutions (u,v)(u,v) where u:ℝ×S1→ℂ​ℙdu:{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}\to\mathbb{CP}^{d}, v:ℝ→S∞v:{\mathbb{R}}\to S^{\infty}, uu is holomorphic of degree d=dx0−dx1d=d_{x_{0}}-d_{x_{1}}, and vv is a flow line connecting x0𝔼x_{0}^{{\mathbb{E}}} to x1𝔼x_{1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}. We impose the negative constraint
u⁡(z−)=[1,0,…,0]∈ℂ​ℙd.u(z_{-})=[1,0,\ldots,0]\in\mathbb{CP}^{d}.
We compactify this space by allowing sphere bubbles and breakings at both positive and negative infinity. Moreover, breakings on either side are treated in the “synchronized” fashion. In this compactification, we also remove those solutions whose images in ℂ​ℙd\mathbb{CP}^{d} lie in some hyperplane. Then one obtains the moduli space Bx0;x1B_{x_{0};x_{1}} over which there is the universal curve Cx0;x1→Bx0;x1C_{x_{0};x_{1}}\to B_{x_{0};x_{1}}. Notice that the space Bx0;x1B_{x_{0};x_{1}} is stratified by the poset
Ax0;x1:={((d−r⋯d−1;d0;d1⋯ds),w−r𝔼⋯w0𝔼;w1𝔼⋯ws+1𝔼)|di≥0,∑i=−rsdi=dx0−dx1x0𝔼=w−r𝔼,x1𝔼=ws+1𝔼,di=0,i≠0,⟹wi𝔼≠wi+1𝔼}.A_{x_{0};x_{1}}:=\left\{\Big((d_{-r}\cdots d_{-1};d_{0};d_{1}\cdots d_{s}),w_{-r}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\cdots w_{0}^{{\mathbb{E}}};w_{1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\cdots w_{s+1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\Big)\left|\begin{array}[]{c}d_{i}\geq 0,\ \displaystyle\sum_{i=-r}^{s}d_{i}=d_{x_{0}}-d_{x_{1}}\\
x_{0}^{{\mathbb{E}}}=w_{-r}^{{\mathbb{E}}},\ x_{1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}=w_{s+1}^{{\mathbb{E}}},\\
d_{i}=0,\ i\neq 0,\Longrightarrow w_{i}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\neq w_{i+1}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\end{array}\right.\right\}.
Let Ax0;x1Ω⊆Ax0;x1A_{x_{0};x_{1}}^{\Omega}\subseteq A_{x_{0};x_{1}} be the open subset of tuples such that every did_{i} is equal to the Ω\Omega-area of some sphere class. Redefine 𝒞x0;x1{\mathcal{C}}_{x_{0};x_{1}} to be the restriction to this open subset.
We can also do the outercollaring and rigidification construction in the equivariant way. We have the following analogue of Proposition 25.4.
Proposition 25.7.
The collection of objects 𝒞x0;x1{\mathcal{C}}_{x_{0};x_{1}} forms a bimodule 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔹01ℤ𝗉\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{B}}_{01}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}} over (𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔽0ℤ𝗉;𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔽1ℤ𝗉)(\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}};\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}_{1}}), whose outercollaring admits an enrichment in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig} which is Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant.
Following Section 15, we can then construct a bimodule
⌊𝕄𝕒𝕡𝔹01ℤ𝗉𝕗​𝕣{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{B}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}_{01}}^{\mathbb{fr}}
over (𝕄⌊𝕒𝕡𝔽0ℤ𝗉𝕗​𝕣,𝕄⌊𝕒𝕡𝔽1ℤ𝗉𝕗​𝕣)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}_{0}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}}^{\mathbb{fr}},{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{F}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}_{1}}^{\mathbb{fr}}) enriched in ⌊𝐌𝐚𝐩¯fr{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Map}}^{\rm fr}. Using the freeness of the Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-action, we learn that:
Lemma 25.8.
There exist Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant group reduction schemes lifting 𝕄​𝕒​𝕡𝔹01ℤ𝗉𝕗​𝕣\mathbb{Map}_{\mathbb{B}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}_{01}}^{\mathbb{fr}} to a flow bimodule enriched in ⌊𝐦𝐚𝐩¯fr{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{{\bf map}}}{}^{\rm fr}.
Furthermore, following Proposition 15.19, the freeness of the Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-action guarantees the following:
Lemma 25.9.
There exists a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant and transverse thickening datum on ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔹01ℤ𝗉{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{B}}_{01}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}}, i.e., a transverse lift to 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤¯rig\underline{\smash{\bf Thick}}_{\rm rig}.
Therefore, the above statements ensure that 𝔹01ℤ𝗉\mathbb{B}_{01}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} admits a lift over ⌊𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Kur}}{}_{\rm rig}. The constructions of normal complex structures and coherent smoothings follow from the recurring discussions of this paper. Therefore, by taking the quotient, we get
𝔹~01ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{B}}_{01}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}
enriched in ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig} which is a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant bimodule over (𝔽~0ℤ𝗉;𝔽~1ℤ𝗉)(\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}};\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}). This finishes the proof of Theorem 25.3 (2).
25.3. Equivariant PSS and SSP maps
One uses spiked disks used to define the ordinary PSS and SSP maps. Here we would like to define equivariant analogues, which are maps
Φ^ℤ𝗉𝕄​𝔽:H∗​(X,ΛΠ​⟨θ⟩)→H​Fℤ𝗉∗​(X),\displaystyle\ \widehat{\Phi}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\mathbb{MF}}:H^{*}(X;\Lambda^{{\mathbb{\Pi}}}\langle\uptheta\rangle)\to HF_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}^{*}(X),\
Φℤ𝗉𝔽​𝕄:H​Fℤ𝗉∗​(X)→H∗​(X,ΛΠ​⟨θ⟩).\displaystyle\ \Phi_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\mathbb{FM}}:HF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{*}(X)\to H^{*}(X;\Lambda^{{\mathbb{\Pi}}}\langle\uptheta\rangle).
To define these maps, we need to describe certain bimodules, denoted by 𝔹𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} and 𝔹𝔽​𝕄,ℤ𝗉\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{FM},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} respectively. Consider the Morse-to-Floer map first. Choose a Morse flow category 𝕄¯\underline{\smash{\mathbb{M}}} on the symplectic manifold (X,ω)(X,\omega) associated to a Morse–Smale pair (f𝕄,g𝕄)(f^{\mathbb{M}},g^{\mathbb{M}}) and let 𝕄{\mathbb{M}} be the trivial product of 𝕄¯\underline{\smash{\mathbb{M}}} with Π\Pi. Consider the coupled flow category
𝕄ℤ𝗉:=𝕄​#​𝔼.{\mathbb{M}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}:=\mathbb{M}\#{{\mathbb{E}}}.
The equivariant Morse-to-Floer bimodule is a bimodule 𝔹𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} over (𝕄ℤ𝗉;𝔽ℤ𝗉)(\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}};\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}).
We consider spiked disks equipped with a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant Floer data. Regard Σ𝕄​𝔽≅ℂ\Sigma^{\mathbb{MF}}\cong{\mathbb{C}} as a surface with cylindrical end which has a natural ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action which rotate the cylindrical coordinates by multiples of 2​π𝗉\frac{2\pi}{{\sf p}}. One can choose the Floer datum σ𝕄​𝔽\sigma^{\mathbb{MF}} on Σ𝕄​𝔽\Sigma^{\mathbb{MF}} which is ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant, such that near ∞\infty it is equal to H♮​𝗉​d​tH^{\natural{\sf p}}dt.
Now we describe the moduli spaces. Choose a pair of objects x=(x𝕄,x𝔼)∈Ob​𝕄ℤ𝗉x=(x^{\mathbb{M}},x^{{{\mathbb{E}}}})\in{\rm Ob}\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} and y=(y𝔽,y𝔼)∈Ob​𝔽ℤ𝗉y=(y^{\mathbb{F}},y^{{\mathbb{E}}})\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}. Consider the set of solutions (γ,u,v)(\gamma,u,v) where γ:(−∞,0]→X\gamma:(-\infty,0]\to X, u:Σ𝕄​𝔽→Xu:\Sigma^{\mathbb{MF}}\to X, and v:ℝ→S∞v:{\mathbb{R}}\to S^{\infty} are smooth maps solving
γ′​(s)+∇f𝕄​(γ⁡(s))=0,∂¯σ𝕄​𝔽​u=0,v′​(s)+∇f𝔼​(v⁡(s))=0,γ⁡(0)=u⁡(0)∈X\gamma^{\prime}(s)+\nabla f^{\mathbb{M}}(\gamma(s))=0,\ \overline{\partial}_{\sigma^{\mathbb{MF}}}u=0,\ v^{\prime}(s)+\nabla f^{{\mathbb{E}}}(v(s))=0,\ \gamma(0)=u(0)\in X
and subject to the following constraint
lims→−∞γ⁡(s)=x𝕄,lims→−∞v⁡(s)=x𝔼,lims→+∞v⁡(s)=y𝔼,lims→+∞u⁡(s,t)=y𝔽.\lim_{s\to-\infty}\gamma(s)=x^{\mathbb{M}},\ \lim_{s\to-\infty}v(s)=x^{{\mathbb{E}}},\ \lim_{s\to+\infty}v(s)=y^{{\mathbb{E}}},\lim_{s\to+\infty}u(s,t)=y^{\mathbb{F}}.
We compactify the space of such solutions (γ,u,v)(\gamma,u,v) by allowing synchronized breakings of Morse trajectories in X×S∞X\times S^{\infty} at the negative end and synchronized breakings of Floer trajectories in XX coupled with Morse trajectories in S∞S^{\infty} at the positive end. The compactified space is denoted by
Mx;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉.M_{x;y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}.
This space is stratified by the poset
Ax;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉:={(x−r⋯x−1;y1⋯ys)|x−r<⋯<x−1,y1<⋯<ys}.A_{x;y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:=\Big\{(x_{-r}\cdots x_{-1};y_{1}\cdots y_{s})\ |\ x_{-r}<\cdots<x_{-1},\ y_{1}<\cdots<y_{s}\Big\}.
There are also natural structural maps
ιx1​x0;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉:Mx1​x0𝕄ℤ𝗉×Mx0;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉→Mx1;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉,\displaystyle\ \iota_{x_{1}x_{0};y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:M_{x_{1}x_{0}}^{\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\times M_{x_{0};y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\to M_{x_{1};y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}},\ \
ιx;y0​y1𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉:Mx;y0𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉×My0​y1𝔽ℤ𝗉→Mx;y1𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\displaystyle\ \iota_{x;y_{0}y_{1}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:M_{x;y_{0}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\times M_{y_{0}y_{1}}^{\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\to M_{x;y_{1}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}
satisfying obvious associativity conditions. Hence one obtains a bimodule 𝔹𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} over (𝕄ℤ𝗉;𝔽ℤ𝗉)(\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}};\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}).
Fix an outercollaring width and let the outercollaring of the involved flow categories be
⌊𝕄ℤ𝗉,\displaystyle\ {}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},\
⌊𝔽ℤ𝗉.\displaystyle\ {}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}.
The source flow category is already enriched in both ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} and ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. The target flow category ⌊𝔽ℤ𝗉{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} admits an AMS lift 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} coming from a lift 𝔽^ℤ𝗉\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} in ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} (see Theorem 25.3). Here we will establish the lift of the bimodule ⌊𝔹𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}.
Proposition 25.10.
Given an equivariant AMS lift 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} of 𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}, there exists a class of lifts of the outercollaring of 𝔹𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}, denoted by 𝔹~𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}, called an equivariant AMS lift, which is a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant Novikov flow category over (𝕄⌊#𝔼;𝔽~ℤ𝗉)({}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{M}}\#{\mathbb{E}};\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}). Moreover, two different equivariant AMS lifts are homotopic via a Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant Novikov homotopy.
The proof of this proposition is given momentarily.
Now using FOP perturbations one can define the equivariant PSS map on the chain level. Choose an FOP perturbation 𝔽̊ℤ𝗉\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} of 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}, one has the associated cochain complex
C∗​(𝔽̊ℤ𝗉)C^{*}(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}})
whose ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part is the equivariant Floer cochain complex
C​Fℤ𝗉∗​(H♮​𝗉).CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{*}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}).
As 𝕄​#​𝔼{\mathbb{M}}\#{\mathbb{E}} can be viewed as its own FOP perturbation, by the multimodule case of Theorem N, one can extend the FOP perturbation 𝔽̊ℤ𝗉\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} to an FOP perturbation 𝔹̊𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\mathring{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} on 𝔹~𝕄​𝔽\tilde{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF}}. Then one obtains a cochain map
Φ~𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉:C∗​(𝕄​#​𝔼)→C∗​(𝔽̊ℤ𝗉)\widetilde{\Phi}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:C^{*}(\mathbb{M}\#{\mathbb{E}})\to C^{*}(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}})
which is Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{{\mathbb{\Pi}}}-linear and ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant.
Lemma 25.11.
The ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant chain homotopy class of Φ~𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\widetilde{\Phi}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} is independent of choices. Moreover, if 𝕄1,𝕄2{\mathbb{M}}_{1},{\mathbb{M}}_{2} are two Morse flow category associated to two Morse–Smale pair (f1,g1)(f_{1},g_{1}) and (f2,g2)(f_{2},g_{2}) on XX and 𝔽1,𝔽2{\mathbb{F}}_{1},{\mathbb{F}}_{2} are Floer flow categories associated to H1♮​𝗉H_{1}^{\natural{\sf p}} and H2♮​𝗉H_{2}^{\natural{\sf p}}, then the following diagram commutes
C∗​(𝕄1​#​𝔼)\textstyle{C^{*}({\mathbb{M}}_{1}\#{\mathbb{E}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}C∗​(𝔽̊1ℤ𝗉)\textstyle{C^{*}(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}C∗​(𝕄2​#​𝔼)\textstyle{C^{*}({\mathbb{M}}_{2}\#{\mathbb{E}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}C∗​(𝔽̊2ℤ𝗉)\textstyle{C^{*}(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}_{2}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}})}
up to ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant chain homotopy. Here the horizontal arrows are the chain-level PSS maps and the vertical arrows are induced from Morse or Floer continuation maps.
Therefore, after restricting to the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part, one obtains a canonical Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{{\mathbb{\Pi}}}-linear map
Φ𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉:H∗​(X,Λ𝐅𝗉Π​⟨θ⟩)→H​Fℤ𝗉∗​(X).\Phi^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:H^{*}(X;\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{{\mathbb{\Pi}}}\langle\uptheta\rangle)\to HF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{*}(X).
In a similar way, one can construct a chain-level Floer-to-Morse (SSP) map, which induces a well-defined Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}-linear map
Φ𝔽​𝕄,ℤ𝗉:H​Fℤ𝗉∗​(X)→H∗​(X,Λ𝐅𝗉Π​⟨θ⟩).\Phi^{\mathbb{FM},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:HF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{*}(X)\to H^{*}(X;\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}\langle\uptheta\rangle).
Just as in the nonequivariant case, we note that the maps Φ𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\Phi^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} and Φ𝔽​𝕄,ℤ𝗉\Phi^{\mathbb{FM},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} are isomorphisms.
Theorem 25.12.
The maps Φ𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\Phi^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} and Φ𝔽​𝕄,ℤ𝗉\Phi^{\mathbb{FM},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} are isomorphisms on cohomology.
Proof.
On the chain level, we can turn on a exhaustive, complete, and decreasing filtration on both C​Fℤ𝗉∗​(H♮​𝗉)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{*}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}) and C∗​(𝕄​#​𝔼)ℤ𝗉C^{*}(\mathbb{M}\#{\mathbb{E}})^{\mathbb{Z}_{\sf p}} by tracking the degree in 𝚄\mathtt{U} and θ\uptheta. Then both the equivariant diffferentials and equivariant PSS/SSP maps respect the filtration. On the other hand, geometrically, the constructions in Section 25.2 can be performed such that the induced differentials and chain maps on the associated graded agrees with the ones coming from the ordinary Morse cohomology, the ordinary Hamiltonian Floer cohomology, and the ordinary PSS/SSP maps. Therefore, based on Theorem F, we conclude the theorem.
∎
25.4. AMS construction for equivariant PSS and SSP maps
We provide detailed construction for the PSS map. The case for SSP map is very similar.
Similar to the non-equivariant case, we first choose an integral action 𝒜Ω:Ob​𝔽→ℤ{\mathcal{A}}^{\Omega}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\to{\mathbb{Z}} which is compatible with respect to the bimodule 𝔹𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} (or more precisely, compatible with the Floer data).
25.4.1. The domain bimodule for the AMS construction
We first describe the analogue of the space of domains, i.e., a bimodule enriched in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}. Recall that the AMS construction for 𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} (see Subsection 25.2) provides a flow category 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} whose objects are the same as those of 𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}. However, the flow category 𝕄ℤ𝗉\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} does not yet have such a corresponding flow category enriched in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}. We define such a flow category as follows. For each pair x0,x1∈Ob​𝕄ℤ𝗉x_{0},x_{1}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{M}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}, define
𝒞x0​x1𝕄ℤ𝗉=(G,Bx0​x1,C){\mathcal{C}}_{x_{0}x_{1}}^{\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}=(G,B_{x_{0}x_{1}},C)
where GG is the trivial group, Bx0​x1=Mx0​x1𝕄ℤ𝗉B_{x_{0}x_{1}}=M_{x_{0}x_{1}}^{\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} is the moduli space of flow lines between x0x_{0} and x1x_{1}, and C=∅C=\emptyset, regarded as a family of empty curves over Bx0​x1B_{x_{0}x_{1}}. After outercollaring, we denote this rather trivial flow category enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}} by
𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝕄ℤ𝗉.\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}.
As the concatenation of Morse flow lines does not involve stabilization and the Lie groups do not change, this flow category is automatically enriched in the rigidified version ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}. However we do not consider stable complex structure.
Now we describe a bimodule over (𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝕄ℤ𝗉;𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔽ℤ𝗉)(\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}};\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}), denoted by 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}. Fix a pair of objects
x=(x𝕄,x𝔼)∈Ob​𝕄ℤ𝗉,\displaystyle\ x=(x^{\mathbb{M}},x^{{\mathbb{E}}})\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{M}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},\
y=(y𝔽,y𝔼)∈Ob​𝔽ℤ𝗉.\displaystyle\ y=(y^{\mathbb{F}},y^{{\mathbb{E}}})\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}.
Notice that xx and yy determines an integer dx;yd_{x;y} which is the difference of the symplectic area of x𝕄x^{\mathbb{M}} and the integrally modified symplectic action of y𝔽y^{\mathbb{F}}.
Consider the the space of triples (γ,ϕ,η)(\gamma,\phi,\eta) where γ:(−∞,0]→X\gamma:(-\infty,0]\to X, ϕ:ℝ×S1→ℂ​ℙdx;y\phi:{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}\to\mathbb{CP}^{d_{x;y}}, and η:ℝ→S^∞\eta:{\mathbb{R}}\to\widehat{S}^{\infty} are smooth maps, solving the following equation
γ′​(s)+∇f𝕄​(γ⁡(s))=0,∂¯​ϕ=0,η′​(s)+∇f𝔼​(η⁡(s))=0\gamma^{\prime}(s)+\nabla f^{\mathbb{M}}(\gamma(s))=0,\ \overline{\partial}\phi=0,\ \eta^{\prime}(s)+\nabla f^{{\mathbb{E}}}(\eta(s))=0
satisfying the following asymptotic constraints
lims→−∞γ⁡(s)=x𝕄,lims→−∞η⁡(s)=x𝔼,lims→+∞η⁡(s)=y𝔼\lim_{s\to-\infty}\gamma(s)=x^{\mathbb{M}},\ \lim_{s\to-\infty}\eta(s)=x^{{\mathbb{E}}},\ \lim_{s\to+\infty}\eta(s)=y^{{\mathbb{E}}}
and the constraint
ϕ⁡(+∞)=[0,…,0,1]∈ℂ​ℙdx;y.\phi(+\infty)=[0,\ldots,0,1]\in\mathbb{CP}^{d_{x;y}}.
Notice that there is no requirement for γ⁡(0)\gamma(0) and u⁡(−∞)u(-\infty). We compactify this space by allowing sychrnoized breakings in X×S^∞X\times\widehat{S}^{\infty} at the negative end and synchronized breakings of holomorphic cylinders in ℂ​ℙdx;y\mathbb{CP}^{d_{x;y}} and Morse trajectories in S∞S^{\infty}. Next, we remove those elements whose images in ℂ​ℙdx;y\mathbb{CP}^{d_{x;y}} lie in any hyperplane. Denote this space by
Bx;y.B_{x;y}.
Then this is a smooth stratified manifold with a 𝒢dx;y{\mathcal{G}}_{d_{x;y}}-action. On top of it there is the universal curve
Cx;y→Bx;y.C_{x;y}\to B_{x;y}.
Then the triple
𝒞x;y:=(𝒢x;y,Bx;y,Cx;y)​where​𝒢x;y=𝒢dx;y{\mathcal{C}}_{x;y}:=({\mathcal{G}}_{x;y},B_{x;y},C_{x;y})\ {\rm where}\ {\mathcal{G}}_{x;y}={\mathcal{G}}_{d_{x;y}}
is an object of 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}. We can also define structural maps
𝒞x0​x1𝕄ℤ𝗉×𝒞x1;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉→𝒞x0;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉,𝒞x;y0𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉×𝒞y0​y1𝔽ℤ𝗉→𝒞x;y1𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉.{\mathcal{C}}_{x_{0}x_{1}}^{{\mathbb{M}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\times{\mathcal{C}}_{x_{1};y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{x_{0};y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}},\ {\mathcal{C}}_{x;y_{0}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\times{\mathcal{C}}_{y_{0}y_{1}}^{{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\to{\mathcal{C}}_{x;y_{1}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}.
This provide a flow bimodule 𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} over (𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝕄ℤ𝗉;𝔻​𝕠​𝕞𝔽ℤ𝗉)(\mathbb{Dom}^{{\mathbb{M}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}};\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}). One can check that this bimodule is Π𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}_{\sf p}-equivariant.
25.4.2. Thickening
One can consider the space of framed maps Mapx;yfr​(X){\rm Map}_{x;y}^{\rm fr}(X) whose elements are (ϕ,u,F)(\phi,u,F) where ϕ∈Bx;y\phi\in B_{x;y}, u:Cϕ→Xu:C_{\phi}\to X is an admissible map, and FF is a frame determined by uu and the integral symplectic form Ω\Omega. Recall that ϕ\phi carries the information of a flow ray in XX and we do not require that the evaluation of uu at −∞-\infty coincides with the value of the flow ray at 00. One chooses an equivariant group reduction scheme
λx;y:Mapx;yfr⌊(X)→Qx;y:=Qdx;y\lambda_{x;y}:{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{x;y}^{\rm fr}(X)\to Q_{x;y}:=Q_{d_{x;y}}
which extends the group reduction scheme chosen for the AMS construction for 𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}. On the other hand, we also choose thickening data
νx;y:Wx;y→Γc​(C̊x;y×X,ΛC̊x,y/Bx;y0,1⊗T​X)\nu_{x;y}:W_{x;y}\to\Gamma_{c}(\mathring{C}_{x;y}\times X,\Lambda_{\mathring{C}_{x,y}/B_{x;y}}^{0,1}\otimes TX)
extending the thickening data chosen for the AMS construction for 𝔽^ℤ𝗉\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}. Define the thickening
Vˇx;y:={(ϕ,u,F,e)|(ϕ,u,F)∈⌊Mapx;yfr(X),e∈Wx;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉∂¯​u+νx;y​(e)=0,ϕ=ϕF}.\check{V}_{x;y}:=\left\{(\phi,u,F,e)\ \left|\ \begin{array}[]{c}(\phi,u,F)\in{}_{\lfloor}{\rm Map}_{x;y}^{\rm fr}(X),\ e\in W_{x;y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\\
\overline{\partial}u+\nu_{x;y}(e)=0,\ \phi=\phi_{F}\end{array}\right.\right\}.
The obstruction bundle Ex;yE_{x;y} is the trivial bundle with fiber Wx;y⊕Qx;yW_{x;y}\oplus Q_{x;y} and the Kuranishi section is
Sx;y​(ϕ,u,F,e)=(e,λx;y​(ϕ,u,F)).S_{x;y}(\phi,u,F,e)=(e,\lambda_{x;y}(\phi,u,F)).
We summarize the construction so far in the following proposition.
Proposition 25.13.
The collection of Kuranishi spaces
Kˇx;y:=(Gx;y,Vˇx;y,Ex;y,Sx;y)\check{K}_{x;y}:=(G_{x;y},\check{V}_{x;y},E_{x;y},S_{x;y})
together with the structural maps
⌊Mx0​x1𝕄ℤ𝗉×Kx1;y→Kx0;y{}_{\lfloor}M_{x_{0}x_{1}}^{\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\times K_{x_{1};y}\to K_{x_{0};y}
and
Kx;y0×Ky0​y1𝔽ℤ𝗉→Kx;y1K_{x;y_{0}}\times K_{y_{0}y_{1}}^{\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\to K_{x;y_{1}}
define a bimodule 𝕏ˇ𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\check{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} over (𝕄ℤ𝗉⌊;𝔽^ℤ𝗉)({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{M}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}) enriched in 𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}.
Notice that 𝕏ˇ𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\check{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} is not a lift of 𝕏𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} as we did not impose the matching condition in XX.
We then construct the vertical NC structure. Similar to the case for 𝔽^ℤ𝗉\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}, the construction can be carried out in a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant fashion. Hence one obtains a bimodule enriched in ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}.
We still apply the same smoothing strategy to obtain a stable smoothing of 𝕄ˇ𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\check{\mathbb{M}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}. To simplify notations, we still denote by the same symbol. Moreover, we may require that the natural map
ev:Vˇx;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉→X×X{\rm ev}:\check{V}_{x;y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\to X\times X
is a submersion, hence transverse to the diagonal. Define
Vx;y𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉:=ev−1​(ΔX)V_{x;y}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:={\rm ev}^{-1}(\Delta_{X})
and define Kx;yK_{x;y} be the restriction of Kˇx;y\check{K}_{x;y} to this closed submanifold. Finally, incoporating the stable complex structure on the domain bimodule, one obtains an NC structure. We summarize the construction as follows.
Proposition 25.14.
The collection of Kuranishi spaces Kx;yK_{x;y} together with the restriction of the structural morphisms of Proposition 25.13 define a lift of 𝕏𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}, denoted by 𝕏^𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉\hat{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}, which is a bimodule over (𝕄⌊#𝔼;𝔽^ℤ𝗉)({}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{M}}\#{\mathbb{E}};\hat{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}).
Finally, by taking the quotient by the Lie group actions, we obtain 𝔹𝕄​𝔽,ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF},{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}. One can further follow the machinery of this paper to address the invariance property. This concludes Proposition 25.10.
26. The Equivariant Pair-of-Pants—Proof of Theorem J
The equivariant pair-of-pants product can be viewed as a Floer-theoretic analogue of the quantum Steenrod operation. It is defined via a multimodule associated to a Floer domain having a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-symmetry. The main results regarding such a construction is stated in Theorem J. Given the recurring nature of our arguments, we highlight the distinctive features.
26.1. The equivariant pair-of-pants multimodule
Let (X,ω,J)(X,\omega,J) be a compact almost Kähler manifold. Again, we do not discuss the dependence on JJ, which could be done without new difficulty. Let 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} be the Floer flow category of a Hamiltonian HH and let 𝔽ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} be the coupling of the Floer flow category of the 𝗉{\sf p}-th iteration H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}} with the Morse flow category 𝔼{{\mathbb{E}}} on S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty}.2727
27
In general one could allow the 𝗉{\sf p}-fold iteration of a different Hamiltonian. We describe a multimodule 𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{FSt}} over (𝔽,⋯,𝔽,𝔼,𝔽ℤ𝗉)({\mathbb{F}},\cdots,{\mathbb{F}},{{\mathbb{E}}};{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}) where 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} appears 𝗉{\sf p} times in the source.
26.1.1. The Floer domain and the equation
Let z1,…,z𝗉∈ℂ⊆ℂ​ℙ1z_{1},\ldots,z_{{\sf p}}\in{\mathbb{C}}\subseteq\mathbb{CP}^{1} be all the 𝗉{\sf p}-th roots of unity. Let
Σ:=ℂ​ℙ1∖{z1,…,z𝗉,z∞=∞}\Sigma:=\mathbb{CP}^{1}\setminus\{z_{1},\ldots,z_{{\sf p}},z_{\infty}=\infty\}
be the punctured sphere, which has a holomorphic ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action permuting the finite punctures. Choose a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant Floer datum σℤ𝗉\sigma^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} on Σ\Sigma whose restriction on the 𝗉{\sf p} negative ends are H​d​tHdt and whose restriction on the positive end is the 𝗉{\sf p}-th iteration H♮​𝗉​d​tH^{\natural{\sf p}}dt. In fact, one can choose different HH for negative and positive ends as in the setup of Theorem J, but we spell out the argument for H−=H+=HH_{-}=H_{+}=H to simplify the notations. Solutions to the Floer equation
∂¯σℤ𝗉​u=0,u:Σ→X\overline{\partial}_{\sigma^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}}u=0,\ u:\Sigma\to X
converge to periodic orbits of HH at negative ends and periodic orbits of H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}} at the positive end.
26.1.2. The moduli spaces and the multimodule
We define the morphism spaces of the multimodule 𝕏ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{X}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}. Choose a collection of objects
(x1𝔽,…​x𝗉𝔽,x𝔼)∈Ob𝔽×⋯×Ob𝔽⏟𝗉×Ob​𝔼(x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}},\ldots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}},x^{{\mathbb{E}}})\in\underbrace{{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}\times\cdots\times{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}}_{{\sf p}}\times{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{E}}
and an object y=(y𝔽♮​𝗉,y𝔼)∈Ob​𝔽ℤ𝗉y=(y^{\mathbb{F}^{\natural{\sf p}}},y^{{\mathbb{E}}})\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}, where y𝔽♮​𝗉y^{\mathbb{F}^{\natural{\sf p}}} is the flow category associated with the Hamiltonian H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}}, we describe a moduli space as follows. Consider pairs
u:Σ→X,v:ℝ→S^∞u:\Sigma\to X,\ v:{\mathbb{R}}\to\widehat{S}^{\infty}
where uu is a solution to ∂¯σℤ𝗉​u=0\overline{\partial}_{\sigma^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}}u=0 converging to xi𝔽x_{i}^{\mathbb{F}} at the ii-th negative cylindrical ends, i=1,…,𝗉i=1,\ldots,{\sf p}, to y𝔽♮​𝗉y^{\mathbb{F}^{\natural{\sf p}}} at the positive cylindrical end, and where vv is a Morse flow line of f𝔼f^{{\mathbb{E}}} connecting x𝔼x^{{\mathbb{E}}} and y𝔼y^{{\mathbb{E}}} at negative and positive ends respectively. We compactify the space of such solutions in the following way: while allowing sphere bubbling, the breakings at negative ends are treated as independent breaking while the breakings at positive ends are synchronized. Let the compactified space be Mx1𝔽⋯x𝗉𝔽x𝔼;y𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥M_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}}}.
There are obvious inclusions given by breakings of the domains. For i=1,…,𝗉i=1,\ldots,{\sf p} and xi𝔽≤wi𝔽x_{i}^{{\mathbb{F}}}\leq w_{i}^{{\mathbb{F}}} in the ii-th source flow category, there is a map
Mxi𝔽​wi𝔽𝔽×Mx1𝔽⋯xi−1𝔽wi𝔽xi+1𝔽⋯x𝗉𝔽x𝔼;y𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥→Mx1𝔽⋯x𝗉𝔽x𝔼;y𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥;M_{x_{i}^{\mathbb{F}}w_{i}^{\mathbb{F}}}^{{\mathbb{F}}}\times M_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}}\cdots x_{i-1}^{\mathbb{F}}w_{i}^{\mathbb{F}}x_{i+1}^{\mathbb{F}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}}x^{{{\mathbb{E}}}};y}^{\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{FSt}}}\to M_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{FSt}}};
for x𝔼≤w𝔼x^{{\mathbb{E}}}\leq w^{{\mathbb{E}}} in 𝔼{{\mathbb{E}}}, a map
Mx𝔼​w𝔼𝔼×Mx1𝔽⋯x𝗉𝔽w𝔼;y𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥→Mx1𝔽⋯x𝗉𝔽x𝔼;y𝕏𝔉​𝔖​𝔱;M_{x^{{\mathbb{E}}}w^{{\mathbb{E}}}}^{{\mathbb{E}}}\times M_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}}w^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}}}\to M_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{\mathbb{X}^{\mathfrak{FSt}}};
for w≤yw\leq y in 𝔽ℤ𝗉\mathbb{F}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}, a map
Mx1𝔽⋯x𝗉𝔽x𝔼;w𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥×Mw​y𝔽ℤ𝗉→Mx1𝔽⋯x𝗉𝔽x𝔼;y𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥.M_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};w}^{\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{FSt}}}\times M_{wy}^{\mathbb{F}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\to M_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{FSt}}}.
These maps satisfy the conditions required for a multimodule. Hence one obtains a multimodule 𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}} over (𝔽,…,𝔽,𝔼,𝔽ℤ𝗉)(\mathbb{F},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}},{{\mathbb{E}}};{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}) enriched in 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯\underline{\smash{\bf Top}}.
26.1.3. The symmetry
Define the Novikov monoid
Π(𝗉):=Π×⋯×Π⏟𝗉×ℤ.\mathbb{\Pi}^{({\sf p})}:=\underbrace{\Pi\times\cdots\times\Pi}_{{\sf p}}\times{\mathbb{Z}}.
There is a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action on Π(𝗉)\mathbb{\Pi}^{({\sf p})} by isomorphisms of Novikov monoids given by permuting the first 𝗉{\sf p} factors in the above product. Then we can form the semi-direct product Π(𝗉)⋊ℤ𝗉\mathbb{\Pi}^{({\sf p})}\rtimes{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}.
We can view the multimodule 𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}} as a weak bimodule over (𝔽×⋯×𝔽×𝔼;𝔽ℤ𝗉)({\mathbb{F}}\times\cdots\times{\mathbb{F}}\times{{\mathbb{E}}};{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}). On the source weak flow category, it has the action
𝒜⁡(x1𝔽,…,x𝗉𝔽,x𝔼)=(𝒜H​(x1𝔽),…,𝒜H​(x𝗉𝔽),𝒜𝔼​(x𝔼))∈ℝ𝗉+1.{\mathcal{A}}(x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}},\ldots,x^{\mathbb{F}}_{\sf p},x^{{{\mathbb{E}}}})=({\mathcal{A}}_{H}(x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}}),\ldots,{\mathcal{A}}_{H}(x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}}),{\mathcal{A}}_{{{\mathbb{E}}}}(x^{{\mathbb{E}}}))\in{\mathbb{R}}^{{\sf p}+1}.
Proposition 26.1.
The collection of moduli spaces Mx1𝔽⋯x𝗉𝔽x𝔼;y𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥M_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{F}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{F}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}}} define a Novikov multimodule over (𝔽,⋯,𝔽,𝔼,𝔽ℤ𝗉)({\mathbb{F}},\cdots,{\mathbb{F}},{{\mathbb{E}}};{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}) which is equivariant with respect to the natural morphism
ρ:Π(𝗉)→Π,(a1,…,a𝗉,l)↦(a1+⋯+a𝗉,l)\rho:\mathbb{\Pi}^{({\sf p})}\to\mathbb{\Pi},\ (a_{1},\ldots,a_{\sf p},l)\mapsto(a_{1}+\cdots+a_{\sf p},l)
of Novikov monoids. Moreover, as a weak bimodule over (𝔽×⋯×𝔽×𝔼;𝔽ℤ𝗉)({\mathbb{F}}\times\cdots\times{\mathbb{F}}\times{{\mathbb{E}}};{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}), it is equivariant with respect to ρ\rho.
Proof.
Straightforward.
∎
26.1.4. Regularization and the equivariant pair-of-pants product
Fix an outercollaring width and a compatible choice of integral actions. Recall that the outercollarings of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} and 𝔽ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} both admit AMS lifts to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}{}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}.
Proposition 26.2.
There exists a lift of the outercollaring of 𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}}, denoted by 𝕏~𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}}, to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯NCrig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}^{\rm NC}_{\rm rig}, which is a ρ\rho-equivariant Novikov multimodule over (𝔽~,…,𝔽~,𝔼⌊;𝔽~ℤ𝗉)(\tilde{\mathbb{F}},\ldots,\tilde{\mathbb{F}},{}_{\lfloor}{{\mathbb{E}}};\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}).
Proof.
The construction is analogous to the AMS construction for a general multimodule induced from a smooth Floer domain, except that the moduli spaces curves now has the parametrization factor from the moduli spaces of Morse trajectories in S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty} as in Section 25.4.1. One can carry out the construction almost verbatim; the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariance condition can be achieved because the action is free.
∎
Now let 𝔽̊\mathring{\mathbb{F}} be an FOP transverse perturbation on 𝔽~\tilde{\mathbb{F}} and 𝔽̊ℤ𝗉\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} be a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant FOP transverse perturbation on 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}. Let C​F​(H)CF(H) resp. C⁡(𝔽̊ℤ𝗉)C(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}) be the associated complex over Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi} resp. over Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{{\mathbb{\Pi}}}; the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part of C⁡(𝔽̊ℤ𝗉)C(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}) is the equivariant complex C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}). By the multimodule case of Theorem N, one can extend these FOP transverse perturbations to a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant FOP transverse perturbation 𝕏̊𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\mathring{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}} on 𝕏~𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}}. Then by Proposition 7.18, it induces a 𝐅𝗉{\bf F}_{\sf p}-linear chain map
P~:CF(H)⊗𝐅𝗉^⋯⊗𝐅𝗉^CF(H)⏞𝗉​⊗𝐅𝗉^​C​(𝔼)→C⁡(𝔽̊ℤ𝗉).\widetilde{P}:\overbrace{CF(H)\widehat{\underset{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}{\otimes}}\cdots\widehat{\underset{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}{\otimes}}CF(H)}^{{\sf p}}\widehat{\underset{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}{\otimes}}C({{\mathbb{E}}})\to C(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}).
The ρ\rho-equivariance condition on the multimodule 𝕏̊𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\mathring{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}} implies that ΦFSt\Phi^{\rm FSt} induces a map
P~:(CF(H)⊗𝐅𝗉^⋯⊗𝐅𝗉^CF(H)⏞𝗉​⊗𝐅𝗉^​C​M​(f𝔼))​⊗Λ𝐅𝗉Π(𝗉)​Λ𝐅𝗉Π→C⁡(𝔽̊ℤ𝗉)\widetilde{P}:\left(\overbrace{CF(H)\widehat{\underset{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}{\otimes}}\cdots\widehat{\underset{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}{\otimes}}CF(H)}^{{\sf p}}\widehat{\underset{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}{\otimes}}CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\right)\underset{\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{{\mathbb{\Pi}}^{({\sf p})}}}{\otimes}\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}\to C(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}})
which is ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant and Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}-linear.
Restricting to the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part, one obtains the chain-level equivariant pair-of-pants product
P:Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)P:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})
hence a map on the cohomology level (denoted by the same notation)
P:Hℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)→H​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉).P:H_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to HF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}).
26.2. Proof of Theorem J
As above, we write down the proof for H−=H+=HH_{-}=H_{+}=H to simplify the notations.
26.2.1. Independence of choices
Lemma 26.3.
P~\widetilde{P} is well-defined up to ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant chain homotopies. Therefore, restricting to the ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}-invariant part, PP is well-defined up to chain homotopies.
Proof.
Two concrete chain level constructions can be connected by a homotopy: we can carry out the construction of multimodule homotopies in the ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}-equivariant setting using families of curves with parametrization having the additional factor from the moduli spaces of Morse trajectories in S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty}, and the ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}-equivariance can be achieved due to the freeness.
∎
Therefore, following the definition of 𝐹𝑆𝑡𝗉{\it FSt}_{{\sf p}} in Theorem J, we see that the Floer-theoretic Steenrod operation does not depend on any choices after passing to cohomology. This finishes proving Theorem J (1) and (3).
26.2.2. Isomorphism on cohomology
Theorem J (2) follows from a stronger assertion in the quantitative setting, Corollary 27.10, which is proven in the next Section. The idea is that instead of directly constructing a chain-homotopy inverse of PP by dualizing the equivariant pair-of-pants product, we turn on the action filtration on the (equivariant) Floer chain complexes, which the operation PP respects, so that the induced operation on the associated graded reduces to the equivariant pants product on local Floer cohomology. Then, by appealing to the known isomorphism property in [60, 62] in the aspherical setting, which, in particular, applies to local Floer theory, we conclude that PP is an isomorphism on cohomology.
Remark 26.4.
Using Proposition 23.3, we further see that 𝐹𝑆𝑡𝗉{\it FSt}_{{\sf p}} is an isomorphism. This is the generalization of the localization results in [60, 62] for general compact symplectic manifolds in Hamiltonian Floer theory. We expect that the method in this paper can also be used for proving an analogous result for the fixed point Floer cohomology associated with a general symplectic automorphism, though one needs a slight different regularization procedure.
26.2.3. The multimodule homotopy
Finally, we prove the commutativity of Diagram (1.7) in Theorem J (4). The core of the proof is the following chain-level assertion. As we only need the cohomological level conclusion, one fixes a Hamiltonian H=H−=H+H=H_{-}=H_{+} such that H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}} is nondegenerate. Moreover, fix a Morse–Smale pair (f,g)(f,g) on XX with associated Morse flow category 𝕄¯\underline{\smash{\mathbb{M}}} (whose cohomology is isomorphic to H⁡(X,ΛℤΠ)H(X;\Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}}^{\Pi})).
