Now we prove Lemma 26.5. The proof is based on a multimodule homotopy between the following two multimodules. The first one is the Steenrod multimodule 𝕏ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{QSt}} over (𝕄,…,𝕄,𝔼,𝕄​#​𝔼)(\mathbb{M},\ldots,\mathbb{M},{{\mathbb{E}}};\mathbb{M}\#{{\mathbb{E}}}), which will lead to the quantum Steenrod operation 𝑄𝑆𝑡𝗉{\it QSt}_{{\sf p}}. The second one is the concatenation of three multimodules: first, there is the non-equivariant Morse-to-Floer bimodule 𝔹𝕄​𝔽\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF}}. Consider the product of 𝗉{\sf p} copies of this bimodule with a copy of the diagonal bimodule Δ𝔼\mathbb{\Delta}^{{{\mathbb{E}}}}
(𝔹𝕄​𝔽)𝗉×Δ𝔼:=𝔹𝕄​𝔽×⋯×𝔹𝕄​𝔽⏟𝗉×Δ𝔼​𝔼,(\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF}})^{\sf p}\times\mathbb{\Delta}^{{{\mathbb{E}}}}:=\underbrace{\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF}}\times\cdots\times\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF}}}_{{\sf p}}\times\mathbb{\Delta}^{{{\mathbb{E}}}{{\mathbb{E}}}},
which is a multimodule over (𝕄,…,𝕄,𝔼,𝔽,…,𝔽,𝔼)(\mathbb{M},\ldots,{\mathbb{M}},{{\mathbb{E}}};\mathbb{F},\ldots,\mathbb{F},{{\mathbb{E}}}). It can be composed with the multimodule 𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}}, followed by the equivariant SSP bimodule 𝔹ℤ𝗉𝔽​𝕄{\mathbb{B}}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\mathbb{FM}}.
Before we move on, we specify the symmetries of the flow categories and multimodules. The flow categories 𝕄{\mathbb{M}} and 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} carry the action by the group Π\Pi and 𝔼{{\mathbb{E}}} carries the action by ℤ{\mathbb{Z}}. The flow category 𝕄​#​𝔼\mathbb{M}\#{{\mathbb{E}}} carries the action by (the trivially twisted) Π×ℤ×ℤ𝗉\Pi\times\mathbb{Z}\times{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}. The multimodule 𝕏ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{QSt}} is equivariant with respect to the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant morphism of Novikov monoids
ρ𝕊​𝕥:Π×⋯×Π×ℤ→Π×ℤ.\rho^{\mathbb{St}}:\Pi\times\cdots\times\Pi\times{\mathbb{Z}}\to\Pi\times{\mathbb{Z}}.
Moreover, as a weak bimodule (see Definition 6.17), 𝕏ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{QSt}} is ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant. It is easy to see that the same is true for the triple concatenation.
Now fix a common outercollaring width. Also choose an integral action 𝒜𝔽Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega} on 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} and an integral action 𝒜𝔽♮​𝗉Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\natural{\sf p}}}^{\Omega} which are compatible with respect to involved Floer data.
Suppose 𝔽~\tilde{\mathbb{F}} is an AMS lift of 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} subject to the outercollaring width and the action 𝒜𝔽Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{F}}^{\Omega}. Let 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} be an equivariant AMS lift of the outercollaring of 𝔽ℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} subject to the outercollaring width and the action 𝒜𝔽♮​𝗉Ω{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{F}}^{\natural{\sf p}}}^{\Omega}. Let 𝔹~𝕄​𝔽\tilde{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF}} is an AMS lift of the outercollaring of 𝔹𝕄​𝔽\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF}} as a bimodule over (𝕄⌊,𝔽~)({}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{M}},\tilde{\mathbb{F}}). Let 𝕏~𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}} be an equivariant AMS lift of the outercollaring of 𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}} extending 𝔽~\tilde{\mathbb{F}} and 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}. Let 𝔹~ℤ𝗉𝔽​𝕄\tilde{\mathbb{B}}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\mathbb{FM}} be an equivariant AMS lift of the outercollaring of 𝔹ℤ𝗉𝔽​𝕄{\mathbb{B}}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\mathbb{FM}}.
Lemma 26.6.
There exists a ρ𝕊​𝕥\rho^{\mathbb{St}}-equivariant homotopy ℍ~\tilde{\mathbb{H}} from 𝕏~ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{QSt}} to
((𝔹~𝕄​𝔽)𝗉×Δ𝔼​𝔼⌊)∘𝕏~𝔽​𝕊​𝕥∘𝔹~ℤ𝗉𝔽​𝕄\Big((\tilde{\mathbb{B}}^{\mathbb{MF}})^{\sf p}\times{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{\Delta}^{{{\mathbb{E}}}{{\mathbb{E}}}}\Big)\circ\tilde{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}}\circ\tilde{\mathbb{B}}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\mathbb{FM}}
enriched in the category ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}.
Assuming this lemma, we can conclude the assertion of Lemma 26.5. Since all actions are free, one can choose equivariant FOP transverse perturbations, firstly on the flow categories 𝔽~\tilde{\mathbb{F}} and 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}, then on the multimodules, and then on the homotopy ℍ~\tilde{\mathbb{H}}, thanks to Theorem N. Then the corresponding homotopy ℍ̊\mathring{\mathbb{H}} enriched in 𝚿​𝐌𝐚𝐧¯\underline{\smash{{\bf\Psi}{\bf Man}}} induces a chain homotopy Ψℍ̊\Psi^{\mathring{\mathbb{H}}} between the two chain maps, the chain map corresponding to the quantum Steenrod operation and the composition of the three chain maps. This means the diagram (26.1) commutes up to homotopy.
26.2.4. Proof of Lemma 26.6
We first describe the homotopy in the category 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯\underline{\smash{\bf Top}} before the outercollaring, from 𝕏ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{QSt}} to the concatenation
𝕐:=((𝔹𝕄​𝔽)𝗉×Δ𝔼​𝔼)∘𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥∘𝔹ℤ𝗉𝔽​𝕄.\mathbb{Y}:=\left((\mathbb{B}^{\mathbb{MF}})^{\sf p}\times\mathbb{\Delta}^{{{\mathbb{E}}}{{\mathbb{E}}}}\right)\circ\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{FSt}}\circ\mathbb{B}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\mathbb{FM}}.
Consider the sphere Σ𝗉𝕊​𝕥≅ℂ​ℙ1\Sigma_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{St}}\cong\mathbb{CP}^{1} equipped with a 1-parameter family of Floer data σt\sigma_{t} parametrized by t∈[0,1]t\in[0,1] where, when t=0t=0, σt≡0\sigma_{t}\equiv 0 while as t→1t\to 1, the long necks around each negative markings have the Hamiltonian connection H​d​tHdt which is ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant while the long neck around the positive marking has the Hamiltonian H♮​𝗉​d​tH^{\natural{\sf p}}dt. Then for any tt, σt\sigma_{t} is invariant under the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action on the domain.
Figure 10. The concatenation of three multimodules. Notice that the gluing on the left have 𝗉+1{\sf p}+1 gluing parameters and the gluing on the right has only one gluing parameter.
Now we can describe the moduli spaces responsible for the homotopy. Choose
x1𝕄,…,x𝗉𝕄∈Ob​𝕄,x𝔼∈Ob​𝔼,y=(y𝕄,y𝔼)∈Ob​𝕄𝔼.x_{1}^{\mathbb{M}},\ldots,x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{M}}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{M}},\ x^{{\mathbb{E}}}\in{\rm Ob}{{\mathbb{E}}},\ y=(y^{\mathbb{M}},y^{{\mathbb{E}}})\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{M}}^{{\mathbb{E}}}.
Consider the moduli space of triples (t,u,v)(t,u,v) where t∈[0,1)t\in[0,1), u:Σ𝗉𝕊​𝕥→Xu:\Sigma_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{St}}\to X and v:ℝ→S^∞v:{\mathbb{R}}\to\widehat{S}^{\infty} are smooth maps solving
(∇σt)0,1​u=0,v′​(s)+∇f𝔼​(v⁡(s))=0(\nabla^{\sigma_{t}})^{0,1}u=0,\ v^{\prime}(s)+\nabla f^{{\mathbb{E}}}(v(s))=0
and
u(zi)∈Wxi𝕄us,i=1,…,𝗉,u(z∞)∈Wy𝕄st,lims→−∞v(s)=x𝔼,lims→+∞v(s)=y𝔼.u(z_{i})\in W^{\rm us}_{x_{i}^{\mathbb{M}}},\ i=1,\ldots,{\sf p},\ u(z_{\infty})\in W^{\rm st}_{y^{\mathbb{M}}},\lim_{s\to-\infty}v(s)=x^{{{\mathbb{E}}}},\ \lim_{s\to+\infty}v(s)=y^{{\mathbb{E}}}.
Let the space of solutions be M̊x1𝕄⋯x𝗉𝕄x𝔼;yℍ\mathring{M}_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{M}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{M}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{{\mathbb{H}}}. We may regard the constraints of uu at ziz_{i} as adding gradient rays of ff in XX. Then let
Mx1𝕄⋯x𝗉𝕄x𝔼;yℍM_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{M}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{M}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{{\mathbb{H}}}
be its natural compactification which allows sphere bubbling, Morse trajectory breaking, and breakings along Floer trajectories as t→1t\to 1. Moreover, when Morse trajectories break in the positive end, the trajectories broken off are regarded as flow lines in the product X×S^∞X\times\widehat{S}^{\infty}. The following lemma can be verified easily.
Lemma 26.7.
The collection of spaces Mx1𝕄⋯x𝗉𝕄x𝔼;yℍM_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{M}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{M}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{{\mathbb{H}}} forms a homotopy from 𝕏ℚ​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{QSt}} to the concatenation 𝕐{\mathbb{Y}}. Moreover, this is a ρ𝕊​𝕥\rho^{\mathbb{St}}-equivariant Novikov homotopy and ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant as a weak homotopy.
26.2.5. The AMS construction
Now we describe the AMS lift of the outercollaring of the homotopy ℍ{\mathbb{H}}, given AMS lifts of involved Floer flow categories and multimodules.
Recall the AMS lift 𝔽~\tilde{\mathbb{F}} of the Floer flow category 𝔽{\mathbb{F}} contains a domain monotone flow category ⌊𝔻om{}_{\lfloor}{\mathbb{D}om} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}. The AMS lift 𝔽~ℤ𝗉\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} also contains a domain monotone flow category ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞ℤ𝗉{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} enriched in ⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} which also has a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action corresponding to the domain rotation.
The lift 𝕏~ℚ​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{QSt}} contains the domain monotone multimodule ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞ℚ​𝕊​𝕥{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{QSt}}. The lift 𝕏~𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\tilde{\mathbb{X}}^{\mathbb{FSt}} has a similar monotone multimodule ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝔽​𝕊​𝕥{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{FSt}}. There are also the monotone bimodules ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞𝕄​𝔽{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{MF}} and ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞ℤ𝗉𝔽​𝕄{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\mathbb{FM}}. Then similar to previous cases of obtaining monotone homotopies involving concatenations and gluing, one can define a monotone homotopy from ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞ℚ​𝕊​𝕥{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{QSt}} to the concatenation
(𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝕄​𝔽)𝗉∘𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞𝔽​𝕊​𝕥∘𝔻⌊𝕠𝕞ℤ𝗉𝔽​𝕄.({}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{MF}})^{{\sf p}}\circ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{FSt}}\circ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{FM}}.
This monotone homotopy, denoted by ⌊𝔻𝕠𝕞ℍ{}_{\lfloor}\mathbb{Dom}^{\mathbb{H}}, is enriched in 𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}} and is ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant.
The remaining construction will be a tedious repetition of existing constructions. We only give a sketch. For a tuple of objects x1𝕄,…,x𝗉𝕄,x𝔼;yx_{1}^{\mathbb{M}},\ldots,x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{M}},x^{\mathbb{E}};y, by using the chosen integral actions, one can pull back the monotone homotopy to obtain objects
𝒞x1𝕄⋯x𝗉𝕄x𝔼;yℍ∈Ob⌊𝐂𝐮𝐫𝐯𝐞¯rigℂ{\mathcal{C}}_{x_{1}^{\mathbb{M}}\cdots x_{\sf p}^{\mathbb{M}}x^{{\mathbb{E}}};y}^{\mathbb{H}}\in{\rm Ob}{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf Curve}}_{\rm rig}^{\mathbb{C}}
which describe configurations containing not only surfaces but also flow lines/rays. The choices we need for the AMS construction can all be extended from existing ones, including the group reduction and thickening data. All the extensions can be made in a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant way.
After these choices, one obtains a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant lift of the outercollaring of ℍ{\mathbb{H}} to ⌊𝐒rel​𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rig{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf S^{\rm rel}Kur}}_{\rm rig}. There is no essential difference from previous cases of constructing vertical NC structures in a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant way. The stable smoothings can also be made equivariantly, first without requiring the matching condition between flow rays and maps defined on surfaces. The submersive condition implies that the incidence condition cuts down smooth Kuranishi spaces. By incorporating the domain stable complex structures, one obtains the lift of ℍ{\mathbb{H}} to ⌊𝐒𝐊𝐮𝐫¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf SKur}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. By passing to the orbifold quotient, we obtain the final construction.
27. Quantitative Results about Equivariant Floer Theory
In this section we discuss the quantitative features of the equivariant Floer theory and prove Theorem M.
27.1. Filtration on the 𝗉{\sf p}-fold tensor product
Let HH be a nondegenerate Hamiltonian on XX. Let C​F​(H)CF(H) be a Floer complex associated to HH, obtained by a particular AMS construction and FOP perturbation. The source of the equivariant pair-of-pants product is the complex
Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})
which is the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part of
C​F​(H)⊗𝗉⊗C​M​(f𝔼).CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}}).
By our convention, this tensor product is a module over the Novikov field
Λ𝐅𝗉Π⊕⋯⊕Π⊕ℤ\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi\oplus\cdots\oplus\Pi\oplus{\mathbb{Z}}}
(where one has 𝗉{\sf p} copies of Π\Pi in the exponent). Here within this section, without introducing further notations, we always change coefficients to the Novikov field Λ𝐊𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi} using the summation homomorphism Π⊕⋯⊕Π→Π\Pi\oplus\cdots\oplus\Pi\to\Pi. Then there is a filtration on
C​F​(H)⊗𝗉⊗C​M​(f𝔼)CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})
corresponding to the sum of the symplectic actions of the 𝗉{\sf p} tensor factors such that the differential preserves this filtration. The filtration restricts to the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part. Moreover, after changing coefficients to Λ𝐊𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}, one obtains a Floer-type complex over this Novikov field
(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉⊗C​M​(f𝔼))⊗Λ𝐊𝗉Π\left(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\right)\otimes\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}
as well as its ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part.
In principle one should hope to establish a chain-level inverse of the equivariant pair-of-pants product via the coproduct construction (cf. [62]). However, the corresponding AMS construction is quite involved. Since our main purpose of the quantitative aspects is to compare barcodes, instead of this potential direct approach, we use more algebraic treatment to bypass the coproduct construction (although we will make use of the local coproduct construction in [62], see the proof of Lemma 27.11).
27.1.1. Homological perturbation
In view of localization, the cohomology of Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}) should only come from generators of the form x⊗⋯⊗xx\otimes\cdots\otimes x for x∈Ob​𝔽x\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}, i.e., ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-fixed points of 𝗉{\sf p}-tuples of HH-orbits. We use the homological perturbation argument to remove the effects of the other free ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-orbits. We would like to construct a complex
Cℤ𝗉red​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})
which is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}) and which is only generated by the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-fixed points.
Let 𝐱=(x1,…,x𝗉){\bf x}=(x_{1},\ldots,x_{\sf p}) denote a 𝗉{\sf p}-tuple of capped HH-orbits. We write
C​F​(H)⊗𝗉⊗C​M​(f𝔼)=⨁𝐱∈𝒪~​(H)𝗉𝐅𝗉​⟨𝐱⟩⊗C​M​(f𝔼).CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})=\bigoplus_{{\bf x}\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H)^{{\sf p}}}{\bf F}_{\sf p}\langle{\bf x}\rangle\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}}).
Here the infinite direct sum indicates we take a completion. This is a decomposition of 𝐊𝗉{\bf K}_{\sf p}-modules. Let [𝐱][{\bf x}] denote the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-orbit of 𝐱{\bf x}. Then there is a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant summand
⨁𝐱∈[𝐱]𝐅𝗉​⟨𝐱⟩⊗C​M​(f𝔼).\bigoplus_{{\bf x}\in[{\bf x}]}{\bf F}_{\sf p}\langle{\bf x}\rangle\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}}).
Its ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-fixed part is denoted by
Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉,[𝐱])⊆Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉).C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}},[{\bf x}])\subseteq C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}).
Lemma 27.1.
The differential dℤ𝗉⊗𝗉d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}} on Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}) admits a decomposition
dℤ𝗉⊗𝗉=δℤ𝗉⊗𝗉+Dℤ𝗉⊗𝗉d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}=\delta_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}+D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}
which satisfies the following conditions.
(1)
δℤ𝗉⊗𝗉\delta_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}} preserves the filtration and for each tuple 𝐱{\bf x},
δℤ𝗉⊗𝗉​(Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉,[𝐱]))⊆Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉,[𝐱]).\delta_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}\Big(C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}},[{\bf x}])\Big)\subseteq C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}},[{\bf x}]).
(2)
The restriction of δℤ𝗉⊗𝗉\delta_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}} to each Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉,[𝐱])C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}},[{\bf x}]), denoted by δ[𝐱]\delta_{[{\bf x}]}, is a differential.
(3)
If 𝐱=(x,…,x){\bf x}=(x,\ldots,x) is a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-fixed point, then δ[𝐱]\delta_{[{\bf x}]} is trivial. If 𝐱{\bf x} is not a fixed point, then the cohomology of δ[𝐱]\delta_{[{\bf x}]} is trivial.
(4)
There exists a constant ϵH>0\epsilon_{H}>0 such that Dℤ𝗉⊗𝗉D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}} increases the filtration by at least ϵH\epsilon_{H}.
Proof.
The differential on the tensor product C​F​(H)⊗𝗉⊗C​M​(f𝔼)CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}}), denoted by d~ℤ𝗉⊗𝗉\tilde{d}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}, is the tensor product differential. Let dH:C​F​(H)→C​F​(H)d_{H}:CF(H)\to CF(H) be the Floer differential and d𝔼d_{{{\mathbb{E}}}} be the Morse differential on C​M​(f𝔼)CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}}). Then the obvious ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant decomposition
d~ℤ𝗉⊗𝗉=δ~ℤ𝗉⊗𝗉+D~ℤ𝗉⊗𝗉:⁣=∗IdC​F​(H)⊗⋯⊗IdC​F​(H)⊗d𝔼+dH⊗𝗉⊗IdC​M​(f𝔼).\begin{split}\tilde{d}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}=&\ \tilde{\delta}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}+\tilde{D}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}\\
:=&\ \ast{\rm Id}_{CF(H)}\otimes\cdots\otimes{\rm Id}_{CF(H)}\otimes d_{{{\mathbb{E}}}}+d_{H}^{\otimes{\sf p}}\otimes{\rm Id}_{CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})}.\end{split}
Here ∗=±1\ast=\pm 1 depends on the degrees of the variables. The restriction to the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part provides the desired decomposition.
∎
Now we would like to apply the homological perturbation argument to construct a differential on the chain group
Cℤ𝗉red(CF(H)⊗𝗉):=⨁x∈𝒪~​(H)Cℤ𝗉(CF(H)⊗𝗉,x⊗⋯⊗x),C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}):=\bigoplus_{x\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H)}C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}},x\otimes\cdots\otimes x),
(27.1)
which is the cohomology of Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}) under the differential δℤ𝗉⊗𝗉\delta_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}} defined above. Notice that there is a natural linear inclusion
σ:Cℤ𝗉red​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)→Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)\sigma:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})
and a projection
π:Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)→Cℤ𝗉red​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉).\pi:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}).
Lemma 27.2.
There exists a differential Dℤ𝗉redD_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red} on Cℤ𝗉red​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}), together with maps
σ′:Cℤ𝗉red​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)→Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉),\displaystyle\ \sigma^{\prime}:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}),\
π′:Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)→Cℤ𝗉red​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)\displaystyle\ \pi^{\prime}:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})
satisfying the following conditions.
(1)
Dℤ𝗉redD_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red} strictly increases the energy filtration.
(2)
σ′\sigma^{\prime} and π′\pi^{\prime} strictly increase the energy filtration.
(3)
σ~=σ+σ′\tilde{\sigma}=\sigma+\sigma^{\prime} and π~=π+π′\tilde{\pi}=\pi+\pi^{\prime} are filtered chain homotopy inverses to each other.
Proof.
For each [𝐱][{\bf x}] which is not a fixed point, since the cohomology of δ[𝐱]\delta_{[{\bf x}]} is trivial, one can find a chain homotopy between identity and zero, denoted by Θ[𝐱]\Theta_{[{\bf x}]} satisfying
Id=δ[𝐱]​Θ[𝐱]+Θ[𝐱]​δ[𝐱].{\rm Id}=\delta_{[{\bf x}]}\Theta_{[{\bf x}]}+\Theta_{[{\bf x}]}\delta_{[{\bf x}]}.
When [𝐱][{\bf x}] is a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-fxed point, define Θ[𝐱]=0\Theta_{[{\bf x}]}=0. One can choose Θ[𝐱]\Theta_{[{\bf x}]} in a Π\Pi-equivariant way. Then define
Θ:=⨁[𝐱]∈𝒪~​(H)𝗉/ℤ𝗉Θ[𝐱].\Theta:=\bigoplus_{[{\bf x}]\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H)^{{\sf p}}/{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\Theta_{[{\bf x}]}.
Then Θ\Theta preserves the filtration. Then following the explicit formula of [37] and [45]), define
D~ℤ𝗉⊗𝗉:=π⁡(∑l=0∞(Dℤ𝗉⊗𝗉∘Θ)l)​Dℤ𝗉⊗𝗉​σ=π​Dℤ𝗉⊗𝗉​(∑l=0∞(Θ​Dℤ𝗉)l)​σ.\tilde{D}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}:=\pi\left(\sum_{l=0}^{\infty}(D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}\circ\Theta)^{l}\right)D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}\sigma=\pi D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\otimes{\sf p}}\left(\sum_{l=0}^{\infty}(\Theta D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}})^{l}\right)\sigma.
Its restriction to the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part is defined to be Dℤ𝗉redD_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}. The terms σ′\sigma^{\prime} and π′\pi^{\prime} are also defined by explicit formulas (see, e.g. [12, Appendix B]), and we omit the details.
∎
27.2. Filtration on equivariant Floer cochain complex
Let HH be a Hamiltonian on XX so that an equivariant Floer cochain complex C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}) can be defined (see Theorem I). Recall that to define this chain group, we first consider the chain group
C(𝔽♮​𝗉#𝔼):={∑i=1∞cipi⊗wi|ci∈𝐅𝗉,pi∈𝒪~(H♮​𝗉),wi∈critf𝔼,infi𝒜(pi)>−∞,infif𝔼(wi)>−∞,limi→∞𝒜⁡(pi)+f𝔼​(wi)=+∞}C({\mathbb{F}}^{\natural{\sf p}}\#{\mathbb{E}}):=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}c_{i}p_{i}\otimes w_{i}\ \left|\ \begin{array}[]{l}c_{i}\in{\bf F}_{\sf p},\ p_{i}\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}),\ w_{i}\in{\rm crit}f^{{\mathbb{E}}},\\
\displaystyle\inf_{i}{\mathcal{A}}(p_{i})>-\infty,\ \inf_{i}f^{{\mathbb{E}}}(w_{i})>-\infty,\\
\displaystyle\lim_{i\to\infty}{\mathcal{A}}(p_{i})+f^{{\mathbb{E}}}(w_{i})=+\infty\end{array}\right.\right\}
It is a module with a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action, and it is defined over the Novikov field Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}. The equivariant complex C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}) is (roughly) its ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-fixed part.
Lemma 27.3.
The ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part C​(F♮​𝗉​#​𝔼)ℤ𝗉C(F^{\natural{\sf p}}\#{\mathbb{E}})_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} is a free module over Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}. Its rank is #​𝒪​(H♮​𝗉)\#{\mathcal{O}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}) when 𝗉=2{\sf p}=2 and 2​#​𝒪​(H♮​𝗉)2\#{\mathcal{O}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}) when 𝗉>2{\sf p}>2.
Proof.
Choose for each contractible 1-periodic orbit a capping. Let p1,…,pmp_{1},\ldots,p_{m} be these capped 1-periodic orbit. Let τ∈ℤ𝗉\tau\in{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} be the generator. When 𝗉=2{\sf p}=2, define a map
F:Λ𝐅2Π​⟨p1,…,pm⟩→C​(𝔽♮​𝗉​#​𝔼)ℤ2F:\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{2}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}\langle p_{1},\ldots,p_{m}\rangle\to C({\mathbb{F}}^{\natural{\sf p}}\#{\mathbb{E}})_{{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}}
by
F⁡(pα)=pα⊗w0++τ⁡(pα)⊗w0−F(p_{\alpha})=p_{\alpha}\otimes w_{0}^{+}+\tau(p_{\alpha})\otimes w_{0}^{-}
where w0±w_{0}^{\pm} are the two critical points of f𝔼f^{{\mathbb{E}}} of index 00. One can see that this is an isomorphism of free Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}-modules. On the other hand, when 𝗉>2{\sf p}>2, define
F:Λ𝐅𝗉Π​⟨p1,…,pm,p1⊗θ,…,pm⊗θ⟩→C​(𝔽♮​𝗉​#​𝔼)ℤ𝗉F:\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}\langle p_{1},\ldots,p_{m},p_{1}\otimes\uptheta,\ldots,p_{m}\otimes\uptheta\rangle\to C({\mathbb{F}}^{\natural{\sf p}}\#{\mathbb{E}})_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}
by sending
F⁡(pα)=∑j=1𝗉τj​(pα)⊗w0j,\displaystyle\ F(p_{\alpha})=\sum_{j=1}^{\sf p}\tau^{j}(p_{\alpha})\otimes w_{0}^{j},\
F⁡(pα⊗θ)=∑j=1𝗉τj​(pα)⊗w1j,\displaystyle\ F(p_{\alpha}\otimes\uptheta)=\sum_{j=1}^{\sf p}\tau^{j}(p_{\alpha})\otimes w_{1}^{j},
where w0jw_{0}^{j}, w1jw_{1}^{j} are the critical points of f𝔼f^{{\mathbb{E}}} of index 00 and 11. One can also verify that FF is a linear isomorphism.
∎
Note the difference between the Novikov fields Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}} and Λ𝐊𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}, where the latter does not require the pole order of the variable 𝚄\mathtt{U} or θ\uptheta is bounded. Then we can write the chain group after tensoring with this larger Novikov field by
C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,Λ𝐊𝗉Π)=C​(𝔽♮​𝗉​#​𝔼)ℤ𝗉⊗Λ𝐊𝗉Π≅{∑i=1∞c~ipi|c~i∈𝐊~𝗉,pi∈𝒪~(H♮​𝗉),limi→∞𝒜H♮​𝗉(pi)=+∞}.CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}};\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi})=C({\mathbb{F}}^{\natural{\sf p}}\#{{\mathbb{E}}})_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\otimes\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}\\
\cong\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\tilde{c}_{i}p_{i}\ |\ \tilde{c}_{i}\in\widetilde{\bf K}_{\sf p},\ p_{i}\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}),\ \lim_{i\to\infty}{\mathcal{A}}_{H^{\natural{\sf p}}}(p_{i})=+\infty\Big\}.
To directly use results from [69], change coefficients to Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}, which becomes only ℤ2{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}-graded. Recall from (7.6) the meaning of the notation |Π||\Pi|.
Lemma 27.4.
The complex
C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|):=C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,Λ𝐊𝗉Π)⊗Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}};\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}):=CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}};\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi})\otimes\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}
is a Floer-type complex (Definition 7.34) over the Novikov field Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}.
Proof.
To see this, we first need to prove that C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}};\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}) is orthogonalizable. Indeed, it is the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant subspace of the cochain complex C⁡(𝔽♮​𝗉​#​𝔼)⊗Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|C({\mathbb{F}}^{\natural{\sf p}}\#{\mathbb{E}})\otimes\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}, which is orthogonalizable. Then by [69, Corollary 2.17], the subspace C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}};\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}) is also orthogonalizable. On the other hand, the differential preserves the energy filtration, hence C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}};\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}) is a Floer-type complex.
∎
As a corollary, by the basic construction of [69], the complex C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}};\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}) has well-defined verbose and concise barcodes.
Proposition 27.5.
The verbose barcode only depends on H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}}.
Proof.
By Theorem 7.40, one only needs to show that the filtered isomorphism type only depends on H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}}. Indeed, given two constructions of C⁡(𝔽♮​𝗉​#​𝔼)C({\mathbb{F}}^{\natural{\sf p}}\#{\mathbb{E}}) as a chain complex of Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\mathbb{\Pi}}-modules with ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action corresponding to two AMS lifts
𝔽~0ℤ𝗉,\displaystyle\ \tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}},
𝔽~1ℤ𝗉,\displaystyle\ \tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}},
by Theorem 25.3, one can construct a lift of the outercollaring of the diagonal bimodule to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC} as a bimodule over (𝔽~0ℤ𝗉;𝔽~1ℤ𝗉)(\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}};\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}). Then by choosing FOP perturbations, one obtains a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-equivariant chain map
Φ:C⁡(𝔽~0ℤ𝗉)→C⁡(𝔽~1ℤ𝗉).\Phi:C(\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{0}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}})\to C(\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{1}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}).
Similar to many other cases, this chain map has a leading order term being the identity map on the same chain group. Hence Φ\Phi is invertible. Moreover, Φ\Phi preserves the energy filtration because all the lifts cover the constant homotopy of H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}}. Therefore, after changing coefficients to Λ𝐊𝗉|Π|\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{|\Pi|}, the chain map Φ\Phi is a filtered isomorphism.
∎
27.3. Local equivariant cohomology and homological perturbation
We would like to compare the barcodes between the ordinary Floer complex of a Hamiltonian and the equivariant Floer complexes of its 𝗉{\sf p}-th iteration using the chain-level equivariant pair-of-pants product. In the presence of simple 𝗉{\sf p}-periodic orbits, we do not expect to obtain a filtered isomorphism. On the other hand, simple 𝗉{\sf p}-periodic orbits, which form free ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-orbits, are not expected to contribute in the Tate equivariant cohomology. We use local equivariant cohomology and the homological perturbation method to remove simple 𝗉{\sf p}-periodic orbits from a reduced version of the equivariant Floer complex.
27.3.1. Local equivariant Floer theory
Now consider the 𝗉{\sf p}-th iteration H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}}. Recall that the chain group C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}) is the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part of the module
⨁y¯∈𝒪⁡(H♮​𝗉)Λ𝐅𝗉Π​⟨y¯⟩⊗C​M​(f𝔼).\bigoplus_{\overline{y}\in{\mathcal{O}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})}\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}\langle\overline{y}\rangle\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}}).
Notice that y¯\overline{y} is either an iterated orbit (fixed point) or a simple 𝗉{\sf p}-periodic orbit (free ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-orbit). Then we can write the above chain group as
(⨁x¯∈𝒪⁡(H)Λ𝐅𝗉Π​⟨x¯(𝗉)⟩⊗C​M​(f𝔼))​⊕^​(⨁y¯∈𝒪simple​(H♮​𝗉)Λ𝐅𝗉Π​⟨y¯⟩⊗C​M​(f𝔼)).\left(\bigoplus_{\underline{\smash{x}}\in{\mathcal{O}}(H)}\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}\langle\underline{\smash{x}}^{({\sf p})}\rangle\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\right)\widehat{\oplus}\left(\bigoplus_{\underline{\smash{y}}\in{\mathcal{O}}^{\rm simple}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})}\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}\langle\underline{\smash{y}}\rangle\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\right).
Notice that ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} acts trivially on the set of iterated orbits and acts freely on the set of simple orbits. Let [y¯][\underline{\smash{y}}] be the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-orbit of y¯\underline{\smash{y}}. Then one reorganizes the decomposition as
C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)⊗Λ𝐊𝗉Π≅⨁x¯∈𝒪⁡(H)Λ𝐊~𝗉Π​⟨x¯(𝗉)⟩​⊕^​(⨁y¯∈𝒪simple​(H♮​𝗉)Λ𝐅𝗉Π​⟨y¯⟩⊗C​M​(f𝔼))ℤ𝗉≅⨁[y¯]∈𝒪⁡(H♮​𝗉)/ℤ𝗉C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,[y¯]),\begin{split}CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})\otimes\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}\cong&\ \bigoplus_{\underline{\smash{x}}\in{\mathcal{O}}(H)}\Lambda_{\widetilde{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}\langle\underline{\smash{x}}^{({\sf p})}\rangle\widehat{\oplus}\left(\bigoplus_{\underline{\smash{y}}\in{\mathcal{O}}^{\rm simple}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})}\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}\langle\underline{\smash{y}}\rangle\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\right)_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\\
\cong&\ \bigoplus_{[\underline{\smash{y}}]\in{\mathcal{O}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})/{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},[\underline{\smash{y}}]),\end{split}
where each C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,[y¯])CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},[\underline{\smash{y}}]) is a submodule coming from each ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-orbit. Notice that for each [y]∈𝒪⁡(H)[y]\in{\mathcal{O}}(H), there is a 𝐊𝗉{\bf K}_{\sf p}-summand
C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮,[y])⊆C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,[y¯]).CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural},[y])\subseteq CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},[\underline{\smash{y}}]).
The following lemma basically says that one can decompose the equivariant differential into a local part and a positive-energy part, where the local part respects the above decomposition.
Lemma 27.6.
The equivariant differential
dℤ𝗉:C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,Λ𝐊𝗉Π)→C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,Λ𝐊𝗉Π)d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}:CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}};\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}};\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi})
can be written as
dℤ𝗉=dℤ𝗉,loc+Dℤ𝗉d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}=d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}+D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}
which satisfy the following conditions.
(1)
For each [y]∈𝒪~​(H♮​𝗉)/ℤ𝗉[y]\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})/{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},
dℤ𝗉,loc​(C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,[y]))⊆C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,[y]).d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}\big(CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},[y])\big)\subseteq CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},[y]).
Therefore dℤ𝗉,locd_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}} preserves the filtration. Denote the restriction of dℤ𝗉,locd_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}} to the summand C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,[y])CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},[y]) by dℤ𝗉,[y]d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},[y]}.
(2)
For each [y][y], dℤ𝗉,[y]2=0d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},[y]}^{2}=0.
(3)
There exists δH♮​𝗉>0\delta_{H^{\natural{\sf p}}}>0 such that Dℤ𝗉D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} increases the filtration by at least δH♮​𝗉\delta_{H^{\natural{\sf p}}}.
(4)
If y=x(𝗉)y=x^{({\sf p})} for x∈𝒪~​(H)x\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H), dℤ𝗉,[y]d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},[y]} vanishes and denote the cohomology by
H​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,x(𝗉))≅𝐊~𝗉.HF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},x^{({\sf p})})\cong\widetilde{\bf K}_{\sf p}.
(5)
If yy is a simple 𝗉{\sf p}-periodic orbit, then the cohomology of dℤ𝗉,[y]d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},[y]} is trivial.
Proof.
The decomposition dℤ𝗉=dℤ𝗉,loc+Dℤ𝗉d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}=d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}+D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} and the first three conditions are due to a basic compactness argument, usually termed under cross-energy lemma, see e.g. [12, Lemma B.1]. In our nondegenerate setting, we know that dℤ𝗉,locd_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}} comes from differentials in C​M​(f𝔼)CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}}) and Dℤ𝗉D_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} comes from the contribution from nontrivial Floer cylinders in XX.
If y=x(𝗉)y=x^{({\sf p})}, the summand C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,x(𝗉))≅C​M​(f𝔼)ℤ𝗉CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},x^{({\sf p})})\cong CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} and the differential is trivial on C​M​(f𝔼)ℤ𝗉CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}. Hence (4) is verified.
If yy is simple, then we have the following identification. Let τ∈ℤ𝗉\tau\in{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}} be the generator and let wl±w_{l}^{\pm} resp. wl0,…,wl𝗉−1w_{l}^{0},\ldots,w_{l}^{{\sf p}-1} be the 𝗉{\sf p} critical points of f𝔼f^{{\mathbb{E}}} in degree ll in 𝗉=2{\sf p}=2 resp. 𝗉>2{\sf p}>2 case.
C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,[y])=⨁τk∈ℤ𝗉(𝐅𝗉​⟨τk​y⟩⊕C​M​(f𝔼))ℤ𝗉≅{𝐊2​⟨y⊗w0−+τ⁡(y)⊗w0+,y⊗w0++τ⁡(y)⊗w0−⟩,𝗉=2,𝐊𝗉⟨∑k=0𝗉−1τk(y)⊗w0k+s,∑k=0𝗉−1τk(y)⊗w1k+s|s=0,1,…,𝗉−1⟩𝗉>2.CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},[y])=\bigoplus_{\tau^{k}\in{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\left({\bf F}_{\sf p}\langle\tau^{k}y\rangle\oplus CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\right)_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\\
\cong\left\{\begin{array}[]{ll}{\bf K}_{2}\Big\langle y\otimes w_{0}^{-}+\tau(y)\otimes w_{0}^{+},y\otimes w_{0}^{+}+\tau(y)\otimes w_{0}^{-}\Big\rangle,&\ {\sf p}=2,\\[5.69046pt]
{\bf K}_{\sf p}\Big\langle\left.\sum_{k=0}^{{\sf p}-1}\tau^{k}(y)\otimes w_{0}^{k+s},\ \sum_{k=0}^{{\sf p}-1}\tau^{k}(y)\otimes w_{1}^{k+s}\right|\ s=0,1,\ldots,{\sf p}-1\Big\rangle&\ {\sf p}>2.\end{array}\right.
One can see from the differential of C​M​(f𝔼)CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}}) that the cohomology is trivial.
∎
Then we would like to apply the homological perturbation argument.
Lemma 27.7.
There exist a differential Dℤ𝗉redD_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red} on the “reduced” equivariant complex
C​Fℤ𝗉red​(H♮​𝗉):=⨁x∈𝒪~​(H)H​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,x(𝗉))CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}):=\bigoplus_{x\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H)}HF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},x^{({\sf p})})
making it a Floer-type complex, filtered chain homotopy equivalences
σ~:C​Fℤ𝗉red​(H♮​𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉),\displaystyle\ \tilde{\sigma}:CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}),\
π~:C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉red​(H♮​𝗉),\displaystyle\ \tilde{\pi}:CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}),
and a filtered chain homotopy
Θ~:C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)\tilde{\Theta}:CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})
such that
π~∘σ~=Id,\displaystyle\ \tilde{\pi}\circ\tilde{\sigma}={\rm Id},\
σ~∘π~=Id+dℤ𝗉∘Θ~+Θ~∘dℤ𝗉.\displaystyle\ \tilde{\sigma}\circ\tilde{\pi}={\rm Id}+d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\circ\tilde{\Theta}+\tilde{\Theta}\circ d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}.
Proof.
This lemma can be proved in the same way as Lemma 27.2. We omit the details.
∎
27.4. Equivariant pair-of-pants product
We consider the quantitative property of the equivariant pair-of-pants product. Let HH be as above. First, the complex C​F​(H)CF(H) is a Floer-type complex over the Novikov field Λ𝐅𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}-modules with a filtration 𝒜H{\mathcal{A}}_{H}. Then consider the completed tensor product
(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉⊗C​M​(f𝔼))⊗Λ𝐊𝗉Π\left(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\right)\otimes\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}
which has the energy filtration 𝒜H⊗𝗉{\mathcal{A}}_{H}^{\otimes{\sf p}}. It is a nonarchimedean normed vector space over Λ𝐊𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi} and is orthogonalizable. Then its ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant subspace
Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉):=((C​F​(H)⊗𝗉⊗C​M​(f𝔼))⊗Λ𝐊𝗉Π)ℤ𝗉C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}):=\Big(\Big(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\Big)\otimes\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}\Big)_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}
is orthogonalizable. Moreover, the differential clearly preserves the filtration. Hence one has a Floer-type complex with associated barcode.
Now consider the chain-level equivariant pair-of-pants product, which was originally defined as
P:(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉⊗C​M​(f𝔼)⊗Λ𝐊𝗉Π)ℤ𝗉→C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)P:\Big(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\otimes\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}\Big)_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})
as a Λ𝐊𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi}-linear chain map.
Proposition 27.8.
There exists a chain-level construction of PP which preserves the nonarchimedean norm, i.e.,
𝒜⁡(P⁡(x))≥𝒜H⊗𝗉​(x).{\mathcal{A}}(P(x))\geq{\mathcal{A}}_{H}^{\otimes{\sf p}}(x).
Proof.
Consider the branched covering Σ𝔽​𝕊​𝕥→ℝ×S1\Sigma^{\mathbb{FSt}}\to{\mathbb{R}}\times S^{1}, which pulls back the trivial Floer data H​d​tHdt on the cylinder to a Hamiltonian connection on σH𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\sigma_{H}^{\mathbb{FSt}} on Σ𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\Sigma^{\mathbb{FSt}}. Consider the multimodule 𝕏𝔽​𝕊​𝕥\mathbb{X}^{\mathbb{FSt}}. From the energy identity for Floer equation, one can see that the multimodule has a threshold zero (Definition 7.41) with respect to the symplectic action. Then by Proposition 7.42, the chain map preserves the filtration.
∎
Theorem 27.9.
There exists a filtered chain isomorphism
Pred:Cℤ𝗉red​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉red​(H♮​𝗉)P^{\rm red}:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})
such that the following diagram commutes up to filtered homotopy, where the vertical arrows are provided by the homological perturbation lemma.
Cℤ𝗉red​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)\textstyle{C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Pred\scriptstyle{P^{\rm red}}C​Fℤ𝗉red​(H♮​𝗉)\textstyle{CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)\textstyle{C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}P\scriptstyle{P}C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)\textstyle{CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})}
The proof is provided momentarily. As the reduced versions of the involved complexes are filtered homotopy equivalent to the original versions, by Theorem 7.40, one has the following immediate corollary.
Corollary 27.10.
PP is a filtered homotopy equivalence. Therefore, the concise barcodes of Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}) and C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}) coincide.
To prove Theorem 27.9, we proceed by building the local inverses.
Lemma 27.11.
We can write the equivariant pair-of-pants product PP as
P=Ploc+PbigP=P_{\rm loc}+P_{\rm big}
which satisfy the following conditions.
(1)
For each x∈𝒪~​(H)x\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H), denote x⊗p=x⊗⋯⊗xx^{\otimes p}=x\otimes\cdots\otimes x. Then one has
Ploc​(Cℤ𝗉,loc​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉,x⊗𝗉))⊆C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,x(𝗉)).P_{\rm loc}(C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}},x^{\otimes{\sf p}}))\subseteq CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},x^{({\sf p})}).
Denote the restriction by
Px:Cℤ𝗉,loc​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉,x⊗𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉,loc​(H♮​𝗉,x(𝗉)).P_{x}:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}},x^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}},{\rm loc}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},x^{({\sf p})}).
(2)
There exists δH′′>0\delta_{H}^{\prime\prime}>0 such that PbigP_{\rm big} increases the filtration by at least δH′′\delta_{H}^{\prime\prime}.
(3)
PxP_{x} is independent of choices and agrees with the local equivariant pair-of-pants product constructed by Seidel [60] (for 𝗉=2{\sf p}=2) and Shelukhin–Zhao [62] (for 𝗉>2{\sf p}>2).
(4)
PxP_{x} is invertible.
Proof.
The decomposition and the first two items are based on the crossing energy argument (cf. [12, Lemma B.1]). To see that PlocP_{\rm loc} is well-defined, suppose P′P^{\prime} is another construction which has a similar decomposition P′=Ploc′+Pbig′P^{\prime}=P_{\rm loc}^{\prime}+P_{\rm big}^{\prime}. Then PP and P′P^{\prime} are homotopic via a filtered chain homotopy KK. So
P−P′=K​dℤ𝗉+dℤ𝗉​K.P-P^{\prime}=Kd_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}+d_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}K.
Since KK also admits the decomposition into the local component and “big” component in view of the cross-energy lemma, by passing to the local piece, one has Ploc=Ploc′P_{\rm loc}=P_{\rm loc}^{\prime} on cohomology.
Furthermore, since the local argument does not involve sphere bubbling, the equivalence between our FOP counts and the counts defined using classical framework as used in [61] and [62] can be made using the same argument as proving Part (2) of Theorem H.
Lastly, the invertibility of PxP_{x} is proved in [61] by a local computation for 𝗉=2{\sf p}=2, and in [62] by constructing the local equivariant coproduct and prove that the local coproduct is the inverse of PxP_{x} for 𝗉>2{\sf p}>2.
∎
Proof of Theorem 27.9.
Now consider the composition
Pred:=π∘P∘σ:Cℤ𝗉red​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉red​(H♮​𝗉)P^{\rm red}:=\pi\circ P\circ\sigma:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(H^{\natural{\sf p}})
which is a filtered chain map. Notice that there is an obvious leading order term, denoted by PlocredP_{\rm loc}^{\rm red}, which is the direct sum of PxP_{x}, while the difference
Pbigred:=Pred−PlocredP_{\rm big}^{\rm red}:=P^{\rm red}-P_{\rm loc}^{\rm red}
strictly increases the energy filtration. Hence PredP^{\rm red} is invertible. Therefore, after tensoring with the correct Novikov field, PredP^{\rm red} is a filtered isomorphism of Floer-type complexes.
∎
27.5. Proof of Theorem M
The first item, which says that the equivariant Floer cochain complex C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}) is a Floer-type complex over Λ𝐊𝗉Π\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Pi} follows directly from the construction.
The second item is exactly Corollary 27.10.
For the third item, by Corollary 27.10, the barcodes of the two complexes Cℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉)C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}) and C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}}) are identical. On the other hand, there exists an algebraically defined quasi-Frobenius map (see (23.3))
q​F:H​F​(H)→Hℤ𝗉​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉).qF:HF(H)\to H_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}).
Although q​FqF is not induced from a cochain map, it still respects the filtration in the following way. For each τ∈ℝ\tau\in{\mathbb{R}}, one has corresponding 𝐅𝗉{\bf F}_{\sf p}-linear map
q​F:H​F≤τ​(H)→Hℤ𝗉≤𝗉​τ​(C​F​(H)⊗𝗉).qF:HF^{\leq\tau}(H)\to H_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\leq{\sf p}\tau}(CF(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}).
In the current setting, it is hard to obtain the relationship between barcodes, but only the bar-length spectrum. Then, following the argument in [65, Section 6.2], one can define a version of Floer complex over the universal Novikov ring
Λ0univ\Lambda_{0}^{\rm univ}
(with base ring 𝐅𝗉{\bf F}_{\sf p}), denoted by C​F​(H,Λ0univ)CF(H;\Lambda_{0}^{\rm univ}). Then by the general structural results of modules over Λ0univ\Lambda_{0}^{\rm univ}, the bar-lengths βi​(H)\beta_{i}(H) correspond to torsion parts of H​F​(H,Λ0univ)HF(H;\Lambda_{0}^{\rm univ}) of the forms Λ0univ/Tβi​(H)​Λ0univ\Lambda_{0}^{\rm univ}/T^{\beta_{i}(H)}\Lambda_{0}^{\rm univ}. Then one can prove that the quasi-Frobenius map is an isomorphism of Λ0univ\Lambda_{0}^{\rm univ}-modules after the rescaling by 𝗉{\sf p}. The result in Theorem M (3) follows from Theorem M (2).
28. Quantitative Theory for Noncontractible Hamiltonian Orbits
In this section we provide constructions for the Floer complex for noncontractible orbits (in the homological sense) and the corresponding quantitative results involving a version of equivariant pair-of-pants product. As mentioned before, the main motivation for developing this variant is to generalize the result of Sugimoto [67] to full generality, which will be done in a separate paper with Shelukhin and Wilkins [12]. Here in this section, we will prove Theorem 1.11 and Theorem 1.12. The only notable technical difference is that the capping of a non-contractible orbit is defined relative to a reference homology class; the rest of the construction is exactly the same as the contractible case.
28.1. The Floer flow category and bimodules
Let γ\gamma be a smooth loop in XX which represents a nontrivial class in H1​(X,ℤ)freeH_{1}(X;{\mathbb{Z}})_{\rm free}. Denote
Γ=H2​(X,ℤ)/ker​ω.\Gamma=H_{2}(X;{\mathbb{Z}})/{\rm ker}\omega.
For a nondegenerate Hamiltonian HH, we describe a ℤ2{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}-graded Γ\Gamma-equivariant flow category 𝔽γ{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma} of orbits of HH which are homologous to γ\gamma. Recall terms defined in Definition 1.10. Define
Ob​𝔽γ:=𝒪~γ​(H).{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}:=\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{\gamma}(H).
To define morphisms of 𝔽γ{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}, choose a 1-periodic family of ω\omega-compatible almost complex structures JJ and considering moduli spaces of Floer equations and their compactifications. Then the morphism set between two γ\gamma-capped orbits is the moduli space of stable Floer trajectories connecting them, where the Floer cylinders naturally concatenate the γ\gamma-cappings. One then obtains the flow category 𝔽γ\mathbb{F}_{\gamma} enriched in 𝐓𝐨𝐩¯\underline{\smash{\bf Top}} where objects are naturally ℤ2{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}-graded. The action functional
𝒜H,γ:Ob​𝔽γ→ℝ{\mathcal{A}}_{H,\gamma}:{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}\to{\mathbb{R}}
makes 𝔽γ{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma} a locally finite flow category (Definition 7.2). The Γ\Gamma-action on objects makes 𝔽γ{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma} a Γ\Gamma-equivariant flow category (Definition 7.24).
Notice that if we choose a different loop γ′\gamma^{\prime} homologous to γ\gamma, then one essentially get the same flow category except that the actions 𝒜H,γ{\mathcal{A}}_{H,\gamma} and 𝒜H,γ′{\mathcal{A}}_{H,\gamma^{\prime}} differ by a constant.
If we choose a different pair (H′,J′)(H^{\prime},J^{\prime}) and consider the same construction (for a fixed loop γ\gamma), then one obtains a similar Floer flow category 𝔽γ′{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}^{\prime}. By choosing a Floer datum on the infinite cylinder interpolating between (H,J)(H,J) and (H′,J′)(H^{\prime},J^{\prime}) and considering moduli spaces of Floer equations associated to the Floer datum, one obtains a bimodule 𝔹γ\mathbb{B}_{\gamma} over (𝔽γ;𝔽γ′)({\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma};{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}^{\prime}), which is naturally Γ\Gamma-equivariant (Definition 7.26). This is completely analogous to the usual contractible case.
28.2. The complex and continuation map
Since the Floer homology of the noncontractible case is (expected to be) trivial, in fact, the Floer complex is null-homotopic, the only interesting theory is the quantitative theory. Consider
CFγ(H):={∑i=1∞aipi|ai∈ℤ,pi∈Ob𝔽γ,limi→∞𝒜H,γ(pi)=−∞}CF_{\gamma}(H):=\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}a_{i}p_{i}\ |\ a_{i}\in{\mathbb{Z}},\ p_{i}\in{\rm Ob}{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma},\ \lim_{i\to\infty}{\mathcal{A}}_{H,\gamma}(p_{i})=-\infty\Big\}
which is a module over ΛℤΓ\Lambda_{{\mathbb{Z}}}^{\Gamma}.
Proof of Theorem 1.11.
The AMS construction for the flow category 𝔽γ{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma} is almost identical to the contractible case. There are only two minor places which we would like to comment. The first one is the existence of integral actions. The proof of Proposition 15.4 works equally well for the noncontractible case. Then one can go through the AMS construction for the flow category. The change of Novikov group from Π\Pi to Γ\Gamma does not affect our argument to make each step of the construction equivariant. Then upon making choices, one obtains a lift of the outercollaring of 𝔽γ{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. Choosing FOP perturbations allows us to construct the differential, hence obtaining a ℤ2{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}-graded chain complex
C​Fγ​(H,J,Ξ)CF_{\gamma}(H,J,\Xi)
(linear over ΛℤΓ\Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}}^{\Gamma}).
After changing coefficients to Λ𝐊Γ\Lambda_{\bf K}^{\Gamma}, one obtains a Floer-type complex because the differential increases the filtration.
To see that the filtered isomorphism class only depends on HH, we compare two different almost complex structures JJ, J′J^{\prime} and two different sets of choices Ξ\Xi, Ξ′\Xi^{\prime}, resulting in AMS lifts 𝔽~γ\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma} and 𝔽~γ′\tilde{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}^{\prime}. Choose an interpolation between JJ and J′J^{\prime} and consider the corresponding bimodule 𝔹γ{\mathbb{B}}_{\gamma} over (𝔽γ;𝔽γ′)({\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma};{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}^{\prime}) via continuation map moduli spaces. One apply the AMS construction for 𝔹γ{\mathbb{B}}_{\gamma}, ending with a chain map
Φ𝔹γ:C​Fγ​(H,J,Ξ)→C​Fγ​(H,J′,Ξ′).\Phi^{{\mathbb{B}}_{\gamma}}:CF_{\gamma}(H,J,\Xi)\to CF_{\gamma}(H,J^{\prime},\Xi^{\prime}).
Notice that the two chain groups are canonically identified since the Hamiltonian HH is fixed. The leading order term of Φ𝔹γ\Phi^{{\mathbb{B}}_{\gamma}} is then the identity map on the chain group C​Fγ​(H)CF_{\gamma}(H). Hence after tensoring with Λ𝐊Γ\Lambda_{{\bf K}}^{\Gamma}, the chain map is a filtered isomorphism.
∎
Therefore, if we switch to field coefficients, for each field 𝐊{\bf K}, we obtain a well-defined verbose barcode ℬγ​(H){\mathcal{B}}_{\gamma}(H). It still depends on the concrete choice of the loop γ\gamma. We shorten the notation for the chain complex by
C​Fγ​(H,Λ𝐊Γ).CF_{\gamma}(H;\Lambda_{\bf K}^{\Gamma}).
Corollary 28.1.
For two homologous loops γ\gamma and γ′\gamma^{\prime}, the bar-length spectrum of C​Fγ​(H,Λ𝐊Γ)CF_{\gamma}(H;\Lambda_{\bf K}^{\Gamma}) coincides with that of C​Fγ′​(H,Λ𝐊Γ)CF_{\gamma^{\prime}}(H;\Lambda_{\bf K}^{\Gamma}).
Proof.
Let γ′\gamma^{\prime} be another loop which is homologous to γ\gamma. Choosing a concrete cobordism between them. Then one obtains a Γ\Gamma-equivariant isomorphism of flow categories 𝔽γ≅𝔽γ′{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}\cong{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma^{\prime}} which shifts the action by a constant. An AMS construction and FOP perturbation for 𝔽γ{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma} can be transported to 𝔽γ′{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma^{\prime}}. Hence the bar-length spectrum does not depend on the representating loop γ\gamma.
∎
Remark 28.2.
It is standard to argue that the barcode ℬγ​(H){\mathcal{B}}_{\gamma}(H) varies Lipschitz continuously with HH, where on barcodes we use the bottleneck distance. Hence the barcode ℬγ​(H){\mathcal{B}}_{\gamma}(H) also extends to degenerate Hamiltonians.
28.3. Equivariant Floer complex
Now we can repeat the equivariant Floer construction to the noncontractible case. Let 𝗉{\sf p} be a prime and suppose H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}} is nondegenerate, which may have noncontractible orbits homologous to γ\gamma. By coupling with the Morse flow category 𝔼{{\mathbb{E}}} on S^∞\widehat{S}^{\infty}, one obtains a flow category (see Definition 25.1)
𝔽γℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}
which has a free action by the twisted Novikov group (Γ×ℤ)⋊ℤ𝗉(\Gamma\times{\mathbb{Z}})\rtimes{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}. Notice that although the reference loop γ\gamma is not invariant under the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action via loop rotation, the symplectic action is still well-defined.
Using exactly the same construction as the contractible case, one can construct an equivariant lift of the outercollaring of 𝔽γℤ𝗉{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}} to ⌊𝐝𝐎𝐫𝐛¯rigNC{}_{\lfloor}\underline{\smash{\bf dOrb}}_{\rm rig}^{\rm NC}. After choose an equivariant FOP perturbation, denoted by 𝔽̊γℤ𝗉\mathring{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}, one obtains a complex with a ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-action, denoted by
C⁡(𝔽̊γℤ𝗉).C(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}).
Its ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part provides a complex
C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,γ)CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},\gamma)
which is a module over Λ𝐅𝗉Γ⊕ℤ\Lambda_{{\bf F}_{\sf p}}^{\Gamma\oplus{\mathbb{Z}}}. By tensoring with the larger Novikov field Λ𝐊𝗉Γ\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Gamma} one obtains a Floer-type complex
C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,γ,Λ𝐊𝗉Γ).CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},\gamma;\Lambda_{{\bf K}_{\sf p}}^{\Gamma}).
By using the equivariant continuation map, one proves that the filtered isomorphism class is well-defined. Hence one obtains a barcode
ℬℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,γ){\mathcal{B}}_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},\gamma)
which only depends on HH. Again, choosing a homologous loop γ′\gamma^{\prime} will shift the barcodes but does not change the bar-length spectrum.
28.4. Equivariant pair-of-pants product
One can construct the noncontractible version of the equivariant pair-of-pants product. Let HH be a Hamiltonian such that H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}} is nondegenerate. Let γ(𝗉)\gamma^{({\sf p})} be the 𝗉{\sf p}-th iteration of γ\gamma. Basically, the same setup as the contractible case provides a multimodule
𝕏γ𝔽​𝕊​𝕥{\mathbb{X}}_{\gamma}^{\mathbb{FSt}}
over (𝔽γ,…,𝔽γ,𝔼,𝔽γ(𝗉)ℤ𝗉)({\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma},\ldots,{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma},{\mathbb{E}};{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma^{({\sf p})}}^{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}). More precisely, let x1,…,x𝗉x_{1},\ldots,x_{\sf p} be objects of 𝔽γ{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma} whose underlying loops x¯1,…,x¯𝗉\underline{\smash{x}}_{1},\ldots,\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p} are homologous to γ\gamma. Let x¯′\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime} be a Hamiltonian loop of H♮​𝗉H^{\natural{\sf p}} homologous to γ(𝗉)\gamma^{({\sf p})}. Consider pp-legged pair-of-pants forming a cobordism (up to equality of symplectic area) between x¯1⊔⋯⊔x¯𝗉\underline{\smash{x}}_{1}\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\underline{\smash{x}}_{\sf p} represented by a map u:Σ𝔽​𝕊​𝕥→Xu:\Sigma^{\mathbb{FSt}}\to X. Then the γ\gamma-cappings x1,…,x𝗉x_{1},\ldots,x_{\sf p} together with the relative homology class of uu induces a γ(𝗉)\gamma^{({\sf p})}-capping of x¯′\underline{\smash{x}}^{\prime} as illustrated in Figure 11.
Figure 11. Configurations of equivariant pair-of-pants product for noncontractible orbits
The AMS construction and FOP perturbation provide a chain map
CFγ(H)⊗⋯⊗⋯CFγ(H)⏟𝗉⊗C​M​(f𝔼)→C⁡(𝔽̊γ(𝗉)ℤ𝗉).\underbrace{CF_{\gamma}(H)\otimes\cdots\otimes\cdots CF_{\gamma}(H)}_{{\sf p}}\otimes CM(f^{{\mathbb{E}}})\to C(\mathring{\mathbb{F}}_{\gamma^{({\sf p})}}^{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}).
Restricting to the ℤ𝗉{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}-invariant part one obtains
Pγ:Cℤ𝗉​(C​Fγ​(H)⊗𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,γ(𝗉)).P_{\gamma}:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(CF_{\gamma}(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},\gamma^{({\sf p})}).
Proposition 28.3.
PγP_{\gamma} is a filtered chain homotopy equivalence of Floer-type complexes.
Proof.
The argument is similar to the contractible case. One can first define the reduced versions
Cℤ𝗉red​(C​Fγ​(H)⊗𝗉),\displaystyle\ C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF_{\gamma}(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}}),\
C​Fℤ𝗉red​(H♮​𝗉,γ(𝗉))\displaystyle\ CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},\gamma^{({\sf p})})
(see (27.1) and Lemma 27.7) which are filtered chain homotopy equivalent to the unreduced versions via the homological perturbation construction. Moreover, for each orbit x∈𝒪~γ​(H)x\in\tilde{\mathcal{O}}_{\gamma}(H), one has a local equivariant pair-of-pants product PxP_{x} which can be proved to be invertible. Moreover, the direct sum of PxP_{x} is the leading order term of PγP_{\gamma}. Then PγP_{\gamma} is transferred to a filtered isomorphism
Pγred:Cℤ𝗉red​(C​Fγ​(H)⊗𝗉)→C​Fℤ𝗉​(H♮​𝗉,γ(𝗉)).∎P_{\gamma}^{\rm red}:C_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}^{\rm red}(CF_{\gamma}(H)^{\otimes{\sf p}})\to CF_{{{\mathbb{Z}}_{\sf p}}}(H^{\natural{\sf p}},\gamma^{({\sf p})}).\qed
Proof of Theorem 1.12.
The isomorphism class of the Floer-type complex is disucssed in Section 28.3. Proposition 28.3 shows Theorem 1.12 (2) holds. Finally, Theorem 1.12 (3) follows from the same argument as in Section 27.5 with the above ingredients.
∎

Instructions for reporting errors
We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
methods listed below:
Click the "Report Issue" (
) button, located in the page header.
Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.
Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
all.
Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a list of packages that need conversion, and welcome developer contributions.
